findings.title: Update artifacts are installed with no hash verification at all — sha256 files generated in CI are never checked by the client
findings.note: _install = ACTION_VIEW (VpnServiceBridge.kt:101-109)/explorer; no digest check anywhere in lib/.
findings.evidence: updates_screen.dart `_install`: `if (Platform.isAndroid) { await const MethodChannel('vpn_service').invokeMethod<void>('installUpdate', {'url': info.assetUrl}); } else if (Platform.isWindows) { await Process.start('explorer', <String>[info.assetUrl]); }` — with the comment 'Install itself is the platform installer (FileProvider intent on Android, Explorer on Windows) launched from the asset URL'. VpnServiceBridge.kt:106-109 implements it as `activity.startActivity(Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url)))` — no download by the app, no digest check, no FileProvider. Repo-wide grep for sha256/digest in lib/ finds only Argon2id in backup_service.dart. Meanwhile CI publishes 'sha256sum "$name"
findings.fix: Download the artifact in-app (or via the platform service) over HTTPS, compute SHA-256, and verify it before handing the file to any installer. findings.title: "Max WFP firewall" kill switch does not exist on any platform; engine death reverts all traffic to cleartext while the UI reports blocked
findings.evidence: lib/main.dart:184-186 admits: "a true OS-level fail-closed filter (device-wide block-all except the tunnel, surviving engine death) needs native code that does not exist yet on either platform". PolicyFirewallAdapter.enforce() (main.dart:200) is a pure Dart array check; android BoxEngine.kt:257 does `builder.setBlocking(false)` (the opposite of lockdown) and adds only routing, never a disallow/lockdown; repo-wide grep over *.dart/*.kt/*.cpp/*.ps1 finds zero WFP/netsh/Fwpm/iptables code (windows/runner has none). On crash, Tunnel._block() only flips Dart state: "_firewallEnforced = true; ... _setState(TunnelState.blocked)" — no OS filtering happens, so the user is told they are protected whil
findings.fix: Implement the native layer: Android — keep the TUN alive in a persistent foreground service with builder.setBlocking(true) + addRoute(0.0.0.0/0) (or platform always-on-VPN lockdown) so engine death blacks out traffic instead of reverting to the physical uplink; Windows — an elevated helper/service that installs WFP block-all-except-tunnel filters r

findings.title: No auto-reconnect on network switch, network loss, or engine crash — TunnelState.reconnecting is dead code and every failure strands the user until a manual tap

findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:321-325: 'Connectivity changes & debounce: ConnectivityManager.registerNetworkCallback ... on onAvailable/onLost/onCapabilitiesChanged, AutoTunnelService queues with debounceDelay (default 500ms)'; README 5.x 'Seamless roaming/recovery' (RoamingHandler.kt); research/06-V2RayNG.md:448: 'START_STICKY ensures OS restarts after kill'. findings.fix: Add a connectivity-recovery seam to Tunnel: listen to default-network changes (Kotlin callback already exists) and engine crashes, re-run connect(lastTag) with a debounce after onAvailable, enter TunnelState.reconnecting during the retry window, and cap retries with backoff; treat blocked(airplaneMode) as retry-on-network-return rather than termina

findings.title: Cold start / reopen shows hardcoded Disconnected: no reconciliation between UI state and the actually-running engine
findings.evidence: FlClash's core 'survives Activity recreation, survives Flutter engine restart, force-restart via core status check and force restart' (research/11-FlClash.md:299) and V2RayNG uses START_STICKY + setOngoing so the OS restores it (research/06-V2RayNG.md:448). In the app, VpnNotifier.build() hardcodes 'return VpnState.disconnected();' (vpn_notifier.dart:103) with no query of engine state (no service-status command per docs/decisions.tsv, and BoxEngine.writeConnectionEvents(events) {} is inert — BoxEngine.kt:166); QanatVpnService returns START_NOT_STICKY (QanatVpnService.kt:27). Result: after hours backgrounded or an Activity recreation, the UI shows Disconnected while the in-process libbox engine
findings.fix: On VpnNotifier.build() (and Activity resume via an AppLifecycleState observer), probe real engine state: on Android attach a CommandClient status/log query or have Kotlin BoxEngine report engineRunning over the box_events channel; reconcile VpnState from that instead of defaulting to disconnected.

findings.fix: Whitelist the wildcard to the fork's transport enum (ws/grpc/httpupgrade/xhttp/http/quic, per option/v2ray_transport.go _V2RayTransportOptions.Type) and return null for anything else, mirroring the legacy-network default branch. Shared with vless/trojan emit paths.

findings.title: Clash SS plugin re-emitted verbatim as clash name 'obfs'/'simple-obfs' — engine FATALs whole profile; plugin-opts map silently dropped
findings.evidence: PROBE (real emitter): ClashYamlParser output for node {plugin: obfs, plugin-opts: {mode: http, host: bing.com}} → {"parsed_plugin":"obfs","parsed_pluginOpts":null,"re_emitted":{..."plugin":"obfs"}} — plugin-opts YAML map never read (only node['plugin'] at :176) and the clash plugin name is passed through verbatim. ENGINE (windows/sing-box.exe check): plugin "obfs" → FATAL initialize outbound[0]: plugin not found: obfs (EXIT=1); "simple-obfs" → same FATAL (EXIT=1); "obfs-local" and "v2ray-plugin" → EXIT=0. One such node FATALs the entire profile at engine start.
findings.fix: Normalize clash plugin names (obfs/simple-obfs → obfs-local) at parse and parse node['plugin-opts'] (YamlMap) into ShadowsocksEndpoint.pluginOpts; drop or flag nodes whose normalized plugin the fork does not embed.

findings.title: Single-port mport (mport=443) emits server_ports ["443"] which FATALs engine init: 'bad port range: 443'
findings.note: _hy2Ports only maps dash→colon; bare '443' passes through; fork ParsePorts requires ':'.
findings.evidence: _hy2Ports only does replaceAll('-',':') per entry (line 323); a bare single port passes through unchanged. Probes (windows/sing-box.exe check -c): server_ports ["443"] -> EXIT=1, 'FATAL initialize outbound[0]: bad port range: 443'; ["20000-30000"] -> EXIT=1 same error; ["443:443"] -> EXIT=0; ["20000:30000","40000:50000"] -> EXIT=0. Root cause: sing-quic@v0.7.0-beta.3/hysteria/client.go ParsePorts line 118: 'if !strings.Contains(portRange, ":") { return nil, E.New("bad port range: ", portRange) }'. A link like hysteria2://a@h:443?mport=443 (legitimate single-port hop) therefore bricks the whole profile at connect (one bad node FATALs service start; import does not run check).
findings.fix: In _hy2Ports, if an entry contains neither ':' nor '-', emit 'N:N' (probed accepted). Dash form is already handled; also consider rejecting out-of-0-65535 entries with FormatException instead of letting the engine FATAL.

findings.fix: Add engine-parity validation: in RoutingCompiler._compileGroups urltest branch, flag interval > 30m when idle_timeout is not emitted (or better, per handoff follow-up #5, add idleTimeout to OutboundGroup.urlTest and emit `idle_timeout: max(interval, 30m)` at BOTH emitter sites — routing_compiler.dart:106 and profile_config_source.dart:_groupJson:30

findings.title: Foreground service uses dataSync type — Android 15+ kills it after the 6h/24h dataSync budget, mid-tunnel
findings.note: Lines 31-34 exact, manifest declares dataSync|remoteMessaging. Android 15+ hard-stops dataSync FGS after 6h/24h: stopSelf demotes the process, then cached-app freeze/Doze kills the in-process libbox engine — the exact overnight-tunnel failure class AGENTS.md's Doze boundary targets.
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/06-V2RayNG.md:472 shows v2rayNG declaring 'FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE (API 34+)' — the special-use type exists precisely because dataSync is restricted. App side: ForegroundService.kt:31-32 starts with `ServiceInfo.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC or ... REMOTE_MESSAGING` and the manifest declares those types (Android 15+ hard-stops a dataSync FGS after 6h cumulative in 24h). The tunnel itself sits in QanatVpnService, but the process-priority/ notification backing dies with ForegroundService — 'app backgrounded for hours' (overnight lock) is exactly the case, after which Doze can reclaim the process and kill the in-process engine. goal.md §1
findings.fix: Switch the foreground service type to specialUse (with the Play justification) or connectedDevice per platform guidance, and re-establish the tunnel from the service if the FGS is restarted.

findings.title: No OS-level fail-closed kill switch on either platform; FirewallAdapter 'enforce' is a self-validating no-op, so every engine-crash / app-kill / revoke window leaks all traffic to the physical interface
findings.note: Confirmed; one correction: _block() DOES close the fd (tunnel.dart:564-567) — TUN dies with engine, so the window is offline/no-filter, not traffic-revert.
findings.evidence: main.dart lines 183-188: "Platform note: a true OS-level fail-closed filter (device-wide block-all except the tunnel, surviving engine death) needs native code that does not exist yet on either platform — Android `VpnService` `setBlocking(true)` + `addRoute(0.0.0.0/0)` lockdown in `QanatVpnService`, Windows WFP rules in the runner." PolicyFirewallAdapter.enforce() body is only "final errors = _policy.validateOrdering(_policy.baseRules());" — it validates its own generated list, not any config sent to the engine. tunnel.dart _block() on crash (line 529) calls this same no-op enforce then closes the fd; nothing blocks subsequent packets at the OS layer. QanatVpnService.kt has no onRevoke overrid
findings.fix: Implement the admitted-missing native layer: Android lockdown mode (addRoute 0.0.0.0/0 + setBlocking(true) or Always-on+block-without-VPN intent), Windows WFP block-all-except-sing-box rules; make enforce() push real state and verify it, not re-validate its own JSON.

findings.title: Log export is a no-op: 'Export' only print()s to stdout, users on Android/Windows cannot obtain or share logs for bug reports
findings.note: Verified: _export only print()s; no Clipboard, no file write, no share_plus. But no security/data-loss impact — user-facing-tooling gap.
findings.evidence: The Logs screen share icon (logs_screen.dart:214) calls _export() which does ONLY `print(buffer.toString())` — on Android the app's stdout goes to logcat (invisible without adb/developer options) and on Windows a release build has no attached console; the user cannot copy or save anything. The method's own comment claims 'copy the visible lines to a buffer the user pastes into a bug report' but there is no Clipboard.setData, no share sheet, and no file write — pubspec.yaml has no share_plus/path_provider, while the same app already writes real files via `FilePicker.saveFile(... bytes:)` for encrypted backups (lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_screen.dart:155-158). Competitors: v2rayNG's
findings.fix: Reuse the existing FilePicker.saveFile byte path (endpoints_screen.dart pattern) to write a `qanatvpn-logs-<ts>.txt`, plus Clipboard.setData for one-tap copy; add share_plus (ask-first per AGENTS.md) for the Android share sheet.

findings.title: Install flow is a browser handoff: 'Download & install' opens the asset URL via explorer / bare ACTION_VIEW — no in-app download, no progress, no installer intent, no post-install detection
findings.note: Windows explorer handoff + Android bare ACTION_VIEW confirmed; no progress/post-install check. Flow does still complete, just abandoned mid-way.
findings.evidence: research/01-Karing.md:523: 'App: AutoUpdateManager ... download via dio to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() + open_file/app_installer install' and :594 'v1.2.19.2200: Fixed macOS failed launch after automatic update package installation' — Karing downloads and hands to the installer fully in-app. QANATVPN instead: updates_screen.dart:117-127 Windows branch `await Process.start('explorer', <String>[info.assetUrl])` (opens the GitHub download URL in a browser and abandons the flow) and Android branch `invokeMethod<void>('installUpdate', {'url': info.assetUrl})` whose Kotlin side (VpnServiceBridge.kt:101-114) is just `Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url))` — the user downloads the APK in
findings.fix: Implement the pending installer service: Android DownloadManager (progress in the update card) + FileProvider ACTION_INSTALL_PACKAGE intent with REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES permission; Windows download to temp with progress bytes and Process.start on the downloaded .zip/.exe, plus a post-install state check comparing package version to the offered one

findings.title: Kill switch is not OS-enforced: engine death fails open, and the Blocked state never tears down the TUN
findings.note: Confirmed no-OS-lockdown core; but its extra claim 'Blocked never tears down the TUN' is wrong — _block closes fd at tunnel.dart:564.
findings.evidence: Competitor side: goal.md §12 locks 'max firewall WFP/iptables/pf + in-tunnel DNS + IPv6 block + 7 tests'; research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:256 documents 'Lockdown mode / kill switch (custom, not just Android Always-On)' and research/10-WireSock.md:289 'KillSwitch / Network Lock — enabled/disabled'. App side: lib/main.dart:184-188 admits in its own comment 'a true OS-level fail-closed filter (device-wide block-all except the tunnel, surviving engine death) needs native code that does not exist yet on either platform — ... Until those land, the engine rule ordering below is the kill-switch'; PolicyFirewallAdapter.enforce() (lib/main.dart:190+) only validates rule ordering of a Dart list — no iptables/
findings.fix: Implement the OS lockdown: Android setBlocking(true)+addRoute(0.0.0.0/0) in QanatVpnService kept alive while blocked, Windows WFP block-all in the runner; and close the TUN on the crash path.

findings.title: No proxy-group member selection or node switching — connect tag is auto-derived
findings.note: Code citations verified, but 'no user choice' overstated: groups_screen.dart:276-362 persists a chosen member as group.defaultMember (policy store) and selectedEndpointProvider honors it. Missing is the tap-to-select/node-picker flow, not selection itself.
findings.evidence: Clash-family clients make member selection the primary interaction: Verge polls 'PUT /proxies/:groupName (body { name: proxyName }) → select node in group' (research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:371) and FlClash 'Tap select → immediate switch, Connections page updates route' (research/11-FlClash.md §8), with Verge persisting it via 'profile.store-selected: true' across restarts. The app auto-derives the connect tag with no user choice: selected_endpoint.dart:38-73 walks 'group.defaultMember / members.first' and falls back to 'endpoints.first.tag' then 'vendoredEndpointTag'; home.dart:94-96 hardcodes 'await notifier.connect(ref.read(selectedEndpointProvider).tag)'. There is no store for a chosen mem
findings.fix: Add a persisted selection store (selected tag per selector group + global tag), a node-picker (tap endpoint/group card to select), and on connect emit the selector's chosen member so the engine honors it; remember the choice across restarts (store-selected parity).

findings.title: No tap-to-select server flow: user cannot choose which endpoint to connect to
findings.note: ListTile verified delete-only, no onTap — flow absent. But absolute claim wrong: user can pick the connect target by setting a selector group's defaultMember in the groups editor (persisted). Missing flow = UX parity gap, not capability.
findings.evidence: Competitors make server picking a primary flow: research/01-Karing.md:545 'Switcher: HomeScreen current select dropdown → select_server screen (lib/screens/select_server_screen.dart), latency badge per proxy, drag-reorder'; research/06-V2RayNG.md:452 'LazyColumn server list, swipe-to-delete'. In this app the endpoints screen is terminal: lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_screen.dart:94-115 renders each StoredEndpoint as a Card/ListTile whose only action is a delete IconButton — the ListTile has no onTap and no 'use this server' control. Active server is computed implicitly in lib/modules/vpn/logic/selected_endpoint.dart:5-14 ('Resolution order: 1. the first group's default member or fir
findings.fix: Make each endpoint row tappable: tap writes a selectedTag to a persisted preference that selectedEndpointProvider reads before the group/first-endpoint fallback, with a check/radio indicator on the active row (plus a 'Test & connect' action). This matches Karing's select_server flow and requires only a small store + provider change.

The v0.1.0 release asset qanatvpn_v0.1.0_windows-x64.zip therefore contains an Authenticode-unsigned qanatvpn

findings.title: Trojan share-link password not percent-decoded (corrupted credentials shipped)
findings.note: parsers.dart:803 raw userInfo confirmed; but corrupted creds fail auth on that one endpoint at connect — profile does not FATAL. Same bug rated high at idx 118; critical inflated.
findings.evidence: PROBE (real Dart emitter, dart --packages=.dart_tool/package_config.json): input 'trojan://pa%40ss%3Aword%2Fx@203.0.113.10:443#t' → {"raw_userInfo_password":"pa%40ss%3Aword%2Fx","expected_decoded":"pa@ss:word/x"}. Dart Uri.userInfo returns the raw percent-encoded string; no decodeComponent is applied, so the engine receives the literal percent-triplets as the password and server auth silently fails. Contrast: SshUriParser (parsers.dart:595-599) explicitly Uri.decodeComponent the password part — the convention exists in the codebase but was missed for trojan.
findings.fix: password: Uri.decodeComponent(uri.userInfo) at parsers.dart:803; audit sibling raw-userInfo reads (vless uuid :635, hysteria2 auth, tuic) for the same gap.

findings.title: hy2/tuic URI userinfo is never percent-decoded, so encoded credentials are emitted corrupted (auth always fails)
findings.note: parsers.dart:841/871-872 raw userInfo confirmed; auth-failure impact, not profile-bricking FATAL. Aggregated as high at idx 118.
findings.evidence: Dart probe (real dart run): Uri.parse('hysteria2://p%40ss:w%3Ard@h.example.com:443').userInfo -> 'p%40ss:w%3Ard' (RAW, Uri.userInfo does not percent-decode in Dart). Hysteria2UriParser stores auth: uri.userInfo verbatim; TuicUriParser splits the same raw string (uuid/password). Emitted JSON then carries the encoded password (endpoint_outbound.dart:145-163 'password': e.auth; _tuic 'password': e.password) -> server auth always fails for any credential containing @ : / % # ?. Contrast: SshUriParser (parsers.dart:~915) correctly wraps its password in Uri.decodeComponent, so the pattern exists but was missed here. Official hy2/tuic URI specs require percent-encoding special chars in userinfo.
findings.fix: Wrap in Uri.decodeComponent: hy2 auth (parsers.dart:841), tuic uuid+password (parsers.dart:871-872). Note: trojan (parsers.dart TrojanUriParser password: uri.userInfo) and vless share the same raw-userInfo pattern and need the identical one-line fix family.

findings.title: Seeded/bundled geo assets are dead wiring: engine must download remote rule-sets through PROXY at every start (Windows: no cache file at all) and a failed fetch aborts box start before the TUN opens
findings.note: No initial_path or cache_file anywhere in repo (grep); ruleSetEntries emits remote-only; seeded cache dir is never referenced by any emitter.

In the fork, a remote rule-set with no cached copy and no initial_path MUST fetch at
findings.fix: Emit `initial_path` in the profile's rule_set entries pointing at the seeded cache (`GeoAsset.getPath(tag)` copied into the engine-accessible filesDir/basePath), or switch the emitted entries to `type:"local"` backed by the seeded files; additionally enable `experimental.cache_file` in the Windows config so successful fetches persist across starts.

findings.title: App exit orphans sing-box.exe: TUN/routes stay up, temp config with private keys persists, relaunch spawns a second engine
findings.note: main.cpp:33 SetQuitOnClose(true); no AppLifecycleListener/didRequestAppExit in lib/; adapter has no teardown hook; Process.start is not Job-object wrapped.
findings.evidence: windows/runner/main.cpp:33 `window.SetQuitOnClose(true);` quits the Flutter process immediately on window close, and nothing stops the engine: grep of lib/ shows no AppLifecycleListener/didRequestAppExit; the only box.stop() path is the user-initiated Tunnel.disconnect (lib/modules/vpn/logic/vpn_notifier.dart:115 `await ref.read(tunnelProvider).disconnect();`), and WindowsBoxProcessAdapter exposes no dispose/teardown hook. dart:io Process.start does not place the child in a kill-on-close Job object, so when the parent dies the child survives. Consequence: connect → close the window → sing-box.exe keeps running with its wintun TUN and auto_route up while the user believes the app is closed; o
findings.fix: Add an exit hook: `AppLifecycleListener(onExitRequested: (type) async { await tunnel.disconnect(); return AppExitResponse.exit; })` (Windows supports didRequestAppExit on last-window close), and/or spawn the child under a Job object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE via a small native shim so abrupt parent death reaps sing-box.exe.

findings.title: Endpoints mutations re-read the store file while a debounced save is pending — rapid consecutive edits resurrect deleted endpoints and silently drop imports
findings.note: delete/importText/saveManual all build next from store.read() disk state while DebouncedSaver (300ms latest-wins, verified) holds pending writes.
findings.fix: Derive the next list from the authoritative in-memory state instead of the file: importText/saveManual use `final existing = state.endpoints;` and delete uses `final next = <StoredEndpoint>[...state.endpoints];` (delete's index already refers to the rendered state list); alternatively call _saver.flush() before store.read().

findings.title: plainFetch has no response/body timeout: a stalled server hangs the fetch (and every consumer) indefinitely
findings.note: plain_fetch.dart has connectionTimeout only; no .timeout on close() or body fold.
findings.evidence: plain_fetch.dart: `final client = HttpClient()..connectionTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 15);` then `final response = await request.close();` and `final body = await response.fold<List<int>>(<int>[], (acc, chunk) => acc..addAll(chunk));`. connectionTimeout only bounds TCP connect; waiting for response headers and draining the body are unbounded. Proven empirically by running this exact function structure against a local server that accepts TCP and never responds: 'STILL HANGING at 0:00:25.0 (connectionTimeout was 3s) - plainFetch unbounded'. Consumers have no watchdog either (grep: no .timeout in any network path): UpdateController.checkNow sets `state = const UpdateChecking()` (updates_c
findings.fix: Bound the whole request lifecycle: `final response = await request.close().timeout(const Duration(seconds: 30));` and `final body = await response.fold<List<int>>(...).timeout(const Duration(seconds: 60));`, and change the finally to `client.close(force: true);` so the abandoned socket is torn down immediately when a timeout fires (close() without

findings.title: VpnNotifier maps TunnelState.connected to VpnState.connected(_lastTag ?? '') — emits an empty-string tag whenever a connected status arrives before/without connect()
findings.note: vpn_notifier.dart:88 '_lastTag ?? ''' with _lastTag assigned only in connect() (lines 107/110).
findings.evidence: build() subscribes: `TunnelState.connected => VpnState.connected(_lastTag ?? '')`. `_lastTag` is only assigned inside `connect()`: `Future<void> connect(String tag) async { _lastTag = tag; ... }`. The Tunnel fires `connected` on its own in several flows without a fresh connect() call on this notifier instance: (1) a crash event arriving while still connecting bumps the epoch and _block()s, and any later state flow can emit connected after a rebuilt notifier; (2) production wiring is `tunnelProvider.overrideWith((ref) => ref.watch(tunnelAssemblyProvider))` with all adapters `overrideWithValue`, but a notifier rebuild (riverpod provider invalidation) re-subscribes to the same live Tunnel whose
findings.fix: In the status listener, resolve the tag independently of connect(): `TunnelState.connected => VpnState.connected(_lastTag ?? ref.read(selectedEndpointProvider).tag)` (or persist the last non-null tag on the notifier and reuse it). Never emit the empty-string sentinel.

findings.title: parseShareLines catches only FormatException — one TypeError from a single bad vmess/sing-box/clash node aborts the entire subscription import
findings.note: parseShareLines catches only FormatException (ingestion_adapter.dart:119-131).
findings.fix: In parseShareLines, catch the boundary broadly and re-wrap: `} on Object catch (e) { failures.add(FormatException(e.toString())); }`. Better: fix the cast sites (next findings) so malformed input throws FormatException as the fuzz tests demand.

findings.title: VmessUriParser casts unvalidated base64-JSON fields — missing/non-string 'add'/'id' throws _TypeError instead of FormatException
findings.note: parsers.dart:688-690 casts doc['add']/doc['id'] unvalidated; stringField coercer exists but unused here.
findings.evidence:
```dart
return VmessEndpoint(
  tag: doc['ps'] as String? ?? '${doc['add']}:$port',
  address: doc['add'] as String,
  port: intField(port, 'vmess port'),
  uuid: doc['id'] as String,
```
`doc['add']`/`doc['id']`/`doc['ps']` are cast, not coerced. Verified against the real parser: `vmess://<b64 of {"v":"2","ps":"x","port":"443","id":"uuid"}>` (missing add) throws `_TypeError: type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'String' in type cast` at parsers.dart:688; a nested `"add":{"x":1}` throws the Map variant. The repo's own fuzz group ('malformed input throws FormatException, not TypeError') is violated — the TypeError escapes the per-line skip in parseShareLines and kills the whole bundle (see se

findings.title: SingboxJsonParser casts engine-shaped fields: hysteria2 'server_ports' list and string 'alter_id' throw _TypeError — importing a real sing-box hysteria2 config crashes
findings.note: parsers.dart:480 'as String?' and :418 'as int? ?? 0' verified verbatim.
findings.evidence: parsers.dart:480: `ports: node['server_ports'] as String?,` — sing-box 1.14 emits `"server_ports": ["20000:50000"]` (Listable). Verified: feeding a well-formed sing-box config `"server_ports":["20000:50000"]` through SingboxJsonParser throws `_TypeError: type 'List<dynamic>' is not a subtype of type 'String?' in type cast` → whole import dies. parsers.dart:418: `alterId: node['alter_id'] as int? ?? 0` — `"alter_id":"0"` throws `_TypeError: type 'String' is not a subtype of type 'int?'` (the URI vmess parser correctly coerces via `intField(doc['aid'], ...)`). Secondary: `hopIntervalSeconds: node['hop_interval'] is String ? int.tryParse(node['hop_interval'] as String) : ...` — `int.tryParse('3
findings.fix: server_ports: accept String or List (`final sp = node['server_ports']; ports: sp is String ? sp : sp is List ? sp.join(',') : null`); alter_id: `node['alter_id'] == null ? 0 : intField(node['alter_id'], 'alter_id')`; hop_interval: reuse `_durationSeconds()` which already parses '1h30m' forms.

findings.title: ClashYamlParser hysteria2: `(node['obfs'] as YamlMap?)` throws on mihomo's standard scalar form `obfs: salamander` — whole clash import crashes
findings.note: Same code as idx 101 at parsers.dart:198.
findings.evidence:
```dart
obfsPassword: (node['obfs'] as YamlMap?)?['password'] as String?,
```
Clash/mihomo's documented hysteria2 shape is `obfs: salamander` + `obfs-password: xxx` (scalar obfs, sibling password key); the map form `{obfs: {type: ..., password: ...}}` is the sing-box style. Verified against the real parser: a mihomo-format config with `obfs: salamander` / `obfs-password: obfspass` throws `_TypeError: type 'String' is not a subtype of type 'YamlMap?' in type cast` at parsers.dart:198 → the entire clash subscription import dies (ClashYamlParser.parse has no per-node catch either). The same file reads `node['obfs-password']` nowhere.

findings.title: 6h parse cache is keyed only on URL; EndpointsController uses the constant Uri.parse('pasted') for all pasted text, so pasting different content returns the FIRST paste's endpoints
findings.note: Cache keyed on subscription.url only; endpoints_controller.dart:90 uses constant origin 'pasted' for all text imports.
findings.evidence: ingestion_adapter.dart:35/46: `final cached = _cache[subscription.url];` / `_cache[subscription.url] = _CachedParse(endpoints, _now());` — key is URL only, never content. The only production caller builds `RawSubscription(bytes: bytes, url: Uri.parse(origin))` where `origin = 'pasted'` for text imports (endpoints_controller.dart: `var origin = 'pasted';` … `url: Uri.parse(origin)`), so every paste shares one key. Verified: `adapter.parseAndNormalize(sub(trojan…, url: Uri.parse('pasted')))` → [A]; then `parseAndNormalize(sub(vless…, url: Uri.parse('pasted')))` with completely different bytes → returns [A] for 6 hours. primeCache after the >64KB isolate path poisons the same key too. Users pas
findings.fix: Make the cache key content-aware, e.g. `Object cacheKey = subscription.url.scheme.isEmpty ? Object() : subscription.url;` or key on `url.toString() + sha256(bytes)`; simplest correct fix: in the controller use a unique Uri for pastes (e.g. `Uri.parse('pasted:#$counter')`) or skip parseAndNormalize caching when origin == 'pasted'.

findings.title: vmess ws Host header silently dropped on all import paths (v2rayN 'host' key, clash ws-opts.headers.Host, and the emitter) — CDN-fronted vmess+ws nodes break
findings.note: VmessUriParser reads only doc['path']; clash vmess only ws-opts path; VmessEndpoint has no wsHost field; emitter passes wsPath only.

Verified: v2rayN JSON `{…"net":"ws","tls":"tls","sni":"s.com","host":"cdn.example.com","path":"/p"}` emits transport `{"type":"ws","path":"/p"}` — no Host header. A vmess+ws+CDN node (the standard censorship setup where Host is the伪装 domain) dials the IP with no Host →

findings.title: Share-link userinfo is never percent-decoded for trojan/hysteria2/tuic/vless — percent-encoded credentials are imported literally and auth fails at connect
findings.note: All four raw-userInfo sites verified (803, 841, 871-872, 623-626); Dart Uri.userInfo is raw. Correct severity anchor for the 96/98 family.
findings.evidence: parsers.dart:803 (trojan): `password: uri.userInfo,` · parsers.dart:841 (hy2): `auth: uri.userInfo,` · parsers.dart:871-872 (tuic): `uuid: split < 0 ? uri.userInfo : uri.userInfo.substring(0, split), password: split < 0 ? '' : uri.userInfo.substring(split + 1),` · parsers.dart:623-626 (vless): `uuid: userInfo.isNotEmpty ? userInfo : requireQuery(...)`. Dart's `Uri.userInfo` returns the raw encoded string (verified: `Uri.parse('hy2://pass%40word@h:443').userInfo == 'pass%40word'`). Verified via the real parser: `trojan://pass%23word%2Fx@h:443` imports password literally `pass%23word%2Fx` (expected `pass#word/x`), `hysteria2://pass%40x@h` imports `pass%40x`, `tuic://uuid:pw%23x@h` imports `pw%
findings.fix: Decode once per parser, e.g. in TrojanUriParser: `password: Uri.decodeComponent(uri.userInfo)`; same for hy2 `auth`, tuic uuid/password halves, vless uuid, and the user part of ssh.

findings.title: Windows release artifact is unsigned and 'installed' by opening a URL in Explorer — no signature, no hash, no origin pinning
findings.note: build-windows.yml has no signtool step; updates_screen.dart:129 opens explorer on the URL; build.gradle.kts:33 debug signingConfig confirmed.
findings.evidence: build-windows.yml bundles only `Copy-Item windows/sing-box.exe ... ; Compress-Archive ... ; Get-FileHash ... SHA256` — no signtool step anywhere in the workflow, and `Process.start('explorer', <String>[info.assetUrl])` opens the zip with no signature or hash validation. Windows SmartScreen will warn on unsigned downloads, but the app's own update flow bypasses even the hash files its own CI publishes. On Android the situation is worse: build.gradle.kts release buildType is `signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug")` with the comment 'Signing with the debug keys for now', so the APK the update flow opens is debug-signed regardless of the optional CI secrets step.
findings.fix: Add Authenticode signing (signtool with an EV/OV cert secret) to build-windows.yml and wire signingConfig from key.properties in build.gradle.kts (the CI secrets step already writes it but the Gradle file never reads it). Until signed, treat the update flow as integrity-unprotected.

findings.title: GitHub Pages mirror fallback is an independent update-decision point with no version-continuity check — downgrade/pinned-artifact window
findings.note: Verified: _fromMirror returns version+assetUrl with no continuity or origin pin; assetUrl launched verbatim. Mitigation nuance: UpdateController gates offering on isNewerThan (updates_controller.dart:70) and empty localVersion bypasses it — a downgrade needs a higher fake version, but arbitrary assetUrl from an unprotected gh-pages origin stands.
findings.evidence: UpdateSource.latestFor: `try { return await _fromApi(platformKey); } on Object { final mirrored = await _fromMirror(platformKey); ... }` — any API failure (including the 403/429 rate-limit exceptions that are correctly thrown) silently falls back to `https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/latest.json` (defaultMirrorUrl, updater.dart:149-150), whose entry supplies both `version` and `assetUrl: entry['url'] as String? ?? ''`. UpdateStore.save then persists it and _install launches `info.assetUrl`. There is no comparison against the API-provided version, no pinning of the artifact URL to the github.com release domain, and no freshness check — the mirror is a second same-org origin (github.io Pages)
findings.fix: In _fromMirror, reject entries older than the currently stored version (monotonic version floor) and validate assetUrl is an https URL on the project's release host before persisting or launching. Long term, the signed manifest from the hash-verification fix also covers the mirror.

findings.title: Engine FATAL on misconfigured WireGuard/AWG endpoint echoes the private key in hex, forwarded verbatim to the on-screen Logs tab (no redaction layer exists)
findings.note: Reproduced live on windows/sing-box.exe: FATAL prints private_key=<hex>; LogBus.add only truncates (4096) and collapses repeats; feed() forwards verbatim.
findings.evidence: Probe on the real shipped engine (windows/sing-box.exe, 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15): a wireguard endpoint with a wrong-length key passes `sing-box check` (exit 0) and at runtime start emits: 'FATAL[0000] start service: start outbound/wireguard[wg-short]: setup wireguard: private_key=73656372657431323334353637383930 public_key=... endpoint=203.0.113.10:51820 allowed_ip=0.0.0.0/0: IPC error -22: failed to set private_key: hex string does not fit the slice' — the hex is the actual private key material. The app pipeline forwards this verbatim: windows_box_process.dart feed() -> '_logBus.add(EngineLogLine.parse(line));' (line 115); log_bus.dart add() only truncates length ('message = message.substring(0
findings.fix: Add a redaction pass in LogBus.add (single choke point both platforms already flow through): scrub value payloads after 'private_key=', 'password=', 'uuid=', 'psk=', and collapse base64/hex runs >=32 chars to '[redacted]', before buffering and emitting. Optionally suppress the multi-line FATAL continuation lines that repeat wireguard device fields.

findings.title: plainFetch sends no User-Agent; GitHub API rejects every updater request with 403, silently forcing all users onto the unauthenticated mirror channel
findings.note: Live probe: no-UA -> 403, UA -> 200 on this repo's API. plainFetch sets no UA; production updater (plainFetch) hits the !=200 HttpException path and silently falls to the mirror (currently 404).
findings.evidence: plain_fetch.dart:8-12: "final client = HttpClient()..connectionTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 15); try { final request = await client.getUrl(url); headers.forEach((name, value) => request.headers.add(name, value));" — no default User-Agent is ever added. The production updater path is UpdateSource(fetchImpl: plainFetch) (updater.dart:369, main updateFetchProvider => plainFetch). Proven live on this repo: `curl -H "User-Agent:" https://api.github.com/repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn/releases/latest` -> 403, `curl -A "curl/8"` same URL -> 200. UpdateFetcher then hits `if (response.statusCode == 403 && response.headers['x-ratelimit-remaining'] == '0')` (false — GitHub's UA 403 is a plain 403) and throw
findings.fix: Add a constant, quoted User-Agent in plainFetch (e.g. request.headers.set(HttpHeaders.userAgentHeader, 'qanatvpn/<version> (+github.com/QMahyar/qanatvpn)')) beforegetUrl, and treat the GitHub API as the trusted primary path again.

findings.title: Subscription/endpoint import fetches http:// URLs in cleartext, exposing WG private keys and server credentials to passive on-path observers and writing them plaintext to the 6h disk cache
findings.note: http:// branch verified at endpoints_controller.dart:92-99; payload parses into privateKey/password fields and is later persisted plaintext.
findings.evidence: endpoints_controller.dart:92-99: "if (maybeUrl != null && (maybeUrl.scheme == 'http' || maybeUrl.scheme == 'https') && maybeUrl.host.isNotEmpty && !trimmed.contains('\n')) { final response = await plainFetch(maybeUrl, ...); ... payload = utf8.decode(response.body, allowMalformed: true);". Subscription payloads parse into NormalizedEndpoint.privateKey / privateKeyPassphrase / protocol secrets (normalized_endpoint.dart:20,27), which are exactly what crosses the wire unencrypted on an http:// import; one on-path observer captures the user's tunnel credentials. After import the same secret-bearing payload is persisted into the HttpCache `<key>.body` plaintext for staleAfter (http_cache.dart:135)
findings.fix: Restrict the URL-fetch branch to scheme == 'https' and reject http with an explicit error; warn before import when the payload will contain private keys; do not write subscription bodies fetched from non-allowlisted origins into the shared disk cache.

findings.title: URI port accepted unvalidated (-1 to 2147483648); one bad share line FATALs the whole engine at connect
findings.note: Dart probe: Uri.parse accepts 99999, 2147483648, -1; parsers.dart lines 593/625/802/840/870 pass uri.port unvalidated; endpoint_outbound emits server_port verbatim; Go uint16 decode failure kills the whole config at start.
findings.evidence: parseShareUri users trust `uri.port` blindly: parsers.dart:625 `final port = uri.port == 0 ? 443 : uri.port;` (same at :593 ssh, :802 trojan, :840 hy2, :870 tuic) and endpoint_outbound.dart emits it verbatim: `'server_port': e.port` (lines 38, 63, 120, 134, 148, 168, 230). Running the repo's real parsers + real `sing-box.exe check`: input `vless://uuid@1.2.3.4:99999#p` -> parsed endpoint server_port `[99999]`; also `ss://...@1.2.3.4:-1` -> `-1`, `vless://...:2147483648` -> `2147483648` (Dart Uri.parse only rejects non-numeric ports, not out-of-range). Engine: `FATAL decode config: outbounds[0].server_port: json: cannot unmarshal number 99999 into Go struct field ... server_port of type uint1
findings.fix: Validate at parse time: accept only `uri.port >= 1 && uri.port <= 65535`, else throw FormatException('port out of range'). Also clamp/validate the ingest-time ints (ss port via intOf, keepalive, mtu) to protocol ranges so no out-of-uint16 value reaches endpointToOutboundJson.

findings.title: 6h ingestion cache keyed by URL only: all pasted imports share the 'pasted' key, so re-imports silently return the previous payload's endpoints
findings.note: Cache keyed on subscription.url only; 'pasted' pseudo-origin shared via Uri.parse('pasted'); 6h window in singleton provider verified. Collision bites the <=64KB parseAndNormalize path (typical pastes).
findings.evidence: ingestion_adapter.dart:35-47: `final cached = _cache[subscription.url]; if (cached != null && _now().difference(cached.parsedAt) < const Duration(hours: 6)) { return cached.endpoints; }` - keyed solely on `subscription.url`, never on payload bytes. Reproduced with repo code: parse payload A (tag `first`) then a different payload B (tag `second`) with the same url `pasted` -> `[cache-collision] OK -> first=first second-import-returned=first` - the second, different payload returned the first payload's endpoints. endpoints_controller.dart:90-114 sets `origin = 'pasted'` for every paste and `url: Uri.parse(origin)`, so ALL pasted imports share one cache key in the singleton `ingestionAdapterPro
findings.fix: Key the cache on a hash of the payload (e.g. sha256 of bytes) plus URL, or drop the cache entirely for the interactive import path (it only exists to dedupe isolate rehydration); at minimum never cache the 'pasted' pseudo-origin.

findings.title: Full engine config with WG/AWG private keys and server passwords written to unprotected %TEMP% file
findings.note: Verified: full config JSON (private_key, passwords) written to %TEMP%/qanatvpn_box_<ms>.json with default ACLs; _cleanupConfig comment 'Temp file leak is acceptable'.
findings.evidence: final json = jsonEncode(config.json); final file = File('${Directory.systemTemp.path}/qanatvpn_box_${DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch}.json'); await file.parent.create(recursive: true); await file.writeAsString(json); — TypedConfig.json is the full engine config including WireGuard/AWG 'private_key', trojan/vless/ssh 'password' and SS2022 keys (endpoint_outbound.dart:122 'password': e.password, :236 'private_key': e.privateKey). findings.title: Windows kill-switch is a no-op: PolicyFirewallAdapter.enforce() sets a bool instead of enforcing any OS firewall, and DesktopPlatformAdapter returns isVpnPermissionGranted()=true unconditionally
findings.note: Verified: enforce() only validates ordering + sets a bool; grep of lib/ and windows/runner for netsh/Wfp/Fwpm is empty; decisions.tsv:58 admits native lockdown missing; DesktopPlatformAdapter.isVpnPermissionGranted() => true.
findings.evidence: lib/main.dart:190-210: class PolicyFirewallAdapter implements FirewallAdapter { ... @override Future<void> enforce() async { final errors = _policy.validateOrdering(_policy.baseRules()); ... _enforced = true; } @override Future<void> relax() async { _enforced = false; } } — enforce() only validates rule ordering in memory; there is no netsh/WFP call anywhere (grep for netsh|Wfp|Fwpm across lib/ and windows/runner/ is empty). decisions.tsv:58 admits: 'firewall: PolicyFirewallAdapter no longer no-op — native OS lockdown documented as missing (QanatVpnService/WFP)'. findings.title: App exit, crash, or force-quit orphans sing-box.exe — an unmanaged VPN that keeps routing after the app is gone (no Windows Job Object, no lifecycle disconnect)
findings.note: Verified: taskkill only in stop(); SetQuitOnClose(true) in main.cpp, no Job Object; no AppLifecycleListener/SystemNavigator anywhere in lib/; vpn_notifier ref.onDispose only cancels a stream sub.
findings.evidence: stop() is the only teardown (taskkill by PID, lines 165-176) and there is no app-exit hook: windows/runner/main.cpp:33 'window.SetQuitOnClose(true);' with no Job object or OnClose disconnect (grep of windows/runner for Job|TerminateProcess|kill|sing-box returns nothing); no AppLifecycleListener/didChangeAppLifecycleState/SystemNavigator anywhere in lib/; VpnNotifier.ref.onDispose (vpn_notifier.dart:99) only cancels a stream subscription and never calls tunnel.disconnect()/box.stop(). If the Flutter app process dies (crash, taskkill, OS logout), the detached sing-box.exe keeps its wintun TUN and routes all traffic through the last config — invisible to the user and unstoppable from the app; c
findings.fix: Wrap the spawned sing-box.exe in a Windows Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE (native runner or FFI), and add an app-exit/shutdown hook (runner OnClose or AppLifecycleListener detached) that calls tunnel.disconnect() so the engine cannot outlive the UI process.

findings.title: Even the engine-level kill-switch rules (::/0 IPv6 block + RFC1918 LAN block) never reach the runtime config — they ship only through dead code

findings.title: Release-gating leak_test.sh cannot fail on a broken kill switch: SKIP counts as PASS, scenarios generate no traffic, and the split-audit check is inverted
findings.note: Verified: SKIP returns 0 -> check() prints PASS; scenario 1 is passive tcpdump, 2 is sleep 60; scenario 6 `! ss | grep 172.19.0` FAILs on any tunneled connection and PASSes on a leaky one, and no workflow references the script at all.
findings.evidence: leak_test.sh:21-22: `if ! have tcpdump; then echo "SKIP tcpdump missing"; return 0; fi` — the SKIP path returns 0, which check() (line 13) prints as PASS; on the Windows target tcpdump does not exist, so scenarios 1/2/4/5/7 pass with zero measurement. No scenario generates traffic: scenario 1 says "resolve a domain" but executes only `tcpdump_dnsleak 5` (passive listen, no resolver command), scenario 2 is just `sleep 60` (no suspend), scenario 3's handoff is a comment. Scenario 6 (line 61) `! ss -tnp 2>/dev/null | grep -q "172.19.0"` is inverted: any WORKING tunneled TCP connection has a local 172.19.0.x address in ss output → FAIL, while a fully leaked (physical-interface) connection has no
findings.fix: Make scenarios active: actually resolve a domain / send QUIC / toggle networks / suspend; exit nonzero on missing tools instead of SKIP-as-PASS; fix or delete the inverted split-audit check; wire the script into a release workflow job. Otherwise the AGENTS.md boundary "ship without sing-box check + 7 leak tests" cannot be enforced.

findings.title: Entire dependency lock (151 hosted packages) pinned to third-party mirror pub.flutter-io.cn; CI resolves against pub.dev and silently rewrites the whole lockfile, breaking the reproducible-builds guarantee
findings.note: Verified: 151/151 hosted entries pinned to pub.flutter-io.cn (single distinct url); no PUB_HOSTED_URL in either workflow; pub rewrites lockfile urls on re-resolve from pub.dev.

AGENTS.md institutionalizes this (`pub.dev 403s on this network → use PUB_HOSTED_URL=https://pub.flutter-io.cn`). The mirror returned a live `502 Bad Gateway (nginx/1.30.0)` during this audit. findings.fix: Run `dart pub get` against canonical pub.dev (or `flutter pub downgrade`/re-lock) so `url:` is https://pub.dev, commit that lock, and add `PUB_HOSTED_URL` explicitly to CI workflows only if the mirror must stay supported. findings.title: The 7-leak-test release gate is vacuous: missing tcpdump counts as PASS, the leak-detection logic is inverted, and two scenarios are placeholders with broken filters
findings.note: Leak-detection sub-claim is wrong: `(pipe) && return 1 || return 0` does return 1 (FAIL) on captured packets; only the comment is confused. SKIP→PASS, zero traffic generation, placeholder scenarios 3/6/7, and broken captive-portal filter all verified.
findings.evidence: (1) tcpdump_dnsleak() line 21: `if ! have tcpdump; then echo "SKIP tcpdump missing"; return 0; fi` — returns 0 which check() treats as PASS, so any environment without tcpdump reports "PASS startup-block" while testing nothing; scenarios 1,2,4,5,7 all inherit this. (2) Line 27-28 inverts the leak detection: `(timeout "$secs" tcpdump ... | grep -q . ) && return 1 || return 0; # any port-53 packets ... = leak → exit 0 above means found → fail` — when tcpdump DOES capture a port-53 packet (a leak), the subshell returns 1 and the function falls through to `return 0` (PASS); the `||` branch fires on grep failing (no packets = no leak) yet is documented as the fail path. The grep-based pass/fail c
findings.fix: Fix tcpdump_dnsleak so a captured packet yields exit 1 (fail) and make SKIP count as SKIP (not PASS); rewrite scenario 3 to actually simulate a handoff; implement the split-audit scenario against the per-app bypass list instead of a placeholder grep; scope the captive-portal capture to the portal's own IP/subnet; assert tcpdump is present and fail

findings.title: Windows sing-box.exe death with exit code 0 is invisible to the state machine: a 'stopped' event is emitted but Tunnel ignores it, leaving UI 'connected' over a dead tunnel
findings.evidence: windows_box_process.dart _exitWait handler: "if (!wasStopping && code != 0) { _events.add(BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.crashed, ...)); } else if (!wasStopping) { _events.add(const BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.stopped)); }" (lines ~100-110) — a zero exit while the app thinks the tunnel is up emits kind 'stopped'. tunnel.dart _onBoxEvent line 580: "if (event.kind != BoxEventKind.crashed) { return; }" — stopped is ignored, so TunnelState stays connected with the engine process gone. wintun adapters are destroyed on process exit, so routes vanish and all traffic reverts to the physical adapter; no restart exists anywhere in Tunnel (crash → _block → manual user action only). Graceful external termination (task
findings.fix: Treat an unrequested process exit as crashed regardless of exit code (or at minimum handle BoxEventKind.stopped in Tunnel._onBoxEvent when state is connected), then block + schedule auto-restart.

findings.title: Android engine-crash detection rides the log stream, can silently disable itself, and misses revoke/kill paths (no onRevoke, START_NOT_STICKY)
findings.note: CommandClientHandler.disconnected() emits crashed on command-stream drop, so engine process death is caught even without a FATAL line; true gaps are no onRevoke, silent attach disable (BoxEngine.kt:178), and START_NOT_STICKY (QanatVpnService.kt:27).
findings.evidence: BoxEngine.kt attachLogWatcher catch block: "Log.w(TAG, \"log watcher attach failed (crash events disabled)\", e)" (line 178) — startup continues with no crash detection at all. Detection itself is a substring scan: "if (message.contains(\"FATAL\")) { ... emitEvent(\"crashed\", message)" — a native/Go-runtime crash that never writes a FATAL log line emits nothing. QanatVpnService.kt: no onRevoke override (grep -rn onRevoke android/ → 0 hits), so system revocation (Settings→VPN off, another VPN connecting) tears down the TUN with no event to Dart; "return START_NOT_STICKY" means process death is never restarted. Combined with finding 2, each of these events is an unbounded plaintext window with
findings.fix: Override onRevoke in QanatVpnService to emit a crashed event to Dart; poll service liveness (or watch process death via onServiceDisconnected) instead of relying solely on the FATAL substring; fail loud if attachLogWatcher fails.

findings.title: The 7 leak tests are a release gate that has never been executed: v0.1.0 tagged and published without any on-device leak run, and CI has no leak job
findings.evidence: git tag v0.1.0 exists ("v0.1.0: first CI-verified release — AWG + 8 protocols ..."). tasks/handoff.md Next item 3: "**On-device proof**: install → wizard → connect → leak tests (`scripts/leak_test.sh`)." — still open after the tag. SPEC.md line 343 gate: "| Leak tests (7) | E2E manual on device (Android 13+, Win 11) | ... | Before every GitHub Release tag |". AGENTS.md Never list: "ship without `sing-box check` + 7 leak tests". CI (.github/workflows/build-android.yml line 68, build-windows.yml line 46) runs only "flutter test" — no workflow contains leak/tcpdump steps (grep -rni leak/tcpdump .github/workflows → 0 hits). AGENTS.md Testing also promises "test/integration/ (engine), androidTest
findings.fix: Make the gate mechanical before any further tag: an emulator/VM job that installs the APK, connects, and runs capture-based leak assertions; block release creation on its exit code.

findings.title: scripts/leak_test.sh is a no-op gate: every scenario SKIPs to PASS when tools are missing and none generates the traffic whose leak it purports to measure
findings.note: duplicate of idx 153; adds verified detail that no dig/nslookup/curl traffic generation exists (only ping in scenario 3).
findings.evidence: leak_test.sh line 21: "if ! have tcpdump; then echo \"SKIP tcpdump missing\"; return 0; fi" — a missing tool returns success, and check() records PASS ("if [ \"$2\" -eq 0 ]; then echo \"PASS  $1\""). tcpdump/ss/windump are absent by default on both Windows (where windump/ss do not ship) and Android termux, so the script exits PASS=7 FAIL=0 having captured nothing. No traffic is ever generated: tcpdump_dnsleak() only passively captures (comment says "while resolving" but the script contains no dig/nslookup/curl — grep count for those tools is 0), so scenario 1/2 measure 5 seconds of ambient silence. Scenario 3's network switch is a comment only: "# simulate switch: (ip link set $PHYS_IF down/
findings.fix: Rewrite as a real harness: require the tools (fail, not SKIP), generate traffic during each capture (dig + curl + browser), drive connect/disconnect/suspend states via adb, and assert per-scenario; only then can FAIL block a tag.

findings.title: No subscription-userinfo handling: remaining traffic/expiry quota from providers is never parsed or displayed

findings.fix: Capture subscription-userinfo + profile-update-interval headers on fetch into the SubscriptionStore record and render remaining traffic/expire on the endpoint tile (home.dart) like the prototype's profile card.

findings.title: Latency test is a raw TCP connect, not a URL test through the proxy, and per-node delay is not shown in the endpoints list

findings.evidence: Competitor: Karing 'Delay detection URL... default http://cp.cloudflare.com/generate_204... per-node latency shown in Select Server screen' (research/01-Karing.md §10); Hiddify 'manual tap runs Box.URLTest(tag) via gRPC → returns ms or timeout' with connection-test-url configurable (research/07-Hiddify.md §9). App: LatencyController sweeps 'final socket = await Socket.connect(host, port)' (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:26) — a TCP handshake that measures server reachability, not proxy health through the tunnel — and the endpoints screen never renders samples at all (no latency text in the ListTile at endpoints_screen.dart:94-121); libbox URLTest/Clash API is unused (grep clash_api: zero h
findings.fix: Route the sweep through the engine (libbox URLTest via CommandClient/Clash API, or an HTTP generate_204 GET through the selected outbound), keep TCP as fallback, and surface per-tag ms on both the endpoints list and group member picker.

findings.title: Rules list cannot be reordered even though sing-box route rules are first-match-wins ordered
findings.note: Workaround exists but is destructive: addRule only appends, so fixing one precedence means deleting and re-adding every later rule; in a first-match-wins system that is a correctness trap.
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/11-FlClash.md — 'Profiles → Rules tab visualizes ordered list with drag-to-reorder, type dropdown, target group dropdown'; first-match-wins is stated in the same file ('Rules matched top-to-bottom, first match wins — order matters, top = highest priority'). App side: lib/modules/routing/rules_controller.dart offers only addRule (line 63, appends to list end), updateRule, deleteRule (removeAt, line 81); lib/modules/routing/rules_screen.dart builds a plain ListView.builder with edit/delete trailing icons — grep for ReorderableList/reorder/drag across the routing module finds nothing. A user whose catch-all rule was added before a specific rule cannot fix precedence wi
findings.fix: Swap the rules list for ReorderableListView and add a `move(int old, int to)` mutation to RulesController that persists the reordered RuleDocument.

findings.fix: Expose a keygen either via a tiny Go binding (X25519 GenerateKey from the fork's wgtypes dep) or implement Curve25519 in Dart (cryptography package is already a dependency) with a 'Generate keypair' button in the AWG sheet that fills private key and optionally renders the public key for the server admin.

findings.title: AmneziaWG 3.1 params (HeaderProtectionKey, ContentPaddingAddition, timing ranges) accepted by the pinned engine are absent from the model and silently dropped on import

The pinned engine accepts these: go/amnezia-box/option/awg.go:37-43 HeaderProtectionKey string `json:"header_protection_key"`, ContentPaddingAddition, RekeyAfterTime...MaxHandshakeAttempts. App: AwgValues (lib/utils/amnezia_values.dart) has no fields for them, toEngineJson can never emit them, and WgIniParser's key switch (parsers.dart:885, cases privatekey..ib) has no headerprotectionkey/contentpaddi
findings.fix: Extend AwgValues with headerProtectionKey/contentPaddingAddition/timing-range fields (strings), add the corresponding WgIniParser and sing-box-JSON parser cases, emit them in toEngineJson (the fork's option struct already accepts them), and warn in AwgConfig.validate when they are absent while i1 is set.

App: the shell gates on the wizard — 'wizard.step == WizardStep.done ? child : Center(child: Wizard(...))' (app.dart:136) — and grep shows SplitChoice is written only by the wizard's finish(), read by profile_config_source.dart:85 and backup_service.dart, with no route or screen that re-opens it; the home WizardTile just navigates to '/home'.

findings.title: ETag machinery exists but is never wired to subscription fetches — subs use headerless plainFetch
findings.evidence: goal.md:9 'All formats + ETag 24h'; SPEC.md:404 'ETag checks for SRS + subs'; docs/prototype-final.html:319 shows per-sub 'ETag 304 • 6h cache' status. The cache layer is complete: http_cache.dart:31-86 implements If-None-Match, 304 refresh, 6h staleAfter, stale-while-revalidate. But its only production consumer is GeoAsset (main.dart:155, geo refreshAll). The endpoint import path (endpoints_controller.dart:96-105) calls plainFetch with headers const {'Accept': '*/*'} — plain_fetch.dart is explicitly 'no cache semantics', discards ETag handling, and the response headers are thrown away after the body is decoded. grep shows no other use of HttpCache. research/01-Karing.md:394 notes providers
findings.fix: Route subscription fetches through HttpCache (disk-backed per-URL entries) so If-None-Match/304 and 6h stale-while-revalidate apply to subs, and persist etag/fetchedAt per subscription.

findings.fix: Parse the subscription-userinfo header on fetch (plainFetch already returns headers), store upload/download/total/expire on the Subscription model, and render a traffic/expiry bar on the sub card.

Worse, START_STICKY (line 38) means a system kill restarts this service, which then shows 'Tunnel active' with a dead eng

App: AndroidManifest.xml has no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission and no <receiver>; QanatVpnService returns START_NOT_STICKY (line 27). tasks/plan.md:83 even promises the mitigation 'flutter_foreground_task with dataSync|remoteMessaging, autoRunOnBoot true' — flutter_foreground_task sits unused in pubspec.yaml (zero imports). After reboot the app stays di
findings.fix: Add RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED + a BOOT_COMPLETED receiver that either starts the tunnel via a persisted last-config path (requires a Kotlin-side start that can assemble config, or a headless Flutter engine call into ProfileConfigSource + Tunnel) plus an explicit user preference for auto-connect.

findings.title: No auto-reconnect on network switch or engine death: TunnelState.reconnecting is dead code and every crash lands in a terminal 'blocked' state requiring a manual tap
findings.evidence: Competitors: WireSock Global Preferences 'Auto-reconnect, Connection timeout (Continuous Retry)' (research/10-WireSock.md:505); WG Tunnel 'Seamless roaming feature for tunnel recovery' + reconnect loop with RECONNECT_DELAY (research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §6, go/amnezia-box desktop client state.ts uses a 3s reconnect loop). App: tunnel.dart defines TunnelState.reconnecting (line 11) but grep proves it is never set — no _setState(TunnelState.reconnecting) exists; a FATAL only reaches _onBoxEvent -> _block(boxCrashed) (terminal, tunnel.dart:595-608); there is no retry/backoff code in Tunnel or VpnNotifier. The SPEC's own leak-test scenario 'Wi-Fi↔hotspot handoff (continuous ping, no reply when reconn
findings.fix: Add a bounded retry loop with debounce (engine crash or boxStop-wedged -> reconnecting -> attempt reconnect N times with backoff, fail closed to blocked), emit TunnelState.reconnecting during attempts, and expose an auto-reconnect toggle in settings.

findings.title: No last-state restore on app open: the UI always boots as Disconnected, the last tag is in-memory only, and engine state is never queried at startup
findings.evidence: Competitors: FlClash 'profile.store-selected: true remembers last selected proxy per group across restarts' (research/11-FlClash.md:307); WG Tunnel 'Lockdown and previous tunnel restoration on boot' (research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:258). App: VpnNotifier.build() unconditionally returns VpnState.disconnected() (vpn_notifier.dart:103); _lastTag lives only in memory (vpn_notifier.dart:96); selectedEndpointProvider recomputes a heuristic (first group/endpoint) instead of the last-used tag (selected_endpoint.dart). No startup code queries the running engine: BoxEngine subscribes only Libbox.CommandLog (BoxEngine.kt:172) and stubs writeStatus to {} (BoxEngine.kt:169), so if the activity is relaunched whi
findings.fix: Persist the last connected tag (and desired state) in a store; on startup, ask BoxEngine for engineRunning (new channel method or subscribe CommandStatus) and reconcile VpnState, optionally auto-connecting if the saved desired state was connected.

findings.title: No system Always-on VPN support or onRevoke handling: revoking/always-on leaves the app showing Connected on a dead tunnel, and the engine has no service-side start path
findings.evidence: Competitors: v2rayNG 'Always-on VPN + Block connections without VPN ... App-level: onRevoke() -> stopAllService() ... ensures no bare traffic after VPN revoked' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:328); NekoBox 'App supports onRevoke() callback' (research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:293); Exclave relies on system Always-on with setUnderlyingNetworks(null) (research/08-Exclave.md:382-383); WG Tunnel adds an Always-On settings deep link + AlwaysOnReceiver (research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:327-329). App: QanatVpnService has no onRevoke override and its onStartCommand is an empty stub ('service start is only needed so INSTANCE is available', lines 24-28) — under system Always-on the OS restarts this service at boot and no
findings.fix: Override onRevoke() in QanatVpnService to stop the engine + foreground service and emit a revoked event to Dart; implement Always-on compatibility (setUnderlyingNetworks(null) in openTun) and a settings deep link to the system VPN page.

findings.title: Windows TUN cannot be established from an unelevated app: no elevation manifest, no service mode, no admin guidance — the core Windows connect flow fails on stock installs
findings.evidence: Competitors: Clash Verge explicitly splits 'Sidecar mode (default, no admin): cannot create TUN interface (TUN needs elevated)' vs 'Service mode (elevated, recommended for TUN): Verge installs clash-verge-service ... handles TUN adapter ... without per-launch UAC' (research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:388-397); WireSock documents 'Auto-start on login (Task Scheduler workaround for UAC)' (research/10-WireSock.md:506). App: windows/runner/runner.exe.manifest contains only dpiAwareness — no requestedExecutionLevel; WindowsBoxProcessAdapter spawns 'sing-box.exe run -c <temp>' directly with no elevation, no service mode, and no runas/IsUserAnAdmin check anywhere (grep = zero hits). First Windows connec
findings.fix: Either request elevation (requestedExecutionLevel requireAdministrator with a clear explanation), or install a one-time elevated helper/service that owns sing-box.exe lifecycle (IPC back to the app), plus a pre-connect check that surfaces a 'run as administrator' guidance screen instead of a generic boxStartFailed.

findings.title: Per-endpoint latency badges absent from the endpoints (node list) screen — measured values are computed but never displayed per endpoint anywhere
findings.evidence: Competitors put delay on every node row: research/07-Hiddify.md:381 "each proxy row shows `delay ms` (`Proxies` screenshot `919020e5`)"; research/01-Karing.md:545 "latency badge per proxy, drag-reorder"; the frozen design prototype shows color-coded per-server pills "HKG-02 34ms / NRT-01 48ms / FRA-01 112ms / LAX-03 189ms" (docs/prototype-final.html:237, thresholds at :397-398). The app: LatencyController._sweep computes tag->ms samples (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:155-180), but the endpoints ListView renders only title `Text(stored.label)` and subtitle `'${_protocolName(stored)} · ${stored.sourceUrl ?? 'manual'}'` plus a delete button (lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_screen.dart
findings.fix: Watch latencyProvider in EndpointsScreen's ListTile and render a per-row badge (ms, color-coded ok/warn/bad per the prototype thresholds), including a distinct 'unreachable' state for null.

findings.title: The only latency test-all button is a speed icon buried on the Groups tab — the endpoints screen and home have no way to trigger a sweep, and no progress indication while sweeping
findings.note: LatencyController._inFlight exists but no widget surfaces a sweeping indicator; only consumer is the static groups speed icon.
findings.evidence: Competitors: research/06-V2RayNG.md:426 "`MainActivity → Test real delay` batch"; research/07-Hiddify.md:381 "Proxies page bottom-right test button"; research/11-FlClash.md:573 whole-group delay test with Windows firewall fix. App: the endpoints screen has no test affordance at all (no button, no ListTile onTap — lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_screen.dart:89-118); home.dart has no test trigger either. The single call to `ref.read(latencyProvider.notifier).refresh()` lives under a speed icon on the Groups tab (lib/modules/routing/groups_screen.dart:36-38, tooltip 'Measure latency'), and it gives no in-flight feedback — LatencyController._inFlight (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:144,
findings.fix: Add the measure-all button (with a sweeping spinner driven by LatencyController state) to the endpoints screen header, and optionally a per-row tap-to-test like Hiddify's Box.URLTest(tag).

findings.title: Latency sweep measures only a direct TCP connect to the server address — no 'real delay' through the outbound, unlike every researched competitor
findings.evidence: Competitors measure actual tunneled delay: research/06-V2RayNG.md:426 "`LibXray.measureDelay(configJson, timeout=8000ms)` — creates temporary Xray instance per node with `inbound: SOCKS` + `outbound: node's config` ... fetches `generate_204` via proxy, measures RTT"; research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:452 "opens `http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204` ... via each outbound's `Dialer`"; research/07-Hiddify.md:381 "manual tap runs `Box.URLTest(tag)` via gRPC". intent.md:134 promises exactly this: "Yes, `urltest` + TCP ping + real-delay". The app's only prober is `SocketLatencyPinger` doing `Socket.connect(host, port)` to the raw server address (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:19-30); grep shows no
findings.fix: Add a through-engine probe path (temporary sing-box config with a URLTest group over the candidate outbounds, or the libbox CommandClient delay command) and use it for the badge when the engine is available; keep raw TCP connect as a fast pre-filter like v2rayNG 2.3.x.

findings.title: WireGuard/AmneziaWG endpoints — the star protocol — can never get a latency sample because the pinger is TCP-only against a UDP port
findings.note: Strongest latency finding: Socket.connect (TCP) against WG/AWG UDP peer endpoint can never succeed, and the star protocol is exactly wg/awg.
findings.evidence: App: `SocketLatencyPinger.ping` uses `Socket.connect` (TCP) (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:19-30), while `_peerTarget` returns the WireGuard peer's `endpoint: host:port` — a UDP-only service (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:65-93). A TCP SYN to a WG/AWG port never gets a SYN-ACK, so every WG/AWG endpoint times out to null after 4s and is recorded as "null = unreachable or never measured" (latency.dart:117). Nulls are skipped by bestTag() (latency.dart:122-124) and never render. The product's differentiator is "WG+AmneziaWG priority first" (AGENTS.md; goal.md:4), and the vendored profile is `awg-hkg-02` (lib/modules/vpn/logic/selected_endpoint.dart:36). Competitors avoid this by probing t
findings.fix: Probe WG/AWG endpoints through the engine (temp config with the wg/awg endpoint + URLTest group) or via a UDP-aware probe (RawDatagramSocket keepalive/handshake), falling back to TCP-connect only for TCP-based protocols.

findings.title: bestTag() (auto-pick fastest endpoint) is dead code — latency never influences what the app connects to, and the default selector prefers DIRECT
findings.evidence: App: `LatencyState.bestTag()` (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:119-130) is referenced by no caller (grep: only its definition and a comment at :37). Default selection resolves urltest-group tag / default member / `endpoints.first.tag` / vendored tag (lib/modules/vpn/logic/selected_endpoint.dart:52-73) without consulting latencyProvider; the generated PROXY selector lists `'DIRECT'` first (lib/modules/routing/config_assembler.dart:89). Competitors: research/01-Karing.md:537 "`urltest` group auto picks lowest latency after `testLatencyAfterProfileUpdate()` with `tolerance 50ms`"; research/05-V2RayN.md:446 LeastPing policy group backed by observatory probing. goal.md:84 locks "observatory leas
findings.fix: Wire bestTag() into the default selection (e.g. an implicit leastPing group or pre-sweep on connect that picks the fastest endpoint when no urltest group exists), or remove the dead API; either way close the goal.md:84 gap.

(hiddify.com/app/How-to-use-Hiddify-app: General settings)'. On Windows especially (no per-app system language), an Iranian user on an English Windows gets an
findings.fix: Add a language preference (system/English/فارسی) persisted next to the other stores under ~/.qanatvpn/ and pass it as MaterialApp.locale; settings screen section 'Language'.

findings.evidence: lib/modules/dns/dns_config.dart:12 hardcodes dohServer = '1.1.1.1' with dohPath '/dns-query', FakeIP 198.18.0.0/15, and strategy 'prefer_ipv4' as const constructor defaults; grep for any UI touching DnsConfig finds none (config_assembler.dart:19 instantiates const DnsConfig() directly). research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:418-423: 'Settings: DNS → Enable FakeIP (toggle). Range editable... FILE: app/src/main/java/io/nekohasekai/sagernet/fmt/.../DNSSettingsActivity.kt'. docs/prototype-final.html:332 plans the exact surface: Network tile with editable 'FakeIP 198.18.0.0/15' and 'DoH https://1.1.1.1/dns-query' fields. Censored-region users whose ISPs poison 1.1.1.1 — the exact audience in goal.md:3 —
