Tunnel on Wi-Fi (enable/disable + mapping WiFi SSID → Tunnel via Trusted Wi-Fi Names)... Stop Tunnel on No Internet'; research/07-Hiddify.md:395: 'Start on Boot (launch_at_startup), Silent Start (tray only)'; research/13-Matsuri-SagerNet.md:428 lists RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED '(auto-connect)' as standard manifest surface. For a
findings.fix: Add settings: auto-connect on app launch (trivial — call VpnNotifier.connect after wizard done), Android BOOT_COMPLETED receiver, and optionally SSID-trusted auto-tunnel; Windows autostart registry entry.

findings.title: TOR-CHAIN detour has no user-facing toggle — Tor chaining is engine-ready but unreachable from any screen
findings.note: TorChainOptions constructed only in test files (p0_fail_closed_test, routing_test); routing_compiler.dart supports it end to end but no store write or UI exists.
findings.evidence: lib/modules/routing/routing_policy.dart:45-52 defines TorChainOptions (127.0.0.1:9050, tag tor-entry) and lib/modules/routing/config_assembler.dart:28-54 injects the detour 'when [policy].torChain is set AND the endpoint tag is TOR-CHAIN', but grep 'torChain:' across lib/ returns zero construction sites — GroupsScreen and RulesScreen never write the field, so the outbound is only emitted in tests. research/audit.md item 2 mandates 'Isolate Tor: run tor sidecar + SOCKS chaining (127.0.0.1:9050, detour tor-socks)' as one of the 6 must-changes, and goal.md:4 lists 'Tor (SOCKS sidecar)' as a ship protocol. The star anti-censorship chain is unreachable from the product surface.
findings.fix: Add a Tor-chain toggle (with sidecar health check via TorAdapter.isSocksUp) on the settings screen or groups editor that persists TorChainOptions into the policy document and routes it through ProfileConfigSource.

findings.title: Imported endpoints are uneditable: no per-protocol editor for 7 of 8 protocols, no rename, even AWG cannot be re-opened
findings.evidence: v2rayNG manual add opens a per-protocol 'ServerConfigActivity form' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:265) and Nekoray ships a full profile editor; audit.md scope requires 'editing depth (every protocol field)'. In the app the endpoint list row offers only delete (endpoints_screen.dart:94-112), and the only editor in lib/ is AwgProfileSheet (awg_profile_screen.dart:12) whose header is literally 'New AWG profile' (line 84) with `const AwgProfileSheet({super.key})` — no existing-endpoint parameter, so even AWG profiles cannot be re-opened with values loaded. EndpointsState has no edit/rename mutation (endpoints_controller.dart: only importText/saveManual/delete), and StoredEndpoint.label 'Editor-facing
findings.fix: Add a tap-to-edit bottom sheet per protocol driven off NormalizedEndpoint (the typed model already carries transport/TLS/reality fields), plus a label-rename field and an 'edit existing' constructor for the AWG sheet.

findings.title: Server list has no search, no filter (protocol/source), no sort — unfiltered flat list regardless of size
findings.evidence: FlClash added 'search bar (v0.8.85 Support proxies search)' and 'profiles sort' (research/11-FlClash.md:259); Hiddify has a 'top-right sort button by name vs delay' (research/07-Hiddify.md:381); Nekoray groups offer Sort + auto-sort after test (research/04-Nekoray.md:367). The app renders a plain ListView.builder over state.endpoints in import order (endpoints_screen.dart:86-113) — the only search field in lib/ is the logs search (logs_screen.dart:28), and EndpointsState/EndpointsController contain no query, filter, or sort state (endpoints_controller.dart:31-43). A 300-node subscription becomes an unscannable flat list, and filtering by protocol or sourceUrl (both already stored) is impossi
findings.fix: Add a search field (tag/address substring), filter chips (protocol, source/subscription), and sort controls (name, latency) over the existing store list.

findings.title: No per-node latency on the server list, and the only probe is a TCP handshake that misses TLS/Reality failures
findings.note: Largely a merge of idx 187 (no badges) + 189 (TCP-only); keep one when synthesizing.
findings.evidence: Karing's select_server screen shows a 'latency badge per proxy' (research/01-Karing.md:545) and Hiddify's proxy rows show 'delay ms' (research/07-Hiddify.md:381); Nekoray's own docs warn 'Use Tcp Ping to quickly filter dead nodes; use Url Test to rank usable nodes (catches TLS/Reality failures Tcp Ping misses)' (research/04-Nekoray.md:376). The app's SocketLatencyPinger is a raw Socket.connect (latency.dart:19-33), and latencyProvider is consumed only by the Groups tab ('Measure latency' action + urltest best-ms suffix, groups_screen.dart:36-37,130-141) — endpoints_screen.dart contains zero latency references and no per-endpoint test button. Reality/Vision nodes behind dead TLS pass TCP ping
findings.fix: Show a latency badge on each endpoint row and a 'test all' action (the LatencyController sweep already exists); add a URL-test (generate_204 through the node's outbound) as a second, truer metric alongside TCP ping.

findings.title: No QR import and no QR export anywhere in the app
findings.evidence: goal.md §9 locks 'All formats + ETag 24h + QR/ZIP deeplink'. v2rayNG: 'Scan QR uses CameraX + MLKit BarcodeScanning → decode → same import' and 'Share → … QR code bitmap via ZXing' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:265); Karing imports via qr_code_scanner_plus (research/01-Karing.md:381); WG-Tunnel uses mobile_scanner for wireguard:// QRs (research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:360). In the app, grep for qr|barcode|zxing|mobile_scanner across lib/ returns nothing, pubspec.yaml lists no scanner/QR package, and the endpoints import box is a 3-line paste TextField (endpoints_screen.dart:296-308) — on mobile, the canonical provider-onboarding flow (scan the QR the provider shows) does not exist, and nodes cannot be han
findings.fix: Add a scanner package (e.g. mobile_scanner) feeding importText for onboarding, and a QR render of a selected endpoint's share URI for export once per-endpoint serialization exists.

findings.title: No custom-scheme deeplink import (qanatvpn://) on any platform
findings.evidence: intent.md:113 promises 'Yes, SIP008, mrs/srs, hiddify://, qanatvpn:// deeplink' and goal.md §11 lists deeplinks as day-1. Hiddify 'app_links 6.4.0 registers hiddify:// on all platforms' (Android intent-filter, Windows registry, Linux mime) triggering addFromUrl (research/07-Hiddify.md:186); Throne registers throne:// add/addsub schemes with a self-healing OS handler (research/02-Throne.md:391). In the app, AndroidManifest.xml declares only MAIN/LAUNCHER (lines 31-34) and VpnService (44-46) intent-filters, pubspec.yaml has no app_links, windows/runner/main.cpp forwards argv into Dart entrypoint arguments but main() (lib/main.dart:38-98) never reads them, and grep for deeplink/protocol_handler
findings.fix: Register a qanatvpn:// scheme (Android VIEW intent-filter + Windows registry/argv parsing) and route the payload into EndpointsController.importText.

findings.title: Last FATAL/crash reason is captured then thrown away — blocked state shows generic 'Engine crashed' with no cause and no path to logs
findings.evidence: BoxEvent.crashed carries the engine message (`StateError(message ?? 'engine died')`, channel_adapters.dart:49) and WindowsBoxProcessAdapter tracks `_lastErrorLine` (windows_box_process.dart:117,140), but Tunnel._onBoxEvent discards `event.error` and calls `_block(TunnelBlockReason.boxCrashed)` (tunnel.dart:584); TunnelBlockReason is a bare enum with 6 fixed labels, and the home StateTile shows only the generic l10n string 'Engine crashed' (home.dart:161-164) — no error text, no link to Logs or Diagnostics. When box.start throws, `PlatformException.message` propagates into a thrown StateError (channel_adapters.dart:86-88) that Tunnel also swallows into boxStartFailed. Competitors: WG-Tunnel's
findings.fix: Keep the BoxEvent.error string on TunnelBlockReason.boxCrashed (e.g. `reason.detail`), render it in StateTile under the label, and make the blocked state a tap target that routes to /logs filtered to the errors segment.

findings.title: Diagnostics tab is 3 passive tiles — the promised Slipnet-style DNS scanner 0-6 (per-resolver EDNS/NXDOMAIN/DPI table) was never built
findings.evidence: SPEC.md:146 and goal.md §15 lock the diag module as 'DNS scanner 0-6 + Prism HMAC (Slipnet-like), Simple Ping TCP 5000ms, sort by ping, PingRoute per-hop (fl_chart), network_reachability Rust stability 0-100', and the design prototype renders exactly that screen ('EDNS, NXDOMAIN, RND, DPI, score 0-6. UDP / TCP / Both' per-resolver table with E2E WORKING/TIMEOUT pills, docs/prototype-final.html:290-296). The shipped DiagnosticsScreen is three static ListTiles — one FakeIP wildcard lookup ('probe.qanatvpn.internal', health.dart:103-109), one TCP ping to a single hardcoded target 1.1.1.1:443, and a stability percent — with no resolver table, no EDNS/NXDOMAIN/DPI probes, no Prism HMAC, no per-hop
findings.fix: Implement the prototype's resolver sweep (NS/TXT/RND/DPI/EDNS badges + per-resolver E2E verdict) in Health behind the existing DnsProber seam, with Simple/Advanced modes and the 0-6 per-resolver score the UI already renders.

findings.title: No stepwise connectivity test — no config check (sing-box check), no handshake/endpoint reachability, no per-site verification for the stuck user
findings.note: Engine truth that shipped profile passes check but FATALs at run start actually argues for the runtime handshake probe, not against the finding.
findings.evidence: Grep for `sing-box check|configCheck|validateConfig` in lib/ returns only comments in dns_config.dart and endpoint_outbound.dart — the real `sing-box check -c` runs in CI and Makefile but never in-app. There is no diagnostics step that assembles the current TypedConfig, calls the engine's check path, and shows errors before a connect attempt; all FATAL detection happens only after a failed start (tunnel.dart `_block(boxStartFailed)`). Competitors: v2rayNG ships a rule-level dry-run 'Test routing -> input URL -> checks which routing.rules matches' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:429-430), and Nekoray builds `forTest=true` temporary configs to probe profiles without touching the live tunnel (research/
findings.fix: Add a pre-flight probe to the Health interface: run the assembled config through the engine's check command (Windows subprocess or libbox check) and a TCP-connect of the selected endpoint, then expose stepwise results (config OK / endpoint reachable / DNS hijacked / site 204) on the diagnostics tab.

findings.title: No in-app language switcher and no Settings screen at all — FA renders only when the OS locale is Persian; FA users on English-locale devices get pure English
findings.note: Duplicate of idx 192 plus the settings-route-absent detail; merge at synthesis.

The settings screen was planned but never built: lib/l10n/app_fa.arb:8 has `"settings": "تنظیمات"` and app_en.arb has 'Settings', yet grep finds no reference to `.settings` anywhere in lib/, and the GoRouter route table (lib/app/app.dart:30-79) contains /home /groups /endpoints /r

findings.evidence: goal.md lock (line 110): 'i18n/RTL/a11y | EN + FA RTL + ARB ... Semantics + Dynamic Type clamped 0.9-1.35 + ReduceMotion'; AGENTS.md code style requires l10n everywhere. findings.title: Logs export is a fake success: print() to stdout, no share/file sink, yet snackbar claims 'Exported'
findings.note: Code comment even misdescribes itself as 'copy to a buffer the user pastes' but there is no Clipboard.setData either; print is invisible on release Android.

QANATVPN logs_screen.dart _export only does print('--- qanatvpn log export (${visible.length} lines) ---') + print(buffer) then shows SnackBar '${l10n.logsExported} (${visible.length})'. pubspec.yaml has no share_plus/path_provider — there is no share sheet or file write on any platform. On Android release builds print goes to logcat, invisible to the user

findings.title: Update install has no states at all: 'Download & install' just opens a browser; no download progress, no install-pending, no completion state
findings.note: In-code comment admits 'the platform service lands with the release todo'; bridge VpnServiceBridge.kt:108 is ACTION_VIEW on the browser_download_url.
findings.evidence: goal.md §13 (frozen): daily updates via 'FileProvider' install path; updates_screen.dart comment claims 'FileProvider ACTION_VIEW intent is the Play-safe install path' but the actual bridge (android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/qanatvpn/qanatvpn/VpnServiceBridge.kt:101-114) does Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url)) on the https browser_download_url — it opens the browser; no APK is downloaded or handed to a package installer, so no progress/pending/completed state can exist. Windows: Process.start('explorer', [info.assetUrl]) just opens the browser to the zip URL. The _install button stays enabled during the handoff (double-tap re-opens the browser), and the only failure state is a raw error.
findings.fix: Download the asset in-app with a progress state (DownloadManager on Android, HttpClient with progress on Windows), then FileProvider ACTION_VIEW install intent on Android / open the extracted installer on Windows, with distinct downloading/ready/failed states and a disabled button while running.

findings.title: Wizard re-gates the entire app on every launch and the VPN-permission step has no skip, so a denied permission is a dead-end state
findings.evidence: app.dart:136 'wizard.step == WizardStep.done ? child : Center(child: Wizard(...))' gates every tab behind the wizard. WizardController.build() returns 'const WizardState()' (step = vpnPermission) on every process start and nothing persists completion — SplitStore (split_store.dart) only stores the split choice, not 'done'. So every cold start the user must tap through 3 steps again. Worse, the vpnPermission step (_VpnStep) has only the Grant button — no skip/close; if the user denies the consent dialog (VpnServiceBridge.handleActivityResult resolves RESULT_CANCELED → granted=false), the wizard stays on step 1 and home/rules/logs/diagnostics are permanently unreachable for that session. Compe
findings.fix: Persist wizard completion (e.g. a flag file or SplitStore sibling), show the wizard only on first run, and add a 'Skip for now' affordance on the VPN-permission step so a denied permission leaves the app usable with connect-blocked feedback instead of a modal dead-end.

findings.title: No Tor sidecar — TOR-CHAIN only works if the user separately runs a tor daemon on 127.0.0.1:9050
findings.note: Code comment itself admits: 'The Tor sidecar is a later milestone' — only a TCP probe of 127.0.0.1:9050 exists; no Process.start('tor') anywhere.

findings.fix: Bundle/manage a tor sidecar: spawn tor.exe next to sing-box.exe on Windows (with data-dir + control port), embed an Android tor lib or libbox tor outbound; keep the existing isSocksUp gate as the isolation seam.

findings.title: No local SOCKS5 10808 / HTTP 10809 inbound and no Windows system-proxy/PAC mode — TUN is the only capture path
findings.evidence: goal.md section 7: "Both TUN mixed + Proxy PAC + max firewall + Local SOCKS5 10808/HTTP 10809"; intent.md 2.5: "Yes, 127.0.0.1:10808 SOCKS5 + 10809 HTTP for AdGuard chaining" (V2RayN 10808/10809, WG Tunnel Local Proxy) and "Yes, PAC/manual, sysproxy.exe helper". Windows users have no proxy-only mode and other devices on the LAN cannot chain into the client.
findings.fix: Add a local mixed inbound (127.0.0.1:10808 socks+http) behind a settings toggle and a Windows system-proxy (PAC/manual) adapter that flips WinINET settings around box start/stop.

findings.title: Secrets lock broken: WG private keys and passwords persisted as plaintext JSON; flutter_secure_storage and drift declared but never used

Code: EndpointStore.save writes jsonEncode(endpoints) to ~/.qanatvpn/endpoints.json via atomicWriteString (endpoint_store.dart:21-23) — NormalizedEndpoint.toJson carries WireGuard private_key, hysteria2/tuic passwords in the clear; grep flutter_secure_storage across lib returns zero imports despite pubspec.yaml listing it, and grep drift finds zero usage/tables in lib (drift + drift_flutter + drift_dev are dead dependencies). findings.title: Windows never checks for updates automatically: the daily 24h workmanager task is Android-only and the promised 'checks on launch' path does not exist

findings.title: Engine death mid-session has no automatic recovery: reconnecting state exists but is never emitted, blocked is terminal

A
findings.fix: Emit reconnecting on engine death and auto-retry connect with the last tag (bounded backoff), or at minimum re-run connect on app lifecycle resume when the last state was connected/blocked-after-crash.

findings.title: No always-on VPN support and no onRevoke handling: system revocation silently desyncs UI state, and no OS lockdown path exists

App supports onRevoke() callback'; research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:328: 'Always-On VPN Control toggle ... system Always-On will start tunnel on boot via VpnService onRevoke detection'; research/08-Exclave.md:382: 'Always-on VPN + Block connections without VPN ... system sets LOCKDOWN_VPN that blocks leaks even when app killed'. App: QanatVpnService.kt overrides only onCreate/onDestroy/onStartCommand (START_NOT_STICKY) — no onRevoke, so when the system revokes the VPN (another VPN app starts, user toggles system Always-On) the Dart Tunnel stays 'connected' while the TUN is
findings.fix: Override onRevoke() in QanatVpnService to emit a 'crashed'-class event on box_events so Dart flips to blocked/disconnected; add a wizard/settings step that deep-links to Settings.ACTION_VPN_SETTINGS for system Always-On, and declare SERVICE_META_DATA_SUPPORTS_ALWAYS_ON so the OS can restart the service under lockdown.

findings.title: Windows suspend/resume: dead subprocess after sleep is undetected — UI shows connected while traffic is broken
findings.note: start() watches only process.exitCode (:80-104); grep WidgetsBindingObserver/AppLifecycle across lib/ = zero; DesktopPlatformAdapter is a const no-op. After sleep the process lives, tunnel dies, UI stays connected.
findings.evidence: research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:525: 'Also watches for OS sleep/wake: re-applies after resume'; research/10-WireSock.md:505: 'Auto-reconnect, Connection timeout (Continuous Retry)'. App: lib/core/services/windows_box_process.dart:80-104 spawns sing-box.exe and watches only process.exitCode for early death — no power-broadcast/resume handling exists anywhere (grep for WidgetsBindingObserver/AppLifecycle/Connectivity in lib/ = no match), and DesktopPlatformAdapter is a const no-op for every guard (desktop_platform_adapter.dart:7-26). After a Windows sleep/hibernate the process is alive but the tunnel is dead while the UI keeps showing connected; the app never re-establishes.
findings.fix: Listen for resume/sleep (Windows power broadcast via a small native channel, or Dart AppLifecycleState on desktop) and on resume re-validate the tunnel: probe health (Health.snapshot already exists) and restart sing-box.exe when it is dead or unreachable.

findings.note: Merge comment 'Re-importing the same tag replaces the previous entry' (:134); fold keeps last occurrence so incoming subscription entries silently destroy prior ones — including manual AWG profiles sharing a '#HK'-style fragment tag; no summary or collision policy.
findings.evidence: Competitors surface dedupe: research/01-Karing.md:405 'duplicate detection by remark/url hash'; research/04-Nekoray.md:367 'Delete Duplicates'. Here tags come straight from share-link remarks (lib/modules/vpn/repositories/ingestion/parsers.dart:600-631 tag = uri.fragment), so two different servers with the same '#HK' fragment collide, and endpoints_controller.dart:134-160 merges by tag keeping the last occurrence — the comment reads 'Re-importing the same tag replaces the previous entry' — with no confirm dialog and no snackbar reporting how many nodes were added/replaced/dropped. A manual AWG profile whose tag matches an incoming subscription node is silently destroyed.
findings.fix: After import, show a summary ('Imported 120 · replaced 3 · skipped 2 duplicates') and make collision policy explicit (keep-both with a suffix / replace / skip), mirroring Karing's dedupe detection.

findings.title: AWG manual editor cannot author the locked value set: I1-I5 fields missing, Id/Ip/Ib absent from the sheet
findings.note: _advancedFields renders only Jc/Jmin/Jmax, S1-S4, H1-H4; _copyWith params stop at h4; model carries i1-i5/id/ip/ib (amnezia_values.dart) and toEngineJson accepts i1-i5. id/ip/ib FATAL the fork per engine truth, so the fix's hide-or-route-correctly guidance is right. SPEC.md:10 + goal.md:42 lock all values.
findings.evidence: goal.md §4 (FROZEN): 'WireGuard + AmneziaWG (all values: Jc/Jmin/Jmax/S1-S4/H1-H4/I1-I5 + masquerade Id/Ip/Ib + ChaCha header protection)'; SPEC.md:10 'ALL values Jc/Jmin/Jmax/S1-S4/H1-H4/I1-I5/Id/Ip/Ib'. The data model carries all of them (lib/utils/amnezia_values.dart:55-73 toJson includes i1-i5, id, ip, ib) and parsed imports round-trip them, but the sheet — the app's ONLY manual authoring path — renders just Jc/Jmin/Jmax, S1-S4, and H1-H4 rows (awg_profile_screen.dart:191-258 _advancedFields); _copyWith (~:297-315) hard-copies i1..i5 with no setter fields and no Id/Ip/Ib inputs exist. A user adding a fresh AWG server by hand can never author the init-packet junk values that are the produ
findings.fix: Extend _advancedFields with an I1-I5 row (the fork accepts them in toEngineJson, amnezia_values.dart:76-100), hoist the numeric controllers to State fields, and (since id/ip/ib FATAL the fork's endpoints[] per AGENTS.md engine truths) either hide them or emit them only where the fork accepts masquerade keys.

findings.title: Manual refresh is broken: re-pasting the same sub URL within 6h re-fetches fresh bytes then discards them for a cached parse
findings.note: Cache-by-URL consulted before parsing (ingestion_adapter.dart:35-39); importText fetches fresh bytes at endpoints_controller.dart:96-102 then discards them for the cached parse on ≤64KB payloads; test 'same url within 6h returns cached parse (no re-parse)' locks identical() in. >64KB isolate path actually parses fresh (finder noted the small-subs scoping).
findings.evidence: App: lib/modules/vpn/repositories/ingestion_adapter.dart... lib/modules/vpn/repositories/ingestion/ingestion_adapter.dart:35-39 'final cached = _cache[subscription.url]; if (cached != null && _now().difference(cached.parsedAt) < const Duration(hours: 6)) { return cached.endpoints; }' — the cache is keyed by URL and consulted BEFORE parsing, so in EndpointsController.importText (endpoints_controller.dart:96-125) the fresh plainFetch bytes fetched at :96-102 are thrown away whenever the same URL was parsed <6h ago (small subs <64KB take the cached path; the test test/ingestion/ingestion_test.dart:460 'same url within 6h returns cached parse (no re-parse)' locks this in). Competitor: research/1
findings.fix: Bypass or key the parse cache by content hash (e.g. sha of bytes) so an explicit import always parses the freshly fetched payload; reserve the 6h cache for opportunistic same-URL dedupe only, or drop it once a real per-sub refresh with ETag exists.

findings.title: subscription-userinfo / traffic-expiry headers are never parsed or displayed anywhere
findings.note: Same root fact as 254 from a second finder: only statusCode and body are read; profile-update-interval likewise unparsed. Merge into one fix.
findings.evidence: Competitors: research/07-Hiddify.md:190-191 'Hiddify reads response headers subscription-userinfo: upload=123; download=456; total=10737418240; expire=1700000000 and profile-update-interval ... displays remaining traffic/days in Proxies UI'; research/08-Exclave.md:256-264 'SIP008 → read bytes_used + bytes_remaining ... Others → read Subscription-Userinfo private HTTP header (upload, download, total, expire)'; research/01-Karing.md:394 'subscription-userinfo: upload=123 headers parsed for traffic stats'. App: endpoints_controller.dart:96-102 reads only statusCode and response.body; grep across lib/ for 'subscription-userinfo|userinfo|bytes_used|expire' returns zero header-parsing hits (only U
findings.fix: In importText capture response.headers, parse subscription-userinfo (upload/download/total/expire) and profile-update-interval, persist them on the sub record, and render a remaining-traffic/expiry bar on the Endpoints list plus a Home tile; use profile-update-interval to schedule the next refresh.

findings.title: No subscription entity: multiple named subs, enable/disable, per-sub grouping and replace-on-refresh semantics are absent
findings.note: StoredEndpoint is {endpoint, label, sourceUrl} only (endpoint_store.dart:66-90); no Subscription record anywhere — grep matches only RawSubscription payload and URI userInfo. No enable/disable, per-sub grouping, or replace-on-refresh semantics.
findings.evidence: Competitors: research/06-V2RayNG.md:251 'SubscriptionItem model ... Fields: remarks (name), url (https), enabled: Boolean, autoUpdate: Boolean, updateInterval: Long (min, default 1440 = 24h), lastUpdated ... filter: String (regex), userAgent, requestHeaders'; research/01-Karing.md:16 'unified rule-set across multiple subscriptions' and :405 'duplicate detection by remark/url hash'; research/05-V2RayN.md:261 'Managed in SubItem + ProfileItem.Subid'. App: endpoint_store.dart:66-85 StoredEndpoint has only {endpoint, label, sourceUrl} — no Subscription type exists anywhere (grep 'subscription' in lib/ matches only RawSubscription payload and StreamSubscription); endpoints_screen.dart:88-98 offer
findings.fix: Introduce a Subscription record and group endpoints under it (endpoints.json keyed by sub id with replace-by-source semantics on refresh), add enable/disable + per-sub delete + name edit to the Endpoints screen, and add a subscriptions section to the app shell (prototype profiles page already reserves it).

findings.title: No QR import (camera scan) or QR export for WireGuard/AWG profiles
findings.note: No QR/scanner package in pubspec dependencies; import is paste-only; no intent-filter in AndroidManifest. goal.md:72 locks 'QR/ZIP deeplink' and docs/prototype promises it — frozen lock violated. Overlaps 257 (general import paths); this one adds QR export for WG/AWG.
findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §7: 'QR code scanning — mobile_scanner → scan wireguard:// or awg:// or raw conf string' plus conf export; research/10-WireSock.md §3 (wg-quick-config): 'Generates QR codes for hassle-free mobile setup'; goal.md §9 locks 'All formats + ETag 24h + QR/ZIP deeplink'; docs/prototype-final.html:314 promises 'QR/ZIP deeplink qanatvpn://'. App: pubspec.yaml dependencies (lines 12-34) contain no QR/scanner package (grep qr/scanner/zxing = 0); import is a paste-only 3-line TextField ('hintText: l10n.endpointsImportHint', endpoints_screen.dart:294-298); FilePicker is used only for encrypted .qnv backups; no qanatvpn:// intent-filter in AndroidManifest.xml.
findings.fix: Add mobile_scanner for camera import (accept raw wg INI, wireguard://, awg://, qanatvpn://) and a QR display sheet per stored endpoint via pretty_qr_code; register the VIEW intent-filter.

findings.title: No WireGuard/AWG keypair generation anywhere in the app
findings.note: Verified: zero genkey/keypair hits in lib/; awg_profile_screen.dart:87-88 are plain TextFields with no generate affordance; the Random chip calls generateRandom() which only draws Jc/S/H values, never keys.
findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §2/§7: obfuscation tuner has 'Generate random' (awg genkey-like RCT) and AWG 3.x configs need generated HeaderProtectionKey; research/10-WireSock.md §3 (wg-quick-config): 'key.go — Curve25519 keypair generation'. App: awg_profile_screen.dart:87 renders '_field(_privateKey, 'Private key (32-byte base64)', '')' and line 88 '_field(_peerKey, 'Peer public key (32-byte base64)', '')' with no generate affordance; grep genkey|keypair|generate_key across lib/ = 0 hits; amnezia_values.dart generateRandom() only draws obfuscation values, never keys.
findings.fix: Add a Generate button that creates an X25519 keypair (package:cryptography is already a dependency), fills the private key, and shows the derived public key for pasting to the server.

findings.title: AWG editor cannot set or edit I1-I5 (CPS) or Id/Ip/Ib (masquerade) values
findings.note: Correct the fix: I1-I5 yes, but Id/Ip/Ib must stay parse-only — AwgValues.toEngineJson never emits them (awg_config.dart:180 comment) because endpoints[].id/ip/ib FATAL the engine (WireSock-only). Editable I1-I5 alone justifies high.
findings.evidence: goal.md §4 locks 'ALL values: Jc/Jmin-Jmax/S1-S2/H1-H4/I1-I5'; AGENTS.md overview: 'star is WG+AmneziaWG (all values Jc/H1-H4/I1-I5/Id/Ip/Ib)'; research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §7: 'I1-I5 CPS multiline with syntax highlight <b> <t> <r>' plus CPS helper; research/10-WireSock.md §2: 'Id = domain to mimic... Ip = QUIC|DNS|SIP|STUN... Ib = Chrome|Firefox|cURL'. App: awg_profile_screen.dart:191 _advancedFields renders only 'Junk packets' (Jc/Jmin/Jmax, line 195), 'Message padding' (S1-S4), and 'Magic headers (H1∩H2=∅)' (line 254) rows; _copyWith carries i1-i5/id/ip/ib through untouched (no setter exists), so a hand-built profile can never carry them and an imported one cannot be inspected or tweaked; the
findings.fix: Extend the Advanced disclosure with I1-I5 multiline CPS fields (tag helper for <b>/<t>/<r>) and Id/Ip/Ib inputs; validation already exists in AwgConfig.validate.

findings.title: No on-demand auto-tunnel, trusted-network triggers, or start-on-boot
findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §5/§7: 'Auto-tunneling by network ... Tunnel on Wi-Fi + Trusted Wi-Fi Names (wildcards * ! ?) ... Tunnel on Mobile Data / Ethernet ... Start on Boot ... Debounce Delay'. App: AndroidManifest.xml declares only ForegroundService (line 36) and QanatVpnService (line 40) — no BOOT_COMPLETED receiver, no network-callback service; grep onBoot|BOOT_COMPLETED|on_demand|auto-tunnel across lib/ and kotlin/ = 0; wifi_ssid/wifi_bssid exist solely as sing-box route-rule fields (routing_compiler.dart:240 'addList('wifi_bssid', rule.wifiBssids)'), never as tunnel on/off triggers.
findings.fix: Add a boot receiver plus a connectivity-triggered auto-connect service keyed on trusted SSID/BSSID lists persisted like SplitStore, honoring the existing Doze exemption work.

findings.title: No Quick Settings tile or launcher shortcut for one-tap connect
findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §7: 'Quick Settings Tile (TileService ... tap toggles default tunnel or auto-tunnel ... STATE_ACTIVE green vs STATE_INACTIVE' and 'Home screen Shortcuts ... Toggle Auto-Tunneling, Toggle Default Tunnel'. App: AndroidManifest.xml has no TileService and no shortcuts.xml; the only toggle path is opening the app and tapping PowerTile (home.dart:57-104) — no way to connect/disconnect or see state from outside the app.
findings.fix: Add a QuickTileService that calls the same start/stop MethodChannel the app uses, reflecting TunnelState (active/inactive/connecting).

findings.title: Test-all-servers is TCP-connect only — no URL-test through the proxy, so broken configs rank as healthy
findings.evidence: NekoBox: 'launches temporary sing-box instance per profile (forTest=true config)... then issues GET http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204 through the proxy. Measures time to first byte / HTTP 204... use Url Test to rank usable nodes (catches TLS/Reality failures Tcp Ping misses)' (research/04-Nekoray.md §9). NekoBox Android: 'opens http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204 via each outbound's Dialer... Bulk test via WorkManager' (research/03-NekoBox-Android.md §10). App: SocketLatencyPinger only does 'Socket.connect(host, port); socket.destroy(); return watch.elapsedMilliseconds' — a TCP handshake to the server address that never validates TLS keys, Reality params, or proxy liveness; a dead VLESS en
findings.fix: Add a proxy-path HTTP-204 prober (Dart HTTP client via a local socks inbound pointing at each outbound, or engine-side urltest results) and use it as the primary ranking signal, keeping TCP ping as a fast pre-filter.

findings.title: Traffic sniffing never enabled on the TUN inbound — domain rules and FakeIP routing silently degrade
findings.evidence: NekoBox's generated TUN inbound is '{"type":"tun","tag":"tun-in",...,"sniff":true,"sniff_override_destination":true,...}' (research/03-NekoBox-Android.md §5) — sniffing is what lets FakeIP/routing see real domains. App: the assembler's TUN inbound is {'type': 'tun','tag': tag,'address': [...],'auto_route': true,'strict_route': true} with no sniff keys; grep 'sniff' across lib/ only hits comments about content-sniffing subscription payloads. The vendored fork supports it (go/amnezia-box/option/inbound.go:72 SniffEnabled) and goal.md §6 promises domain routing ('Full UI for all 30 route.rules fields'), but without sniff the engine routes FakeIP'd and raw-IP traffic by IP only, so geosite/domai
findings.fix: Emit sniff:true (+ sniff_override_destination or a sniff action rule) on the tun inbound in the assembled envelope and vendored profile.

findings.title: No live server switching while connected — every node change is a full disconnect/reconnect
findings.evidence: NekoBox Android: 'Switch node: Notification tile + in-app spinner calls BoxInstance.Selector.Select(outboundTag)' (research/03-NekoBox-Android.md §10); nekoray's daemon applies config on profile switch without tearing down the session (research/04-Nekoray.md §8 ConfigBuilder call sites 'mainwindow.cpp on profile switch'). App: BoxAdapter is only 'Future<void> start(TypedConfig config); Future<void> stop();' (tunnel.dart:88-95) and VpnNotifier exposes only connect(tag)/disconnect() (vpn_notifier.dart:104-114); switching endpoints requires stop + full re-run of the guarded connect sequence. goal.md §11 lists 'Groups, stats... main(config)' — the selector switch path is missing.
findings.fix: Expose a selector-switch MethodChannel command (libbox CommandServer select outbound / write new config to the running selector) so the endpoints/groups screens can switch nodes without dropping the tunnel.

findings.title: No local SOCKS/HTTP inbound or Proxy-only mode — no system-proxy path and no per-app local proxy
findings.evidence: NekoBox: 'mixed-in (SOCKS5 + HTTP) default 127.0.0.1:2080' with a dedicated Proxy-Only service mode (research/03-NekoBox-Android.md §6); nekoray 'System Proxy mode — lightweight, no admin after setup' sets OS proxy to the local port (research/04-Nekoray.md §6). goal.md §7 locks 'Both TUN mixed + Proxy PAC + max firewall... + Local SOCKS5 10808/HTTP 10809'. App: the only inbound ever emitted is tun ('inbounds': [{'type': 'tun', ...}]) in config_assembler.dart; windows_box_process.dart runs sing-box.exe with the same TUN-only generated config; grep for 10808/10809/mixed inbound/system proxy in lib/ finds nothing.
findings.fix: Emit a mixed inbound (and Windows OS-proxy registration) as a user-selectable mode in the assembler envelope, matching goal.md §7's local SOCKS5/HTTP ports.

findings.title: Onboarding wizard re-appears on every app launch: done-state is in-memory only, gating the whole UI behind 3 taps each reopen
findings.evidence: Karing persists onboarding state server-side of UI ('SettingConfig.beginnerMode bool guards UI visibility' — research/01-Karing.md:550) and every researched client remembers completed setup. In the app, WizardController.build() returns 'const WizardState()' (wizard.dart:59-60) — step resets to vpnPermission every process start; AppShell gates the entire app on 'wizard.step == WizardStep.done ? child : Center(child: Wizard(...))' (app/app.dart:133-139); finish() persists only the split choice, never a done flag (wizard.dart:101-113 writes SplitStore only). No grep hit for any persisted wizard-done flag. Every unlock-and-check connection = 3 wizard taps (Grant → Allow/Skip → Finish) before the
findings.fix: Persist a wizardDone flag next to SplitStore (same atomic-write pattern), restore it in WizardController.build(), and keep the wizard re-runnable only via an explicit Settings entry.

findings.title: Foreground notification is static text with no Disconnect action and no endpoint/throughput status: tunnel control requires unlocking and opening the app
findings.evidence: V2RayNG's notification 'shows Connected: <remark> — ↑↓ MB/s with Disconnect action; START_STICKY + setOngoing(true)' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:448); Karing has 'foreground VpnService notification with disconnect button' (research/01-Karing.md:607). The app's ForegroundService.buildNotification() is static — 'setContentTitle("QANATVPN").setContentText("Tunnel active")...setOngoing(true)' (ForegroundService.kt:60-70) with zero Notification.Action and no update path (BoxEngine.sendNotification override is 'override fun sendNotification(notification: com.qanatvpn.libbox.Notification?) {}' — BoxEngine.kt). Phone locked and the network dies: the user must unlock, find, open the app, and tap the power
findings.fix: Add a Disconnect PendingIntent action to the notification, forward the selected tag/state from Dart (or read engineRunning in Kotlin), and update the notification text on state changes via the existing box_events channel.

findings.title: No Quick Settings tile: VPN cannot be toggled from the notification shade
findings.evidence: NekoBox ships 'android.service.quicksettings.TileService subclass QuickToggleTileService.kt. Tap toggles VPN on/off' (research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:474-476); Karing's TileService.kt:63-139 handles 'Quick Tile ACTION_START/STOP' (research/01-Karing.md:217,607). The app has exactly six Kotlin files (BatteryOptHelper, BoxEngine, ForegroundService, MainActivity, VpnServiceBridge, QanatVpnService) — no TileService — and the manifest declares no BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE (AndroidManifest.xml). One-tap toggling from the shade, the single most-used daily gesture for VPN users, does not exist.
findings.fix: Add a TileService that calls the same BoxEngine boxStart/boxStop path (reuse the existing executor + config assembly via a lightweight Dart-free default config or a stored last config JSON), declared with BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE in the manifest.

findings.title: No auto-reconnect: engine crash or death lands in a terminal blocked state; the reconnecting state is dead code
findings.evidence: v2rayNG 'setUnderlyingNetworks() (API 28+) handles network switch without reconnect' and WireSock exposes 'Auto-reconnect, Connection timeout (Continuous Retry)' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:316; research/10-WireSock.md:505). The app defines 'reconnecting' in TunnelState (tunnel.dart:11) but it is never emitted (grep: only definition, l10n mapping, and vpn_notifier mapping — no producer), and on engine crash Tunnel._onBoxEvent does '_block(TunnelBlockReason.boxCrashed)' (tunnel.dart:536-547) — a terminal state with no retry timer, no watchdog, and no user-facing 'Reconnect' affordance beyond the generic power tile. Overnight death of the engine means the morning phone is unprotected until the use
findings.fix: On boxCrashed/boxStartFailed, schedule an exponential-backoff auto-reconnect while the user's intent is 'connected' (persist the desired state), emit TunnelState.reconnecting during retries, and cap retries with a notification instead of a silent terminal blocked.

findings.title: No auto-connect on boot, no OS Always-on support, no onRevoke handling: after reboot the tunnel is down until the user taps through 5+ taps
findings.evidence: Karing declares 'RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED (auto-start VPN)' (research/01-Karing.md:337) and v2rayNG likewise (research/06-V2RayNG.md:472); NekoBox documents supporting OS Always-on via the onRevoke callback (research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:293 'App supports onRevoke() callback'). The app manifest has no RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED and no boot receiver (AndroidManifest.xml), QanatVpnService.kt has no onRevoke override, and no always-on request helper exists (grep for BOOT_COMPLETED/always-on: no hits in lib/ or android/). Every reboot = unlock, open app, pass the wizard gate, tap power — and a competing VPN taking over leaves QANATVPN's UI claiming connected.
findings.fix: Add a BOOT_COMPLETED receiver that (after permission check) auto-connects the last/selected endpoint, override onRevoke() in QanatVpnService to emit a blocked/revoked event over box_events, and surface an 'enable Always-on VPN' deep-link in the wizard battery step.

findings.title: No way to select or connect to a specific endpoint: endpoints screen rows have no tap action, connect always auto-picks first group member / first endpoint / vendored fallback
findings.evidence: NekoBox: 'Switch node: Notification tile + in-app spinner calls BoxInstance.Selector.Select(outboundTag)' (research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:449). The app's endpoints list rows render only label/protocol/delete — 'ListTile(leading:..., title: Text(stored.label)... IconButton(delete))' with no onTap and no connect affordance (endpoints_screen.dart:108-133; grep for select/onTap in the file returns only a comment). Connect always uses selectedEndpointProvider, which resolves 'group.defaultMember ... endpoints.first.tag ... vendoredEndpointTag' (selected_endpoint.dart:39-58) — so picking a different node means editing a group's default member in the groups editor first. The daily 'switch to the fa
findings.fix: Add tap-to-select (radio/check indicator + connect action) on endpoint rows writing the chosen tag into a persisted selection store consumed first by selectedEndpointProvider, and show a per-row latency from the existing latency module.

findings.title: Windows: closing the app window strands the tunnel — no tray, no minimize-to-tray, and sing-box.exe is orphaned outside process control
findings.evidence: V2RayN keeps the tunnel when the GUI goes away ('Service Mode installs a Windows Service ... survive UAC, allow auto-start' — research/05-V2RayN.md:382) and WireSock 3.x 'survives UI close in 3.x because service holds tunnel' (research/10-WireSock.md:514); Clash Verge adds 'Red/green tray icon indicates state' + 'launch minimized to tray' (research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:578,774). The app calls 'window.SetQuitOnClose(true)' (windows/runner/main.cpp:33) with no tray (grep tray in windows/: no hits) and no stop-on-exit hook; WindowsBoxProcessAdapter spawns the exe with ProcessStartMode.normal and no Job object (windows_box_process.dart:117-123), so quitting the app leaves an uncontrolled sing-b
findings.fix: On window close while connected either hide-to-tray (add tray icon with connect/disconnect/quit) or run Tunnel.disconnect before exit; put the child process in a Job object with kill-on-close so the engine can never outlive the UI, and on startup detect/kill a stale sing-box.exe before spawning.

findings.title: Max firewall is ordering-validation only: no OS-level kill-switch on either platform, so an engine crash silently unmasks traffic the user believes is protected
findings.note: Even stronger than claimed: BoxEngine.kt openTun explicitly sets builder.setBlocking(false).
findings.evidence: Goal locks 'MAX FIREWALL: max firewall WFP/iptables/pf + in-tunnel DNS + IPv6 block + 7 tests' (goal.md §12); WireSock 'installs NDIS static deny-all filters ... only WG UDP Endpoint + DNS + DHCP survive' (research/10-WireSock.md:292) and WG Tunnel's Lockdown mode blocks all traffic when the tunnel dies (research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:258). The app's main.dart admits the gap verbatim: 'a true OS-level fail-closed filter ... needs native code that does not exist yet on either platform — Android VpnService setBlocking(true) + addRoute(0.0.0.0/0) lockdown in QanatVpnService, Windows WFP rules in the runner. Until those land, the engine rule ordering below is the kill-switch' (main.dart:171-176); Polic
findings.fix: On Android set setBlocking(true) and always addRoute(0.0.0.0/0)+IPv6 so the OS itself blackholes non-tunnel traffic while the VpnService lives; on Windows add WFP deny-all/allow-tunnel filters from the runner at connect and remove them on clean disconnect.

findings.title: Log 'export' writes to stdout and shows a success snackbar — user gets no file, no clipboard, no share sheet
findings.evidence: research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:740: 'Export: Settings → Export Logs zips config.yaml (redacted secret) + verge.yaml + service.log + Mihomo buffer → for issue filing'; research/06-V2RayNG.md:441 records v2rayNG shipping '添加分享日志 #5682' (share log). The app's Logs tab has an Icons.share export button, but _export() only does print('--- qanatvpn log export (${visible.length} lines) ---'); print(buffer.toString()); — raw stdout, no share sheet, no file write, no Clipboard. On Android/Windows release builds nothing consumes that stdout: the user taps Export, sees 'Logs exported (N)' (logs_screen.dart:243-246), and gets nothing they can paste or attach to a bug report.
findings.fix: Route the same buffer to a real sink: file_picker.saveFile (.txt/.log) on Windows and a platform share sheet (or Clipboard.setData + toast) on Android, mirroring the encrypted-backup file flow already in endpoints_screen.dart:146-177.

findings.title: No through-proxy 'real delay' connectivity test — TCP-connect ping to the server address is the only per-endpoint probe
findings.evidence: research/05-V2RayN.md:435-437: 'Modes: TCP Ping (default, Tcping via raw TCP connect to address:port) vs Real Ping (ICMP) vs Proxy Ping via core'; research/06-V2RayNG.md:425-427: real delay test 'fetches http://www.google.com/generate_204 via proxy, measures RTT'; research/01-Karing.md:535: 'Delay detection URL ... default http://cp.cloudflare.com/generate_204 ... per-node latency shown'. The app's only probe is SocketLatencyPinger — Socket.connect(host, port) to the endpoint's server:port (latency.dart:19-31), and Health pings a fixed 1.1.1.1:443 (health.dart:131-146, diagnostics_screen.dart:59 'Ping (TCP 1.1.1.1:443)'). TCP-connect proves a port is open, not that Reality/AWG handshake or r
findings.fix: Add a real (through-tunnel) check: HTTP GET generate_204 with a short timeout while connected (Dart-side fetch already rides the TUN), surfaced on Diagnostics as a step 'site reachable via tunnel', plus per-endpoint delay chips in the endpoints/groups lists like Karing's per-node latency.

findings.title: Goal-frozen stepwise diagnostics suite (DNS scanner 0-6, per-resolver scores, traceroute per-hop, sort by ping, captive portal) reduced to one boolean + one ping
findings.note: Goal lock exists but at goal.md:111, not :15 (same quoted text).

findings.title: gh-pages deploy is rejected by environment protection rules — tag refs cannot satisfy the github-pages branch policy, so the site and the updater mirror have never deployed (both 404 live)
findings.note: Verified: annotation verbatim on check-run 101114851181; deployment statuses waiting->failure; policies master+v* are branch-type only.
findings.evidence: Reality (check-run 101114851181 annotations): "Tag \"v0.1.0\" is not allowed to deploy to github-pages due to environment protection rules." and "The deployment was rejected or didn't satisfy other protection rules." Both attempts (16:51 and 17:31 on 555c223) created deployments that went waiting → failure (deployment-status API). The environment does have policies {"name":"master"},{"name":"v*"} (gh api .../deployment-branch-policies), yet deploys keep failing — GitHub deployment branch policies gate branch refs, and a tag ref (refs/tags/v0.1.0) is rejected, so the v* pattern cannot unblock the tag trigger. Live: `curl -sI https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/latest.json` → HTTP/1.1 404; / → 4
findings.fix: Trigger gh-pages from a branch, not tags: run on push to master (or workflow_dispatch invoked by the metadata job after latest.json is attached) so the ref satisfies the environment's branch policy; or delete the github-pages environment branch-policy protection. Also turn the `|| echo` into a hard failure when latest.json is absent from the releas

findings.title: Root cause of run 33900799115: github-pages environment's `v*` policy is branch-type only, so tag refs are rejected at the environment gate
findings.note: Verified: yml environment block lines 16-18; deployment-branch-policies = [master, v*] branch-type; annotation verbatim.
findings.evidence: Workflow: job triggers on `push: tags: ['v*']` (line 5) and declares `environment: name: github-pages` (lines 16-18). Reality: `gh api repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies` → {"total_count":2,"branch_policies":[{"name":"master","type":"branch"},{"name":"v*","type":"branch"}]} — v* is registered as a BRANCH policy, and run 33900799115's annotation says 'Tag "v0.1.0" is not allowed to deploy to github-pages due to environment protection rules. The deployment was rejected or didn't satisfy other protection rules.' GitHub docs (Managing environments, step 10): "In the 'Ref type' dropdown menu... click **Branch** or **Tag**... Name patterns must be configured
findings.fix: Settings → Environments → github-pages → Deployment branches and tags → Add deployment branch or tag rule → Ref type: Tag → pattern `v*` (the REST deployment-branch-policies endpoint only manages branch-type entries). Then re-run the failed run.

findings.title: latest.json 'single producer' contract silently unfulfilled: release has NO latest.json and gh-pages' fail-open echo ships the site without it
findings.evidence: Doc claim (gh-pages.yml:29-33): "# Mirror latest.json straight from the release the metadata job attached (single producer: build-android metadata job). gh release download \"$TAG\" ... --pattern 'latest.json' ... || echo \"latest.json not on release yet — site ships without it\"" — the || echo exits 0, masking the miss. Reality: gh release view v0.1.0 --json assets → {"assets":["sha256-windows.json","qanatvpn_v0.1.0_windows-x64.zip"]} (no latest.json, no APKs); the producer run build-android 33900799214 died at 'X Install Android SDK + NDK 28 — Process completed with exit code 127', so the metadata job (build-android.yml:123-168) never executed. Consumers hardcode the missing URL: lib/module
findings.fix: Fix the build-android NDK-install step so the metadata job actually attaches latest.json (then re-tag or upload it to the release); change the gh-pages staging step to fail loudly (or emit a visible warning annotation) when latest.json is absent from an existing release instead of swallowing it with echo.

findings.title: Version scheme mismatch: pubspec 1.0.0+1 vs git tag v0.1.0 makes the updater report an update to itself
findings.note: Mismatch real but impact inverted: _semverKey('0.1.0')=1000 < _semverKey('1.0.0')=1000000, so updater reports UpdateUpToDate (misses every v0.x release), never 'an update to itself'. Same fix.
findings.evidence: Reality: pubspec.yaml:4 `version: 1.0.0+1` (same at tag: `git show v0.1.0:pubspec.yaml | grep version` -> 1.0.0+1); tag is v0.1.0. Comparison chain: localVersion comes from PackageInfo (updates_controller.dart:92-93 `final info = await PackageInfo.fromPlatform()`), remote version comes from `tag_name` (updater.dart:79), compared via `isNewerThan` (updater.dart:25-26) using 3-part numeric key. `_semverKey('1.0.0')` == `_semverKey('0.1.0')` == 1000000, so an app whose pubspec says 1.0.0 will report "Update v0.1.0" as available the moment the release gains APKs. AGENTS.md's own example (line 113) uses app version v1.2.3 tags, so the pubspec was bumped ahead of the tag scheme with no single sour
findings.fix: Adopt one scheme: pubspec version is the truth, tags are `v<pubspecVersion>` cut by script (e.g. derive tag from pubspec in CI or a release script). For now set pubspec back to 0.1.0+1 before re-cutting the tag, and add a CI check (build-android/build-windows pre-step) that fails if `git describe --tags --exact-match` (stripped of v) != pubspec ver

findings.title: libbox.ps1 main/legacy variants always crash at exit-handling: ProcessStartInfo streams never redirected, $p.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync() throws in pwsh and Windows PowerShell
findings.evidence: Header claims: `# libbox.ps1 - Windows-local twin of the root Makefile (same args, same order). # Usage: pwsh scripts/libbox.ps1 main|legacy|windows`. Reality: lines 49-51 run gomobile via ProcessStartInfo with `UseShellExecute = $false` but never set `RedirectStandardOutput/$psi.RedirectStandardError = $true`, then call `$outTask = $p.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync()`. Probed on this machine: with an unredirected ProcessStartInfo, `$p.StandardOutput` is $null and `.ReadToEndAsync()` throws 'You cannot call a method on a null-valued expression' (reproduced on both pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1). The script dies after the bind with no `exit $p.ExitCode` and no log files written — callers s
findings.fix: Add `$psi.RedirectStandardOutput = $true; $psi.RedirectStandardError = $true` before `[System.Diagnostics.Process]::Start($psi)`, and either document `winget install GnuWin32.Make`/choco make for Windows or note that android aar builds go through CI/WSL.

findings.title: gh-pages workflow is tag-triggered but the github-pages environment rejects tag deployments — latest.json mirror and site can never go live (both 404 today)
findings.note: Mechanism verified server-side: github-pages env protection_rules = [branch_policy] only, custom_branch_policies=true; both tag gh-pages runs failed; site 404.
findings.evidence: DOC CLAIM: .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:3-5 "on: push: tags: ['v*']" and step "Mirror latest.json straight from the release ... single producer: build-android metadata job" — the design assumes tag runs deploy. REALITY: check-run annotations for gh-pages job 101114851181 (run 33900799115, commit 555c223): "Tag \"v0.1.0\" is not allowed to deploy to github-pages due to environment protection rules." and "The deployment was rejected or didn't satisfy other protection rules."; curl https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/latest.json -> 404 and site root https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/ -> 404. Every future tag will hit the same environment policy, so latest.json/site can never publish from tags a
findings.fix: In repo Settings > Environments > github-pages, add tag pattern v* to the deployment branch/tag policy (or switch gh-pages.yml to deploy from master pushes), then re-run the gh-pages workflow for v0.1.0 after the APK fix lands so latest.json exists to mirror.

findings.title: build-android reliably fails at 'Install Android SDK + NDK 28': sdkmanager not found (exit 127), contradicting the workflow's own comment that setup-android wires it into PATH
findings.note: Facts verified (5/5 runs failed; log shows sdkmanager not found exit 127), but the failed runs executed the pre-fix workflow (tag 555c223 has bare run: sdkmanager, no setup-android). The setup-android@v3 comment exists only on unpushed HEAD 30577ce — unproven, not contradicted.
findings.evidence: Doc: build-android.yml:41-43 comment "ubuntu-latest ships cmdline-tools but not sdkmanager on PATH — probed live (exit 127). android-actions/setup-android wires the preinstalled SDK into the environment; sdkmanager then installs the pinned NDK/platform.". Reality: run 33900799214 log-failed at step 'Install Android SDK + NDK 28': "line 1: sdkmanager: command not found" + "##[error]Process completed with exit code 127"; master push run 33900399270 fails in the same named step — the fix never worked on any real run.
findings.fix: Call the full path: `$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager --install ...` (setup-android@v3 does not add sdkmanager to PATH), or use android-actions/setup-android@v3's documented env wiring, and add a `command -v sdkmanager` assertion so the failure is loud at the right place.

findings.title: latest.json single-producer job is dead code on android failure: metadata `needs: apk` is skipped, so latest.json can never be attached to a windows-only release

findings.title: latest.json mirror is a cross-workflow race gh-pages can never win: consumer triggers in parallel with producer, no wait, silent fallback ships without it
findings.note: Structurally verified: gh-pages stages site ~1 min after tag push with one-shot download + echo fallback; metadata runs needs:apk then polls up to 2400s; no re-deploy trigger.
findings.evidence: Doc side: build-android.yml:123-126 — "Single producer of latest.json: waits until BOTH platform jobs have attached their assets"; gh-pages.yml:29-33 — "Mirror latest.json straight from the release the metadata job attached ... --pattern 'latest.json' --output site/latest.json || echo \"latest.json not on release yet — site ships without it\"". Reality: metadata only runs needs: apk (build-android.yml:127) and then polls up to deadline=$((SECONDS + 2400)) for the windows-x64.zip asset (build-android.yml:138), i.e. latest.json lands many minutes AFTER tag push, while gh-pages stages its site in the first minute. gh run list: build-android, build-windows, build-linux, gh-pages all started 2026
findings.fix: Chain gh-pages after production: replace the tag trigger with workflow_run (completed: build-android, types: [completed]) plus a gate on latest.json presence, or poll inside the Stage-site step for latest.json (with timeout) instead of the one-shot || echo fallback; re-deploy whenever metadata uploads a new latest.json.
