Repo-wide grep of lib/ for 'reserved': zero matches — WireGuardPeer (normalized_endpoint.dart:36) has publicKey/endpoint/allowedIps/presharedKey/persistentKeepalive only; WgIniParser, ClashYamlParser, and SingboxJsonParser all drop it, and wireGuardEndpointToJson cannot emit it. For Cloudflare-WARP-class WG profiles the 3 reserved bytes are required for the handshake, so the impo
findings.fix: Add `reserved` (List<int> or 3-byte field) to WireGuardPeer, read it in the WG INI/Clash/sing-box-JSON parsers, persist in normalizedToJson, and emit `reserved` on wireguard peers (never on awg).

findings.title: wg-quick-legal bare tunnel address (`Address = 10.7.0.2` without prefix) FATALs the engine at connect — no CIDR normalization on parse or emit
findings.evidence: PROBE: endpoints[0].address=["10.7.0.2"] (both awg and wireguard) -> EXIT=1 `FATAL decode config: endpoints[0].address: (json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type **netip.Prefix | netip.ParsePrefix("10.7.0.2"): no '/')`. Address is `badoption.Listable[netip.Prefix]` (option/wireguard.go:11, option/awg.go:10) — netip.ParsePrefix requires '/'. wg-quick explicitly defaults bare addresses to /32 (v4) / /128 (v6), and the INI parser passes `Address =` values through verbatim (parsers.dart:960-962 `addresses.addAll(value.split(',')...)`), as does the AWG editor's comma-split (_address field). wireGuardEndpointToJson/emit does no normalization and AwgConfig.validate only checks non-empty (
findings.fix: Normalize bare tunnel addresses to /32 (IPv4) / /128 (IPv6) in the WG INI parser (and defensively in wireGuardEndpointToJson/emit or AwgConfig.validate).

findings.title: ECH ingest/emit is vless-only; engine accepts ECH on trojan/hysteria2/tuic/vmess TLS, so ECH is silently dropped for those protocols
findings.evidence: parsers.dart has ech reads only at vless sites (line 383-407 sing-box JSON `case 'vless'`, line 655 vless URI `query['ech']`); trojan URI parser (line 788+), hysteria2 URI parser, tuic URI parser and the sing-box JSON `case 'trojan'/'hysteria2'/'tuic'` (parsers.dart 437-500) never read tls.ech. Emitter only forwards ECH for VlessEndpoint (endpoint_outbound.dart 47-48); _trojan (136), _hysteria2 (156), _tuic (173) call _tls without ech params. Real-binary probes (windows/sing-box.exe 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 check, exit 0): ech.enabled:true on tuic tls (cfg-ech-tuic2), trojan (cfg-ech-troj), hysteria2 (cfg-ech-hy2), vmess (cfg-ech-vmess) all accepted. So a trojan-gate ECH subscription imports with
findings.fix: Add echEnabled/echConfig to TrojanEndpoint, Hysteria2Endpoint, TuicEndpoint (and vmess JSON tls if desired), parse tls.ech in the corresponding JSON cases and `ech` query param in the URI parsers, then pass through _tls as vless already does.

findings.title: Imported malformed ECH PEM is shipped unvalidated and FATALs the whole profile at connect (`invalid ECH configs pem`)
findings.evidence: _echConfigString (parsers.dart 345-353) returns any String verbatim; _tls emits `config:[echConfig]` whenever non-empty (endpoint_outbound.dart 209-213); no engine check runs at import. Probes: ech config ["garbage-not-pem"] -> rc=1 `FATAL initialize outbound[0]: invalid ECH configs pem`; config ["   "] -> same FATAL; multi-block ["-----BEGIN ECH CONFIGS-----\nAAAA...","-----BEGIN ECH CONFIGS-----\nBBBB..."] -> same FATAL. The FATAL is at outbound init, so one bad stored endpoint prevents the whole profile from starting until manually removed. (Single AAAA PEM block passed rc=0, so only structurally invalid PEM bricks.)
findings.fix: In _echConfigString, drop entries that lack `-----BEGIN ECH CONFIGS-----` and non-empty base64 body (or keep the value but surface a validation warning and skip emit when the PEM markers are absent), mirroring how the repo guards other engine-FATAL shapes.

findings.title: VMess drops host data from share links: ws Host header, h2 host/path, clash grpc-service-name never emitted
findings.evidence: VmessEndpoint has no wsHost field (normalized_endpoint.dart:142). VmessUriParser reads only doc['path'] (parsers.dart:696) — the v2rayN `host` param (CDN fronting, standard in v2rayN JSON) is ignored. ClashYamlParser vmess reads only ws-opts.path (parsers.dart:167) — ws-opts.headers.Host, h2-opts host/path and grpc-opts.grpc-service-name are all dropped. _vmess (endpoint_outbound.dart:70-74) passes wsPath but NOT wsHost into _resolveTransport (vless does pass wsHost, line 54; trojan builds typed transport with host). Result for a vmess+ws+host link: emits {"type":"ws","path":"/ws"} with no Host header and tls.server_name = sni ?? address (SNI=IP for CDN nodes). Probes: emitted shape (p2.json
findings.fix: Add host to VmessEndpoint (or build TransportOptions in the URI/Clash vmess parsers like VlessUriParser/TrojanUriParser do): parse doc['host'], ws-opts.headers.Host, h2-opts, grpc-opts.grpc-service-name; pass wsHost through _vmess → _resolveTransport so _ws emits headers.Host.

findings.title: ws max_early_data / early_data_header_name parsed-and-dropped and never emitted (0-RTT lost on round-trip)
findings.evidence: Fork V2RayWebsocketOptions has MaxEarlyData uint32 + EarlyDataHeaderName string (option/v2ray_transport.go). Probe: vmess ws transport {"type":"ws","path":"/ws","max_early_data":2048,"early_data_header_name":"Sec-WebSocket-Protocol"} → EXIT=0 (accepted). _transport (parsers.dart:313-341) captures only type/path/host/headers/service_name/mode/idle_timeout/ping_timeout/method, so an imported sing-box JSON ws node with early data round-trips into a config missing 0-RTT setup (silent behavior change against servers configured for early data). V2rayN `ed`/`eh` params riding in the ws path query (?ed=2048) are likewise passed through verbatim instead of mapped. Assignment explicitly covers 'ws (ea
findings.fix: Add maxEarlyData/earlyDataHeaderName to TransportOptions, parse them in _transport, and emit them in the 'ws' branch of _transport (endpoint_outbound.dart:266).

findings.title: vmess network:quic emits type-only {'type':'quic'} → engine init FATAL 'quic: TLS required' when the node has no tls
findings.evidence: _resolveTransport case 'quic' (lines 105-107) → _transport(TransportOptions(type:'quic')) → {'type':'quic'}. Probe: vmess + {"type":"quic"} without tls → EXIT=1 `FATAL initialize outbound[0]: create client transport: quic: TLS required`; with tls {"enabled":true} → EXIT=0. vless/trojan are immune (their emitters always emit tls enabled), but vmess URI links (doc['tls'] null) and clash vmess (tls:false + network:quic) produce a parseable node whose emitted config FATALs init — established repo truth: one bad node bricks the whole profile at connect. Upstream transport docs: quic transport requires TLS.
findings.fix: Gate the quic passthrough on a tls block being emitted (pass a hasTls flag into _resolveTransport, or emit quic only from the vmess/vless/trojan emitters when e.tls is set); otherwise emit no transport or reject the node at import.

findings.title: vmess security passed through verbatim — legacy ciphers (rc4-md5) accepted by the decoder then FATAL the profile at init
findings.evidence: Probe: vmess outbound with "security":"rc4-md5" → EXIT=1 `FATAL initialize outbound[0]: vmess: unsupported security type: rc4-md5` (passes the strict JSON decoder, fails at outbound init). Fork enum (option/vmess.go): enum:"auto,none,zero,aes-128-cfb,aes-128-gcm,chacha20-poly1305"; upstream docs list auto/none/zero/aes-128-gcm/chacha20-poly1305. Sources feed security verbatim: doc['scy'] ?? doc['security'] ?? 'auto' (parsers.dart:691) and clash `cipher` (parsers.dart:158) — rc4-md5 was a standard legacy v2ray cipher and still appears in old v2rayN links. No whitelist/normalization exists on the emit side (endpoint_outbound.dart:65 echoes e.security).
findings.fix: Normalize security at parse or emit: map values outside the fork enum to 'auto' (legacy-server compatible) or reject the node at import with a clear error so one legacy link cannot brick the profile.

findings.title: SS SIP002 plaintext-userinfo links (incl. ALL 2022-blake3 links) always fail to parse
findings.evidence: PROBE: 'ss://2022-blake3-aes-256-gcm:VxaDrWtkVeXqqjRN3n5Af82-YtSSrbL0QkaB4RxB1mc@host:8388#t' → FormatException: Invalid base64 data at decodeBase64Flex. parseShareLines catches per-line and SILENTLY DROPS the node (ingestion_adapter.dart:108-120); a single-link import fails with 'no share links parsed'. For 2022 methods the userinfo is deliberately NOT base64-encoded (the PSK itself is base64); every mainstream producer (shadowrocket/NekoBox/v2rayN) emits this form. Only the legacy fully-base64 userinfo and whole-link forms work (probed OK).
findings.fix: _decodeUser: if the raw string contains ':' and fails strict base64, fall back to splitting method:password on the FIRST ':' without decoding (SIP002 2022 form), after Uri.decodeComponent; keep base64 path for legacy links.

findings.title: SS link with ?query string crashes port extraction — SIP002 plugin params unreadable
findings.evidence: PROBE: 'ss://YWVzLTI1Ni1nY206cGFzc3dvcmQ@203.0.113.20:8388?plugin=obfs-local%3Bobfs%3Dhttp%3Bobfs-host%3Dbing.com#tag1' → FormatException: bad number in ss port: 8388?plugin=obfs-local... (parsers.dart:736 via intOf). The parser strips only '#'/​'/' but never '?', so lastIndexOf(':') lands inside the query. Canonical SIP002 plugin links (no slash before ?) are therefore un-ingestible; the slash-form merely drops the plugin silently. The emitted shape itself is fine — 'plugin':'obfs-local','plugin_opts':'obfs=http;obfs-host=bing.com' passes windows/sing-box.exe check EXIT=0.
findings.fix: Cut the query before slicing hostPort (body.indexOf('?')), then read plugin/plugin opts from queryOf(uri) into ShadowsocksEndpoint.plugin/pluginOpts.

findings.title: Trojan ws transport drops the Host header (TransportOptions.host never emitted)
findings.evidence: PROBE (real emitter): link 'trojan://hunter2@203.0.113.10:443?sni=cdn.example.com&type=ws&path=%2Fws&host=cdn.example.com#tag1' → {"transport":{"type":"ws","path":"/ws"}} — host=cdn.example.com dropped. The 'ws' branch of _transport only emits t.path and t.headers; TransportOptions.host (set by TrojanUriParser:801-813) is never merged. Contradicts TransportOptions docstring normalized_endpoint.dart:75-81 ('ws Host header handled via [host]'). Engine check passes (EXIT=0 probed) so the loss is silent: CDN-fronted ws servers that route on Host break at connect. The legacy vless path (_ws wsPath/wsHost) does map host→headers.Host, so only the typed-transport trojan path regresses.
findings.fix: In _transport 'ws' case, if t.host != null and cleanHeaders has no Host key (any case), inject {'Host': t.host} before emitting headers.

findings.title: SS plugin_opts valueless flags dropped on sing-box JSON round-trip (v2ray-plugin TLS flag lost)
findings.evidence: PROBE (real emitter): SingboxJsonParser round-trip of plugin_opts 'mode=websocket;tls;host=example.com;mux=5' → parsed_pluginOpts {mode, host, mux} ('tls' gone because it has no '=') → re_emitted plugin_opts "mode=websocket;host=example.com;mux=5". The bare `tls` flag is what enables TLS in v2ray-plugin; its silent removal downgrades the plugin to plaintext ws against a TLS server — check passes (EXIT=0) so the break is silent. _parsePluginOpts keeps only k=v parts and the emitter can only re-join k=v.
findings.fix: Represent flags as pluginOpts['tls']='' (emit as bare 'tls' when value is empty) or store the raw plugin_opts string on the model and re-emit verbatim for sing-box JSON imports.

findings.title: Empty obfs-password emits obfs {salamander, password: ""} which FATALs engine init: 'missing obfs password'
findings.evidence: Emitters only guard null: 'if (e.obfsPassword != null)' (endpoint_outbound.dart:154). Hysteria2UriParser reads obfsPassword: query['obfs-password'] — Dart probe: Uri.parse('hysteria2://a@h:443?obfs=salamander&obfs-password=#t').queryParameters -> {obfs: salamander, obfs-password: ''} (empty string, NOT null) -> emitted obfs {type: salamander, password: ""}. Probe: sing-box.exe check -> EXIT=1, 'FATAL initialize outbound[0]: missing obfs password'. Same via Clash yaml obfs: {type: salamander, password: ''} (parsers.dart:198). Non-empty shapes verified good: full hy2 outbound with obfs+hop_interval+up/down+colon ranges EXIT=0.
findings.fix: Treat blank as absent: at parse (parsers.dart:843,198) or emit (line 154), require obfsPassword.trim().isNotEmpty before emitting the obfs block.

findings.title: sing-box JSON import of a hysteria2 node: server_ports array cast TypeError bricks the whole import; hop_interval '30s' silently dropped
findings.evidence: Fork option (go/amnezia-box/option/hysteria2.go): ServerPorts badoption.Listable[string] — canonical sing-box JSON is an array ["20000:30000"] (upstream docs: 'server_ports: ["2080:3000"]', scalar only tolerated on decode); parser's `as String?` on a List throws _TypeError (the exact TypeError-DoS class P1 fixed for Clash per docs/decisions.tsv:72). Import is fail-closed via on Object (endpoints_controller.dart:161) but ALL endpoints in the payload are lost. Same block: hopIntervalSeconds = int.tryParse('30s') -> null, silently dropping the user's hop interval (fork JSON emits badoption.Duration as '30s'); the correct _durationSeconds helper already exists in the same file for transports.
findings.fix: Accept both shapes: if node['server_ports'] is List join entries with ',' (or store list and make Hysteria2Endpoint.ports list-typed); parse hop_interval via the existing _durationSeconds().

findings.title: TUIC alpn degenerates to "alpn": [] (check passes, runtime h3 handshake fails): empty alpn= query and tls.alpn: [] round-trips
findings.evidence: Probed Dart semantics: ''.split(',') == [] (empty pattern quirk), so query['alpn']='' yields [] and TuicEndpoint.alpn=[] survives the store round-trip; the sing-box JSON import path also preserves [] (tls.alpn: [] -> List.from). Emitter 'alpn': ?alpn (endpoint_outbound.dart:191) is a null-aware element — it skips null, not empty — so 'alpn': [] IS emitted. Engine: check EXIT=0 with "alpn": [] and with "alpn": [""] — but fork common/tls/std_client.go:146 only sets NextProtos when len(options.ALPN) > 0, so the QUIC handshake offers no h3; tuic v5 is HTTP/3-based (upstream tuic doc: tls required, QUIC fields) and a real server rejects no-ALPN handshakes. Contrast: TuicUriParser defaults 'h3' on
findings.fix: Enforce the h3 default on all entry paths: in TuicUriParser and the JSON import, map empty/degenerate alpn to ['h3']; optionally in _tls drop empty-string entries.

findings.title: TUIC congestion_control is passed through unvalidated; an invalid value FATALs engine init and bricks the whole profile
findings.evidence: Probes: congestion_control 'bbr2' -> EXIT=1, 'FATAL initialize outbound[0]: unknown congestion control algorithm: bbr2'; 'bbr'/'cubic'/... EXIT=0. The parser copies query['congestion_control'] (parsers.dart:873) and node['congestion-controller'] (parsers.dart:212) unchecked; emitter forwards verbatim (endpoint_outbound.dart:171). Fork option/tuic.go enum is cubic,new_reno,bbr. A single corrupted/malicious sub node therefore FATALs startOrReloadService for the entire profile (the same one-bad-node class the code documents for transports in endpoint_outbound.dart). udp_relay_mode is NOT affected — invalid value silently defaults to native (probed 'turbo' EXIT=0; fork switch has no default erro
findings.fix: Whitelist at parse: {cubic,new_reno,bbr} else throw FormatException('tuic: bad congestion_control') so the per-line failure policy in parseShareLines applies; optionally whitelist udp_relay_mode {native,quic} for a clear error.

findings.title: urltest tolerance is not range-validated against the fork's uint16: 70000 or negative FATALs config decode at start
findings.evidence: Fork option (go/amnezia-box/option/group.go): `Tolerance uint16`. Real binary: `sing-box.exe check -c` with tolerance 70000 → EXIT=1 `FATAL decode config at ...: outbounds[0].tolerance: json: cannot unmarshal number 70000 into Go struct field URLTestOutboundOptions.tolerance of type uint16`; tolerance -1 → same class of decode FATAL. Neither the compiler (routing_compiler.dart:107 emits `group.tolerance` raw) nor profile_config_source.dart:310 nor the form (groups_screen.dart:343-347 `int.tryParse(...) ?? 50`, no range check; policy_store.dart round-trips any int) validates the 0-65535 range — so the per-group fail-closed gate in profile_config_source._merged (which skips invalid groups) nev
findings.fix: Range-validate tolerance in RoutingCompiler._compileGroups (0 < tolerance <= 65535, matching the ports/ip_version pattern) and in the groups form field; the compiler gate makes profile_config_source._merged skip the broken group fail-closed instead of FATALing the engine.

findings.title: SingboxJsonParser silently drops string-form ssh host_key: imported TOFU pin is lost and the engine then accepts any host key
findings.evidence: parsers.dart:451-453: `final hostKey = node['host_key'] is List ? List<String>.from(...) : null` — a bare string yields null, while private_key two lines below handles BOTH String and List (462-464). The fork accepts the string form: `HostKey badoption.Listable[string]` (option/ssh.go) and a real-binary probe with `"host_key": "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3...OZYF"` (valid key, ssh-keygen generated) passes `sing-box.exe check` EXIT=0; the array form also passes. Consequence: importing a sing-box config whose ssh node pins the host key via the string form produces an SshEndpoint with hostKey=null, and _ssh (endpoint_outbound.dart) then emits no host_key — the fork's HostKeyCallback returns nil for any s
findings.fix: In the SingboxJsonParser ssh case, normalize the scalar: `node['host_key'] is List ? List<String>.from(...) : (node['host_key'] is String ? [node['host_key'] as String] : null)`.

findings.title: fakeIpFilters/filterMode are dead data: never emitted, so LAN/NTP/connectivity domains receive FakeIPs and local name resolution breaks while tunneled
findings.evidence: DnsConfig.fakeIpFilters ('+.lan','+.local','+.msftconnecttest.com','time.*.com','ntp.*.com') is defaulted, doc-commented as 'Local discovery and pairing must resolve real IPs', and asserted Dart-side by test/dns/dns_config_test.dart:69-73 ('fake-ip filters exclude lan + ntp from the pool'), but toDnsJson emits no rule that consumes them. Emit shape: rules[0] geosite-cn, clash rules, then {query_type:[A,AAAA]→dns-fakeip}; a +.lan A/AAAA query matches nothing before the fakeip rule and gets a 198.18.x.x fake IP (sing-box check on hand-derived emitted config, probe p1: exit 0). While tunneled, LAN is BLOCKed (FirewallPolicy) and the fake-IP connection maps back to the domain and dials remotely,
findings.fix: In toDnsJson, emit the fakeIpFilters as exclusion DNS rules before the A/AAAA fakeip rule (map each '+.x' to domain_suffix, 'time.*.com' style to domain, server: dns-local for whitelist mode), or delete the dead fields and the misleading test. Probe p3 proves the emission passes the real binary.

findings.title: Clash vless reality-opts and client-fingerprint silently dropped — Reality node imports as plain TLS (dead node, no error)
findings.evidence: grep confirms zero occurrences of reality-opts/client-fingerprint/grpc-opts/h2-opts anywhere in parsers.dart — the entire clash _proxy switch reads only ws-opts.path (vmess only, line 167). Probe (dart harness, real repo code): clash vless with tls:true + reality-opts{public-key,short-id} + client-fingerprint:chrome → EMIT '..."tls":{"enabled":true,"server_name":"real.example.com"},"transport":{"type":"grpc"}' — no tls.reality, no tls.utls. Reality public-key/short-id are the node's core credentials; without them a Reality server rejects the plain-TLS handshake, so the imported node is silently dead (emit also drops utls because fingerprint is only defaulted to chrome when realityPublicKey !
findings.fix: In the clash vless case map realityPublicKey: node['reality-opts']?['public-key'], realityShortId: node['reality-opts']?['short-id'], fingerprint: node['client-fingerprint'] ?? node['fingerprint']. Emit path needs no change (already probe-verified).

findings.title: vless emitted with tls.enabled=true even when the source node has no TLS (clash tls:false) — connect fails on plain-CDN nodes
findings.evidence: _vless unconditionally emits 'tls': _tls(enabled: true, ...) ignoring VlessEndpoint.security. Probe: clash vless tls:false + network:ws (classic port-80 CDN node) → EMIT '..."server_port":80,..."tls":{"enabled":true,"server_name":"cdn.example.com"},"transport":{"type":"ws"}'. The engine accepts the correct shape — probe: same outbound with NO tls key → check EXIT=0. With forced TLS the client performs a TLS handshake against a plaintext ws server → every connection fails. Note the same forcing also affects plain vless:// share links (security absent). The model already records the distinction (security: null); only the emitter loses it.
findings.fix: In _vless, emit the tls block only when security == 'tls' || realityPublicKey != null: 'tls': ?((e.security != null || e.realityPublicKey != null) ? _tls(...) : null). Add a plain-vless round-trip test.

findings.title: Clash ss plugin passed through untranslated and plugin-opts never mapped — plugin 'obfs' FATALs the engine at start ('plugin not found: obfs')
findings.evidence: parser:176 'plugin: node["plugin"] as String?' passes clash plugin names through verbatim and never reads 'plugin-opts'. Probes (windows/sing-box.exe check): plugin "obfs" (canonical clash name per mihomo; sing-box valid names are obfs-local/v2ray-plugin) → 'FATAL initialize outbound[0]: plugin not found: obfs' EXIT=1 — one such node bricks the whole profile at start; plugin "obfs-local" with mihomo-style opts 'mode=http;host=...' → EXIT=0 but is a silent no-op (simple-obfs expects 'obfs=http;obfs-host=...'; with NO opts also EXIT=0) — obfs host loss weakens the camouflage invisibly. Emit side (_shadowsocks) only joins the never-populated pluginOpts map. Emitted evidence: '{..."plugin":"obfs
findings.fix: In the clash ss case: translate plugin obfs→obfs-local (pass v2ray-plugin through), map plugin-opts YamlMap to the pluginOpts Map<String,String> (for obfs also rename mode→obfs and host→obfs-host), and reject/flag unsupported clash-only plugins (shadow-tls/restls) at import instead of emitting a FATAL config.

findings.title: Clash wireguard simplified single-peer form (no 'peers:' key — the mihomo documented default) imports a peerless, non-functional endpoint
findings.evidence: clash case only reads node['peers']; mihomo's simplified single-peer form is top-level fields (wiki.metacubex.one/config/proxies/wg/: 'server/port/public-key/pre-shared-key/allowed-ips/persistent-keepalive/reserved' at proxy level). Probe (dart harness): that doc form → 'WG peers=0'. wireGuardEndpointToJson then emits "'peers': []" which the engine ACCEPTS (probe: endpoints[0] wireguard, prefixed address, peers:[] → check EXIT=0), producing a profile that looks valid and connects to nothing; peer public-key/pre-shared-key/allowed-ips/reserved are all silently lost (reserved is required for Cloudflare-WARP peers). Multi-peer form works (tested by repo test) — only the flat form is broken.
findings.fix: In the clash wireguard case, when node['peers'] is absent but node['public-key'] or node['server'] is present, synthesize one WireGuardPeer from server/port/public-key/pre-shared-key/allowed-ips/persistent-keepalive (reserved stays unmapped — note it in the report). Add fixture test.

findings.title: All clash transport detail is dropped except vmess ws path: grpc-opts, ws-opts.headers (Host), max-early-data, h2-opts, xhttp-opts.mode — bare {'type':'grpc'}/{'type':'ws'} transports emitted and silently mis-route
findings.evidence: grep: the whole clash branch reads exactly one *-opts key (ws-opts.path, vmess only). Probes (dart harness + real repo emitter): vless network:grpc + grpc-opts.grpc-service-name → EMIT '"transport":{"type":"grpc"}' (sing-box check on the bare grpc transport → EXIT=0, so it silently ships; engine dials empty service name and real servers reject); vless/vmess ws-opts.headers.Host → EMIT lacks 'headers' entirely (vmess probe with Host: front.example.com emitted '{"type":"ws","path":"/vp"}'); vless ws-opts.path AND headers both dropped (bare '{"type":"ws"}'); ws-opts.max-early-data/early-data-header-name dropped though the fork supports them (go/amnezia-box/option/v2ray_transport.go:107-108); h2
findings.fix: Extract a shared clash-transport helper: grpc-opts.grpc-service-name→TransportOptions(type:'grpc', serviceName), ws-opts.headers.Host→host (plus max-early-data if the model gains the field), h2-opts→http transport, network-opts/xhttp-opts→path/mode. Reuse for vless/vmess/trojan uniformly.

findings.title: _validateKey uses base64Url decoder: accepts URL-safe-alphabet keys ('-'/'_') the engine FATALs on at connect
findings.evidence: Probe (real binary, scratch config with crafted 44-char key containing '-'): windows/sing-box.exe run -> "FATAL create service: initialize endpoint[0]: illegal base64 data at input byte 34". Same key through the app's validator logic in dart: length==44 && endsWith('=') true, base64Url.decode OK (base64Url accepts BOTH alphabets, verified in dart). Go StdEncoding (endpoint.go genIpcConfig base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString) rejects '-'/'_'. Note repo decision 'decodeBase64Flex standard-first' acknowledges real configs use +/ alphabet - so a url-safe-pasted key should be rejected or normalized, not accepted verbatim.
findings.fix: Decode with base64.decode (standard alphabet) instead of base64Url.decode, or explicitly reject '-'/'_' chars and/or normalize url-safe keys to standard base64 before emitting.

findings.title: H1-H4 'pairwise distinct' string check misses engine's numeric UintRange-overlap rule (and range/reversed/non-numeric formats)
findings.evidence: Probes (real binary run): h1=1,h2=01,h3=8929,h4=2 -> "IPC error -22: failed to merge with device: headers must not overlap"; h1=8925-8935,h2=8929,h3=8930,h4=8931 -> same FATAL; h1=1-100,h2=50-150 -> same FATAL; h1=300-100 -> "failed to parse H1: wrong range specified"; h1=abc -> "failed to parse H1: strconv.ParseUint: parsing \"abc\": invalid syntax". Source: amneziawg-go v3.1.0-awgm.2 device/uapi.go mergeWithDevice checks left.Overlap(right) over 4 UintRanges; noise-types.go UintRange.FromString accepts 'lo-hi' with uint32 bounds. The app stores H as String so range values round-trip, but the validator neither parses ranges nor checks numeric overlap - it blesses configs that FATAL at conne
findings.fix: Parse each H as decimal or lo-hi (both halves ParseUint(value,10,32), hi>=lo) and reject on pairwise numeric overlap of the 4 intervals instead of string-set equality.

findings.title: AWG values are validated only in the editor: ingestion -> wireGuardEndpointToJson -> engine ships unvalidated values (negative jc/s1, oversized s3, jmin>jmax)

findings.title: FATAL-substring crash detector in the log stream can never fire — mid-run engine failures are invisible
findings.evidence: Kotlin scans message.contains("FATAL") but in this daemon fork a Fatal-level log never reaches the log stream: log/observable.go output() does writer.Write then os.Exit(1) BEFORE f.subscriber.Emit and BEFORE platformWriter.WriteMessage (lines ~148-175), so the process dies first (that death is only catchable via the separate disconnected() callback). Grep across engine runtime (route/, dns/, adapter/, box.go, transport/, inbound/, outbound/) finds zero logger.Fatal calls — FATAL lines exist only in CLI tools (cmd/, experimental/boxdd/). Exported log entries come from StartedService.WriteMessage (platform formatter includes level prefix, log/observable.go:55-58), but only ERROR/WARN/... level
findings.fix: Scan entry.level from LogEntry (LevelError=2 per log/level.go) instead of substring FATAL: crash-or-degraded when level <= 2 while running, keep disconnected() as process-death signal; drop the text scan.

findings.title: useProcFS=true hardcoded on all Android versions while findConnectionOwner throws 'unsupported' — process_name rules dead on Android 10+
findings.evidence: useProcFS() = true always. In fork service.go:107-137, with useProcFS the wrapper resolves uid itself via procfs.ResolveSocketByProcSearch (/proc/net/tcp) and never calls the platform method, so the Kotlin throw is consistent — but /proc/net is restricted for apps on Android 10+ (hidepid/SELinux), returning -1 → E.New("procfs: not found"). Upstream SFA reference: override fun useProcFS(): Boolean = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.Q, with findConnectionOwner using ConnectivityManager.getConnectionOwnerUid on Q+. The compiler can emit process_name rules (lib/modules/routing/routing_compiler.dart:227 addList('process_name', rule.processNames)), so those rules silently never match on
findings.fix: Gate useProcFS on SDK < 29 and implement findConnectionOwner via ConnectivityManager.getConnectionOwnerUid (API 29+) like upstream; alternatively reject process_name rules in the compiler until implemented.

findings.title: HttpCache accepts ANY 200 byte sequence as valid fresh content (no length, content-type, or format validation) and serves it for 6h including as endpoint credentials

Blast radius = corrupt geo file -> fail-stop engine FATAL, not credential exposure.
findings.evidence: http_cache.dart:43-50: "final fresh = _CacheEntry(body: response.body, etag: response.headers['etag'], fetchedAt: _now()); _memory[url] = fresh; await _writeDisk(url, fresh);" then http_cache.dart:55-58: "} on Object { if (entry != null) { return entry.body; } rethrow; }". The catch-all applies to the whole fetch block, so a 200 response carrying an HTML ISP/captive-portal/CDN error page — or a truncated, corrupt, or redirected body — is cached to disk and served as authoritative for staleAfter (6h). There is no Content-Length check, no Content-Type check, no size cap and no integrity check anywhere in getBytes. Impact concentrates where it matters: the endpoint importer's fetched payloads (
findings.fix: Validate before caching: pin expected Content-Type per URL class, enforce a max body size, and (for geo .srs) verify a known magic/format marker; on any mismatch throw instead of caching. findings.title: Per-app split has no data-plane enforcement: sing-box routing applies to all captured traffic, the split exists only as a single VpnService builder route decision
findings.note: instance.go merge verified verbatim, but VpnService builder addAllowed/addDisallowedApplication IS kernel-level data-plane enforcement — the same architecture upstream sing-box uses on Android. findings.evidence: The override merge in the Go engine does exactly one thing: `tunInboundOptions.AutoRedirect = overrideOptions.AutoRedirect; tunInboundOptions.IncludePackage = append(tunInboundOptions.IncludePackage, overrideOptions.IncludePackage...); tunInboundOptions.ExcludePackage = append(tunInboundOptions.ExcludePackage, ...); break`. Your BoxEngine.openTun forwards these to `builder.addAllowedApplication/addDisallowedApplication` — that is the only enforcement. Grep of lib/ shows no include_package/exclude_package/package_name/uid filtering is ever emitted into the config JSON itself (only the unrelated user rule fields exist at routing_compiler.dart:226-227, unused by the split path). Consequences: (
findings.fix: Emit the user's package list also as engine-side route rules (package_name on Android via find_process) for defense-in-depth, and include/exclude the app's own package explicitly like upstream BoxService.kt:225-227 does, instead of relying solely on the VpnService.Builder route layer.

findings.title: Envelope KDF salt and header fields are not AEAD-authenticated (no associated data), enabling offline brute-force cost reduction
findings.note: No-AAD is real and cited correctly, but the brute-force-cost-reduction claim fails: _deriveKey uses hardcoded constants (kdfMemoryKiB/iterations/parallelism) and reads only the salt from the envelope, so header tampering cannot lower KDF cost; missing AAD is header-integrity hardening here, not a live attack.
findings.evidence: Encrypt ignores AEAD associated data: `final box = await AesGcm.with256bits().encrypt(bytes, secretKey: key);` (line 196) and decrypt likewise: `return await AesGcm.with256bits().decrypt(SecretBox(...), secretKey: key);` (lines 232-238). Meanwhile the key is derived from envelope-controlled values: `final kdf = envelope['kdf'] as Map<String, dynamic>; final key = await _deriveKey(password, base64Decode(kdf['salt'] as String));` (lines 229-230). GCM MAC covers only nonce+ciphertext; magic, version, `kdf` (salt, and the decorative algo/memoryKiB/iterations/parallelism fields), and `cipher` are unauthenticated. An attacker who obtains the backup file (cloud sync, email, shared storage — the nor
findings.fix: Bind all envelope header fields as AES-GCM associated data on encrypt and verify on decrypt: `encrypt(bytes, secretKey: key, aad: headerBytes)` / `decrypt(box, secretKey: key, aad: headerBytes)` where headerBytes = utf8(jsonEncode({magic, version, kdf, cipher})). findings.title: In-flight leak window: firewall 'enforce' runs only after box.start has traffic flowing, contradicting the module's own 'firewall ON before traffic flows' guarantee
findings.note: baseRules are baked into config.json at assembly (config_assembler.dart:106) before box.start, so hijack-dns/DNS-direct/::/0/RFC1918 blocks are engine-active from the first packet; enforce() is a late re-verification. No actual unfiltered window; real defect is the broken doc contract and a dropped-rules config flowing before being caught.
findings.evidence: firewall.dart:7-9 states "firewall ON before traffic flows, relaxed only after box.stop", but tunnel.dart:479-481 does the opposite: "// firewall — enforced last, only once traffic is already flowing; await _timed(phases, 'firewall', () => firewall.enforce().timeout(timeouts.firewallEnforce));" — box.start(config) (line ~462) precedes the firewall phase, and box.start is what opens the TUN and starts routing. Between the started event and enforce() (plus up to an 8s timeout, timeouts.firewallEnforce = const Duration(seconds: 8)) every packet matches route.final=PROXY; only rules evaluated before it (hijack-dns, pinned DNS, ::/0, RFC1918) block anything. Additionally PolicyFirewallAdapter.enf
findings.fix: Run enforce() (or a real config validation of the TypedConfig JSON's route.rules) before box.start, after configSource.resolve — the config is fully assembled there. Delete the misleading 'checked before the engine is allowed to carry traffic' comment or make it true by validating config.json inside enforce().

findings.title: Only selector/urltest groups exist — no fallback or load-balance group type that Karing ships for node resilience
findings.note: goal.md §6 locks a 3-tier selector/urltest/proxy model, not fallback/load-balance; this is a Karing parity gap, not a frozen-commitment violation.
findings.evidence: Competitor: Karing group types are 'selector (manual), urltest (lowest latency), fallback, load-balance (Consistent Hashing/Round Robin per deepwiki 5.2)' with urltest tuning 'testLatencyAutoRemove hides high-latency/failing nodes' (research/01-Karing.md §5); goal.md §6 locks 'sing-box 3-tier (auto urltest → selector → proxy)'. App: _GroupFormSheet offers a two-value SegmentedButton ('ButtonSegment(value: false, label: Text("Selector")), ButtonSegment(value: true, label: Text("Urltest"))' — lib/modules/routing/groups_screen.dart:242-248) and OutboundGroup (routing_policy.dart:25-66) has no fallback/loadbalance constructors; the compiler (routing_compiler.dart) emits only selector/urltest.
findings.fix: Extend OutboundGroup + _GroupFormSheet with a fallback type (members ordered, engine picks first alive) and load-balance (method field), and add a testLatencyAutoRemove-style sweep that prunes dead members from urltest groups after the latency sweep.

findings.title: No node export/share: stored endpoints cannot be re-emitted as share links or QR for another device
findings.note: Real gap (only .qnv encrypted backup exists, no URI emitter) but post-setup convenience rather than an onboarding blocker.
findings.evidence: Competitor: Karing 'Share Plus + QR encode (zxing2) — Node share via tools.karing.app' and Hiddify 'share_plus + url_launcher for export... Text to QR code tool' (research/01-Karing.md §7, research/07-Hiddify.md §9). App: EndpointsScreen's only outbound flow is the whole-store encrypted backup ('Export encrypted backup' → .qnv file, endpoints_screen.dart:139-166); there is no per-endpoint share-link builder (endpointToOutboundJson emits engine JSON, not URIs) and no QR/share dependency in pubspec.yaml.
findings.fix: Add a per-row share action that serializes NormalizedEndpoint back to its canonical URI (vless://, ss://, hysteria2://...) with share_plus, and QR rendering for device-to-device transfer.

findings.title: Rule sets are a hardcoded 2-asset registry — no user URL rule providers with per-provider update intervals
findings.note: Registry is exactly 2 hardcoded assets and the compiler rejects all other tags; user URL rule providers are a Clash-Verge parity extension, not a frozen lock (intent.md locks mrs/srs format support, which exists for the 2 seeds).
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md — '`rule-providers: { name: { type: http, behavior: domain/ipcidr/classical, format: yaml/text/mrs, url, path, interval } }`' and 'Rule Providers section shows last-updated, type, behavior, format chips; manual Update per provider pulls with header auth'; research/11-FlClash.md — rule providers 'fetches with `interval: 600` (10 min) or `86400` (daily) per provider; can force via manual refresh'. App side: lib/modules/geo/geo_asset.dart:38-50 `static const Map registry` contains exactly geosite-cn + geoip-cn; lib/modules/routing/routing_compiler.dart:268 rejects anything else — `'unknown rule_set "$tag" (not in GeoAsset registry)'` — so the rule
findings.fix: Promote the registry to a user-editable RuleSetStore (tag, url, type domain/ip, update interval) persisted like rule_store, seed it with geosite-cn/geoip-cn, and have ruleSetEntries/refreshAll/compile read from it.

findings.title: No custom subscription HTTP headers or User-Agent — HWID/Bearer-gated panels are unusable
findings.note: Niche (HWID/Bearer-gated panels); missing default UA can 403 some providers, but impact is below high.
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/06-V2RayNG.md — 'SubEditActivity exposes Custom HTTP headers JSON textarea → SubscriptionItem.requestHeaders (example {"X-hwid":"my_test_device","Authorization":"Bearer test"}) … Useful for HWID-locked panels (Marzban, 3x-ui)' and 'userAgent field defaults to `v2rayNG/<version>` but editable'. App side: lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_controller.dart:96-98 is the only header site — `plainFetch(maybeUrl, const <String, String>{'Accept': '*/*'})` — hardcoded, no UA sent, no per-source header storage; plain_fetch.dart adds no default UA. Panels that gate subscriptions by UA or HWID return 403 to QANATVPN.
findings.fix: Send a default User-Agent (qanatvpn/<version>) on subscription fetches and persist optional per-source custom headers/UA in the subscription store, applying them on every refresh.

findings.title: No .conf or ZIP file import — WG-family configs (the canonical artifact of this class) cannot be opened, only hand-pasted
findings.note: Single .conf content already works via the paste path (WG INI sniffing in importText); what is truly missing is file-picker convenience and ZIP/batch import.

findings.title: No notification when an update is found: the only cue is a recolored tile inside the app, while competitors push a daily-check notification
findings.note: No notification surface confirmed, but the Home UpdateTile recolors on every app open and UpdateController.build() loads stored results at startup — cue exists in-app, only the system-notification parity is missing.

On Windows the user completes the per-app step, believes the b

findings.title: No last-state restore on app open and no silent start / launch-at-login on either platform

Silent start checkbox: launch minimized to tray'; research/11-FlClash.md:749: silent launching '--hidden' / autostart. App: vpn_notifier.dart:103 VpnNotifier.build() returns VpnState.disconnected() unconditionally; grep for lastEndpoint/last_connected/restore across lib/core/persistence and lib/ finds nothing — no 'was connected' bit is persisted anywhere; selected_endpoint.dart re-derives a d
findings.fix: Persist lastConnectedTag + wasConnected on connect/disconnect; on app start (and on Windows via a registry Run entry / --silent flag), show a one-tap 'Reconnect HKG-02' affordance and optionally auto-connect when the setting is enabled; surface it in a settings screen.

findings.title: Rule providers limited to a hardcoded 2-entry registry — custom rule_set URLs rejected
findings.note: Registry is exactly geosite-cn + geoip-cn (:38-52) and _validRuleSetTag = registry.containsKey (routing_compiler.dart:~400), but that is a deliberate documented FATAL guard (dangling rule_set ref kills the engine at start). Gap vs competitors is real; supporting custom URLs needs a sing-box check probe first — feature gap, not defect.

The app's universe is two hardcoded entries: geo_asset.dart:38 'static const Map<String, GeoAssetSpec> registry = {'geosite-cn', 'geoip-cn'}', and the compiler rejects everything else — routing_compiler.dart:400-402 '_validRuleSetTag(tag) => GeoAsset.registry.containsKey(tag)' with error 'unknown rule_se
findings.fix: Let users add custom remote rule-sets (url + format) through the rules editor: validate by compiling/probing (sing-box check path) instead of registry membership, register them into GeoAsset at runtime, and include them in the daily ETag refresh.

findings.title: No search, filter, or sort on the endpoint list
findings.note: Flat ListView keyed by import order; no searchfield/filterChip anywhere in lib/modules/vpn. Real but list-management polish distinct from the frozen sort-by-ping promise already tracked at 244/261.

The app's endpoints screen (endpoints_screen.dart:75-116) is a flat ListView.builder keyed by import order — no search field, no filter chips, no sort menu. The only search box in the entire app is on the Logs screen (lib/l10n/app_localizations_en.dart:249 logsSearchHint 'Search logs'); grep for search/filter across lib/modules/vpn returns nothing.
findings.fix: Add a search TextField + sort menu (by tag/protocol/latency) above the list, filtering state.endpoints in the build — trivial against the existing ListView.

findings.title: No bulk operations — no multi-select, bulk delete/test/move, or export-selection
findings.note: delete(int) removes exactly one item (:183-193); no selection state or checkboxes on the screen. Real for large subscriptions but same polish class as 262.

In this app lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_controller.dart:183-193 delete(int index) removes exactly one item and the screen has no selection state or checkboxes — deleting 50 dead nodes from a subscription is 50 taps. The only multi-item operation is whole-store encrypted backup (.qnv), which is not a per-selection or shareable format (endpoints_screen.dart:117-206).
findings.fix: Add long-press multi-select with select-all, bulk delete, and 'delete all from sourceUrl' (per-subscription wipe) to the endpoints screen; extend EndpointsController with deleteMany(List<String> tags).

findings.note: Hardcoded strings are real (verified in rules_screen, groups_screen, awg_profile_screen, backup flow, ingestion errors), but the key evidence is wrong: app_en/app_fa.arb are at full parity (84/84, zero missing FA keys), not 86 vs 91. Main flows are localized; the gap is unlocalized literals in forms/errors.

App side: app_fa.arb has only 86 keys vs app_en.arb's 91, and the missing ones are errors the user actually hits: the whole backup flow ('Export failed: $error', 'Import failed: $error', 'Backup written (N bytes)', 'Picked file has no readable path' at endpoints_screen.dart:164-192), the backup dialogs, the AWG editor incl. its 'Validation errors' card (awg_profile_screen.dart:135), every field label in the rules and groups forms (rules_screen.dart:319+ 'Domain suffixes (comma separated)', groups_screen.dart:301 'Members'), the inline import errors ('nothing to import', endpoints_controller.dart:84), the

findings.title: Network import failures surface as raw jargon ('HTTP 403 fetching URL', 'unsupported scheme "ssr"') with no offline/rate-limit distinction
findings.note: 'HTTP 403 fetching URL' verbatim at endpoints_controller.dart:100 and GitHubRateLimitException exists unused on this path; real wording gap but message-quality, not functional breakage.
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/06-V2RayNG.md:125 documents even the weaker precedent as a localized toast ('tuic:// links will fail to import → toast "unsupported protocol"'), and research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:283 'on failure Verge keeps last-good cached file and shows red dot + error toast'. App side: endpoints_controller.dart:100 throws UrlFetchException('HTTP ${response.statusCode} fetching URL') for any non-200 — a GitHub-hosted subscription that rate-limits returns 403 and the user sees 'HTTP 403 fetching URL' with no rate-limit explanation, even though the codebase already has GitHubRateLimitException with resetAt parsing (core/network/http_cache.dart:65-70) that this path never uses becau
findings.fix: Map fetch outcomes to localized, actionable messages: rate-limited → 'GitHub limit reached, retry at HH:MM' (reuse GitHubRateLimitException.resetAt), offline → 'No network — check connection', non-200 → 'Subscription server returned 403 — link may be expired'.

findings.title: subscription-userinfo quota/expiry headers are never parsed or shown

findings.title: No SECURITY.md for a security-sensitive VPN app despite security-first spec
findings.note: File genuinely absent (.github/ holds only workflows) — but a missing disclosure policy is a docs/compliance gap, not a broken release path like the rest of this batch.
findings.evidence: Doc claim: AGENTS.md:100 "leak tests via tcpdump/dnsleaktest.com/ipleak.net"; AGENTS.md:109 "ship without ... 7 leak tests" (never); AGENTS.md:128 "security-and-hardening → max WFP firewall, 7 leak tests". Reality: `ls .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE .github/SECURITY.md SECURITY.md ...` → "No such file or directory" for all; `gh api repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn/contents/SECURITY.md` → 404; community profile health shows codeofconduct: null, contributing: null, issue_template: null, pr_template: null.
findings.fix: Add SECURITY.md with a private reporting channel (GitHub security advisories are free on this repo), plus CONTRIBUTING.md and ISSUE_TEMPLATE/PR_TEMPLATE. For a VPN client, a published disclosure policy is the minimum expected artifact.

findings.title: MethodChannelBoxAdapter.stop() emits BoxEvent(stopped) in a finally block even when the stop timed out and was rethrown — one engine lifecycle produces conflicting terminal events
findings.fix: Move the `stopped` emission out of `finally` into the success path (and drop it on the TimeoutException/rethrow branch), so exactly one terminal event is published per stop.

findings.title: Box-start failure path never stops a half-started engine; the late 'started' event is ignored, leaving the engine running while the UI shows blocked (and permanently wedging retries on Windows)
findings.fix: In the box-start `on Object` catch, mirror the crash path: `try { await box.stop().timeout(timeouts.boxStop); } on Object { /* engine already gone */ }` before `_block(...)`. Optionally, have Tunnel react to a `started` event while in `blocked`/`disconnecting` (log a warning at minimum) instead of ignoring all non-crashed events.

findings.title: MethodChannelBoxAdapter emits a synthetic 'crashed' BoxEvent on every start failure, so Android start failures always surface as boxCrashed (never boxStartFailed) and the connect's own failure-cleanup branch becomes dead code
findings.evidence: `MethodChannelBoxAdapter.start` emits `BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.crashed, ...)` before throwing on all three failure paths (channel_adapters.dart:69, 84, 87), e.g. `on PlatformException catch (e) { _events.add(BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.crashed, e)); throw StateError(e.message ?? e.code); }`. `Tunnel._onBoxEvent` (tunnel.dart:580-596) reacts to `crashed` while `_state == connecting` by running `_epoch++; _block(TunnelBlockReason.boxCrashed);`. `_events.add` schedules listener delivery before the awaited `box.start` future in `connect` resumes, so the epoch bump wins and `connect`'s catch (`if (_stale(epoch)) { publishMetrics(); return; }` at tunnel.dart:437-440) aborts without its own `boxStartFailed
findings.fix: Remove the synthetic `_events.add(BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.crashed, e))` from `start`'s three failure paths — the thrown StateError is the failure signal; a crashed event should only represent an engine that was running and died. Alternatively, have Tunnel distinguish adapter-synthetic from engine-sourced crashes (e.g. a flag on BoxEvent).

findings.title: stop() emits stopped and clears _process even when the kill failed and the process is still alive (5s timeout path)
findings.evidence: Lines 186-196: `await _exitWait?.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5), onTimeout: () => -1); _process = null; _stderrSub?.cancel(); _stdoutSub?.cancel(); _stderrSub = null; _stdoutSub = null; await _cleanupConfig(); _events.add(const BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.stopped));` — the result of the timeout is discarded, so stop() cannot tell whether the process actually exited. If both taskkill attempts (they are best-effort inside try/catch, lines 165-179) and `process.kill()` fail, stop() still completes, clears _process, emits `stopped`, and the late exit watcher fires with `wasStopping=true` (line 95) and emits nothing. Tunnel then relaxes the firewall and reports disconnected while the engine is aliv
findings.fix: Check whether the exit actually happened: run `final exited = await _exitWait?.timeout(...);` and, when it timed out, re-kill (taskkill /F /T) and surface failure — e.g. emit BoxEvent(crashed) and keep _process set — instead of unconditionally emitting stopped and nulling _process.

findings.title: Exit watcher cancels stdout/stderr subscriptions as soon as exitCode completes, racing away the FATAL line the startup error is supposed to carry
findings.evidence: Lines 94-104: `_exitWait = process.exitCode.then<int>((code) { final wasStopping = _stopping; _process = null; _stderrSub?.cancel(); _stdoutSub?.cancel(); ... _cleanupConfig(); ...` — the exitCode future and the delivery of buffered stderr data events are independent event-loop events on Windows, so exitCode can complete while the final FATAL line is still queued on process.stderr. Cancelling the subscriptions then drops it: `feed` (lines 122-129) never sees it, `_lastErrorLine` stays null (or stale), and start()'s failure path `throw StateError(_lastErrorLine ?? 'sing-box.exe exited during startup');` (lines 133-136) reports the generic fallback while the Logs screen shows nothing about the
findings.fix: Drain before cancel: in the exit watcher, don't cancel immediately — await the stream done futures (or a short drain delay) so pending stdout/stderr lines reach feed() first, e.g. `unawaited(Future.wait([_stderrSub?.cancel() ?? Future.value(), _stdoutSub?.cancel() ?? Future.value()]))` scheduled after the pipe close events.

findings.title: _lastErrorLine is never reset in start(): a new failure can be reported with the previous run's FATAL text
findings.evidence: `_lastErrorLine` is only written in `feed` (lines 122-129: `if (line.contains('FATAL') || line.contains('ERROR')) { _lastErrorLine = line; }`) and only read in start() at line 135 (`throw StateError(_lastErrorLine ?? 'sing-box.exe exited during startup');`). start() never assigns it null. After run #1 fails with FATAL X, a later start() whose process dies without printing an ERROR/FATAL line (e.g. silent spawn-time death, or the line lost to the cancel race above) surfaces run #1's stale message as the reason for run #2's failure — misleading diagnostics for the user and for any code branching on blockReason.
findings.fix: Add `_lastErrorLine = null;` near the top of start() (e.g. right after the running-guard) so each startup failure reports only its own error output.

findings.title: Double-start guard is check-then-act across awaits: concurrent start() calls spawn two engines and orphan the first
findings.evidence: start() checks `if (_process != null) { throw StateError('box process already running'); }` (lines 64-66) and then awaits twice before setting state: `await file.writeAsString(json);` (line 76) and `process = await processFactory(...)` (line 80), with `_process = process;` only at line 90. Two overlapping start() calls both pass the guard and both spawn. The second start overwrites `_configFile` (line 78) and `_exitWait`/subscriptions; the first process is then unreachable — stop() will never kill it, its exit watcher was replaced, and its temp config file leaks (worse: if the first start's factory throws, its `_cleanupConfig()` (line 87) deletes the SECOND start's config file and nulls `_co
findings.fix: Add a synchronous in-flight flag checked/declared before the first await, e.g. `if (_starting || _process != null) throw ...; _starting = true;` at the very top of start() and clear it on every exit path (success, spawn failure, early-exit throw).

findings.title: pid-only tmp filename: concurrent writers to one file inside a single process collide on the same tmp path — second rename throws PathNotFoundException and the first writer's data is lost
findings.fix: Make the tmp name unique per write, e.g. `File('${file.path}.${pid}.${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}.tmp')` (or a static counter/Random.secure suffix), so concurrent writers in one process never share a tmp path.

findings.title: getBytes caches any HTTP 200 body without validation: a 200 HTML/error/truncated page is stored as a .srs rule-set and served as asset bytes forever
findings.evidence: http_cache.dart:77-84: `final fresh = _CacheEntry(body: response.body, etag: response.headers['etag'], fetchedAt: _now()); _memory[url] = fresh; await _writeDisk(url, fresh); return fresh.body;` — the only check is `response.statusCode != 200` (line 74); body content is never inspected. Proven empirically by driving the real HttpCache with a fake fetch returning '<html>captcha page</html>': output was 'A1 returned: <html>captcha page</html>'. Downstream, geo_asset.dart refreshAll writes those bytes: `await atomicWriteBytes(File('${cacheDir.path}/${entry.key}.srs'), bytes);` (geo_asset.dart:155-158) and ensure() prefers the cached file: `final cached = File('${cacheDir.path}/$tag.srs'); if (c
findings.fix: Validate content before caching: reject empty bodies in HttpCache, and in GeoAsset (ensure/refreshAll) verify the sing-box binary rule-set magic (first bytes 'SRS' + version 1) before writing tag.srs; treat invalid bytes like a fetch error so the stale/bundled fallback applies.

findings.title: Disk-write failure inside the try turns a successful fetch into an exception (and, for the 304/fresh paths, discards the fresh bytes from the return path)
findings.evidence: http_cache.dart:82-84: `_memory[url] = fresh; await _writeDisk(url, fresh); return fresh.body;` sits inside the try whose handler is `} on Object { if (entry != null) { return entry.body; } rethrow; }` (lines 89-94). Proven empirically with the real HttpCache pointed at an unwritable cacheDir (parent ancestor is a file) while the fetch returned HTTP 200 'FRESH-BYTES': 'B1 THREW despite HTTP 200 FRESH-BYTES (network success, write failure): PathExistsException' and then 'B2 second call returned: FRESH-BYTES (memory self-healed, calls=1)'. So with no prior entry the successfully fetched bytes are discarded from the return path (only the inconsistent memory entry survives), and with a prior ent
findings.fix: Make disk persistence best-effort so storage errors cannot mask a network result: wrap both _writeDisk calls (lines 60 and 83) in `try { ... } on Object { /* best-effort cache write */ }`, or move the write outside the try/catch that implements stale-while-revalidate.

findings.title: Endpoint URL import fetches plain-http:// subscription payloads in cleartext, leaking the most sensitive config (server list/auth tokens) to on-path observers
findings.evidence: endpoints_controller.dart:92-96: `if (maybeUrl != null && (maybeUrl.scheme == 'http' || maybeUrl.scheme == 'https') && maybeUrl.host.isNotEmpty && !trimmed.contains('\n')) { final response = await plainFetch(maybeUrl, const <String, String>{'Accept': '*/*'});`. Subscription URLs almost always embed an auth token in the query string and the payload is the user's server list — the most sensitive config in the app. Fetching over http on a censored network lets a passive observer read the token/endpoints and an active one rewrite the payload (endpoint injection -> all traffic later routed through attacker servers). The import result is persisted with `origin = maybeUrl.toString()` and re-fetched
findings.fix: Require `maybeUrl.scheme == 'https'` for URL import (reject http:// with a clear error), or keep http only for explicit private/LAN hosts; do not fetch user subscription URLs in cleartext by default.

findings.title: Crash during connect() races connect's own error path: blockReason and final state are nondeterministic (double _block; blocked can be flipped to disconnected)
findings.evidence: MethodChannelBoxAdapter.start() emits a synthetic crash AND throws: `on TimeoutException catch (e) { _events.add(BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.crashed, e)); throw StateError('box start timed out: $e'); }` (same for PlatformException at lines 86-88). The Tunnel subscribes in its constructor (`_boxSub = box.events.listen(_onBoxEvent)`), so both paths run. In connect()'s catch: `} on Object { ... if (_stale(epoch)) { publishMetrics(); return; } publishMetrics(); await _block(TunnelBlockReason.boxStartFailed); return; }`. _onBoxEvent for kind crashed while connecting does `_epoch++; _block(TunnelBlockReason.boxCrashed);`. The two _block calls race on the event loop: whichever runs second overwrites bloc
findings.fix: Pick one owner per failure: have the adapter throw without emitting a crashed event (the throw already maps to a _block), or have Tunnel's catch check `if (_state == TunnelState.blocked) return;` before _block(boxStartFailed). Additionally make disconnect() a no-op for the blocked phase (see related finding) so the stale-path teardown cannot flip b

findings.title: ProfileConfigSource resolve cache can serve a stale config after external store changes (backup restore) when the fingerprint collides by shape
findings.evidence: `final hit = _resolved[tag]; if (hit != null && hit.fingerprint == fingerprint) { _cacheHits++; return TypedConfig(tag: tag, json: _deepCopy(hit.json), ...) }` where the fingerprint is `json.encode([for (final item in stored) item.toJson()])` — the full endpoint list is embedded, so content changes DO invalidate. But the policy fingerprint is `final groups = policy?.toJsonString() ?? '';` while ruleDoc is `json.encode(rules.toJson())` and split is `'${allowMode ?? '-'}=${(packages ?? const <String>{}).join(',')}'`. If the stored document and in-memory read() ever disagree — e.g. backup import writes the store file externally and the controller state was flushed but ProfileConfigSource reads
findings.fix: Include a content hash of the resolved inputs rather than trusting shape strings, or version the cache key with the store files' (path, mtime, length); on backup import, call ProfileConfigSource.resetCacheStats() alongside flushPendingWrites.

findings.title: selected_endpoint reports a deadTag for a legitimate resolution order: a selector group with a dead defaultMember but a live members.first surfaces a false 'fell back' warning
findings.evidence: `final candidates = <String?>[ if (group.isUrlTest) group.tag, group.defaultMember, if (group.members.isNotEmpty) group.members.first ];` then `for (final tag in candidates) { if (tag == null || tag.isEmpty) continue; if (tag == 'DIRECT' || liveTags.contains(tag)) { return SelectedEndpoint(tag: tag, source: 'group'); } deadTag ??= tag; }`. For a selector group whose `defaultMember` is dead ('ghost-tag') but whose members.first is live, the loop sets `deadTag ??= 'ghost-tag'`, then returns on members.first with `SelectedEndpoint(tag: members.first, deadTag: 'ghost-tag')`. That is the documented resolution order (defaultMember tried, then first member) — the user never 'fell back', yet home.da
findings.fix: Reset deadTag when a later candidate resolves: `if (tag == 'DIRECT' || liveTags.contains(tag)) { return SelectedEndpoint(tag: tag, source: 'group', deadTag: deadTag); }` is fine, but only report deadTag when it was the tag that determined the outcome — i.e. clear `deadTag = null` whenever the returned tag came from the same group's higher-priority

findings.title: selected_endpoint hardcodes 'BLOCK' as a live connectable tag; tapping connect on it silently starts a full tunnel session that routes everything to reject
findings.evidence: `final liveTags = <String>{...endpoints.map((e) => e.tag), 'DIRECT', 'BLOCK'};` makes the pseudo-tag 'BLOCK' selectable by the home PowerTile, which calls `notifier.connect(ref.read(selectedEndpointProvider).tag)` unconditionally. Tunnel.connect runs its full guarded sequence (permission, foreground service, config resolve, box.start, firewall.enforce) and transitions to TunnelState.connected with no engine-side reject outbound emitted — the routing compiler maps BLOCK to a per-rule reject *action* (routing_compiler.dart:306-307: "1.14-native reject action; no BLOCK outbound tag needed"), so a config selected this way has `route.final = PROXY` and normal egress, or blocks all traffic only if
findings.fix: Exclude 'BLOCK' from selectable connect tags: `final liveTags = <String>{...endpoints.map((e) => e.tag), 'DIRECT'};` and let the selected-endpoint provider fall through to the next candidate when a group's resolved tag is BLOCK (or have Tunnel.connect reject tag == 'BLOCK' with a blocked state instead of starting the engine).

findings.title: disconnect() short-circuits on TunnelState.disconnected only: calling disconnect while blocked (e.g. after boxCrashed/boxStartFailed) is a silent no-op even though the UI offers Disconnect
findings.evidence: `Future<void> disconnect() async { if (_state == TunnelState.disconnected) { return; } ... }` — the guard does not treat TunnelState.blocked as disconnectable. The blocked phase is entered via _block() for vpnPermissionDenied/airplaneMode/torDown/boxStartFailed/boxCrashed, and home.dart's PowerTile renders Disconnect for every non-connecting phase: `if (connected) { await notifier.disconnect(); } else { await notifier.connect(...) }` — for blocked, `connected` is false so the else branch runs, but even a direct disconnect() call returns immediately because state is blocked, not disconnected. The firewall flag _firewallEnforced (set true by _block) also stays set. The only exits are a new con
findings.fix: Give disconnect() an explicit blocked branch: `if (_state == TunnelState.disconnected) return; if (_state == TunnelState.blocked) { _firewallEnforced cleanup + _setState(TunnelState.disconnected); return; }` — or relax the firewall and reset the flag before returning so the kill-switch bookkeeping does not outlive the blocked phase.

findings.title: ShadowsocksUriParser ignores the query string entirely: SIP002 `?plugin=` links hard-fail (no slash) or silently drop plugin/plugin_opts (with slash)
findings.evidence: parsers.dart:720-722: `final slash = body.indexOf('/'); if (slash >= 0) { body = body.substring(0, slash); }` — the query is never separated, so for `ss://…@1.2.3.4:8388?plugin=obfs-local;obfs=http;obfs-host=www.example.com` (no path slash) hostPort becomes `1.2.3.4:8388?plugin=…` and `intOf(hostPort.substring(split + 1), 'ss port')` (line 736) throws on `8388?plugin=…` → verified: the line fails, single-line import throws 'no share links parsed (1 malformed lines)'. When a `/` IS present (verified AL2), the link parses but `plugin=null pluginOpts=null` — ShadowsocksEndpoint.plugin/pluginOpts are never populated from the query anywhere. Also `body.indexOf('/')` can truncate the base64 userin
findings.fix: Find `@` first, split `hostPort` at `?` before parsing the port, and parse `Uri.parse('ss://$body').queryParameters` (safe once base64 is out of the host position) to fill `plugin` / `pluginOpts` (split plugin value on ';' into k=v pairs like _parsePluginOpts).

findings.title: No port range validation anywhere: negative (`:-1`) and oversized (99999) ports are stored and emitted, FATALing the whole engine profile at start
findings.evidence: `final port = uri.port == 0 ? 443 : uri.port;` appears in VlessUriParser (625), SshUriParser (591), TrojanUriParser (~806), Hysteria2UriParser (836), TuicUriParser (~868); Dart parses `vless://u@h:-1` to port -1 (verified: probe prints port=-1, stored as VmessEndpoint.port=-1; same for trojan). ss/vmess use `intOf(...)`/`intField` with no range check: `ss://…@1.2.3.4:99999` stores port 99999, vmess JSON `"port":-5` stores -5 (verified). Emitted configs were checked with the real engine: `windows/sing-box.exe check` → `FATAL decode config: outbounds[0].server_port: json: cannot unmarshal number -1 into Go struct field VLESSOutboundOptions.ServerOptions.server_port of type uint16` (same FATAL
findings.fix: Add a shared helper `int portOf(int raw, String what)` that throws FormatException outside 1..65535 and use it in every URI parser (replacing `uri.port == 0 ? N : uri.port`) and in the intOf/intField port call sites.

findings.title: vless links with `security=none` are emitted with TLS forced on — parsed `security` field is never consulted by the emitter
findings.evidence:
Parser stores the field: parsers.dart:633 `security: query['security'],` but endpoint_outbound.dart:38-49 `_vless` always emits:
```dart
'tls': _tls(
  enabled: true,
  serverName: e.sni ?? e.address,
  ...
```
Verified: `vless://uuid@h:80?type=tcp&security=none#plainvless` → outbound `tls: {enabled: true, server_name: h}`. A client dialing TLS against a plaintext vless server (the explicit meaning of security=none in the Xray URI spec) fails the handshake — the imported node is dead with no import-time warning. (The sing-box JSON path gates on `tls?['enabled']` correctly; only the URI path forces it.)
findings.fix: In `_vless`, gate the tls block: emit it only when `e.security == 'tls' || e.security == 'reality' || e.realityPublicKey != null || e.echEnabled` (pass `enabled` through to `_tls`).

findings.title: Base64-wrapped sing-box JSON / clash YAML subscriptions fail: after _shareLines unwraps, the decoded text is fed only to parseShareLines, never re-sniffed
findings.evidence: ingestion_adapter.dart:111-112: `final lines = _shareLines(source); return parseShareLines(lines);` — _shareLines unwraps one base64 level but the decoded text only ever reaches _parseOne (scheme sniff). Verified: `base64(<{"outbounds":[{"type":"vless",…}]}}>)` → throws `FormatException: no share links parsed (1 malformed lines)` (the unwrapped JSON line hits `unsupported scheme ""`). Same for base64-wrapped clash YAML or WG INI. The class doc claims base64-bundle support generically; only base64-of-share-lines works. v2rayN-style sub providers that wrap a sing-box/clash config in base64 are unusable.
findings.fix: After a successful base64 unwrap in `_shareLines`, feed the decoded text back through the format sniffers (e.g. make `_parse` take a `allowUnwrap` flag and recurse once on the decoded payload instead of falling straight to parseShareLines).

findings.title: Android installUpdate channel opens an attacker-influenceable remote URI directly via ACTION_VIEW — no FileProvider, no download stage, no scheme validation
findings.evidence: _install on Android sends `{'url': info.assetUrl}` over the 'vpn_service' channel and the comment claims 'FileProvider ACTION_VIEW intent is the Play-safe install path; the platform service lands with the release todo', but VpnServiceBridge.kt does `Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url))` with no scheme allowlist and no DownloadManager/FileProvider stage. The intent is dispatched to whatever app registers the URL (browser or any handler); the download happens entirely outside the app's control (no TLS pinning, no hash, no REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES gate in-app). The install step is exactly where hash verification belongs, and it does not exist. (No file is written by the app, so no local f
findings.fix: Implement the promised platform service: download via DownloadManager/HTTPS to app storage, verify SHA-256 against the signed manifest, then open the downloaded file through FileProvider with the APK installer intent.

findings.title: Envelope header (magic/version/kdf params) is not AEAD-associated data; cipher field never even read on decrypt
findings.evidence: `final box = await AesGcm.with256bits().encrypt(bytes, secretKey: key);` — no `aad` parameter (package:cryptography 2.9.0 defaults `aad = const <int>[]`, verified in cipher.dart:297). The same-password secret key is thus not committed to magic/version/kdf metadata: an attacker who can modify a backup file can transplant the whole (salt, nonce, mac, ciphertext) quartet from any other backup encrypted with the same password and it decrypts silently as if it were the local file. `_decryptEnvelope` also reads `kdf['salt'] as String` (line 230) from this unauthenticated header. Practical impact today is bounded — memoryKiB/iterations/parallelism are code constants (lines 47-49), version pinned to
findings.fix: Pass `aad: utf8.encode(jsonEncode({'magic': magic, 'version': version, 'kdf': <String,dynamic>{'algo':'argon2id','memoryKiB':kdfMemoryKiB,'iterations':kdfIterations,'parallelism':kdfParallelism}}))` to both encrypt and decrypt, and bind a format identifier. If a future version ever reads kdf params from the envelope, AAD becomes mandatory, not opti

findings.title: Backup protects the export file, but the secrets it restores live plaintext on disk (documented known debt) with no ACL hardening and a systemTemp fallback
findings.evidence: Docstring line 23-24: "the payload is 100% credentials-bearing (WG private keys, preshared keys, every protocol uuid/password — stores keep them plaintext at rest today)". endpoint_store.dart:60-62: `File(baseDir != null ? '$baseDir/endpoints.json' : '${Platform.environment['HOME'] ?? Platform.environment['USERPROFILE'] ?? Directory.systemTemp.path}/.qanatvpn/endpoints.json')` — grep confirms no chmod/ACL hardening anywhere (only VPN-permission matches). Every store the backup reads/restores keeps WG private keys and protocol passwords in world-default-ACL JSON in the user profile; if HOME and USERPROFILE are both unset, plaintext credentials land under Directory.systemTemp. The encrypted env
findings.fix: Encrypt the stores at rest with an OS-keychain-derived key (Windows DPAPI / Android Keystore), or at minimum set restrictive file ACLs on ~/.qanatvpn and drop the systemTemp fallback to a hard failure.

findings.title: Release signing chain is dead: CI writes key.properties but no Gradle code reads it; releases always debug-signed
findings.evidence: android/app/build.gradle.kts:33 — `signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug")` (with the template TODO comment). .github/workflows/build-android.yml:82-88 — `echo "$KEYSTORE_BASE64" | base64 -d > android/app/upload-keystore.jks; cat > android/key.properties <<EOF ...` runs when secrets are present, but a full read of build.gradle.kts shows NO signingConfigs block and NO reference to key.properties, so the written file is dead and `flutter build apk --release` keeps debug-signing. tasks/handoff.md:32 documents this as done-adjacent: "release currently debug-signs — set the 4 GitHub secrets (`KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `STORE_PASSWORD`, `KEY_ALIAS`, `KEY_PASSWORD`) ...; Gradle already reads `key
findings.fix: Add a signingConfigs block in build.gradle.kts that loads android/key.properties (or fail the release build when HAS_KEYSTORE != 'true' in CI); after enabling, publish the cert fingerprint (plan.md's `e9fe39...`) in README/latest.json metadata and enforce it in the updater or install docs.

findings.title: No credential redaction in engine log pipeline; raw FATAL/ERROR engine lines (potentially containing endpoint keys/passwords) reach the UI
findings.evidence: lib/modules/logs/log_bus.dart:33-47 — `void add(EngineLogLine line) { var message = line.message; if (message.length > maxLineLength) { message = message.substring(0, maxLineLength); } ...` — only truncation and repeat collapsing; no masking. lib/core/services/windows_box_process.dart:113-135 — `if (line.contains('FATAL') || line.contains('ERROR')) { _lastErrorLine = line; } ... throw StateError(_lastErrorLine ?? 'sing-box.exe exited during startup');` — raw engine output (which for config errors echoes endpoint JSON: WG/AWG private_key, SSH passwords, SS2022 passwords) is surfaced to the UI/diagnostics unmasked. The repo's own review recorded the gap: tasks/review-swarm-full.md:247 — "no re
findings.fix: Add a shared maskSecrets() pass (regex over `private_key`, `password`, `auth`, `obfs_password`, `token`, base64/PEM blocks) applied in LogBus.add() and before StateError is thrown from windows_box_process; add a test that a log line containing an AWG private_key renders masked.

findings.title: BoxEngine writes raw engine FATAL lines and boxStart exception text (which contains key material) to Android logcat
findings.evidence: BoxEngine.kt:141 'Log.e(TAG, "engine fatal: $message")' and BoxEngine.kt:99 'Log.e(TAG, "box start failed", e)'. The same Go error string that the probe showed (containing 'private_key=<hex of key>') is the message of the FATAL log entry on Android and the exception message from startOrReloadService at start failure — both are written to logcat. Logcat persists in system ring buffers, is included in adb bugreport output, and is readable over USB debugging. decisions.tsv row 51 confirms the design ('Kotlin writeLogs forwards every line') with no redaction step anywhere in lib/ or Kotlin (grep for redact/scrub/mask/sanitiz: zero hits).
findings.fix: Redact before Log.e in Kotlin (same scrub rules as the Dart LogBus) or log only the first line / a level tag and keep the full line on the Dart side post-redaction. Never log exception e that may embed engine config payloads unredacted.

findings.title: Logs 'export' prints the entire visible log buffer to the platform console (logcat on Android) instead of the clipboard as the code comment claims
findings.evidence: logs_screen.dart:240-242: "print('--- qanatvpn log export (${visible.length} lines) ---'); print(buffer.toString());" — the comment above (lines 232-235) says 'copy the visible lines to a buffer the user pastes into a bug report', but there is no Clipboard.setData anywhere (grep for Clipboard in lib/: zero matches). On Android, Dart print lands in logcat; the buffer holds up to 2000 lines x up to 4096 chars from the shared LogBus, which the probe proved can contain 'private_key=<hex>' on key-setup failures. The intended bug-report flow therefore (a) does not reach the clipboard at all and (b) pushes the full log, secrets included, into the system log that users then attach to issues.
findings.fix: Replace the print calls with Clipboard.setData(ClipboardData(text: buffer.toString())) so the content goes only where the user intends; rely on the LogBus redaction pass so nothing secret ever reaches the buffer in the first place.

findings.title: No FLAG_SECURE / screen-capture guard anywhere in the Android app while the Logs tab can display key material
findings.evidence: grep for 'FLAG_SECURE|setFlags|snapshot' across android Kotlin sources and lib/ returns only unrelated Dart 'snapshot' hits; AndroidManifest.xml declares no secure flag and MainActivity never calls window.setFlags. The Logs screen renders every engine line via SelectableText, and the engine probe showed the FATAL path places 'private_key=73656372657431323334353637383930' (raw key hex) directly in a rendered line. Screen recorders, assistant screenshots, and the recent-apps task switcher capture it without any OS restriction.
findings.fix: Set FLAG_SECURE when the Logs tab is the active route (clear on leave) — e.g. via a MethodChannel call from LogsScreen's lifecycle observer — or apply it app-wide as a VPN-app baseline.

findings.title: Windows adapter writes the full engine config (private keys, passwords, UUIDs, PSKs) as plaintext JSON to %TEMP% for the whole engine session; crash/kill leaves credentials on disk
findings.evidence: windows_box_process.dart:72-75: "File('${Directory.systemTemp.path}/qanatvpn_box_${DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch}.json') ... await file.writeAsString(json);" where json is jsonEncode(config.json) — the assembled config containing WG/AWG private keys, vless/trojan uuid+password, PSKs. The file exists for the whole engine run and _cleanupConfig is best-effort: line 205 comment states 'Temp file leak is acceptable; system temp cleans up.' If the app process dies (crash, kill, power loss) the deletion never runs, and Windows does not auto-clean %TEMP%; stale files from prior runs are never swept. Any same-user process (or malware) can read the key material for an unbounded period.
findings.fix: Write the config into the app's own data directory (not shared %TEMP%), sweep stale qanatvpn_box_*.json files on each start, and treat deletion failure as loud (log+retry) rather than 'acceptable'; if the engine supports it, prefer a pipe/stdin hand-off over a file at all.

findings.title: plainFetch keeps Dart's default auto-follow of up to 5 cross-origin redirects (https to http downgrade included); redirect hops are invisible to the cache and subscription layers, so a 302 on any pinned URL silently swaps the cached body
findings.evidence: plain_fetch.dart:8-12 sets only `connectionTimeout`; followRedirects stays true (Dart SDK http_impl.dart:1491-1493: `bool _followRedirects = true; int _maxRedirects = 5;`) and _handleIncoming auto-follows: "if (followRedirects && response.isRedirect) { if (response.redirects.length < maxRedirects) { future = response.drain().then<HttpClientResponse>((_) => response.redirect());". `_openUrl` accepts any http/https target (http_impl.dart: "if (... !uri.isScheme("http") && !uri.isScheme("https")) throw"), so https->http downgrades and cross-host hops both execute invisibly. Every redirect response is consumed by drain() and never reaches plainFetch's return, so HttpCache caches the final attack
findings.fix: Set request.followRedirects = false in plainFetch and either fail on 3xx or expose the Location for an allowlist check (scheme https, expected host), so the cache layer can attribute bodies to the real origin.

findings.title: HTTP cache persists fetched bodies (including endpoint subscription payloads with private keys) as plaintext world-readable files, and can land in a shared system temp dir
