findings.evidence: http_cache.dart:132-135: "await atomicWriteString(File('${dir.path}/$key.meta.json'), jsonEncode(...'fetchedAt'...)); await atomicWriteBytes(File('${dir.path}/$key.body'), entry.body);" — no FileMode/permissions restriction and no encryption; the .body may hold full subscription payloads with WG private keys (see importer finding). The cache directory on Windows comes from main.dart:146-149: "final home = Platform.environment['HOME'] ?? Platform.environment['USERPROFILE'] ?? Directory.systemTemp.path; ... cacheDir: Directory('$home/.qanatvpn/geo/http')" — the Directory.systemTemp.path fallback resolves to C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp (TMP/TEMP env), a writable, commonly world-readable p
findings.fix: Never fall back to Directory.systemTemp for the cache root; prefer the app-support dir. Delete .body files when entries expire instead of retaining stale bytes indefinitely, and exclude secret-bearing subscription fetches from disk caching (memory-only), or reuse the existing BackupService crypto envelope for them.

findings.title: WgIniParser accepts garbage/oversized keys, MTU and AWG values verbatim; engine FATALs at connect with no import-time validation
findings.evidence:
Reproduced with repo code: WgIniParser on `[Interface]
PrivateKey = not-a-real-key
Address = 10.0.0.2/32
[Peer]...` -> `wg: privateKey="not-a-real-key" accepted (len 14)`. parsers.dart:1006 only checks presence: `if (privateKey == null) { throw const FormatException('wg ini: missing PrivateKey'); }`. wireGuardEndpointToJson (awg_config.dart:180-188) emits `'private_key': endpoint.privateKey` verbatim. Real engine: `FATAL initialize endpoint[0]: decode private key: illegal base64 data at input byte 3`. The project's own AwgConfig.validate() (44-char base64 check, awg_config.dart:216-227) is never applied to imported endpoints - ProfileConfigSource._merged ships wireGuardEndpointToJson outp
findings.fix: Validate imported WG/AWG material at ingestion: private/public/preshared keys must be 44-char base64 (reuse AwgConfig._validateKey), peer endpoint must parse as host:port; reject the endpoint (or whole file) with a clear FormatException at import time.

findings.title: allowInsecure/insecure/skip-cert-verify from share links silently disable TLS verification with no user-visible warning
findings.evidence: parsers.dart:806 `allowInsecure: boolOf(query['allowInsecure'])` (trojan) and :848 `insecure: boolOf(query['insecure'])` (hysteria2); clash `skip-cert-verify` at :186/:203. endpoint_outbound.dart:190 emits `if (insecure) 'insecure': true`. Verified the engine accepts it: `sing-box check` on a trojan outbound with `"insecure": true` exits 0 (FATAL only when server_name is empty AND insecure is false). Nothing in the ingestion path or the endpoints UI (no grep hits outside ingestion/) marks or warns on insecure=true, so a subscription link quietly downgrades the user's TLS verification to none - a subscription-driven MITM downgrade that persists invisibly in the profile.
findings.fix: Surface insecure=true in the endpoint list/tile with a warning badge and a confirmation on import (or force the user to re-enable it manually after import); never let a pasted link silently disable certificate verification.

findings.title: Content sniffing: any line matching ^\s*\[Interface\] (even inside an encoded fragment) routes the whole bundle to WgIniParser, discarding all valid share links
findings.evidence: ingestion_adapter.dart:158-159 `bool _looksLikeWgIni(String source) => RegExp(r'^\s*\[Interface\]', multiLine: true).hasMatch(source);` runs before share-link parsing (:101-102). Reproduced: valid bundle `trojan://pw@1.2.3.4:443#good\n[Interface]\n` -> `bundle: FormatException: wg ini: missing PrivateKey` - all valid trojan links are discarded because one stray line matched the sniff. Even encoded payloads trigger it: fragment `#good%0A%5BInterface%5D` (containing encoded `[Interface]`) matched after line splitting, routing the bundle to WgIniParser. A subscription provider (or anyone in position to alter the feed) can force this to make every subsequent import fail, or mix it into an otherw
findings.fix: Require WG-INI shape before committing to that parser: first non-comment line matches `^\[Interface\]$` AND a `PrivateKey =` line is present; otherwise fall through to share-line parsing. Alternatively parse share links first and only fall back to INI when zero links parsed.

findings.title: Clash-YAML sniff short-circuits share-link parsing: a `proxies:` line makes share links in the same payload invisible
findings.evidence: ingestion_adapter.dart:148-155: any text matching `^\s*(proxies|listeners)\s*:` (multiline) routes the entire payload to ClashYamlParser. Reproduced: subscription containing just `proxies:\n` -> `yaml-only: parsed 0`, then importText throws 'no endpoints found in input' (endpoints_controller.dart:130). ClashYamlParser.parse silently skips every proxy entry whose fields are missing (stringField throws inside _proxy per typed entry, and non-YamlMap nodes are skipped at :111 `if (node is YamlMap)`), so a real-world stripped feed with a `proxies:` line yields zero endpoints even when valid share links coexist in the same payload - the user sees 'no endpoints found' with no hint that share links
findings.fix: Attempt share-link extraction as a fallback when ClashYamlParser returns an empty list, and include per-format parse counts in the error message ('0 endpoints from 12 lines; yaml parse skipped N').

findings.title: Deeply nested YAML freezes the main isolate for seconds and escapes as StackOverflowError (no size/depth guard before loadYamlDocument)
findings.evidence: parsers.dart:107 `yamlDoc = loadYamlDocument(source);` has no depth/size guard and loadYamlDocument is recursive-descent. Reproduced with the repo's parser code: input `proxies: ` + 29000 nested `[` (58,010 bytes, i.e. below endpoints_controller.dart:116's `bytes.length > 64 * 1024` isolate threshold, so it runs on the UI isolate) -> `deep60k StackOverflowError after 6621ms`. A 100KB payload -> `deep StackOverflowError after 20989ms`. Two impacts: (1) multi-second main-isolate freeze of the whole app from one paste/URL import; (2) StackOverflowError is an Error, not a FormatException, so it escapes parseShareLines' `on FormatException` and is only saved by importText's broad `on Object catch
findings.fix: Cap YAML ingestion: reject payloads > ~256KB before loadYamlDocument, run the YAML branch always inside parseInIsolate (drop the 64KB heuristic for the yaml branch), and add a flow-nesting depth limit (count '[' while scanning, reject > 1000) before handing to the yaml package.

findings.title: URL import fetch has no response size cap and quadratic buffering: unbounded memory use from a hostile subscription URL
findings.evidence: plain_fetch.dart:14-16 `final body = await response.fold<List<int>>(<int>[], (acc, chunk) => acc..addAll(chunk));` - no cap and quadratic append; importText (endpoints_controller.dart:96-110) then does `utf8.decode(response.body, allowMalformed: true)` and `utf8.encode(payload)` - a hostile subscription URL behind a 200 response (the only status checked) can stream gigabytes: ~1x in the fold list, ~2x as a UTF-16 Dart String, +1x on re-encode, plus quadratic fold cost. connectionTimeout (15s) limits connect, not body size. Memory exhaustion is reachable by any URL the user pastes.
findings.fix: Enforce a max body size in plainFetch for imports (e.g. 10MB, matching the isolate threshold's purpose): abort the subscription when accumulated length exceeds the cap and throw UrlFetchException; use BytesBuilder instead of fold+addAll to avoid quadratic copies.

findings.title: stop() kills by bare PID lookup (taskkill /PID n) — PID-reuse race can terminate an unrelated process, and 'taskkill' itself is resolved through PATH
findings.evidence: final result = await Process.run('taskkill', <String>['/PID', process.pid.toString()]); ... await Process.run('taskkill', <String>['/F', '/PID', process.pid.toString()]); — (1) process.pid was read at spawn time; if sing-box.exe exits and Windows reuses the PID for an unrelated process before taskkill runs, a graceful WM_CLOSE (and, if it still 'fails', a force-kill) is delivered to that unrelated process, e.g. the user's editor or another security tool. (2) Process.run('taskkill', ...) resolves taskkill via PATH search; a user-writable PATH entry can shadow System32\taskkill.exe. (3) the backstop process.kill() is only reached when taskkill returns non-zero, but taskkill can also fail benig
findings.fix: Kill by retained process handle, not by PID lookup: call process.kill() first, use OpenProcess(PROCESS_TERMINATE) + TerminateProcess on a freshly-opened handle (guarding against reuse), or eliminate the race entirely with the Job Object kill-on-close; invoke taskkill by absolute path (C:\Windows\System32\taskkill.exe) if kept at all.

findings.title: DLL search-order exposure for wintun.dll: sing-box.exe LoadLibrary's wintun.dll from its exe directory, which is not vendored, not hash-pinned, and windows/wintun.dll is not even gitignored
findings.evidence: The exe loads 'wintun.dll' dynamically (binary strings: 'wintun.dll' + 'golang.zx2c4.com/wintun.(*lazyDLL).Load' + import table 'wintun.dll\0WintunAllocateSendPacket\0WintunCreateAdapter...'; the 6 embedded PE blobs found are gVisor netstack data, not a bundled driver), so at TUN-open time sing-box.exe resolves wintun.dll from its own directory first (windows/ next to the app in the CI zip: build-windows.yml:56 'Copy-Item windows/sing-box.exe "$dir/sing-box.exe"'). There is no wintun.dll in the repo, no integrity pinning, and .gitignore:36 covers only 'windows/sing-box.exe' — so a developer or packager who drops a wintun.dll to 'fix' a startup error silently makes a security-critical DLL the
findings.fix: Ship wintun.dll explicitly from a pinned, hash-verified source (or bundle and load it from a driver store path), record its SHA-256 in THIRD_PARTY/CI and verify at startup or packaging time; add windows/wintun.dll to .gitignore now so it can never be accidentally committed.

findings.title: No OS-level fail-closed kill-switch: TUN established with setBlocking(false) and engine-death reverts traffic to the physical network
findings.evidence: `builder.setBlocking(false)` in PlatformInterfaceWrapper.openTun (BoxEngine.kt:257), and the repo itself admits the gap in main.dart:184-187: "Platform note: a true OS-level fail-closed filter (device-wide block-all except the tunnel, surviving engine death) needs native code that does not exist yet on either platform — Android VpnService setBlocking(true) + addRoute(0.0.0.0/0) lockdown in QanatVpnService. Until those land, the engine rule ordering below is the kill-switch". The PolicyFirewallAdapter 'enforce' only validates config ordering (`_policy.validateOrdering(...)`) — it performs no OS-level action. QanatVpnService.onStartCommand returns START_NOT_STICKY. Net effect: on engine FATAL cr
findings.fix: Call builder.setBlocking(true) (fail-closed fd behavior, API 29+), keep 0.0.0.0/0 + ::/0 routes while connected, and implement crash-path lockdown in QanatVpnService (block-all until engine restarts); document/direct users to always-on VPN + 'Block connections without VPN'.

findings.title: Backup/restore participation left at defaults while VPN secrets persist as plaintext JSON outside the proper app files dir
findings.evidence: Application tag declares only label/name/icon (lines 10-13) — no android:allowBackup, no android:dataExtractionRules, no android:fullBackupContent, and android/app/src contains no backup-rule XML (verified via file listing). allowBackup therefore defaults to true. Meanwhile the secret store is plaintext JSON, not the Keystore-backed flutter_secure_storage that pubspec.yaml declares (^11.0.0) but which has ZERO usages in lib/ (grep: 0 matches). decisions.tsv row 80 states: "endpoints.json holds WG private keys + every protocol secret in plaintext". EndpointStore._file() resolves to `Platform.environment['HOME'] ?? Platform.environment['USERPROFILE'] ?? Directory.systemTemp.path` + '/.qanatvpn/
findings.fix: Set android:allowBackup="false" (or dataExtractionRules excluding all secret stores), resolve Android storage through getApplicationSupportDirectory instead of HOME/USERPROFILE/systemTemp, and migrate secret material into flutter_secure_storage (already a dependency).

findings.title: installUpdate opens an arbitrary URL via ACTION_VIEW with no scheme/host validation
findings.evidence: "installUpdate" handler: `val url = call.argument<String>("url") ... activity.startActivity(Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url)))` (VpnServiceBridge.kt:101-112) — no https/scheme/host validation. The url flows from UpdateInfo.assetUrl, which on the mirror path is taken verbatim from the gh-pages latest.json: `assetUrl: entry['url'] as String? ?? ''` (updater.dart:201). Today the callers are internal and both sources are https constants, so this is defense-in-depth rather than an open hole — but any future writer of UpdateStore/mirror JSON (or a compromised gh-pages branch) can point the user's browser to an arbitrary http:// APK download with a single JSON field, and the platform side
findings.fix: Validate the URL before launching: require https scheme and pin the host to github.com/qmahyar.github.io (reject otherwise); keep the scheme check on both Dart and Kotlin sides.

findings.title: FirewallPolicy.baseRules emits outbound:"BLOCK" referencing a nonexistent outbound — contradicts the project's own probed 1.14 decision and blocks only via the router error path
findings.evidence: baseRules emits `{'ip_cidr': <String>['::/0'], 'outbound': 'BLOCK'}` (and the same for RFC1918) with no BLOCK outbound defined in any config. docs/decisions.tsv already probed this: "1.14 deprecates block outbound; check cannot catch dangling tag refs (probe)" → "compiler emits action: reject". Probe on the repo's windows/sing-box.exe confirms: `sing-box check` returns 0 for a config with such rules, but at runtime every matching connection logs `ERROR[0001] [...] router: outbound not found: BLOCK` and dies on the error path (v6 CONNECT via mixed proxy: listener hits=0 + that exact log line). Blocks only work as a side effect of the router error path; a future engine that falls back to `fina
findings.fix: Emit `action: reject` for the ::/0 and RFC1918 rules (same as RoutingCompiler already does per decisions.tsv) instead of `outbound: 'BLOCK'`.

findings.title: Connect-time "fail-closed" firewall gate validates a constant, never the config actually shipped to the engine
findings.evidence: main.dart:200: `final errors = _policy.validateOrdering(_policy.baseRules());` — it feeds the policy's own hardcoded, by-construction-hijack-first list back into the validator, so it can never fail. The doc comment above (main.dart:184-188) claims "the vendored profile and every assembled config are checked for the hijack-first ordering before the engine is allowed to carry traffic" — no code passes the resolved config (Tunnel connect's configSource.resolve(tag) output, or the merged vendored profile) to the firewall; FirewallAdapter.enforce() takes no argument (tunnel.dart:103-108). A profile whose rules lack hijack-dns or put proxy rules first would connect unimpeded. tests only ever valid
findings.fix: Change FirewallAdapter.enforce(List<Map<String,dynamic>> routeRules) and have Tunnel.connect pass the resolved config's route.rules; fail the connect (StateError) when validateOrdering reports violations, so the gate actually guards the artifact that ships.

findings.title: 10 of 18 direct dependencies are entirely unused (zero imports in lib/ or tests), yet their native plugin code still compiles into the shipped APK — including an unused secret-storage plugin and an unused SQLite plugin
findings.evidence: pubspec.yaml declares 18 direct hosted deps; repo-wide grep for `package:<name>/` imports across lib/, test/, integration_test/ finds ZERO files for: material_3_expressive (line 18, comment claims "full 45 M3E widget set"), material_ui (19), cue (20), drift (23), drift_flutter (24), flutter_secure_storage (25), http (26), flutter_cache_manager (27), fl_chart (30), flutter_foreground_task (31) — 10 of 18. The app instead hand-rolls `dart:io` HttpClient (lib/core/network/plain_fetch.dart:9 `final client = HttpClient()..connectionTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 15);`) and file persistence (lib/core/persistence/atomic_write.dart). Because Flutter registers every plugin in the dependency closur
findings.fix: Remove material_3_expressive, material_ui, cue, drift, drift_flutter, flutter_secure_storage, http, flutter_cache_manager, fl_chart, flutter_foreground_task (and drift_dev/build_runner if codegen is not used) from pubspec.yaml, run `dart pub get` to re-lock, and confirm GeneratedPluginRegistrant.java only registers actually-used plugins.

findings.title: CI publishes sha256-android.json / sha256-windows.json but no code in the repo ever verifies them — update artifacts are downloaded with zero integrity verification beyond TLS
findings.evidence: build-windows.yml:59 writes `@{ "qanatvpn_v${v}_windows-x64.zip" = $hash } | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content sha256-windows.json` and build-android.yml:112 `sha256sum "$name" >> sha256-android.json`; both files are attached to the public release. But `grep -rn "sha256|checksum|digest" lib/ --include="*.dart"` returns zero matches outside comments: UpdateFetcher._fromApi / _fromMirror build UpdateInfo straight from asset["browser_download_url"] with no integrity check, and there is no artifact signing (cosign/minisign/jarsigner metadata) anywhere in the pipeline. The published manifests create a false verification story; actual integrity rests entirely on GitHub TLS and repo write access. Combine
findings.fix: Either verify the release-attached sha256 in-app before exposing 'Update available' (or at install time), or drop the manifests; longer term sign artifacts (minisign/cosign with a pinned public key) and verify the signature client-side.

findings.title: All third-party actions pinned by mutable tags, not commit SHAs — softprops/action-gh-release@v2 executes at the release moment holding contents:write, and flutter-action/setup-android run inside every build
findings.evidence: All 17 `uses:` entries are mutable tag refs; the third-party ones are build-android.yml:24 / build-windows.yml:19 `uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2`, build-android.yml:44 `uses: android-actions/setup-android@v3`, and build-android.yml:116 / build-windows.yml:62 `uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2` — the latter runs with `permissions: contents: write` and attaches the release assets. A retargeted v2 tag on any of these is arbitrary code execution in the release job: it can tamper the shipped sing-box.exe/APKs, rewrite latest.json, and, in build-android, the real keystore was already decoded to android/app/upload-keystore.jks on the runner (build-android.yml:82) — exfiltratable by the action
findings.fix: Pin every action to a full-length commit SHA (esp. softprops/action-gh-release), add dependabot.yml with the github-actions package-ecosystem, and set persist-credentials: false on checkout where the token is not needed.

findings.title: SPEC/goal promise flutter_secure_storage and 'encrypted secrets' with OS keystore (Android Keystore / DPAPI); zero usage anywhere — the claimed control does not exist
findings.evidence: SPEC.md:37 stack row: "flutter_riverpod 2.0 + go_router + drift + flutter_secure_storage + flutter_cache_manager"; SPEC.md:38 Diagnostics row: "drift sqlite + flutter_secure_storage + ... secure storage"; goal.md:90: "AGPL, zero telemetry, encrypted secrets, max firewall WFP/iptables/pf"; goal.md:78 lists flutter_secure_storage in the frozen stack. Reality: grep for 'flutter_secure_storage|secure_storage' across lib/ returns no matches; grep for 'KeyStore|keystore|EncryptedSharedPreferences|MasterKey' across android/app/src/main/kotlin, lib/ and windows/runner returns nothing; the only reference is the auto-generated plugin registration leftover (GeneratedPluginRegistrant.java registers com.
findings.fix: Either implement the SecretsVault seam backed by flutter_secure_storage/Android Keystore + Windows DPAPI (see finding 1 fix), or correct SPEC.md/goal.md to state the actual posture so the spec stops claiming a control that is absent.

findings.title: On Android all secret-bearing store writes fall back to Directory.systemTemp (/data/local/tmp per Dart SDK) — outside app-private storage; writes fail silently or land in a shared shell-writable location
findings.evidence: All five stores use the identical fallback: "'${Platform.environment['HOME'] ?? Platform.environment['USERPROFILE'] ?? Directory.systemTemp.path}' '/.qanatvpn/endpoints.json'" (same in split_store.dart:74, rule_store.dart:37, policy_store.dart:32, updater.dart:301). Android app processes have no HOME/USERPROFILE, and the Dart VM resolves Directory.systemTemp on Android to a shell-owned path — dart-lang/sdk runtime/bin/directory_linux.cc SystemTemp(): "#if defined(DART_HOST_OS_ANDROID) temp_dir = \"/data/local/tmp\";". App UIDs cannot write /data/local/tmp, so every save() throws; DebouncedSaver swallows it: "// Fire and forget: a failed disk write must not crash the UI." and the controllers n
findings.fix: Add path_provider and use getApplicationSupportDirectory (Android app-private, sandboxed) as the baseDir on Android; wire it once in main.dart when constructing the stores (the baseDir injection seam already exists on every store).

findings.title: Full engine config with all credentials written plaintext to a predictable %TEMP% path and deleted only on clean paths; optional stale-file injection on next start
findings.evidence: start() writes `final file = File('${Directory.systemTemp.path}/qanatvpn_box_${DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch}.json'); await file.writeAsString(json);` where json is the assembled profile: endpoint_outbound.dart emits `'private_key': e.privateKey` and `'private_key_passphrase': e.privateKeyPassphrase` for SSH, `'uuid'`/`'password'` for vless/vmess/tuic, trojan/hysteria2 passwords, and profiles/config.wg-awg.json contains a WG `private_key`; awg_config.dart ships the same for WireGuard/AWG endpoints. _cleanupConfig() (`await file.delete()` in `try { } on Object { // Temp file leak is acceptable... }`) is invoked only from the exitCode.then handler and stop(); if the Flutter VM dies (win
findings.fix: Delete the config right after the engine confirms startup (sing-box only re-reads it on reload, which this adapter never performs), set a restrictive ACL at creation, use a random (unguessable) filename, sweep leftover qanatvpn_box_*.json from the app's temp prefix on startup, and shrink stop()'s 5s force-continue so teardown completes before the ap

findings.title: Update card spawns explorer.exe with an unvalidated URL deserialized from a user-writable store — explorer.exe <path> executes arbitrary local binaries
findings.evidence: updates_screen.dart:127-130: `await Process.start('explorer', <String>[info.assetUrl]);` (comment elsewhere says 'explorer.exe <url>' opens a browser, but explorer.exe given a local path launches whatever the path points at — `explorer.exe C:\...\evil.exe` executes it). assetUrl is deserialized without checks from the plaintext store `~/.qanatvpn/last_update_check.json` (`return StoredUpdate(info: UpdateInfo(version: doc['version'] as String, changelog: ..., assetUrl: doc['assetUrl'] as String? ?? '', ...))`, updater.dart:336-353) and also accepted raw from the gh-pages mirror (`entry['url'] as String? ?? ''`, updater.dart:201). There is no `Uri.tryParse` + `https` + host allowlist anywhere i
findings.fix: Validate before launching: require Uri.parse(assetUrl) with scheme https and host equal to github.com/<owner>/<repo> download path (or the exact gh-pages origin); otherwise ignore the stored entry and force a fresh network check. Keep the browser-open behavior (https URLs only) rather than passing raw strings to explorer.

findings.title: All pasted (non-URL) subscriptions share one ingestion-cache key — the second paste within 6 hours silently re-imports the first paste's endpoints
findings.evidence: var origin = 'pasted'; ... payload = utf8.encode(payload); ... final subscription = RawSubscription(bytes: bytes, url: Uri.parse(origin)); ... parsed = ref.read(ingestionAdapterProvider).parseAndNormalize(subscription);  // ingestion_adapter.dart: final cached = _cache[subscription.url]; if (cached != null && _now().difference(cached.parsedAt) < const Duration(hours: 6)) { return cached.endpoints; }
findings.fix: Only construct RawSubscription with a URL when the input actually was a URL; for pasted text pass a unique per-import key (e.g. Uri with a random path/query) or bypass the cache for origin == 'pasted'.

findings.title: HttpCache serves a stale cached body indefinitely on any fetch error — a permanently poisoned on-disk cache can never be healed while responses keep failing
findings.evidence: try { final response = await fetch(url, requestHeaders); ... } ... on Object { if (entry != null) { return entry.body; } rethrow; }  — no age cap: a month-old entry.fetchedAt still returns entry.body
findings.fix: Bound stale serving (e.g. max 48h since entry.fetchedAt), or at minimum annotate stale-with-age in the return path so the UI/refresh loop can warn. For security-relevant payloads (SRS rule sets feed the routing/kill-switch config), also sanity-check byte shape (SRS magic bytes) before accepting any response — cache or fresh — as poison detection.

findings.title: Disk cache meta is trusted unvalidated: arbitrary If-None-Match request header is replayed from the meta JSON and non-200/304 bytes already on disk win when fetch throws
findings.evidence: final meta = jsonDecode(metaFile.readAsStringSync()) as Map<String, dynamic>; final entry = _CacheEntry(body: bodyFile.readAsBytesSync(), etag: meta['etag'] as String?, fetchedAt: DateTime.parse(meta['fetchedAt'] as String)); ... if (entry?.etag != null) { requestHeaders['If-None-Match'] = entry!.etag!; }
findings.fix: Validate the etag against a strict format (^"[^"]{1,128}"$ or W/ variant) before sending, and cap meta fetchedAt age. This keeps a corrupted (not attacker-grade) meta file from producing malformed outbound requests.

findings.title: Stale package name in the split choice crashes TUN establishment: addAllowedApplication called without NameNotFoundException guard → every connect fails
findings.evidence: `val include = options.getIncludePackage(); while (include.hasNext()) { builder.addAllowedApplication(include.next()) }` — no try/catch. VpnService.Builder.addAllowedApplication throws NameNotFoundException for a package that is not installed (the fork's own reference implementation guards exactly this: go/amnezia-box .../VPNService.kt:139-145 `catch (e: NameNotFoundException) { Log.e(...) }`). The split list is persisted verbatim from the wizard (SplitChoice.fromJson only casts types — split_store.dart:26-29, no existence check, no dedupe, no empty-string filter) and is never re-validated against installed packages at connect time. So a stale package (app uninstalled after the wizard) or a
findings.fix: Wrap both loops in try/catch (NameNotFoundException) logging like upstream, and additionally prune the persisted SplitChoice against PackageManager.getInstalledPackages at ProfileConfigSource.resolve time, failing loudly (not just skipping) when a stored package is gone.

findings.title: Split choice on mobile is persisted to the system temp/cache directory — subject to OS deletion — silently reverting to whole-device tunneling
findings.evidence: `File _file() => File(baseDir != null ? '$baseDir/split_choice.json' : '${Platform.environment['HOME'] ?? Platform.environment['USERPROFILE'] ?? Directory.systemTemp.path}' '/.qanatvpn/split_choice.json');` — on Android, HOME is normally absent from an app process environment, so the choice lands under Directory.systemTemp (TMPDIR = the app's cache dir, which the system may clear at any time under storage pressure). wizard.dart:130-131 says the store is "overridden in main.dart with a real base dir on desktop and left default (HOME-based) on mobile", but main.dart:81 wires `splitStore: const SplitStore()` unconditionally — no override exists. After a cache clear, SplitStore.read() returns nul
findings.fix: Pass a real base dir (context.getFilesDir equivalent) for mobile, or at minimum read() should distinguish 'no choice saved' from 'file unreadable/missing after being previously present' and surface the split-lost state in the UI/diagnostics.

findings.title: Fail-open default position: allowlist mode with an empty selection silently means tunnel-everything, and any malformed stored choice degrades to the same
findings.evidence: `if (state.selectedApps.isNotEmpty) { await store.save(...) } else { await store.clear(); }` — the wizard's initial state is `allowMode = true` (allowlist) with `selectedApps = const <String>{}`, and Finish is always enabled; one accidental tap on the last step = no split at all. Parsing side compounds it: SplitChoice.fromJson returns null on any parse error (`on Object { return null; }`) and defaults `allowMode: doc['allowMode'] as bool? ?? true`, so a corrupt or truncated split_choice.json degrades to whole-device tunneling. Note the asymmetry: for an exclude/bypass choice, empty selection → clear → whole-device is fail-closed, but for allowlist (the default mode) it is fail-open. For a pr
findings.fix: Treat 'allowlist with zero selections' as an error state in the UI (disable Finish or show a distinct 'whole device will be tunneled' confirmation), and make SplitStore.read() surface corrupt-file conditions instead of silently returning null.

findings.title: Split changes (including backup import) never reach a running engine — stale include/exclude list persists until a manual reconnect
findings.evidence: `SplitStore.read()` appears only in lib/modules/vpn/repositories/profile_config_source.dart:85, and ConfigSource.resolve is only awaited inside Tunnel.connect (tunnel.dart:337 `configSource.resolve(tag).timeout(timeouts.resolve)`). There is no listener on SplitStore and no VpnNotifier reaction to changes. BackupService.import with BackupMerge.replace writes the split choice (`backup_service.dart:146-151`) with no connected-state guard, so restoring a backup mid-session leaves the previously established include/exclude set live inside the running engine — for bypass users the app they tried to exclude keeps tunneling until a manual disconnect+reconnect, with no UI indication. On a mid-run box
findings.fix: Either stop the engine when a split-relevant store changes while connected (VpnNotifier watches splitStore and forces disconnect), or add a 'config changed — reconnect to apply' banner; and on boxCrashed call box.stop()/closeTun so no TUN survives the engine.

findings.title: Default profile asset ships a committed WireGuard/AWG private key and dials TEST-NET-1 on first connect — it is also the base config every split choice merges into
findings.evidence: `"private_key": "eCbtX5g5Pof3zH0Gu6dzulIzLB0B5xj+OhIfgVtWu1A="` committed to the public GitHub repo (verified via `git show HEAD:profiles/config.wg-awg.json` — value present at HEAD). It is almost certainly a demo fixture (peer 203.0.113.10 is TEST-NET-1, h1 "1234567"), but the file is wired as the production default: ProfileConfigSource.assetPath = 'profiles/config.wg-awg.json' is loaded by every connect and is the base into which all split/groups/rules merges happen. Two problems: (1) a real-looking Curve25519 private key published in an AGPL repo invites copy-paste into real deployments; (2) a fresh install that connects before importing anything dials TEST-NET-1 and fails handshakes with
findings.fix: Generate the fixture key at build/test time instead of committing it (or blank the field and fail the connect with 'no endpoint configured' before the engine starts), and document the fixture status inline.

findings.title: No password strength floor or confirmation field for the credential-bearing backup password
findings.evidence: Export's only guard is `if (password.isEmpty) { throw ArgumentError('backup password must not be empty'); }` (lines 71-73) — no length or entropy floor. The UI prompt is a single obscure TextField with an OK button: `final controller = TextEditingController(); ... TextField(controller: controller, obscureText: true, ...) ... onPressed: () => Navigator.of(context).pop(controller.text)` (endpoints_screen.dart lines 233-258); there is no repeat-entry confirmation and no strength check, so a typo or a one-character password both encrypt the file "successfully". The doc comment admits the payload is "100% credentials-bearing (WG private keys, preshared keys, every protocol uuid/password)" (lines
findings.fix: Enforce a minimum length (e.g. 12 chars) in BackupService.exportBytes and show a two-field password+confirm dialog with a strength indicator in the UI; optionally add a zxcvbn-style estimator. Keep the KDF at OWASP interactive params or raise memory for this offline-file use case.

findings.title: FATAL log lines are double-written to Android system logcat (Log.e) on every engine crash, independent of the app's Logs screen
findings.evidence: `grep Log.[deiwv]( android/app/src/main/kotlin` shows BoxEngine.kt:141 `Log.e(TAG, "engine fatal: $message")` inside the writeLogs FATAL scan — the same `message` is simultaneously forwarded to Dart via `emitEvent("log", message)` and `emitEvent("crashed", message)` (lines 140, 142). BoxEngine.kt:151 also logs `"engine command stream dropped: $message"`. Since the engine log stream is the only channel carrying key-decode errors and connectivity error text (probed: `FATAL initialize endpoint[0]: decode private key: illegal base64 data at input byte 4`), each such event is duplicated into the system log where `adb logcat`/bugreports capture it, in addition to the app's own LogsScreen. Other Lo
findings.fix: Downgrade the FATAL forward from Log.e to Log.d (stripped in release builds by default with R8 `assumenosideeffects` on android.util.Log if configured), or pass a sanitized substring (level + error class only) to Log.e while keeping the full line for the in-app LogBus.

findings.title: Import failure paths echo raw user input (whole share links containing passwords) into on-screen error text and SnackBars
findings.evidence: `state = state.copyWith(error: error.toString(), importing: false)` in EndpointsController (endpoints_controller.dart:128-136) is rendered verbatim as a persistent `Text(state.error!, style: colorScheme.error)` block with `Semantics(liveRegion: true)` (endpoints_screen.dart:63-74) — announced aloud by screen readers and readable in any screen recording. parsers.dart:707 `throw FormatException('not an ss link: $trimmed')` and :666 `throw FormatException('not a vmess link: $trimmed')` interpolate the entire pasted line; an `ss://` link embeds `method:password@host` directly, and `intField` at parsers.dart:48 echoes the raw value (`'bad integer in $what: $value'`). The same exception strings al
findings.fix: Make parse-error messages content-free (scheme/tag + reason only, never `$trimmed`/`$value`), and clamp state.error before rendering (e.g. first 160 chars with credential-shaped runs masked).

findings.title: No test or runtime guard ties 'encrypted secrets' posture to the logging layer — the 7-scenario leak suite (scripts/leak_test.sh) covers network leaks only, not log leaks
findings.evidence: `grep -rni "redact|scrub|sanitiz" lib android/app/src/main/kotlin` returns zero hits; tests in test/logs/log_bus_test.dart cover parsing, 2000-line caps, repeat collapse, and 250ms batching only — no test asserts that a line like 'decode private key: <base64>' or 'password=...' gets masked before LogBus emits it. The stated product posture ('encrypted secrets, zero telemetry') has no enforced counterpart at the logging boundary, and the export button (logs_screen.dart:238-243) produces a buffer that is never redacted.
findings.fix: Add a LogBus-level redaction unit (regex list for base64 32+/hex 64+ runs, 'password', 'private_key', 'uuid=' patterns) plus a test asserting a canary secret fed through EngineLogLine.parse never survives into bus.lines or the export buffer; gate release on it alongside the 7 leak tests.

findings.title: upstream-check.yml drift detection is inert: fetches upstream but never compares, builds, or notifies
findings.evidence: The entire 'Report drift' step is: `PINNED=$(git -C go/amnezia-box rev-parse HEAD)` / `echo "pinned: $PINNED"` / `echo "If upstream has a new awg tag, open a bump PR:"` — it only echoes instructions into CI logs. It never compares `git describe --tags` output against the pin, never runs the promised `make lib_android` sanity (tasks/plan.md:54 documents the tracker as 'Weekly `git fetch --all` + `make lib_android` + `softprops/action-gh-release` version check'), creates no issue/PR/step-summary, and never exits non-zero on drift. Upstream security fixes (or a malicious tag pushed to hoaxisr/amnezia-box) can therefore sit undetected forever; detection relies on a human reading ephemeral Action
findings.fix: Make the check a real tripwire: fetch upstream tags, compare the latest `1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.*` tag against the pinned SHA, and on mismatch fail the job (emailed/visible failure) and/or `gh issue create --label upstream-drift` with the tag diff. Optionally also run `make test_libbox` on the fetched source (never on a bumped pin) so upstream changes ge

findings.title: Release-artifact trust boundary ends unverified: client never validates sha256 manifests and opens assetUrl unvalidated
findings.evidence: The CI builds and attaches `sha256-android.json` / `sha256-windows.json` (build-android.yml 'Rename artifacts + sha256'; build-windows.yml `Get-FileHash ... sha256-windows.json`), but grep for `sha256|MessageDigest|checksum|verifyHash|integrity` across lib/, android/app/src/main/kotlin/, and windows/runner returns zero hits — the app never checks them. The consumer path is: updater.dart `_fromMirror` takes `entry['url']` from the Pages mirror (or `browser_download_url` from the API) into `assetUrl`, then updates_screen.dart:129 runs `await Process.start('explorer', <String>[info.assetUrl])` and VpnServiceBridge.kt:107-108 does `activity.startActivity(Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url)
findings.fix: Fetch `sha256-<platform>.json` from the same release in the updater, hash the downloaded artifact before install, and compare before invoking installUpdate; additionally constrain `assetUrl` to `https://github.com/QMahyar/qanatvpn/releases/...` (reject anything else) so a tampered store file or mirror JSON cannot redirect the install path.

findings.title: Engine-kill-switch rule set does not cover the FakeIP range (198.18.0.0/15, fc00::/18) and the vendored profile carries no ::/0, RFC1918, or pinned-DNS rules until regenerated
findings.evidence: baseRules() (firewall.dart:28-53) emits exactly: hijack-dns, pinned-DNS DIRECT, ::/0 BLOCK, RFC1918 BLOCK — there is no rule for the FakeIP range. config_assembler.dart:82-86 puts the FakeIP pool on the TUN itself (`'address': <String>['172.19.0.1/30', 'fdfe:dcba:9876::1/126', dns.fakeIpRange]`) and its comment states "baseRules() before user rules: validateOrdering stays green" — the assembly path (ConfigAssembler.build) is the only one that inserts baseRules. But the config the engine actually runs comes from ProfileConfigSource.resolve (profile_config_source.dart:30 `assetPath = 'profiles/config.wg-awg.json'`), which never invokes baseRules(): it only appends user rules (`route['rules'] =
findings.fix: Insert FirewallPolicy.baseRules()/baseRulesScoped() into route.rules inside ProfileConfigSource._withRules (or re-generate + CI-assert the vendored profile carries the four base rules via validateOrdering), and add a rule blocking 198.18.0.0/15 and fc00::/18 egress for defense-in-depth on gvisor-stack setups.

findings.title: Firewall 'policy' is a dead abstraction: shouldEnforce/baseRulesScoped/enforced are unused, and no user-facing toggle ever changes what the engine enforces
findings.evidence: PolicyFirewallAdapter.enforce() (main.dart:199-206) is the entire firewall implementation: `final errors = _policy.validateOrdering(_policy.baseRules()); if (errors.isNotEmpty) { throw StateError(...); } _enforced = true;` — no native call, no config inspection beyond its own constant. Its `_enforced` flag is only exposed as `bool get enforced` "for diagnostics" (main.dart:216-218) and grep shows no production reader; FirewallPolicy.shouldEnforce() (firewall.dart:52) is defined but never called anywhere in lib/. baseRulesScoped() (firewall.dart:62) is likewise unreferenced in lib/ (only tests). FirewallPolicy therefore exists as a compile-time-checked rule generator plus dead toggle surface,
findings.fix: Either wire FirewallPolicy knobs into ProfileConfigSource/ConfigAssembler (plumb the policy into config building and use baseRulesScoped for merges) and read enforced for a real status pill, or delete the dead API until the native lockdown lands; update goal.md §12/SPEC/UI copy to state the current engine-rules-only scope.

findings.title: Windows per-app split tunneling is silently dropped: wizard include/exclude choices never reach the engine config, so the user's split intent does not hold on Windows
findings.evidence: windows_box_process.dart start() lines 67-70: "// Per-app split on Windows: the config file carries the tun route // policy, engine-level per-app filtering is Android-only (VpnService // builder). Documented: Windows split ships with the routing editor." followed by "final json = jsonEncode(config.json);" — TypedConfig.includePackages/excludePackages (sent to Android via boxStart 'includePackages'/'excludePackages') are simply not serialized on Windows. The wizard (SplitStore) still stores the allowlist/bypass choice with no platform guard or warning, so a Windows user who selects 'only these apps tunnel' gets tunnel-all. The split-audit leak scenario cannot catch it (script scenario 6 is An
findings.fix: Either emit tun include_package/exclude_package (or process_name rules) into the Windows config JSON, or disable the wizard split step on Windows until it is implemented.

findings.title: Spec claims 'max firewall WFP/iptables/pf + in-tunnel DNS + IPv6 block' but zero WFP/iptables/pf code exists anywhere in the repo
findings.evidence: goal.md section 12: "AGPL, zero telemetry, encrypted secrets, max firewall WFP/iptables/pf + in-tunnel DNS + IPv6 block + 7 tests per RTINGS July 2026." grep -ril "wfp|firewall|Fwpm" windows/ → only windows/sing-box.exe (binary); windows/runner sources contain no filtering code. The shipped profile lacks the ::/0 and RFC1918 BLOCK rules and the pinned-DNS DIRECT rule that FirewallPolicy.baseRules() defines (see config_assembler.dart line 106, never wired), so 'in-tunnel DNS' (dns-local type local for geosite-cn resolves via the system resolver, per the vendored dns block) and 'IPv6 block' are also unimplemented on the live path.
findings.fix: Either implement the platform firewall (WFP on Windows, per-fd enforcement on Android) or rewrite the docs to state the actual guarantee: in-engine rule filtering only, active solely while the engine runs.

findings.title: No region routing presets (Iran/China/Russia bypass): the rules editor ships empty with only geosite-cn/geoip-cn assets bundled
findings.evidence: Competitor: Hiddify 'Settings → Routing → Region preset buttons: Iran (bypass .ir/IR IPs, proxy rest), China... Russia, Others' — README: 'Appropriate configuration for Iran, China, Russia and other countries' (research/07-Hiddify.md §5); Karing 'Country Or Region selector auto-injects geosite:cn/geoip:cn direct rules... similar logic for RU/IR presets' (research/01-Karing.md §5). App: GeoAsset.registry contains only geosite-cn + geoip-cn (lib/modules/geo/geo_asset.dart:39-48), the rules screen opens on 'No rules. Traffic follows the engine default outbound.' (l10n rulesEmpty, rules_screen.dart:52-54), and no preset-injection code exists (grep preset hits only AWG junk-value presets).
findings.fix: Extend GeoAsset.registry with geosite/geoip ir+ru srs assets and add a first-run region picker that seeds rules_screen with direct rules (geosite/geoip → DIRECT) matching the chosen region.

findings.title: No live traffic statistics, connections table, or speed test — the only metric is connect-phase milliseconds
findings.evidence: Competitor: Karing 'Connections screen shows active connections table (data_table_2), per-outbound traffic chart (fl_chart), long-press to kill all... per-node traffic accounting via sing-box experimental.clash_api' (research/01-Karing.md §10); Hiddify shows real-time speed/traffic in the notification (research/07-Hiddify.md §10). App: the StatsTile headline is connect timing only — "headline = 'connect ${metrics.total.inMilliseconds} ms'" (lib/modules/vpn/screens/home.dart:271) — the Tunnel service exposes lastConnectMetrics but no bytes/connections API (grep stats/traffic: no hit), and goal.md §11 locks 'stats' plus 'logs/requests/connections' day 1.
findings.fix: Wire libbox Clash-API/CommandClient traffic + connections streams into a Connections screen (table + fl_chart throughput), replace the connect-ms tile with live up/down rates while connected.

findings.title: No system-proxy (non-TUN) fallback mode: config always emits a TUN inbound, so unprivileged Windows users and proxy-only use cases have no path
findings.evidence: Competitor: Karing 'System Proxy Mode: Only apps respecting system HTTP/SOCKS proxy... mixed inbound (http+socks) on 127.0.0.1:port' as a mutually toggleable mode (research/01-Karing.md §6); Hiddify 'set-system-proxy: true (System Proxy mode) puts mixed-port 2334 as OS proxy' with 'enable-tun' a ConfigOptions toggle (research/07-Hiddify.md §6). App: ConfigAssembler.build hardcodes a single tun inbound ("'inbounds': <dynamic>[<String, dynamic>{'type': 'tun', 'tag': tag...' — lib/modules/routing/config_assembler.dart:71-81) with no mixed inbound, no set-system-proxy path on Windows (windows_box_process.dart spawns sing-box run only), while goal.md §7 locks 'Both TUN mixed + Proxy PAC + Local S
findings.fix: Add a tunnel-mode setting that swaps the inbounds array (tun vs mixed 127.0.0.1:10808) and sets the Windows system proxy via registry when TUN is off — restoring the non-admin fallback and the locked 10808/10809 ports.

findings.title: No settings surface at all: DoH server, TUN stack/MTU, mux, theme, and language are hardcoded constants with no settings screen
findings.evidence: Competitor: Karing exposes 'DNS Server screen... Up to 4 servers... udp/tcp/tls/https/quic/h3' plus 'Auto Setup Server picks fastest DNS by probing delay detection URL' (research/01-Karing.md §9); Hiddify has remote-dns-address/direct-dns-address/domain-strategy settings per #529 dump (research/07-Hiddify.md §7). App: DnsConfig hardcodes "this.dohServer = '1.1.1.1'" with a const default (lib/modules/dns/dns_config.dart:19-32) and ConfigAssembler news it up with no injection ('this.dns = const DnsConfig()' — config_assembler.dart:14), while app.dart's route table (app.dart:33-63: /home /groups /endpoints /rules /logs /diagnostics /updates) contains no settings route — the 'Settings' l10n stri
findings.fix: Add a Settings screen owning DNS (remote/direct server + strategy), TUN MTU/stack, and language/theme toggles, plumbed through DnsConfig/ConfigAssembler constructor args with a small store; goal.md §8 'DoH split + bootstrap' implies user-configurable endpoints.

findings.title: No Windows tray icon, hotkeys, or launch-at-startup — desktop parity features both competitors ship are absent
findings.evidence: Competitor: Karing uses 'window_manager, tray_manager, hotkey_manager' on desktop (research/01-Karing.md §1) and Hiddify ships 'tray_manager 0.5.0 + window_manager... desktop tray icon states connected/disconnected/dark' (research/07-Hiddify.md §9). App: pubspec.yaml has no tray/window/hotkey deps (dependencies list: riverpod, go_router, drift, http, workmanager, etc.) and windows/runner/ contains only the default Flutter template files (main.cpp, flutter_window.cpp, win32_window.cpp — no tray/elevation code), while goal.md §11 locks 'main(config), hotkeys/tray/deeplink' and AGENTS.md positions Windows as an MVP platform.
findings.fix: Add tray_manager + window_manager with connected/disconnected tray icons and a quick connect/disconnect menu, plus launch-at-startup on Windows; a single elevated-runner manifest entry fixes the TUN-permission UX.

findings.title: Urltest auto-selection is invisible: UI never shows which member the engine actually picked
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/11-FlClash.md — urltest group semantics with 'url-test optimizes speed' and the proxies page showing which member is active ('Tap select → immediate switch'); research/06-V2RayNG.md — foreground notification shows the active profile remark. App side: lib/modules/vpn/logic/selected_endpoint.dart:47-57 deliberately connects to the group tag ('connecting to the group tag lets the engine pick the best member (and fail over) — members.first would pin a fixed node'), and home.dart StateTile renders `Text(vpn.tag ?? l10n.homeNoEndpoint)` — the group tag, never the engine's chosen leaf; latency.dart samples are TCP-only and not surfaced against urltest members per node. The
findings.fix: Subscribe to the engine's group state (clash_api /proxies or libbox equivalent) to display the currently-selected urltest member and its delay next to the group tag on the home StateTile.

findings.title: Group member picking is a raw checkbox list — no filter/exclude regex or include-all for 200+ node subscriptions
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/11-FlClash.md — groups support '`filter: "(?i)港|hk|hongkong"` / `exclude-filter: "美|日"` / `exclude-type: ss|http`' plus 'include-all: true — auto-include all inline + providers members'. App side: lib/modules/routing/groups_screen.dart:250-260 renders one `CheckboxListTile` per tag from `widget.knownTags` with no search, no filter input, no include-all toggle; lib/modules/routing/routing_policy.dart OutboundGroup has only tag/members/defaultMember/interval/tolerance fields. On a 300-line airport subscription the editor is effectively unusable.
findings.fix: Add a filter/exclude regex pair to OutboundGroup (compiled at config-source time against the leaf universe) plus an include-all-proxies switch and a search box over knownTags in the member picker.

findings.title: Subscription fetch is direct-only — blocked subscription URLs cannot be fetched through the tunnel (no provider proxy: option)
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/11-FlClash.md — proxy-providers carry '`url`, `path` …, `interval`, `proxy: DIRECT` (fetch via proxy or direct)'; research/05-V2RayN.md — sub fetch 'honors `PreSocksPort` if update via proxy enabled'. App side: lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_controller.dart:93-101 always uses `plainFetch(maybeUrl, …)` on the device's direct network; there is no detour/through-tunnel option anywhere in the import path (plain_fetch.dart is a bare HttpClient wrapper). The core differentiator audience (highly censored networks per goal.md §1) is exactly where the subscription domain itself is blocked.
findings.fix: Add a 'fetch via VPN' toggle that routes the subscription fetch through the engine's local mixed inbound (127.0.0.1) when the tunnel is up, mirroring provider `proxy:` semantics.

findings.title: No live connections view — goal.md §11 promised logs/requests/connections, only logs exist
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/11-FlClash.md — 'Connections page features … Show: src → dst, domain, process, rule, proxy chain, upload/download, duration; Actions: Close single conn, Close all'; research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md — 'Connections table (src/pages/connections.tsx)' with keyword search. App side: lib/modules has only dns, geo, health, logs, onboarding, routing, sec, updates, vpn — no connections module; grep for connections across lib/ matches only unrelated identifiers (routing policy maps), and BoxEngine.kt subscribes CommandLog only (line 172), never CommandConnections. goal.md §11 froze 'logs/requests/connections' as day-1 extras.
findings.fix: Wire CommandConnections through BoxEngine + the channel adapter and add a connections tab listing active flows (destination, rule, chain, bytes) with a close action via the clash API.

findings.title: AWG manual editor stops at H1-H4: no I1-I5 CPS fields, no Id/Ip/Ib masquerade, hardcoded AllowedIPs and keepalive
findings.evidence: goal.md §4: 'all values: ... I1-I5 + masquerade Id/Ip/Ib'; research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §2/§7: WG Tunnel exposes 'I1-I5 CPS text fields with CPS helper (tag autocomplete <b hex>)'; research/10-WireSock.md §8: WireSock GUI 'DPI tab (Junk Packets, Magic Headers, Protocol Masking)' for Id/Ip/Ib. App: _advancedFields() (awg_profile_screen.dart:191) renders only Jc/Jmin/Jmax, S1-S4, H1-H4; _copyWith passes i1: _values.i1 through untouched and has no id/ip/ib parameters; peers are hardcoded allowedIps: const ['0.0.0.0/0', '::/0'] (line 168) with persistentKeepalive = 25 (awg_config.dart:59) — the flagship 'ALL values' capability is import-only in the UI, and masquerade values can never reach the engin
findings.fix: Add I1-I5 multiline text fields (with a <b>/<t>/<r> tag helper) and a per-peer advanced section (AllowedIPs, keepalive, preshared key) to the sheet; document in the editor that Id/Ip/Ib are stored but inert with this engine, or surface a validation warning when they are set.

findings.title: No Quick Settings tile, home-screen shortcuts, or start-on-boot
findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §7: 'Quick Settings Tile (TileService ... tile state STATE_ACTIVE (green) vs STATE_INACTIVE; onClick() calls TunnelService.toggle() ... Home screen Shortcuts (ShortcutManager dynamic shortcuts)' plus 'Start on Boot'. App: AndroidManifest.xml declares only MainActivity, ForegroundService and QanatVpnService; grep 'TileService|BOOT_COMPLETED|AppWidget|quicksettings' over android/app/src returns nothing, and lib/ tile matches are only NavigationBar/group rule tiles.
findings.fix: Add a TileService that toggles the tunnel through the existing MethodChannel (connect/disconnect of the selected tag), a BOOT_COMPLETED receiver that restarts the last tunnel if the user opted in, and a simple AppWidget provider.

findings.title: No network-based on-demand tunneling (trusted Wi-Fi SSID / mobile-data auto-start) — SSIDs exist only as in-tunnel routing rules
findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §5: AutoTunnelService 'Tunnel on Wi-Fi ... Trusted Wi-Fi Names ... Tunnel Mapping (SSID glob → Tunnel) ... Tunnel on Mobile Data ... Stop Tunnel on No Internet ... Start on Boot ... wildcards'. App: the only SSID logic is inside-tunnel routing — addList('wifi_ssid', rule.wifiSsids) (lib/modules/routing/routing_compiler.dart:239) routes traffic by SSID but never starts/stops the tunnel; PlatformAdapter (lib/core/services/tunnel.dart:60) exposes only permission/battery/airplane checks, and BoxEngine.kt:372 registerDefaultNetworkCallback feeds only the libbox InterfaceUpdateListener (engine interface monitoring), not app-level auto-connect.
findings.fix: Add an on-demand store (trusted SSID list, per-network tunnel choice, mobile-data toggle) and wire a platform channel using ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION + NetworkCallback to call Tunnel.connect/disconnect on network transitions; debounce like WG Tunnel.

findings.title: No live tunnel stats: RX/TX bytes, handshake freshness, or health LED; the home tile shows only last-connect phase timing
findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §6: 'Tunnel health shown on main Tunnels screen via LED indicator: green=healthy, red=unhealthy, gray=unknown ... hierarchical: Logs Check → Ping Check → Stats Check' and §7 'Live statistics (handshake time, RX/TX bytes, ping latency)'. App: StatsTile (home.dart:259) renders only connect timing — headline = 'connect ${metrics.total.inMilliseconds} ms' with metrics.phases — and grep 'rxBytes|txBytes|rx_bytes|handshake' across lib/ and android/ returns nothing; TunnelState.reconnecting (lib/core/services/tunnel.dart:11) is defined and localized but no code path ever emits it.
findings.fix: Stream the engine's clash-api traffic stats (the fork is built with with_clash_api) into a periodic stats tile, derive a health indicator from the existing log-stream FATAL scan plus a TCP ping to the endpoint, and emit TunnelState.reconnecting on connection loss for the localized label that already exists.

findings.title: Onboarding wizard state is not persisted — the full 3-step wizard replays on every app launch
findings.evidence: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §7: settings/tunnels persist in Room/DataStore and the app reopens directly into the tunnels screen — onboarding is one-time. App: WizardController.build() => const WizardState() (wizard.dart:58) is in-memory only; the shell condition 'wizard.step == WizardStep.done' (app.dart:136) resets to WizardStep.vpnPermission on every process start, and grep shows no store or backup writes wizard state — so each launch re-plays VPN-permission → battery → per-app split before any tab is reachable.
findings.fix: Persist a completed flag (e.g. alongside SplitStore or a tiny prefs file) and short-circuit the shell gate when set; keep the split editor reachable post-onboarding per the separate split-screen finding.

findings.title: No per-subscription enable/disable, update interval, or remark filtering
findings.evidence: research/06-V2RayNG.md:251: 'Fields: remarks (name), url (https), enabled: Boolean, autoUpdate: Boolean, updateInterval ... filter: String (regex)'; research/05-V2RayN.md:264: 'SubItem{Remarks, Url, Enabled, Filter, Sort}'. Since the app has no subscription entity at all (see finding 1), none of these per-sub controls exist: endpoints_controller.dart merges every import into one flat list keyed only by tag, endpoints_screen.dart exposes a single delete per endpoint, and there is no regex filter applied at import (ingestion_adapter.dart parseShareLines accepts every parsed line). A user with a 200-node airport sub cannot pause it or hide garbage nodes short of deleting all its endpoints one b
findings.fix: With a Subscription model in place, add enabled/disable toggle and a regex filter field applied during parse, matching v2rayNG's SubItem semantics.

findings.title: No subscription-scoped grouping or cross-sub dedupe semantics — all subs collapse into one flat tag-keyed list
findings.evidence: research/04-Nekoray.md:366-368: 'Top QTabBar = groups ... Two types: MANUAL ... and SUBSCRIPTION (URL + interval +UA, auto-fetched)' with group context menu 'Update Subscription, Delete Duplicates'; research/01-Karing.md:16 'unified rule-set across multiple subscriptions' where one rule set applies across sources. In the app, EndpointsController.importText (endpoints_controller.dart:133-150) merges all pasted payloads into one map deduped by tag only, so importing two subs that both contain 'HKG-01' keeps whichever came last regardless of which sub it came from, and deleting a sub is impossible (only per-endpoint delete exists). sourceUrl is persisted (endpoint_store.dart:85) but used solely
findings.fix: Group the endpoints list by sourceUrl (real sub vs manual), expose per-group refresh/delete, and scope tag replacement within a single sub so one provider cannot stomp another's nodes.

findings.title: No QR scan or qanatvpn:// deeplink import despite goal and prototype promising both
findings.evidence: goal.md:9 locks 'QR/ZIP deeplink'; docs/prototype-final.html:314 promises 'QR/ZIP deeplink qanatvpn://' and the prototype's Profiles table has per-row QR and Export ZIP buttons (lines 319-325). The shipped app has none of it: AndroidManifest.xml (lines 31-47) declares only MAIN/LAUNCHER plus VpnService intent-filters — no VIEW/BROWSABLE filter for share-link or qanatvpn:// URIs; pubspec has no QR scanner/reader dependency (grep zxing/mobile_scanner/barcode: no matches); no screen offers a share-link QR export (endpoints_screen.dart has only backup/restore/AWG-editor buttons), and grep 'qanatvpn://' matches only the prototype HTML. research/02-Throne.md:278 shows the competitor bar: 'Deeplink th
findings.fix: Add a VIEW/BROWSABLE intent-filter for vless/vmess/ss/trojan/hysteria2/tuic and a qanatvpn:// scheme routing into importText, plus a QR share/export action on the endpoints screen.

findings.title: Subscription fetch sends no User-Agent and no custom request headers — providers that gate by UA will reject or serve garbage
findings.evidence: research/04-Nekoray.md:52-53: 'subscription update fetches provider URL with User-Agent: nekoray/<version>'; research/05-V2RayN.md:54: 'subscription fetch uses User-Agent default v2rayN/<version> (customizable)'; research/06-V2RayNG.md:251: subscription fields include 'userAgent: String, requestHeaders: String (JSON {"X-hwid":"...","Authorization":"Bearer ..."})'; research/01-Karing.md:403: configurable UA list that 'rotates to mimic Clash/Mihomo/Surge to satisfy provider allowlists'. The app's import fetch sends exactly one header (endpoints_controller.dart:96-98: plainFetch(maybeUrl, const {'Accept': '*/*'})) — Dart's HttpClient default UA ('Dart/x.y (dart:io)') identifies the client to an
findings.fix: Send a configurable UA (default mimicking clash/mihomo) on sub fetches and add per-sub custom headers to the Subscription model.

findings.title: No one-tap clipboard import — users must manually paste into the import TextField while all competitors read the clipboard directly
findings.evidence: Competitors: research/06-V2RayNG.md:265 'Import from Clipboard → Utils.getClipboard() → AngConfigManager.importBatchConfig() handles single URI or base64 batch'; research/07-Hiddify.md:194 'Home → + → Add from clipboard (auto-detects any of above)'; research/01-Karing.md:406 'clipboard monitor (lib/app/utils/clipboard_utils.dart)'. App: import requires manual typing into the endpoints TextField (endpoints_screen.dart:24 import-box doc); grep 'Clipboard\.' across lib/ finds no clipboard API usage — only the l10n string 'No endpoints. Paste a share link or subscription URL above.' (l10n/app_en.arb:54) and the comment 'Ingests raw text pasted by the user' (endpoints_controller.dart:79). The con
findings.fix: Add a paste-import affordance (Clipboard.getData → importText) on the EndpointsScreen import box, or auto-suggest import when the app resumes with a share link on the clipboard, like Karing's clipboard monitor.

findings.title: No config-file import (raw txt/conf/yaml/zip) — file picking is reserved exclusively for encrypted .qnv backups
findings.evidence: Competitors: research/06-V2RayNG.md:265 'File: Import from file → ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT → read text → import'; research/01-Karing.md:381 'Add Profiles — supports: paste URL, paste content, scan QR, import from file, import ZIP'. App: FilePicker is used exactly twice, both for the encrypted backup (.qnv): saveFile with allowedExtensions ['qnv'] (endpoints_screen.dart:155-161) and pickFiles with allowedExtensions ['qnv'] (endpoints_screen.dart:176-180). No code path feeds picked-file bytes into EndpointsController.importText or IngestionAdapter — grep 'FilePicker|pickFiles' shows only endpoints_screen.dart:155/176 and backup_service.dart:66. A user holding a saved clash.yaml or wg conf file mus
findings.fix: Add an 'import from file' action next to the import box that picks txt/conf/yaml/json/zip files and pipes bytes (utf8-decoded, or zip member extraction for multi-node archives) into the existing importText/parseShareLines pipeline.

findings.title: Windows has no tray, no hotkeys, no autostart, no deep link — goal.md section 11 'hotkeys/tray/deeplink' is absent and app exit orphans the sing-box.exe child holding the TUN
findings.evidence: Competitors: WireSock 'Tray: Minimize to tray, Auto-start on login (Task Scheduler workaround for UAC)' (research/10-WireSock.md:505-507); FlClash 'Admin auto launch' + silent launching (research/11-FlClash.md:723,749); Throne 'Tray menu improvements' (research/02-Throne.md:509). App: grep for tray/autostart/hotkey/deeplink across lib/ and windows/ returns nothing; WindowsBoxProcessAdapter spawns sing-box.exe with ProcessStartMode.normal (windows_box_process.dart:85) and taskkill cleanup only runs inside stop() (line 166) — there is no window-close handler in windows/runner/win32_window.cpp, so closing the app mid-tunnel orphans the engine holding the TUN, and relaunching spawns a second eng
findings.fix: Add minimize-to-tray with tunnel state, an autostart-on-login toggle (registry Run key or StartupTask), a window-close handler that stops or detaches the engine cleanly (job object to guarantee child teardown), and optional global hotkeys.

findings.title: POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission is never requested: on Android 13+ the persistent notification is silently suppressed
findings.evidence: Competitors: v2rayNG handles runtime POST_NOTIFICATIONS per API via PermissionType.kt ('POST_NOTIFICATIONS (API 33+)', research/06-V2RayNG.md:472); Karing requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS in its permission set (research/01-Karing.md:337). App: AndroidManifest.xml line 7 declares the permission, but grep for requestPermissions/Permission.notification across android/ and lib/ returns nothing; the wizard (wizard.dart _VpnStep/_BatteryStep/_SplitStep) never asks. On API 33+ the ongoing notification — the only persistent tunnel surface the app has — is invisible while the FGS still runs, so users see neither state nor any disconnect affordance.
findings.fix: Request POST_NOTIFICATIONS at runtime in the wizard (new step or alongside the VPN step) and degrade gracefully when denied; pair with the notification-actions fix so the shade is actually useful once granted.

findings.title: No suspend/resume or app-lifecycle handling anywhere: nothing observes lifecycle state despite the SPEC leak test requiring a sleep/wake scenario
findings.evidence: Competitors: WireSock 'KillSwitch, Auto-reconnect, Connection timeout (Continuous Retry)' covers suspend/resume loss (research/10-WireSock.md:505); WG Tunnel ping/stats monitoring recovers the tunnel after wake (research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §6 'Seamless tunnel recovery'). App: grep for AppLifecycle/WidgetsBindingObserver/didChangeAppLifecycleState across lib/ returns zero hits; Tunnel has no wake/recovery path and VpnNotifier never re-queries the engine (vpn_notifier.dart:96-103), so after wake the home screen can show Connected with a stale tunnel while SPEC.md:343 leak test 2 'sleep/wake 60s' expects verified state.
findings.fix: Add an AppLifecycleListener that on resume reconciles engine state (probe or CommandStatus) and triggers the reconnect loop after wake; log the wake/recovery into ConnectMetrics for the diagnostics screen.

findings.title: No sort-by-latency anywhere despite it being a frozen lock ("sort by ping")
findings.evidence: Competitors: research/06-V2RayNG.md:426 "UI sorts by delay (`sortByTestResults`)"; research/07-Hiddify.md:381 "top-right sort button by name vs delay (`95ca6072`)"; goal.md:111 locks "Simple Ping TCP 5000ms + sort by ping" in the frozen Extra Deeps; docs/prototype-final.html:299 ships a 'Sort by ping' button. App: grep 'sort|Sort' across lib/ returns zero matches; the endpoints list renders store order via ListView.builder over state.endpoints (endpoints_screen.dart:89-90) and the groups list likewise (groups_screen.dart:55-56).
findings.fix: Add a sort control to the endpoints list (latency asc / name) and sort members by latency in the group editor member list, matching the prototype's 'Sort by ping' affordance.

findings.title: No refresh cadence: the sweep is strictly manual — never re-runs after import, after connect, or on a timer, with no staleness indicator
findings.evidence: App: lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:111-113 — "Never auto-measures on watch (no surprise network I/O) — [LatencyController.refresh] is the only sweeper"; the sole refresh() call is the Groups-tab icon (groups_screen.dart:37); importText never triggers a sweep (endpoints_controller.dart:106-175 has no latency reference); main.dart:118-132 registers only the 24h 'updatesDaily' workmanager task — no latency task. Competitors: research/01-Karing.md:537 latency runs after every profile update; research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:452 "Bulk test via `WorkManager` coroutine"; research/07-Hiddify.md:381 "core `urltest` group auto-probes `url-test-interval 600s`"; research/08-Exclave.md:459 "Toggle `Auto
findings.fix: Trigger LatencyController.refresh() after subscription import and on connect, and add an optional periodic/background sweep (workmanager or on-app-open) so badges are never stale; show sample age on the badge.

findings.title: No latency history or persistence: one int per tag, replaced on every sweep, wiped on restart — no min/avg/last, no trend
findings.evidence: App: LatencyState is a single `Map<String, int?> samples` of the latest sweep (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart:114); LatencyController replaces state wholesale each refresh (latency.dart:174-179) and persists nothing (endpoint_store persists endpoints only; no latency store exists). The only rolling samples in the app are boolean ping-OK values for the fixed 1.1.1.1 target in the health module (lib/modules/health/health.dart:66,76-79) — not per-endpoint and not ms values. Competitors: research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:452 "Results cached per entity"; research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:730 "`src/services/cmds.ts` `calcuProxies` + `delay.ts` inject latency history"; docs/prototype-final.html:302 "Pi
findings.fix: Persist the last sweep (and a small rolling history) per tag to disk, and expose min/avg/last per endpoint row or detail sheet as the prototype specifies.

findings.title: Theme mode control missing — app follows system with no user override
findings.evidence: lib/app/app.dart:83-94 registers both theme and darkTheme but never themeMode, so dark mode is OS-gated only; grep 'themeMode|ThemeMode' in lib/ returns zero hits. docs/prototype-final.html:330 (the design source of truth) ships a Theme select with 'System/Light/Dark/AMOLED #000' plus 'Dynamic color' and 'Reduce motion' pills. research/01-Karing.md:540-541: 'Appearance / Theme: flutter Material 3 + Cupertino adaptive; follows system dark/light; manual toggle in SettingsScreen'. A VPN left connected in a lit room at night with a system-light phone has no manual override.
findings.fix: Add a ThemeMode setting (system/light/dark, optionally AMOLED via a black surface scheme) persisted and fed to MaterialApp.themeMode on the settings screen.

findings.title: TUN MTU and stack settings missing from the assembled config and from any screen
findings.evidence: lib/modules/routing/config_assembler.dart:71-79 emits the tun inbound as {'type': 'tun', 'tag': tag, 'address': [...], 'auto_route': true, 'strict_route': true} with no mtu and no stack key, and nothing lets the user change them (grep 'mtu' in lib/modules/routing returns only AWG peer config). research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:281: 'Default 9000... User editable Settings → Tun → MTU. Affects Builder.setMtu()' and :277 'Stack options: mixed (auto), gvisor (userspace TCP/IP), system'; research/01-Karing.md:331: 'SettingsScreen TUN section... controls tun.enable, tun.stack, tun.mtu'. docs/prototype-final.html:334 plans a Tunnel tile with a Stack select (mixed/gvisor/system) and MTU input. On flaky
findings.fix: Add MTU and stack fields to the tun inbound sourced from a settings store; settings screen 'Tunnel' section mirroring the prototype tile.

findings.title: Notification preferences and quick-toggle surfaces absent — foreground service is fixed and uncontrollable
findings.evidence: ForegroundAdapter is start/stop only (lib/core/services/tunnel.dart:82-85) and the connect path fires channel.invokeMethod<void>('startForeground') unconditionally (lib/core/services/channel_adapters.dart:116); grep 'notification|tray|quick' finds no preference and no QuickSettings TileService anywhere. research/06-V2RayNG.md:448: foreground notification 'shows Connected: <remark> — ↑↓ MB/s with Disconnect action' — actionable notification is table stakes; research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:475: 'android.service.quicksettings.TileService subclass QuickToggleTileService.kt. Tap toggles VPN on/off'; research/01-Karing.md:575: 'Notification: Karing official / vpn provider notification' as a setting
findings.fix: Add notification preferences (show/hide, show speed, disconnect action) passed through startForeground; add a Quick Settings TileService in the Android plugin and a Windows tray icon with connect/disconnect menu.

findings.title: Firewall policy is a const Dart object with no user toggle — blockIpv6/allowLan/pinnedDns uneditable
findings.evidence: lib/modules/sec/firewall.dart:8-14 defines FirewallPolicy {blockIpv6: true, allowLan: false, allowPinnedDnsOnly: true, pinnedDns: ['172.19.0.1']} as a const with no store, no provider, and no screen (grep 'FirewallPolicy(' outside sec/ and main.dart's PolicyFirewallAdapter shows no user-driven construction); the LAN blocker at firewall.dart:70-75 means a printer or NAS is unreachable while tunneled and the user cannot change it. goal.md:12 brands 'max firewall' as a headline lock, and docs/prototype-final.html:339 shows the Security tile where toggles belong. research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:261 exposes the parity surface: 'Settings → App Mode → Lockdown → Allow LAN Traffic switch' — WG Tunnel ships
findings.fix: Persist FirewallPolicy fields to a store, expose Allow LAN and Block IPv6 switches on the settings screen (with the leak-warning copy), and pass the policy into PolicyFirewallAdapter and config assembly.

findings.title: No drag reorder or swipe actions — list order is import order and cannot be rearranged
findings.evidence: Karing's select_server screen supports 'drag-reorder' (research/01-Karing.md:545); v2rayNG has 'swipe-to-delete, drag-reorder subscriptions via SubscriptionsViewModel.swapSubscriptions()' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:452); Matsuri supports 'move profile between groups (drag-sort via ItemTouchHelper)' (research/13-Matsuri-SagerNet.md:387); Nekoray MANUAL groups are drag-drop reordered (research/04-Nekoray.md:367). The app's grep for ReorderableList|Dismissible|onReorder across lib/ matches nothing; endpoint rows expose only a trailing delete IconButton (endpoints_screen.dart:94-112) and EndpointStore persists the import-order list verbatim (endpoint_store.dart:17-25), so an accidental delete at po
findings.fix: Use ReorderableListView with a persisted order key on StoredEndpoint, and Dismissible/long-press actions for delete; also stops silent changes to the implicit 'first endpoint' selection.

findings.title: No bulk operations: single-item delete is the only action, no multi-select, no remove-duplicates or remove-unavailable
findings.evidence: Nekoray's group context menu offers 'Update Subscription, Export All, Copy All Links, Delete Duplicates, Sort' plus 'Remove Unavailable' regex removal (research/04-Nekoray.md:367,393); v2rayN supports 'multi-select nodes → Share → Export selected as Base64 subscription' (research/05-V2RayN.md:458). The app's EndpointsState holds only a List<StoredEndpoint> with no selection model (endpoints_controller.dart:31-43), and the only list mutation besides import is delete(int index) (endpoints_controller.dart:183-191). A dead subscription re-import leaves stale duplicates that must be deleted one tap at a time; a 200-node bundle cannot be pruned in bulk.
findings.fix: Long-press multi-select with select-all, bulk delete/export of selected nodes, and one-tap 'delete duplicates by tag/address' — the tag-merge logic from importText is already the dedupe primitive.

findings.title: No duplicate/clone of a server and no per-endpoint share/export (URI/QR/clipboard) — only the whole-store encrypted backup
findings.evidence: Matsuri supports 'copy/share profile (long-press → QR or clipboard URI)' (research/13-Matsuri-SagerNet.md:387); v2rayN offers 'Share → QR Code … Share → Copy Link' per node (research/05-V2RayN.md:458); v2rayNG 'Share → Export to Clipboard → FmtBase.toUri()' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:265). In the app there is no duplicate/copy/clone anywhere in endpoints_controller.dart (grep duplicate|clone|copyTo: none) and no share-link serialization for stored endpoints — the parsers in ingestion/parsers.dart only decode inbound URIs, and the sole export path is the whole-store encrypted .qnv backup (endpoints_screen.dart:127-160). Moving one AWG profile from phone to PC is impossible without exporting ever
findings.fix: Add a duplicate row action and a per-endpoint 'copy share URI' that inverts the existing per-protocol parsers (endpoint → uri), enabling device-to-device transfer without the full encrypted backup.

findings.title: No file or ZIP config import — ingestion is paste-text or single URL only
findings.evidence: Karing 'My Profiles → Add Profiles — supports: paste URL, paste content, scan QR, import from file, import ZIP' (research/01-Karing.md:381); v2rayNG 'File: Import from file → ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:265); Throne adds 'Multiple file selection for importing from file' (research/02-Throne.md:413). The app's _ImportBox is a 3-line paste TextField (endpoints_screen.dart:296-308) whose importText fetches only when the entire trimmed input is a single http(s) URL (endpoints_controller.dart:93-103); file_picker appears exclusively in the backup export/import flows for .qnv (endpoints_screen.dart:98,142). A user with a .conf WireGuard file, a Clash .yaml, or a provider ZIP canno
findings.fix: Add an 'Import from file' button (multi-select .conf/.yaml/.json/.txt/.zip) that pipes picked file bytes into the existing IngestionAdapter — the parsers already handle WG INI, Clash YAML, and sing-box JSON payloads.

findings.title: No diagnostics export/share — the health snapshot, hijack verdict, and ping history cannot leave the screen
findings.evidence: grep for `Clipboard|share_plus|Share\.` across lib/ returns zero matches, and the DIAGNOSTICS screen has no export affordance at all (only a Refresh IconButton, diagnostics_screen.dart:39-46); the HealthReport (score/hijacked/pingMs/stability) is recomputed every 10s and discarded. SPEC.md:246 makes Drift persistence part of the Health deep module, and a diagnostic that cannot be saved defeats the purpose for a censored user asking a support channel 'is my ISP hijacking DNS right now?'. Competitors: WireSock's pcap logging writes captures to %TEMP% for offline triage (research/10-WireSock.md:659) and Exclave bundles PCAP as a preference (research/08-Exclave.md:466); even this repo's encrypte
findings.fix: Add an export action next to Refresh that serializes the HealthReport + last N log lines to clipboard or a picked file, mirroring the backup exportBytes/FilePicker.saveFile flow.

findings.title: No engine log-level control — DEBUG/TRACE verbosity toggle missing, so FATAL-adjacent detail cannot be reproduced for a bug report
findings.evidence: The engine log arrives on box_events ('log' events, channel_adapters.dart:52) at whatever the Go CommandServer emits; there is no UI or setting to request DEBUG/TRACE level, and only two UI segments exist (all/errors). Tasks/progress-2026-09-03.md:18 even lists 'log level filter/search/export' as an unstarted leftover.
