findings.title: _semverKey silently ignores pubspec build suffix — restart/update comparison can misjudge builds
findings.evidence: Code claim (updater.dart:25-29): "isNewerThan(String localVersion) => _semverKey(version).compareTo(_semverKey(localVersion)) > 0" with `core = version.replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^v'), '').split('-').first` — only the prerelease suffix is stripped; the pubspec build suffix (+N) is not. Reality: `_semverKey('1.0.0+1')`: parts = ['1','0','0+1'], int.tryParse('0+1') = null -> 0, so the build identifier is silently dropped (no crash, no error). Local '1.0.1+1' vs remote 'v1.0.1' compare equal, so a rebuilt +2 APK with a stale tag is "up to date"; buildNumber is never compared anywhere (grep: only version flows through main.dart:121 and updates_controller.dart:92).
findings.fix: Strip build suffix too: `version.split('+').first.split('-').first` before the 3-part key, and (optionally) compare buildNumber as a tie-breaker for identical 3-part versions. Add a unit test for '1.0.1+1' vs 'v1.0.1' semantics.

findings.title: sha256 release files use two different JSON schemas and the updater verifies neither
findings.evidence: Reality: build-windows.yml:59 writes `@{ "qanatvpn_v${v}_windows-x64.zip" = $hash } | ConvertTo-Json` (object map, hash UPPERCASE->lower), while build-android.yml:112 writes `sha256sum "$name" >> sha256-android.json` producing raw sha256sum lines like `<hash>  qanatvpn_v0.1.0_arm64-v8a.apk` — two incompatible schemas under sibling names. Doc claim (updater.dart:40-42): "Parsed GitHub release + platform-aware asset selection... 6h stale-while-revalidate cache" and platformFilters at :55-60 list only name fragments — no sha256 verification anywhere in lib/ (grep: no 'sha256' in lib). AGENTS.md:113 claims tags produce "`latest.json` + `sha256`" implying a coherent integrity story.
findings.fix: Standardize one schema (recommend the map form {filename: sha256} in both files, or plain sha256sum text in both) and note it in the updater docs; when the updater gains install verification it should consume the release's sha256-<platform>.json for the chosen asset.

findings.title: gh-pages deploy can ship without latest.json by design, and the actual run failed leaving the site 404
findings.evidence: Code claim (gh-pages.yml:29-33): "Mirror latest.json straight from the release the metadata job attached (single producer: build-android metadata job)... `gh release download ... || echo 'latest.json not on release yet — site ships without it'`". Reality: gh-pages run 33900799115 (push, tag v0.1.0) FAILED at the deploy job (`gh api .../runs/33900799115/jobs` -> {"conclusion":"failure","name":"deploy","steps":[]}); Pages API shows build_type=workflow yet `curl -sI https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/` -> HTTP/1.1 404. Even on success, the race is structural: build-android's metadata waits up to 2400s for the Windows zip, but gh-pages starts in parallel and downloads nothing if the metadata job
findings.fix: Sequence the site deploy: make gh-pages `needs` the latest.json producer (split metadata into its own workflow and trigger gh-pages via workflow_run after it succeeds), drop the soft-fail `|| echo`, and fail loudly if site/latest.json is missing so a Pages deploy never publishes a mirror-less site. Diagnose the current deploy failure (logs expired

findings.title: Shipped app presents zero license information: no LicensePage/LicenseRegistry/showLicensePage anywhere in lib/, so Flutter (BSD-3) and pub package notices are never conveyed

The distributed Windows zip bundles flutter_windows.dll and 157 packages' code; BSD-3 packages (including Flutter itself) condition binary redistribution on reproducing the copyright notice "in the documentation and/or other materials provided with the distribution". Also `gh api repos/SagerNet/sing-box --jq .license.spdx_id` → NOASSERTION, so GitHub detection should not be trusted over the LICENSE file. Wrong license facts in the compatibility analysis can misdirect future compliance work (e.g., assuming AWG parts impose

findings.title: leak_test.sh not runnable as documented on either platform: wlan0 capture requires root (Termux lacks it), Git Bash lacks tcpdump/ip/ss, and scenario 6 is an admitted placeholder
findings.evidence: Doc (leak_test.sh:3): `# Run on-device (Android: adb shell termux / Windows: Git Bash as admin).` Reality: capturing on `$PHYS_IF` (default wlan0, line 8) with tcpdump requires root/CAP_NET_RAW — a Termux shell on a non-rooted Android cannot sniff wlan0, so the Android path needs an undisclosed rooted device; Git Bash has no tcpdump, no `ip` command (scenario 3's handoff simulation is only a comment: '# simulate switch: (ip link set $PHYS_IF down/up here in a lab)'), no `ss` (scenario 6), and Windows `ping` does not accept `-c 30`. Scenario 6 is an admitted placeholder inside a release-blocking suite (line 58: `# Placeholder: verify with `ss -tnp` that bypass app's remote is not via tun.`) —
findings.fix: State the root-device precondition in the header, replace the placeholder scenario with a real per-app check (netstat -an + UID mapping via dumpsys, or drop it to explicit TODO), and generate traffic inside each scenario instead of passive-only captures.

findings.title: Makefile TAGS_LEGACY filter-out is a no-op on the comma-joined single-word list, so make lib_legacy builds WITH with_naive_outbound (diverges from libbox.ps1 and the fork recipe it claims to mirror)
findings.evidence: Makefile:15 `TAGS_LEGACY := $(filter-out with_naive_outbound,$(TAGS_MAIN))` — TAGS_MAIN (line 13) is a single comma-joined word containing no spaces, and GNU make filter-out compares whole whitespace-separated words, so the pattern never matches and TAGS_LEGACY == TAGS_MAIN (with_naive_outbound still present). The two sibling implementations both strip it correctly: scripts/libbox.ps1 line 15 `$tagsLegacy = $tagsMain -replace 'with_naive_outbound,', ''` and the fork recipe this mirrors (build_libbox main.go:80 `filterTags` + line 188 legacy variant, commented 'legacy variant (SDK 21, no naive outbound)'). Net: `make lib_legacy` emits a legacy aar with naive outbound that the documented recip
findings.fix: Use `TAGS_LEGACY := $(subst with_naive_outbound,,subst-double-comma...)` or simply `TAGS_LEGACY := $(TAGS_MAIN),minus...` — simplest: `TAGS_LEGACY := $(TAGS_MAIN:with_naive_outbound,=)` (subst on the literal 'with_naive_outbound,'), matching the ps1 regex.

findings.title: SPEC declares the legacy aar dead weight ('no legacy aar'), yet Makefile and libbox.ps1 still build and document libbox-legacy.aar (API 21 vs minSdk 24)

findings.title: gh-pages snapshots latest.json at tag-push time with a silent fallback — the mirror would be missing even if deploys were allowed
findings.evidence: Doc: gh-pages.yml:26-28 "# Mirror latest.json straight from the release the metadata job attached (single producer: build-android metadata job)" with fallback line 33 `|| echo "latest.json not on release yet — site ships without it"`. Reality: gh-pages triggers on `push: tags` at the same instant as build-android, whose metadata job `needs: apk` and waits up to 40 min for windows assets — by the time latest.json exists the site artifact was uploaded seconds after checkout. Even a green run publishes without the mirror.
findings.fix: Either poll `gh release download` for latest.json (retry up to ~45 min, then fail loudly instead of `|| echo`), or trigger the site deploy from metadata completion via workflow_run so ordering is guaranteed.

findings.title: Tracked binary libbox-sources.jar (131 KB) is generated output unreferenced by any build file
findings.evidence: Doc claim: AGENTS.md Build commands "make -C go/amnezia-box lib_android && cp go/amnezia-box/libbox.aar android/app/libs/" (sources jar never mentioned). Reality: android/app/libs/libbox-sources.jar is 130,753 bytes, 4th-largest tracked blob; `grep -rn "libbox-sources" --include=*.kts --include=*.gradle --include=*.yml` → no references anywhere (build.gradle.kts, CI workflows, Makefile all ignore it); jar holds 157 uncompiled .java files (344 KB unpacked) generated by the gomobile bind step.

findings.title: master branch has zero protection while AGENTS.md documents 'main' as the workflow branch
findings.evidence: Doc claim: AGENTS.md:113 "Branch: `main` + feature branches feat/<module-id>". Reality: `gh api repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn --jq .default_branch` → "master"; `gh api .../branches/master/protection` → 404 {"message":"Branch not protected"}. With CI publishing releases on tag push, an accidental force-push to master rewrites the release source of truth; the doc's branch name also misleads contributors (and the repo owner) about workflow.
findings.fix: Either rename master→main to match the documented workflow or update AGENTS.md; then enable branch protection on master: require PRs before merging (or at minimum block force-pushes/deletions) and restrict tag creation for v* patterns. Single-maintainer repos typically pick force-push protection only.

findings.title: Version skew: pubspec 1.0.0+1 vs release tag v0.1.0 — updater semver compare makes the release never 'newer'
findings.evidence: pubspec.yaml:4 'version: 1.0.0+1'; release tag/asset = v0.1.0 (gh api: name 'v0.1.0', asset 'qanatvpn_v0.1.0_windows-x64.zip'); metadata job writes latest.json {'version': tag} per build-android.yml python block. updater.dart:26-29 `isNewerThan` → `_semverKey(version).compareTo(_semverKey(localVersion)) > 0` with `_semverKey('v0.1.0') = 0.1.0 < 1.0.0` → any installed 1.0.0 build never sees v0.1.0 (or later 0.x) as an update; About screen would report 1.0.0 while the site shows 'Latest release: v0.1.0'.
findings.fix: Align pubspec version with the release channel (0.1.0+1 for v0.1.0) or generate tags from pubspec version in CI; add a test pinning latest.json version ≥ pubspec version.

findings.title: Workflow is un-failable by construction, masking any upstream problem even after registration

findings.fix: Make drift a hard failure (non-zero exit when upstream head != pinned SHA), remove the || true, and add an explicit permissions: block (least privilege, e.g. contents:read) so future PR-automation changes are deliberate.

findings.title: sha256 artifact format drift across jobs: sha256-android.json is raw sha256sum lines (not JSON) while sha256-windows.json is a real JSON map
findings.evidence: Doc side (implicit contract): both jobs attach a 'sha256-*.json' release asset (SPEC.md:405 promises "with sha256 + latest.json"). Reality: build-android.yml:112 — "sha256sum \"$name\" >> sha256-android.json" produces raw sha256sum text lines (<hash>  <file>), which is not valid JSON despite the .json extension; build-windows.yml:59 — "@{ \"qanatvpn_v${v}_windows-x64.zip\" = $hash } | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content sha256-windows.json" produces a real single-line JSON object. A consumer parsing both uniformly (or parsing the android file as JSON) fails.
findings.fix: Generate sha256-android.json as a JSON object with the same shape as windows (e.g. printf '%s\n' "$name" | jq -R --arg h "$(sha256sum "$name" | cut -d' ' -f1)" '{($argv[1]): $h}' style, or python -c json.dump) so both per-platform hash files share one schema.

findings.title: Updater assumes universal APKs while CI builds split-per-ABI APKs: non-arm64 devices are served an arm64 APK they cannot install
findings.evidence: Reality: lib/modules/updates/updater.dart:211-213 — "no caller supplies it today (universal-APK releases make arm64 the correct default; wire Android abiList into the dispatcher when per-ABI splits land)"; resolvePlatformKey returns 'android-arm64' for any Android device when androidAbi is null. Reality in CI: build-android.yml:91 `flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi` produces three ABI-specific APKs (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64), each containing only its ABI's libbox.so. An armeabi-v7a or x86_64 user following the in-app update prompt installs the arm64-only APK and gets a silent 'App not installed' / instant crash on start.
findings.fix: Wire the device ABI into resolvePlatformKey at the update-check call site (the seam already exists), or emit a universal APK alongside the splits so arm64-default is actually correct.

findings.title: metadata job (latest.json single producer) is gated `needs: apk`, so any android failure kills latest.json for ALL platforms
findings.evidence: Doc: build-android.yml:114-116 comment 'Single producer of latest.json: waits until BOTH platform jobs have attached their assets, then builds the merged platform map from the release's real asset list' and AGENTS.md:46 '+ `latest.json` + `sha256`'. Reality: jobs JSON for run 33900799214 shows metadata conclusion 'skipped' (needs: apk, line 127-128), so even though build-windows succeeded and attached qanatvpn_v0.1.0_windows-x64.zip + sha256-windows.json, no latest.json was ever produced; the release asset list has no latest.json and https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/latest.json returns HTTP 404 (verified by curl). One android-only failure therefore disables the updater feed for all platforms
findings.fix: Give the metadata job `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` and build the platform map from whatever assets the release actually has (the python already filters), or move latest.json production to a separate workflow_run-triggered job so a windows-only release still publishes a windows-only map.

findings.title: Updater semver compare discards pre-release suffixes: v0.2.0-rc.1 outranks nothing and blocks its own stable v0.2.0
findings.evidence: Doc: test/updater/updater_test.dart:130 group 'UpdateInfo.semver' / :404 "semver compare" (SPEC.md). Reality: updater.dart:30 `final core = version.replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^v'), '').split('-').first;` discards everything after '-': _semverKey('0.2.0-rc.1') == _semverKey('0.2.0') == 2000. Consequence: a v0.2.0-rc.1 release is offered to v0.1.0 users (RC pushed to stable channel), and after installing it, the stable v0.2.0 tag is isNewerThan == false, so RC users are never offered the stable fix.
findings.fix: Either implement prerelease ordering in _semverKey (bit-flag: prerelease sorts below release) and add a test case, or document in AGENTS.md Git-workflow that release tags must never carry pre-release suffixes (gate: CI rejects tag names matching v*-rc*/*-beta*).

findings.title: gh-pages '|| echo' swallow plus same-tag race: even a green pipeline ships the site without latest.json
findings.evidence: DOC: gh-pages.yml:29 — "Mirror latest.json straight from the release the metadata job attached (single producer: build-android metadata job)." REALITY: gh-pages.yml:32-33 — `--pattern 'latest.json' --output site/latest.json || echo "latest.json not on release yet — site ships without it"`. Both workflows fire on tag push (build-android.yml:4-5, gh-pages.yml:4-5); the metadata job can wait up to 2400s for the windows asset (build-android.yml:135-141) while gh-pages deploys in seconds — so even on a fully green pipeline the site can permanently ship without latest.json for that tag, with only the echo as a trace. The `|| echo` converts the failure this audit observed (release with no latest.js
findings.fix: Make gh-pages run_after the metadata job (workflow_run trigger or needs via a reusable workflow) and fail the deploy if latest.json is absent, instead of the || echo swallow.

findings.evidence: Doc: "VPN Research/  (repo root — no empty dirs)"; "├── todo.md  # 16 tasks ≤5 files each"; lib/, android/, go/, rule_sets/, .github/workflows/ listed under "(future — create on demand per todo, not now)" with "YAGNI enforcement: No `lib/`, `android/`, `go/`, `rule_sets/` until `todo:1-2` touches them"; handoff.md/progress-*.md/decisions.tsv marked "future". Reality: actual root is E:/code/Qanat-VPN (remote QMahyar/qanatvpn); `ls lib/` → app, core, l10n, main.dart, modules, utils; android/app/libs/libbox.aar, go/amnezia-box/ (SHA 57276220, tag 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15), rule_sets/initial_assets/ and 5 workflow files all exist; tasks/ has handoff.md, 5 progress files (08-30..09-04), decisions.tsv l

findings.title: AWG 3.0 keepalive range `PersistentKeepalive = min-max` is silently truncated to the lower bound (sing-box JSON path) or fails the whole import (INI path); the fork accepts the range form
findings.evidence: PROBE: awg peer with "persistent_keepalive_interval":"25-35" -> EXIT=0; the fork's AwgKeepalive unmarshals both `uint16` and `"min-max"` strings (go/amnezia-box/option/awg.go:73-102: 'AWG 3.0 made it a range... draws a fresh value inside the range'). Ingestion: INI `PersistentKeepalive = 20-30` -> intOf('20-30') throws FormatException 'bad number in keepalive' (parsers.dart:31-37 at case :950) so the whole import fails; sing-box JSON awg endpoints -> _keepaliveInt returns int.tryParse(value.split('-').first) = 20 (parsers.dart:563), silently pinning the draw to the range lower bound. Model type int? (WireGuardPeer.persistentKeepalive) blocks pass-through; emitter sends int only (awg_config.d
findings.fix: Make persistentKeepalive a String (or add an isRange flag) in WireGuardPeer, emit it verbatim (AwgKeepalive accepts number and "min-max"), and replace the INI intOf call with a range-aware parse.

findings.title: Import->store->emit pipeline performs zero peer validation: keepalive -1/70000 FATALs at decode on connect, port 0 and empty peer address ship silently
findings.evidence: PROBEs on the exact emitter output shapes: persistent_keepalive_interval=70000 -> EXIT=1 `FATAL decode config: endpoints[0].peers[0].persistent_keepalive_interval: expected a number or a "min-max" range` (uint16 bound in AwgKeepalive/WireGuardPeer); -1 -> EXIT=1 same. port=0 -> EXIT=0 (ships; runtime dials :0, endpoint dead); peer address="" -> EXIT=0 (ships). AWG INI `PersistentKeepalive = 70000` parses fine via intOf (parsers.dart:31-37, no range check) and persists through EndpointsController.import -> store -> wireGuardEndpointToJson on every connect. AwgConfig.validate (key format, endpoint host:port, Jc/S/H ranges) exists but is only called by the AWG preset sheet (awg_profile_screen.d
findings.fix: Validate WireGuardEndpoint material (keepalive 0-65535, peer endpoint host:port, port 1-65535) before persisting in EndpointsController.import, or route stored endpoints through AwgConfig-style validation at emit and skip/refuse invalid ones.

findings.title: Stored endpoint tag colliding with the vendored profile's endpoint tag (e.g. user imports/renames to 'awg-hkg-02') FATALs every connect — merge prepends endpoints without tag-collision check
findings.evidence: PROBE: two awg endpoints both tagged awg-hkg-02 -> EXIT=1 `FATAL decode config at dup_tags.json: duplicate outbound/endpoint tag: awg-hkg-02` (check-time error, not just runtime). profile_config_source.dart:241 prepends `...wgEndpoints` before `profile['endpoints']` with no uniqueness check, and the selector prepended-member dedup (line ~275) only dedups member tags. EndpointsController.import dedupes by tag only against other stored entries (endpoints_controller.dart:131-155), never against the vendored profile's `endpoints` (profiles/config.wg-awg.json tag `awg-hkg-02`) nor against group tags. A single imported/renamed colliding endpoint breaks every connect until manually removed. Fix: on
findings.fix: In _merged, skip/rename stored endpoints whose tag collides with the base profile's endpoints or outbound tags, and surface the collision in the endpoints UI.

findings.title: sing-box JSON import silently drops `type: "wireguard"` endpoints (only 'awg' is read) and legacy wireguard outbounds — imported config loses the endpoint with no error
findings.evidence: SingboxJsonParser handles only `node['type'] == 'awg'` from the top-level endpoints array (parsers.dart:305) — a standard sing-box 1.11+ `type: "wireguard"` endpoint block (the upstream canonical form, schema probed EXIT=0 on this binary with pre_shared_key/reserved/udp_timeout) is silently skipped; legacy `type: "wireguard"` in outbounds[] also returns null (no wireguard case in _outbound, default at parsers.dart:497-499). So a WG node in a sing-box config import vanishes with no error and no item in the failure count ('no endpoints found' only fires when EVERYTHING failed). The _awgEndpoint handler (parsers.dart:507) is a near drop-in for the wireguard type (same shape minus amnezia keys).
findings.fix: In SingboxJsonParser.parse, accept endpoints where type is 'awg' OR 'wireguard' (reuse _awgEndpoint with awg: null), and treat outbounds[] wireguard nodes as unsupported-with-counted-error rather than silent null.

findings.title: packet_encoding never emitted — vmess UDP packet encoding falls back to legacy/none (fork accepts xudp/packetaddr)
findings.evidence: Probe: vmess outbound with "packet_encoding":"xudp" → EXIT=0 (accepted). Fork protocol/vmess/outbound.go switch on options.PacketEncoding: "" → neither packetAddr nor xudp (legacy UDP path); upstream vmess outbound docs list packet_encoding with '(none) Disabled | packetaddr | xudp'. The assignment's emit shape (uuid, security auto/zero, alter_id 0, packet_encoding) is missing this key entirely, so vmess UDP relay (QUIC/games over the tunnel) runs the legacy encoding instead of xudp like every other mainstream client default.
findings.fix: Emit 'packet_encoding': 'xudp' by default for vmess outbounds (or expose a per-endpoint option mapping to packetaddr/xudp).

findings.title: xhttp download split sub-transport unsupported end-to-end: parser drops it, emitter never produces it (x_padding_bytes mandatory inside download — probed)
findings.evidence: Fork _V2RayXHTTPOptions has Download *V2RayXHTTPDownloadOptions and checkV2RayXHTTPBaseOptions runs on the download block too. Probes: download sub-block WITHOUT x_padding_bytes → EXIT=1 `FATAL decode config: outbounds[0].transport: x_padding_bytes cannot be disabled` (p24); WITH "100-1000" → EXIT=0 (p25). TransportOptions (normalized_endpoint.dart:57) has no download fields, SingboxJsonParser._transport drops `download` silently, and the emitter's mandatory x_padding_bytes hardcode ('100-1000', verified load-bearing: top-level xhttp without it → EXIT=1 same error, p9) exists only in the top-level block — so an imported xhttp+download node silently loses its download transport and the FATAL
findings.fix: Either add download fields to TransportOptions (path/host/mode/x_padding_bytes minimum) and always emit x_padding_bytes inside the download block too, or explicitly document the limitation; today the silent drop at least keeps the FATAL unreachable.

findings.title: Trojan grpc serviceName query param dropped — emits type-only {"type":"grpc"}
findings.evidence: PROBE (real emitter): link 'trojan://hunter2@203.0.113.10:443?type=grpc&serviceName=grpc-svc#tag1' → {"transport":{"type":"grpc"}}. TrojanUriParser only builds TransportOptions for type==ws (parsers.dart:801-813); network='grpc' reaches _resolveTransport which fabricates TransportOptions(type:'grpc', serviceName: wsPath) with wsPath null (endpoint_outbound.dart:99), so service_name is emitted empty. Engine check passes (EXIT=0) but grpc service routing silently changes — servers requiring a named service cannot connect. Same for clash trojan grpc-opts (never read).
findings.fix: In TrojanUriParser, when query['type']=='grpc', build TransportOptions(type:'grpc', serviceName: query['serviceName'] ?? query['path']); for clash trojan read grpc-opts.grpc-service-name.

findings.title: No SS method/2022-psk validation before emit — wrong-length psk or unknown cipher FATALs the entire profile at engine init
findings.evidence: Emitters pass e.method/e.password through with no validation (endpoint_outbound.dart:116-128). PROBES (windows/sing-box.exe check): {method:'2022-blake3-aes-256-gcm', password:'shortkey'} → FATAL initialize outbound[0]: bad key length, required 32, got 6 (EXIT=1); method 'chacha20' → FATAL unknown method: chacha20 (EXIT=1). Valid 32-byte psk and legacy aes-256-cfb pass (EXIT=0). Fork enum (go/amnezia-box/option/shadowsocks.go:24): none + AEAD + 2022-blake3 family + legacy ctr/cfb/rc4-md5/chacha20-ietf/xchacha20; 2022 psks are base64 of 16 (aes-128) / 32 (aes-256, chacha20) bytes. Ingest accepts any string; engine FATAL kills the entire profile at start (fail-closed but total).
findings.fix: Validate at ingest/emit against the fork enum and 2022 key lengths (base64-decoded length 16/24/32B per method); reject/flag the node with a surfaced error instead of shipping a profile that FATALs.

findings.title: udp_over_tcp silently dropped when importing sing-box JSON (model has no field; re-emit loses it)
findings.evidence: PROBE (real emitter): sing-box JSON node with 'udp_over_tcp': true → parsed and re-emitted WITHOUT the field ({"re_emitted":{"type":"shadowsocks",...no udp_over_tcp}}). ENGINE: both legacy bool form and {"enabled":true} pass check (EXIT=0) on this fork, and option/shadowsocks.go:33 still carries UDPOverTCP *UDPOverTCPOptions — so the drop is a real behavior change (client stops wrapping UDP in UoT against servers that require it), not dead-field cleanup. Multiplex is dropped by the same model gap.
findings.fix: Add udpOverTcp (and consider multiplex) fields to ShadowsocksEndpoint + store/emit, or document the intentional drop in normalizedToJson so it stops being silent.

findings.title: Clash YAML trojan with network:'ws' emits bare {"type":"ws"} — ws-opts never parsed for trojan
findings.evidence: PROBE (real emitter): TrojanEndpoint(network:'ws', no transport) → {"transport":{"type":"ws"}} — the exact bare-ws shape decisions.tsv:79 says was fixed for share links; the clash path still produces it because ClashYamlParser trojan reads only name/server/port/password/sni/network/skip-cert-verify. Engine check passes (EXIT=0 probed) so the node dials default path '/' with no Host header — servers routing on path/host silently break.
findings.fix: Read node['ws-opts'] (path + headers.Host) and node['grpc-opts'] for clash trojan into TransportOptions, mirroring the vmess case.

findings.title: TUIC zero_rtt_handshake/heartbeat/udp_over_stream (and hy2 hop_interval_max, disable_chrome_parrot, network) are dropped on import and can never be emitted, though the engine accepts them
findings.evidence: Fork option/tuic.go TUICOutboundOptions declares ZeroRTTHandshake, Heartbeat, UDPOverStream; probes: {zero_rtt_handshake: true, heartbeat: '10s'} EXIT=0, udp_over_stream true EXIT=0. Hy2: hop_interval_max '60s' EXIT=0, disable_chrome_parrot true EXIT=0 (both new in 1.14 per upstream doc). TuicEndpoint/Hysteria2Endpoint models lack these fields, SingboxJsonParser never reads them, and _tuic/_hysteria2 never emit them — so a tuic node imported with zero_rtt_handshake: true round-trips to 0-RTT disabled and no heartbeat (slower handshakes, dead-session behavior change). Assignment-named zero_rtt_handshake verified: engine accepts it, emitter cannot produce it.
findings.fix: Add zeroRttHandshake/heartbeatSeconds (tuic) and hopIntervalMaxSeconds/disableChromeParrot (hy2) to the models + JSON import/export + emitter; gate udp_over_stream behind the existing udp_relay_mode conflict rule (fork errors when both set).

findings.title: hy2 obfs type is coerced to salamander: a gecko node (fork+docs supported, sing-box 1.14) imports with the wrong obfs and cannot connect
findings.evidence: Parser reads only the password: obfsPassword: query['obfs-password'] (parsers.dart:843) / Clash (node['obfs'] as YamlMap)?['password'] (parsers.dart:198); emitter hardcodes {'type': 'salamander', 'password': obfsPassword} (endpoint_outbound.dart:154-155). Fork option/hysteria2.go enum 'salamander,gecko' and upstream 1.14 doc list obfs.type 'salamander gecko' with gecko-only min/max_packet_size (defaults 512/1200); probe {type: gecko, password: y, min_packet_size: 10, max_packet_size: 100} -> EXIT=0. A gecko link imports as a salamander client: obfs mismatch means the server cannot de-obfuscate the QUIC initial -> total connection failure, silently misconfigured rather than erroring at import
findings.fix: Carry obfs type (and gecko min/max) through the model; when the parsed type is unknown/unsupported, drop the obfs block or fail the line with FormatException instead of emitting a mismatched salamander.

findings.title: hy2 pinSHA256 (official URI cert-pinning param) is silently dropped although the engine supports tls.certificate_public_key_sha256
findings.evidence: Hysteria2UriParser reads only sni/obfs-password/mport/hopIntervalSeconds/insecure (parsers.dart:839-846); Dart probe confirms pinSHA256 lands in queryParameters (keys: [insecure, pinSHA256]). Fork option/tls.go:120 CertificatePublicKeySHA256 badoption.Listable[[]byte] json:"certificate_public_key_sha256"; probe tls.certificate_public_key_sha256 [base64] under a hysteria2 outbound -> EXIT=0. Upstream hysteria2's URI schema uses pinSHA256 as the safe alternative to insecure=1; after import the user either must enable insecure (MITM-able) or cannot connect at all, with no error shown.
findings.fix: Parse pinSHA256 (repeatable param) into a tlsPins list on Hysteria2Endpoint and emit tls.certificate_public_key_sha256 (probed-accepted base64 form).

findings.title: Clash hy2 with scalar obfs (obfs: salamander) throws uncaught TypeError — whole import fails (same TypeError-DoS class P1 fixed elsewhere)
findings.evidence: Real Dart run with repo's yaml package: `node['obfs'] as YamlMap?` on obfs: salamander throws '_TypeError: type 'String' is not a subtype of type 'YamlMap?' in type cast'. The cast is not in the hardened stringField/intField helpers (decisions.tsv:72 records this exact class was fixed for ports/ciphers), so one scalar obfs field makes the entire import fail with a raw TypeError string in the error state.
findings.fix: Accept scalar obfs: treat a String value as the obfs type (salamander/gecko) with password from obfs-password, or throw FormatException for a clear per-line failure.

findings.title: urltest model gap: OutboundGroup.urlTest cannot express engine-accepted idle_timeout or interrupt_exist_connections (selector has the latter); both emitter sites consistently omit both
findings.evidence: OutboundGroup.urlTest constructor (routing_policy.dart:56-64) exposes only url/interval/tolerance and hardcodes `interruptExistConnections = false`; there is no idleTimeout field. Both emitter sites are mutually consistent (routing_compiler.dart:100-108 and profile_config_source.dart:302-313 emit identical url/interval/tolerance, and selector emits interrupt_exist_connections at both — routing_compiler.dart:119-120, profile_config_source.dart:317-318), but urltest cannot express two engine-accepted fields. Fork struct option/group.go URLTestOutboundOptions has `IdleTimeout badoption.Duration` + `InterruptExistConnections bool`; real-binary probe with idle_timeout:"30m" + interrupt_exist_conn
findings.fix: Add idleTimeout + interruptExistConnections to OutboundGroup.urlTest, persist them in PolicyDocument (_groupToJson/_groupFromJson, policy_store.dart:69-104), and emit them at BOTH sites (routing_compiler.dart urltest branch and profile_config_source._groupJson) — exactly the dual-site update handoff.md:14 anticipates.

findings.title: FakeIP always-on but experimental.cache_file.store_fakeip never emitted: connections to stale fake IPs abort after every engine restart
findings.evidence: grep 'experimental|cache_file|store_fakeip' over lib/ → no matches; assembler build() emits only log/dns/inbounds/outbounds/endpoints/route and profiles/config.wg-awg.json has no experimental block. Fork dns/transport/fakeip/store.go:66-71 uses cacheFile storage only when cacheFile.StoreFakeIP(), else NewMemoryStorage() (in-memory, wiped each boot). Fork route/route.go:545-548: for EVERY routed connection, if the destination is inside the fakeip range (Store().Contains is a range check, store.go:118-121) it looks up the mapping and on miss returns fatalErr = E.New("missing fakeip record, try enable `experimental.cache_file`") — aborting the connection. Windows first-pp: client DNS caches sur
findings.fix: Add an experimental block: {cache_file: {enabled: true, path: <app dir>, store_fakeip: true}} on both emit paths (assembler + vendored profile). Probe first: check passes with an experimental.cache_file block (schema per option/experimental.go StoreFakeIP).

findings.title: dns.reverse_mapping never emitted: real-IP connections (dns-local path: geosite-cn split, clash Direct) carry no domain metadata, so domain-based route rules never match them
findings.evidence: DnsConfig.toDnsJson emits only servers/rules/final/strategy; RawDNSOptions has ReverseMapping (option/dns.go:15) and probe p5b (dns block with reverse_mapping:true) → exit 0. Fork route/route.go:559-565: for non-fakeip destinations metadata.Domain is populated only via r.dns.LookupReverseMapping, which is nil unless reverse_mapping is enabled (dns/router.go:116-117). No sniff action is emitted either. Consequence: everything resolved via dns-local (geosite-cn split + clash Direct) produces real-IP connections with no domain metadata, so domain/rule_set(domain) route rules can never match them — the vendored profile's {domain_suffix:[cn], rule_set:[geosite-cn,geoip-cn]} DIRECT rule survives o
findings.fix: Emit reverse_mapping: true in the dns block (probed accepted, p5b exit 0), or add a first route rule {action: sniff} so SNI supplies domain metadata; document the tradeoff (upstream notes system-proxied DNS can hinder reverse mapping).

findings.title: Clash vmess reality-opts + client-fingerprint dropped (Reality-over-vmess nodes import as plain vmess)
findings.evidence: Probe (dart harness): clash vmess with reality-opts{public-key,short-id} + client-fingerprint:chrome (mihomo supports Reality-over-vmess, wiki.metacubex.one vmess TLS fields) → EMIT '{"type":"vmess",...,"tls":{"enabled":true,"server_name":...},"transport":{...}}' — no reality, no utls; _vmess (endpoint_outbound.dart:68) never emits utls/reality at all, so even if parsed, vmess Reality cannot round-trip today. Contrast: the vless:// URI parser and sing-box JSON parser both capture these fields into the model.
findings.fix: Short term: read reality-opts/client-fingerprint in the clash vmess case (requires giving VmessEndpoint reality/utls fields or normalizing to vless-style emit). Until the emit side gains vmess-Reality support, drop the node with a per-node warning instead of importing a dead profile.

findings.title: One unsupported/malformed proxy node aborts the ENTIRE clash subscription import (all-or-nothing, competitors skip bad nodes)
findings.evidence: Probes (dart harness over IngestionAdapter.parseAndNormalize): a 3-node list (trojan + socks5 + http) → 'ADAPTER ERROR: FormatException: clash: unsupported type "socks5"' — zero endpoints imported, the good trojan is discarded; a trojan+tuic list where tuic lacks uuid → 'ADAPTER ERROR: FormatException: missing sing-box uuid' (error text also names the wrong dialect for a clash source). endpoints_controller.dart:161 catches as a whole-import failure. Clash bundles in the wild routinely contain socks5/http/ssr/snell/anytls/mieru nodes (mihomo supports ~20 types; the parser handles 7), so a single unsupported entry makes the whole provider un-importable. Competitor behavior per repo research: K
findings.fix: Wrap the per-node _proxy call in try/catch inside ClashYamlParser.parse, skip failed nodes (collect a warnings list the UI can surface), and reserve FormatException for structural YAML errors only. Optionally map type http→http outbound and socks5→direct-with-warning rather than throwing.

findings.title: Clash YAML support exists and is wired (gap half of the assignment resolved: NOT absent) — confirming the integration surface for the findings above
findings.evidence: README-level check per assignment: pubspec.yaml:32 declares yaml ^3.1.4 and parsers.dart:3 imports package:yaml; endpoints_screen.dart:25 and endpoints_controller.dart:58 document clash YAML as a supported import format, and test/ingestion/ingestion_test.dart:184 has a 'clash yaml' group. The gap is not presence but depth: against the mihomo documented field set, the parser maps only name/server/port/uuid/flow/cipher/alterId/tls/servername/sni/network/skip-cert-verify/plugin/password/auth/up/down/ports/hop-interval/obfs(broken)/private-key/peers/mtu/amnezia-wg-option — every *-opts sub-block (ws headers, grpc, h2, http, xhttp, reality, shadow-tls, restls, smux) is silently discarded. So the
findings.fix: No new dependency needed. Prioritize the critical/high fixes in this list, ordered by real-world blast radius: hy2 obfs crash (line 198) and bare-IP FATAL (line 234) first, then reality/transport/ss-plugin mapping.

findings.title: S1/S2 upper bound 0-1500 is narrower than engine uint16 (0-65535), and S3/S4 are never range-checked despite the editor exposing them
findings.evidence: Probes: s1=2000 STARTED OK, s1=65535 STARTED OK, s1=65536 -> "failed to parse s1: strconv.ParseUint: parsing \"65536\": value out of range" (ParseUint(value,10,16) in device/uapi.go); s3=65535 STARTED OK, s3=70000 -> "failed to parse s3: value out of range". The 1500 cap rejects engine-valid configs; simultaneously s3=70000 from an import sails through validation and FATALs the endpoint at connect.
findings.fix: Widen S1/S2 checks to 0-65535 and add the same range check for values.s3/values.s4 (engine treats all four as uint16).

findings.title: Jc cap 0-128 rejects engine-valid values: fork accepts the full uint32 range
findings.evidence: Probes: jc=129 STARTED OK, jc=1000 STARTED OK, jc=4294967295 STARTED OK (only negatives FATAL: "failed to parse jc: parsing \"-1\": invalid syntax"). device/uapi.go stores junk.count as uint32 with no upper check. A server profile legitimately using Jc>128 is flagged invalid by the app while the engine accepts it; meanwhile Jc=0 (validator-allowed) is fine too. Wiki 'recommended 1-128' is a guideline, not the engine's validation.
findings.fix: Either widen the accepted range to 0-4294967295 or keep 0-128 as a non-blocking warning so imported Jc>128 configs are not rejected.

findings.title: I1-I5 get zero validation anywhere while the engine strictly parses obfuscation-chain specs
findings.evidence: validate() calls _validateMasquerade on values.id/ip/ib only. Engine probes: i1="<x 1>" -> "IPC error -22: failed to parse I1: unknown tag <x>"; i1="<b 0x01" -> "failed to parse I1: missing enclosing >"; while i1="aabbccdd" (legacy hex) and i1="<b 0x41424344><t><r 8>" STARTED OK. Source: amneziawg-go v3.1.0-awgm.2 device/uapi.go 'i1'..'i5' cases call newObfChain; device/obf.go knows tags b/t/r/rc/rd/d/ds/dz, errors on unknown tags/missing '>'. So a typo'd I value from an INI/Clash import is invisible until the whole endpoint FATALs at connect.
findings.fix: Add a format check for i1-i5: value must be pure hex (legacy) or a well-formed chain of <tag [val]> with known tags and enclosing '>', and surface errors in the editor before the config reaches the engine.

findings.title: S1 + 56 != S2 enforced as a hard error but the engine has no such rule; generateRandom's guard for it is dead code
findings.evidence: Probes: s1=15,s2=71 (exactly S1+56) STARTED OK; s1=74,s2=74 STARTED OK. No such rule exists in amneziawg-go v3.1.0-awgm.2 uapi/device paths, and the comment's 'init1+msg1 padding rule (56 = WireGuard init msg size)' rationale does not match the fork (S-values are uint16 paddings checked only for header_protection_key >= 12). Hard-rejecting this combination blocks configs the engine interoperates with. Also amnezia_values.dart:168-169: 'var s2 = s1 + 57; if (s2 == s1 + 56) { s2 += 1; }' is unreachable since s2 is always s1+57.
findings.fix: Demote the S1+56==S2 rule to a non-blocking warning (or drop it), and delete the dead branch in generateRandom.

findings.title: getInterfaces() sets flags=0 and empty dnsServer/gateway — Go filters every interface out of NetworkManager (FlagUp filter)
findings.evidence: item.flags = 0 and item.dnsServer/gateway = StringListIterator(emptyList()); metered never set. Go: route/network.go:319-321 newInterfaces := common.Filter(interfaces, it.Flags&net.FlagUp != 0) → with flags=0 the store is always empty. Consumers: route/rule/rule_network_interface_address.go:42 matches nothing (network-interface rules silently dead); network.go:549 type/expensive reporting skipped; upstream SFA sets IFF_UP|IFF_RUNNING dump flags, linkProperties.dnsServers, gateways, and metered. Compiler currently emits no network_interface rules, so impact today is reporting/latent, but the PlatformInterface contract is half-implemented vs upstream.
findings.fix: Set flags from NetworkInterface.isUp/isLoopback/isPointToPoint/supportsMulticast (upstream uses OsConstants IFF_* via reflection), fill dnsServer from LinkProperties.dnsServers, gateway from routes with prefixLength==0, set metered from NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_METERED.

findings.title: openTun drops inet4/6RouteExcludeAddress (and route ranges) — TunOptions contract only half-implemented
findings.evidence: Kotlin openTun reads only getInet4RouteAddress/getInet6RouteAddress with 0.0.0.0/:: fallback and never iterates the exclude iterators; aar javap com.qanatvpn.libbox.TunOptions exposes getInet4RouteExcludeAddress/getInet6RouteExcludeAddress. Upstream SFA VPNService.kt calls builder.excludeRoute(...) for both on API 33+. Latent today (lib/modules/routing/config_assembler.dart:71-80 emits only type/tag/address/auto_route/strict_route — no route_address/route_exclude_address, and the daemon OverrideOptions merge only touches include/exclude package), but any future emission of inet4_route_exclude_address would be silently dropped, weakening split-tunnel/kill-switch routes.
findings.fix: Consume the exclude iterators in openTun (builder.excludeRoute on API 33+, or drop via fallback handling on older APIs); add a guard/assert if exclude addresses ever appear pre-33.

findings.title: CI-built release sing-box.exe gets an EMPTY version stamp: build-windows.yml uses git describe --tags in the submodule, but actions/checkout@v4 fetches submodules by SHA with --depth=1 (no tags), and the sanity check cannot catch it
findings.evidence: Workflow: `working-directory: go/amnezia-box` + `$version = git describe --tags` (line 33), checkout step has `submodules: recursive` but NO fetch-depth. actions/checkout source (github.com/actions/checkout src/git-command-manager.ts:455-459) runs `git submodule update --init --force [--depth=N]` with N=fetchDepth default 1. Real repro of that exact fetch path (scratch temp dir): `git init && git remote add origin https://github.com/hoaxisr/amnezia-box && git fetch --quiet --depth=1 origin 57276220a20679cad762c9644f6abdaf39ab7688` -> `git tag -l | wc -l` = 0; `git describe --tags` -> 'fatal: No names found, cannot describe anything.' exit 128. In pwsh a native-command failure does not throw

findings.title: Engine base is sing-box 1.14.0-rc.1 while upstream shipped 1.14.0 stable (plus rc.2/rc.4/rc.5) and 1.15.0-alpha.1/2 — and upstream-check.yml only watches the fork, so fork-vs-upstream staleness is structurally invisible
findings.evidence: upstream-check.yml 'Fetch upstream amnezia-box' step: `working-directory: go/amnezia-box; git fetch --all --tags; git describe --tags || true` — only the fork repo is fetched; no step touches SagerNet/sing-box. Live data (GitHub API, fetched today): SagerNet/sing-box releases include v1.15.0-alpha.2, v1.15.0-alpha.1, v1.14.0 (stable, prerelease=false), v1.14.0-rc.5, v1.14.0-rc.4, v1.14.0-rc.2 after the fork's base rc.1. The fork has NOT rebased (git ls-remote --tags origin | grep awgm: newest is 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 -> 57276220a; branch awg-1.14-rc1 at that SHA), so the weekly check will report 'no drift' forever. tasks/plan.md:54 promises an upstream tracker for amnezia-box AND sing-box AND
findings.fix: Add a step in upstream-check.yml that queries https://api.github.com/repos/SagerNet/sing-box/releases/latest (and hoaxisr/amnezia-box) and fails or opens an issue when the tag is newer than the pinned base; treat 'fork has no new tag for >N weeks while upstream is at stable' as a reportable drift event. Track sing-box/Xray-core per plan.md:54.

findings.title: windows/sing-box.exe is an untracked, hash-unpinned 71 MB artifact built with go1.26.5 while the repo pins Go 1.25 — the dev-machine probe binary is not guaranteed to match anything reproducible
findings.evidence: Not tracked: `git cat-file -e HEAD:windows/sing-box.exe` -> "fatal: path ... exists on disk, but not in 'HEAD'"; `git log --all -- windows/sing-box.exe` -> empty (never committed); `git check-ignore -v windows/sing-box.exe` -> .gitignore:36. No pin: grep of scripts/, Makefile, .github/ shows sha256 only for release zips/AAps (build-windows.yml:58, build-android.yml:112) — nothing hashes the exe itself. `git ls-files | grep -E '\.(exe|dll|aar)$'` -> exit 1 (no engine binary committed anywhere). File mtime Sep 1 15:09; `./windows/sing-box.exe version` -> 'Environment: go1.26.5 windows/amd64' while AGENTS.md pins 'Go 1.25', workflows use `go-version: '1.25'`, and the fork's go.mod requires `go
findings.fix: Record the exe's SHA256 (and submodule SHA + Go version used) in docs/decisions.tsv or a committed pin file at build time (`pwsh scripts/libbox.ps1 windows` can emit it), and add a toolchain guard to libbox.ps1/Makefile (abort if go version < 1.25.5 or != pinned major.minor) so local rebuilds stay within the pinned toolchain.

findings.title: CN-direct route rule is a logical AND of domain_suffix cn + rule_set geosite-cn + rule_set geoip-cn — matches far less than the 'CN direct' intent
findings.evidence: Gen intent (tool/gen_profile.dart) is 'CN traffic direct'. Engine source: go/amnezia-box route/rule/rule_abstract.go abstractDefaultRule.matchInner — 'for _, item := range r.items { if !item.Match(metadata) { return false } }' — all fields AND. Effect: baidu.com (CN, geosite-cn + geoip-cn, but no .cn suffix) never matches -> goes PROXY; a CN IP connection with no domain never matches -> PROXY. With FakeIP (dns.rules sends all non-CN A/AAAA to the fakeip pool), even sniffed CN .com domains land on fake IPs that geoip-cn cannot match. Today the shipped PROXY selector is ["DIRECT"] so the damage is masked; it bites as soon as a real endpoint is selectable.
findings.fix: Split into two OR rules (domain_suffix cn + geosite-cn in one; rule_set geoip-cn in another) or drop domain_suffix so the rule means 'match geosite OR geoip' as intended; verify with sing-box check + a routing-level runtime probe.

findings.title: check/runtime gap: a route rule with a dangling outbound tag passes check and starts silently — matched connections then fail per-connection at runtime
findings.evidence: p2rl probe: check -> EXIT=0; `sing-box.exe run -c` (8s, no inbounds, endpoint removed, local rule_sets) -> no FATAL, service runs until killed. Contrast: dangling selector member probe (outbounds[0].outbounds=["GHOST"]) -> check EXIT=0 but run FATAL 'start service: dependency[GHOST] not found for outbound[PROXY]'. Risk: ProfileConfigSource prepends group/endpoint tags into the selector (_merged) and appends user rules (_withRules: 'Rules referencing unknown rule_sets ship unmodified') — any tag typo FATALs the connect (selector path) or silently breaks routing (rule path); Windows adapter's crash detection (CommandServer log-stream FATAL scan) catches only the FATAL case.
findings.fix: Add a Dart-side pre-start validator: every route.rules outbound and selector member must resolve against outbounds + endpoints + {DIRECT, BLOCK}; surface invalid rules in the rules editor instead of shipping them.

findings.title: The profile regeneration gate is broken: tool/gen_profile.dart can no longer run with plain dart run (flutter imports leaked into the pure-Dart chain), so AGENTS.md's 'generated from real modules' no longer holds
findings.evidence: dart run tool/gen_profile.dart on current HEAD -> exit 254: "Dart library 'dart:ui' is not available on this platform" via gen_profile => config_assembler => sec/firewall.dart => core/services/tunnel.dart => package:flutter/services.dart, and separately gen_profile => modules/geo/geo_asset.dart => rootBundle; additionally the sqlite3 3.5.2 build hook needs a network download (blocked on this network — repo .dart_tool hooks_runner cache had to be copied into the sandbox). My regen worked only after stubbing rootBundle use, the flutter/services import, and the MethodChannel in temp copies — meaning the shipped artifact can silently diverge from the builder (it already has, see stale-profile fi
findings.fix: Decouple the generator: move the ConfigAssembler chain's platform imports behind injectable seams (rootBundle already has the bundledLoader seam — use it in geo_asset; move tunnel.dart out of firewall.dart's import graph or split baseRules into a pure module), then add the regen + check to the pre-commit gate.

findings.title: Goldens render the M3 baseline purple theme, not QanatVpnApp's seeded green theme — committed PNGs prove it, so color/theme regressions are invisible and goldens verify a look production never shows
findings.evidence: Pixel forensics on the committed goldens: dominant colors of power_tile_connected_135.png are #E6E0E9 (surfaceContainerHighest) / #1D1B20 (onSurface) / #49454F — these are the Material 3 baseline light scheme values, not the green-seeded scheme (ColorScheme.fromSeed(0xFF245C4F), app.dart:70-71). _wrap's MaterialApp (line 42) passes no theme/darkTheme, so goldens rasterize the default M3 baseline palette; UpdateTile/PowerTile colors reference theme.colorScheme.* (home.dart:296,357,366) and are therefore verified against the WRONG colors — a regression that swaps production colors would leave all goldens green. The wrapper also bypasses QanatVpnApp entirely: the clamp under test is a hand-copie
findings.fix: Extract the app's ThemeData/darkTheme construction into a shared factory used by both QanatVpnApp and the test harness (or render via QanatVpnApp with the fake tunnel injected through ProviderScope overrides), so goldens rasterize the production seed, clamp wiring, and app shell.

findings.title: No font-loading infrastructure: no flutter_test_config.dart, no FontLoader/golden_toolkit — text renders in the embedded deterministic test font, so goldens are typography-blind and cannot catch real-font overflow at any scale
findings.evidence: Probe: 'cat test/flutter_test_config.dart' -> 'NO flutter_test_config.dart'; grep for FontLoader|loadAppFonts|golden_toolkit|alchemist across test/ and pubspec returns nothing; pubspec has no fonts: section (only uses-material-design: true) and no fontFamily anywhere in lib/app/app.dart. All golden text is therefore rasterized with the deterministic embedded widget-test font while production text on Android/Windows uses Roboto/Segoe fallbacks with different advance widths, kerning, and line-breaking. Consequence: the 1.35 goldens and the 200% overflow pass measure test-font layout, not device-font layout — a string that fits at 1.35 in the test font can wrap/overflow in Roboto, and Persian t
findings.fix: Add test/flutter_test_config.dart that loads the app's production fonts (or a pinned Roboto/Noto Sans Arabic pair) via FontLoader before goldens run, and add one FA-locale golden so Persian shaping/metrics are actually rasterized. If the app intentionally ships no bundled font, document that goldens verify layout-box only.

findings.title: Golden coverage matrix is 3 files vs 7 tiles x 5 tunnel states x 2 themes x 2 locales x 4 scales; no 100% golden, no UpdateAvailable variant, and the historically-fixed EndpointTile overflow has no protecting golden
findings.evidence: matchesGoldenFile appears exactly 3 times (lines 120, 134, 148) covering StatsTile-connected (which actually renders disconnected, see separate finding) and PowerTile connected/blocked (byte-identical). No golden exists for StateTile's blockReason text, EndpointTile, SplitTile, WizardTile, or UpdateTile's UpdateAvailable variant (tertiaryContainer background + 'Update x.y.z' label, home.dart:352-366) — the highest-contrast UpdateTile state is untested. The only text-visibility guard is height>40 on 4 of 7 tiles (Power/State/Stats/Update); EndpointTile (which has its own long endpoint strings) is not asserted at 200% despite AGENTS.md's progress note that a real EndpointTile overflow was once
findings.fix: Add goldens per state that matters: StateTile blocked (blockReason text), UpdateTile with UpdateAvailable (override updates.updateControllerProvider), and one 0.9-scale golden; parameterize the harness over (phase, scale) instead of copy-pasting tests.

findings.title: Released exe is built with Go 1.25 (CI) while the validated dev exe is Go 1.26.5 — parity evidence gathered on a toolchain CI never produces
findings.evidence: windows/sing-box.exe version output: `Environment: go1.26.5 windows/amd64` — the exe on disk (sha256 e79cf6f19c41f294899144832979cff49bab4e4e1580e63494711ea777723bd4, bit-reproducible: rebuilding go/amnezia-box @ pinned 5727622 with the committed recipe reproduced this exact hash) was compiled with Go 1.26.5, but every workflow pins go-version '1.25' and AGENTS.md pins Go 1.25. The exe that all engine-truth probes and the 302-test parity suite ran against is not the binary CI ships in release zips (different Go minor = different binary bytes).
findings.fix: Align the toolchain: either bump the project pin (AGENTS.md + all three workflows) to the exact Go version used locally (1.26.5) or rebuild windows/sing-box.exe with Go 1.25.x and re-run the probe suite. Record the canonical toolchain next to the VERSION pin in Makefile/libbox.ps1.

findings.title: Engine base is upstream sing-box 1.14.0-rc.1 while upstream has shipped rc.2, rc.4, rc.5 and 1.14.0 stable; fork has no newer tag than awgm.15
findings.evidence: `git ls-remote --tags origin` on the fork shows the newest awgm tag is 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 (default branch awg-1.14-rc1 HEAD = pinned SHA 57276220 — fork is current within its own series), but the upstream SagerNet/sing-box releases API shows v1.14.0-rc.2, v1.14.0-rc.4, v1.14.0-rc.5, and stable v1.14.0 already shipped (plus v1.15.0-alpha.1/2), carrying evaluate DNS rule action, optimistic DNS cache, sniff pre-match, mDNS server, unified HTTP client, L3 forwarding/bridge outbound, and OpenVPN/OpenConnect/Snell clients. The rc.1-base engine lacks all of it, and every engine truth in docs/decisions.tsv (endpoints id/ip/ib FATAL, tuic tls.alpn, reality+utls, xhttp x_padding_bytes mandatory, ECH
findings.fix: Keep the pin (deliberate per goal.md), but extend upstream-check.yml to also fetch SagerNet/sing-box tags and open/report a bump ticket when upstream 1.14.0.x stable advances beyond the fork's base, so the rc.1→stable delta is a tracked decision rather than invisible drift.

findings.title: Goldens render MaterialApp's default theme, not QanatVpnApp's seedColor/darkTheme — color regressions in the real scheme are invisible
findings.evidence: _wrap's MaterialApp (lines 46-60) sets no theme/darkTheme, so goldens verify the DEFAULT M3 purple-seeded scheme: pixel probe of power_tile_connected_135.png background = #E6E0E9 (default surfaceContainerHighest), whereas the production connected card is primaryContainer of ColorScheme.fromSeed(seedColor: Color(0xFF245C4F)) (lib/app/app.dart:47) — a green-tinted container that would render differently. Any change to the app's colorScheme/theme wiring is invisible to all three goldens, and dark mode (shipped darkTheme, app.dart:51-55) is never rendered. Combined with finding 1, the goldens currently pin a default-themed, disconnected tile.
findings.fix: Reuse the production theme: either pump QanatVpnApp (router + theme + clamp builder) with overridden providers, or at minimum copy QanatVpnApp's ThemeData/darkTheme into _wrap. Add one dark-brightness golden to lock the shipped darkTheme.

findings.title: No FA locale and no RTL visual coverage anywhere — goldens always render EN, LTR
findings.evidence: _wrap never sets locale; MaterialApp resolves en_US in tests. grep across test/ for Locale('fa') in a widget pump, Directionality, or TextDirection.rtl returns zero matches — FA exists only as string-equality unit tests (polish_test.dart:54, l10n_parity_test.dart:64). HomeScreen is direction-sensitive by design (EdgeInsetsDirectional, AGENTS.md RTL rule), so a mirrored-layout or RTL-ellipsis regression ships unverified. Caveat: with the default Ahem test font (flutter_test binding.dart:2665: 'This forces all text to use the Ahem font'), Persian glyphs render as identical boxes, so a FA golden still couldn't validate shaping — but it WOULD validate RTL geometry, text alignment, and FA string
findings.fix: Add one testWidgets that pumps HomeScreen with locale: Locale('fa') (MaterialApp handles RTL via flutter_localizations) at 1.35 with a clip/scroll-extent assertion; optionally one FA PNG golden for the power/state tile pair.

findings.title: Zero-tolerance pixel comparison + cross-OS CI with no flutter_test_config.dart: single-pixel icon drift breaks both jobs
findings.evidence: Default LocalFileComparator via GoldenFileComparator.compareLists fails on any single differing pixel (flutter_test _goldens_io.dart:254-258: 'if (pixelDiffCount > 0) ... passed: false'). No flutter_test_config.dart exists in test/ (find returns none), so no tolerant comparator is installed and the threshold cannot be tuned without editing tests. Ahem text is deterministic across platforms, but icons rasterize from the real bundled MaterialIcons font (the goldens show real glyph outlines, not Ahem boxes), so Flutter/Skia/icon-font version drift turns both CI jobs red simultaneously; decisions.tsv:53 documents only '--update-goldens regenerates' with no pinning note.
findings.fix: Either pin comparator tolerance via a test/flutter_test_config.dart that installs LocalFileComparator with a small thresholdTolerance, or document the regen command against the pinned Flutter 3.47.2 and regenerate only on version bumps. Prefer explicit update commits when regenerating.

findings.title: Golden coverage: 2 of 7 home tiles, one scale (1.35), no 1.0 baseline, no full-home golden; the historically bugged EndpointTile has none

findings.fix: Add a full-home golden at 1.0 (all 7 tiles in one PNG) plus per-state PNGs for StatsTile (connected with metrics, disconnected) — that alone would have caught the identical-golden bug. EndpointTile deserves a golden given its overflow history.

findings.title: Hysteria2 hop_interval '30s' shape is asserted but never engine-checked; number-form FATAL shape untested
findings.evidence: p1_emit_parity_test.dart:111-122 ('Hysteria2 hop_interval seconds emitted') asserts json['hop_interval']=='30s' but, unlike its siblings at lines 108 and 135, never calls checkOutbound. Probes: hop_interval:'30s' → exit 0; hop_interval:30 (number) → exit 1 `FATAL outbounds[0].hop_interval: json: cannot unmarshal number into Go struct field Hysteria2OutboundOptions.hop_interval of type string`. The emitter '${n}s' interpolation is correct today; a regression emitting the raw int passes all tests and FATALs every hy2 profile with a hop interval.
findings.fix: Change the test to async and add `await checkOutbound(json);` after the assertion — one line, matches the sibling pattern.

findings.title: SSH empty/whitespace private_key trim-guard untested despite probed engine FATAL 'ssh: no key found'

findings.fix: Add: endpointToOutboundJson(SshEndpoint(..., privateKey: '   ')) → expect json.containsKey('private_key'), isFalse; and a real check on an emitted no-key ssh outbound (exit 0).

findings.fix: Add one p0 test mirroring routing_test.dart's pattern: assembler.build(endpointJson: _awg, policy: <user domainSuffix rule>) → write temp json → sing-box check exit 0 (skip when exe absent, matching the file's offline-safe style).

findings.title: LogBus repeat-collapse drops the terminal run's count: the 'repeated N times' summary is only emitted when a later distinct line arrives, and it carries an empty level so the Logs 'errors' filter hides it
findings.evidence: log_bus.dart:38-42: duplicates increment `_repeatCount` and return: `if (message == _lastMessage && line.level == _lastLevel) { _repeatCount++; droppedRepeats++; return; }`. The summary is emitted only in `_flushRepeats()` (lines 50-57), which runs only when a DIFFERENT line arrives: `if (_repeatCount >= 3 && _lastMessage != null) { _emit(EngineLogLine(level: '', message: '‹repeated $_repeatCount times›')); }`. If the engine's final state is a run of identical lines (e.g. the same FATAL/ERROR text before death, or a crash loop replaying the same error), the user sees a single line and the N-times count is dropped entirely (also on `clear()`, line 71). Additionally the summary is emitted with
findings.fix: Emit the pending summary inside `clear()` and provide a `flush()`/snapshot accessor that appends the pending `‹repeated N times›` line, and give the summary a pass-through level (or tag) so the errors filter retains it.

findings.title: WindowsBoxProcessAdapter cancels stdout/stderr subscriptions as soon as exitCode resolves, so the actual FATAL line can be lost and start reports a generic 'sing-box.exe exited during startup'; _lastErrorLine is never reset between starts
findings.evidence: windows_box_process.dart:73-80: `process.exitCode.then<int>((code) { ... _stderrSub?.cancel(); _stdoutSub?.cancel(); ... })` cancels the pipe subscriptions the moment the exit code future resolves, but stderr/stdout stream delivery is not ordered against exitCode completion — a FATAL line still buffered in the pipe is discarded, leaving `_lastErrorLine` null, so `start` throws `StateError(_lastErrorLine ?? 'sing-box.exe exited during startup')` (line 105 area) with no diagnostic. Also `_lastErrorLine` (declared line 92) is never reset in `start()`, so a later failed start can report the PREVIOUS run's error if the new one's stderr is lost in the same race.
findings.fix: Before throwing in `start`, give the pipes a short grace await (e.g. await stderr/stdout subscription `asFuture()` with a 1-2s timeout) instead of relying on the already-canceled subs, and reset `_lastErrorLine = null` at the top of `start()`.

findings.title: Deferred startup is registered via addPostFrameCallback before runApp, and HttpCache only writes freshness metadata on a successful fetch — an offline-first launch never seeds the 6h stale-while-revalidate window, so every subsequent launch re-hits raw.githubusercontent, contradi
findings.evidence: main.dart:65-66: `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) { unawaited(_deferredStartup()); });` runs before `runApp(...)` — acceptable only because runApp schedules the first frame afterwards; if the first build throws, update registration and geo seeding silently never run (no onError hook catches it). More concretely, `HttpCache._writeDisk` (http_cache.dart) is only called on the 200/304 success paths, so a user who launches while offline (or GitHub-rate-limited) never persists `fetchedAt` metadata: the next launch's `getBytes` sees no entry, treats it as stale, and fetches again — the rate-limit mitigation claimed in main.dart:154-156 ("without it the daily refresh re-downloads f
findings.fix: Persist a timestamp/etag record even when the fetch fails (serve stale + record the attempt), or seed the disk cache from the bundled SRS bytes with fetchedAt=now so the 6h window starts from the copy-in; register the post-frame callback from inside the widget tree (first-frame-safe).

findings.title: _block sets _firewallEnforced = true unconditionally, including when firewall.enforce() timed out or threw — contradicting its own documented fail-closed intent
findings.fix: Set the flag only on success: `var ok = true; try { await firewall.enforce()...; } on Object { ok = false; } if (ok) { _firewallEnforced = true; }` (or move the assignment inside the try before the catch).

findings.title: grant/airplane/tor block paths skip the _stale(epoch) check, so a stale aborted connect can override a newer transition's state with blocked and re-enforce the firewall
findings.evidence: Every other failure decision inside connect checks the epoch first, e.g. the airplane catch (tunnel.dart:297-298) and the tor catch (tunnel.dart:363-364) run `if (_stale(epoch)) { publishMetrics(); return; }` before blocking. But these sites do not: grant denial (tunnel.dart:255-258: `if (!granted) { publishMetrics(); await _block(TunnelBlockReason.vpnPermissionDenied); return; }`), grant error (tunnel.dart:260-263), airplane on (tunnel.dart:293-295), tor down (tunnel.dart:358-361), and the fd==null case (tunnel.dart:394-397). `disconnect()` is callable while `connecting` (its only guard is `if (_state == TunnelState.disconnected) return;`, tunnel.dart:521-523) and bumps `_epoch` (tunnel.dar
findings.fix: Add `if (_stale(epoch)) { publishMetrics(); return; }` immediately before each `await _block(...)` in the grant, airplane, tor, and fd==null paths (same pattern as the airplane catch).

findings.title: MethodChannelForegroundAdapter swallows every error via onError((_, _) {}), making Tunnel's foreground-failure → block(establishFailed) guard dead code with the real adapter
findings.evidence: `Future<void> start() => channel.invokeMethod<void>('startForeground').onError((_, _) {});` converts every failure (PlatformException, MissingPluginException) into success. `Tunnel.connect`'s designed guard — `try { await _timed(phases, 'foreground', () => foreground.start().timeout(timeouts.foregroundStart)); } on Object { ... await _block(TunnelBlockReason.establishFailed); return; }` (tunnel.dart:311-325) — is therefore unreachable with the real adapter: a platform-side FGS start failure (Android 12+ background-start restriction, OEM-specific blocks, missing handler) proceeds silently into box.start with no foreground notification, exposing the tunnel to Doze eviction (AGENTS.md: 'skip is
findings.fix: Let `start()` propagate errors (drop the `.onError((_, _) {})` on start, keep it on stop), so Tunnel's foreground-failure block path functions; if a best-effort teardown is wanted, keep the swallow only on `stop()`.

findings.title: protect/closeFd are fire-and-forget: platform errors become unhandled async exceptions and the protect phase can never fail or time out
findings.evidence: `void protect(int fd) { _channel.invokeMethod<void>('protect', {'fd': fd}); }` and `void closeFd(int fd) { _channel.invokeMethod<void>('closeFd', {'fd': fd}); }` discard the futures, so any platform error becomes an unhandled zone exception instead of reaching Tunnel. The protect phase in connect is correspondingly inert: `await _timed(phases, 'protect', () async { platform.protect(protectFd); });` (tunnel.dart:404-411) completes immediately, so neither the `on Object` catch nor a timeout can ever fire — the guarded sequence proceeds with an unprotected VPN fd on any failure. This is latent today (both shipped adapters hardcode `engineManagedTun => true`, and VpnServiceBridge.kt has no prote
findings.fix: Change the PlatformAdapter seam to `Future<void> protect(int fd)` / `Future<void> closeFd(int fd)`, await them in Tunnel.connect (and in the fd cleanup paths), and have the method-channel adapter await `_channel.invokeMethod`.

findings.title: LocalSocksTorAdapter.isSocksUp accepts any TCP listener on 127.0.0.1:9050 as 'Tor up', so the TOR-CHAIN guard false-positives on a foreign or non-SOCKS listener
findings.evidence: `Future<bool> isSocksUp() async { final socket = await Socket.connect(host, port, timeout: const Duration(milliseconds: 500)); socket.destroy(); return true; } on Object { return false; }` proves only that something accepts TCP on 127.0.0.1:9050. The gate in `Tunnel.connect` (`config.requiresTor && !await tor.isSocksUp()`, tunnel.dart:355-358) then lets the engine start, so a TOR-CHAIN tag proceeds through a dead or foreign listener: the engine starts, the UI shows connected, and all traffic routed via that chain fails. The class comment states the intent — 'until it exists the port is down, which correctly blocks TOR-CHAIN tags' — but any other process binding 9050 defeats that fail-closed
findings.fix: After connecting, perform a minimal SOCKS5 greeting read (send `0x05 0x01 0x00`, expect a 2-byte reply starting with 0x05) before returning true; destroy and return false otherwise.

findings.title: Tunnel.dispose() leaves a running engine alive and any subsequent connect/disconnect throws StateError from the closed status controller
findings.evidence: `Future<void> dispose() async { await _boxSub.cancel(); await _status.close(); }` neither stops the box nor relaxes the firewall. After dispose, `_boxSub` is cancelled so `_onBoxEvent` no longer runs (an engine death is invisible), and `_setState` (`_status.add(next)`, tunnel.dart:597-601) throws `StateError: Cannot add event after closing` for any later connect/disconnect/block — including `_block` invoked from a still-queued box event via another path. Production currently never disposes (tunnelProvider is app-lifetime in main.dart/vpn_notifier.dart), so exposure is test/hot-restart only, but the class's own API permits the broken sequence.
findings.fix: In dispose, tear down first (if state is connecting/connected/blocked: best-effort `await box.stop()`, close fd, relax firewall, stop foreground) before cancelling the subscription and closing the controller, or guard `_setState` with an `_disposed` flag.

findings.title: _hasExited() uses exit code -1 as its 'timed out' sentinel, so a real exit code of -1 during the 300ms startup window yields started for a dead engine
findings.evidence: Lines 143-155: `Future<bool> _hasExited() async { final process = _process; if (process == null) return true; final result = await process.exitCode.timeout(Duration.zero, onTimeout: () => -1).catchError((_) => -1); return result != -1; }` — the timeout sentinel -1 collides with a real exit code of -1. dart:io on Windows delivers int32-signed exit codes (e.g. a process terminated with TerminateProcess(0xFFFFFFFF) reports -1, same family as the well-known negative STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION codes). In that case start() proceeds past `if (await _hasExited())` (line 133), emits `BoxEventKind.started` for a dead process, and Tunnel reports connected while all traffic flows direct — a silent leak.
findings.fix: Use a non-colliding sentinel: complete the race against a nullable marker, e.g. `int? result; try { result = await process.exitCode.timeout(Duration.zero); } on TimeoutException { result = null; } return result != null;`

findings.title: workingDir constructor parameter is dead code: never passed to Process.start, and the ProcessFactory typedef cannot even accept it
findings.evidence: `this.workingDir` is a documented constructor field (line 18, `final String? workingDir;` line 29) but the spawn call (lines 80-85) passes only `mode: ProcessStartMode.normal`: `process = await processFactory(_resolvedExe, <String>['run', '-c', file.path, '--disable-color'], mode: ProcessStartMode.normal);` and the ProcessFactory typedef has no workingDirectory parameter, so the field cannot be honored even if set. The child inherits the Flutter app's CWD, which is unreliable on Windows (C:\Windows\System32 for scheduled/startup launches). Today's config happens to carry only absolute/URL resources, but any future CWD-relative engine path (or the declared intent of the parameter) silently re
findings.fix: Either wire it through — extend the typedef/call to pass `workingDirectory: workingDir` to Process.start — or delete the parameter so the API does not advertise an option that does nothing.

findings.title: Engine death with exit code 0 emits stopped, which Tunnel ignores: UI stays connected on a dead engine and traffic goes direct
findings.evidence: Lines 107-110 in the exit watcher: `} else if (!wasStopping) { _events.add(const BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.stopped)); }` — a self-terminated process exiting 0 emits `stopped`, not `crashed`. Tunnel only reacts to crashes: lib/core/services/tunnel.dart `_onBoxEvent(BoxEvent event) { if (event.kind != BoxEventKind.crashed) { return; } ... }`, so on an unrequested exit-0 death of the engine (external graceful taskkill that succeeds, console close, engine self-shutdown) TunnelState stays `connected` with no engine and no firewall enforcement change — traffic quietly reverts to the physical interface while the UI shows the VPN on. The class doc itself promises 'A non-zero exit or early death surfaces
findings.fix: Track 'started' state in the adapter: when the exit watcher fires with wasStopping==false, emit crashed for any exit code (including 0) — a stop() that was requested sets _stopping first, so the !wasStopping branch is by definition an unrequested death.

findings.title: Windows rename-over-target fails with PathAccessException while any other handle has the target open — overlapping reader during atomic write makes the write throw
findings.fix: Retry the rename on PathAccessException/FileSystemException with a short bounded backoff (reads are sub-millisecond), and surface failed saves in DebouncedSaver (e.g. an onError callback) instead of swallowing them in the fire-and-forget run().

findings.title: plainFetch buffers the response body unbounded in memory with no size cap
findings.evidence: plain_fetch.dart:14-17: `final body = await response.fold<List<int>>(<int>[], (acc, chunk) => acc..addAll(chunk)); ... body: Uint8List.fromList(body)` — no Content-Length check and no max-bytes guard; the entire response is accumulated in memory and then copied again by Uint8List.fromList (2x peak). Any caller-facing URL (endpoint importText accepts arbitrary user URLs; geo/mirror URLs are fixed) can point at a multi-GB response and OOM the UI isolate, or a slow-drip server can buffer indefinitely (compounding the missing-timeout finding).
findings.fix: Reject when `response.contentLength` exceeds a sane cap (e.g. 32MB) when present, and abort the fold once the accumulated length passes the cap (throw a StateError/HttpException); build the body with BytesBuilder instead of List<int> addAll to avoid the second copy.

findings.title: Staleness math never goes stale when the device clock moves backwards: negative age keeps an entry 'fresh' indefinitely
findings.evidence: http_cache.dart:39-40: `final isStale = entry == null || _now().difference(entry.fetchedAt) > staleAfter;`. If the device clock is corrected backwards after an entry was stored (fetchedAt in the wall-clock future), difference() is negative, `> staleAfter` is false, and line 42-44 (`if (entry != null && !isStale) { return entry.body; }`) serves the cached body with no revalidation until real time catches up with the stored timestamp — potentially days of stale geo data with zero network checks, silently. (Positive clock jumps are handled fine; only rollback breaks it.)
findings.fix: Treat a future fetchedAt as stale: `final age = _now().difference(entry.fetchedAt); final isStale = entry == null || age < Duration.zero || age > staleAfter;`

findings.title: _block() sets _firewallEnforced = true even when firewall.enforce() timed out, permanently disabling relax-on-disconnect until the next successful connect
findings.evidence: _block(): `try { await firewall.enforce().timeout(timeouts.firewallEnforce); } on Object { // The block state itself must never hang: a wedged firewall still leaves the tunnel blocked (fail closed), just without the flag that would relax it later. } _firewallEnforced = true;` — the comment says the flag stays unset on failure, but `_firewallEnforced = true` runs unconditionally after the try/catch. disconnect() then guards relaxation: `if (_firewallEnforced) { try { await firewall.relax(); } ... _firewallEnforced = false; }`. With the flag stuck true, disconnect runs relax (harmless), but the invariant the comment promises (flag only when enforcement succeeded) is broken — a later diagnostic
findings.fix: Move `_firewallEnforced = true;` into the try block after the awaited enforce succeeds (or set it from the catch as `false`), matching the comment's stated intent.

findings.title: TOR-CHAIN: tor.isSocksUp() probe is not re-checked after box.start, so a sidecar that dies in the probe→start window starts the engine on a dead chain
findings.evidence: `final torDown = await _timed(phases, 'tor', () async { return config.requiresTor && !await tor.isSocksUp(); });` — LocalSocksTorAdapter.isSocksUp() does a single Socket.connect with a 500ms timeout and destroys the socket. If the probe succeeds but the sidecar dies before box.start finishes dialing the chain, the engine starts with a dead detour: sing-box logs FATAL/connection errors for the chained outbound, which on Android surfaces via the log-watcher as a crashed event (tunnel goes blocked boxCrashed) — but on Windows the crash path depends on the process exiting (WindowsBoxProcessAdapter only emits crashed on non-zero exit), and a hung engine with a dead chain can leave the UI on conne
findings.fix: Re-probe the chain immediately before `_setState(TunnelState.connected)` when config.requiresTor (cheap socket check), or subscribe to a tor health stream and _block(torDown) on loss; at minimum verify after box.start returns rather than only before it.

findings.title: No engine-state reconciliation after app restart: UI initializes to disconnected while the Android libbox service may still be running; connect() then no-ops and crash detection is lost for the old session
findings.evidence: VpnNotifier.build() unconditionally returns `VpnState.disconnected()` and only mirrors future status events. On Android, libbox runs in-process (BoxEngine is an object; QanatVpnService is START_NOT_STICKY but the engine can outlive activity recreation), and boxStart re-attaches with `server.startOrReloadService(configJson, overrides)` without a state query (CommandClient has no service-status command — documented engine truth). If the Flutter engine is recreated while the tunnel is still up (activity killed under memory pressure, process kept alive by the foreground service), the notifier shows disconnected; the PowerTile's connect() calls Tunnel.connect, which early-returns `if (_state == Tu
findings.fix: Reconcile at startup: add a 'boxStatus' channel method (Kotlin already tracks engineRunning) consulted by VpnNotifier.build()/Tunnel construction to seed the initial state, or at minimum have BoxEngine.boxStart detect an already-running engine and emit 'started' so a fresh Tunnel converges to connected.

findings.title: UpdateStore persists last_update_check.json under a world-writable system temp directory when HOME/USERPROFILE are unset
findings.evidence: `File _file() => File(baseDir != null ? '$baseDir/last_update_check.json' : '${Platform.environment['HOME'] ?? Platform.environment['USERPROFILE'] ?? Directory.systemTemp.path}' '/.qanatvpn/last_update_check.json');` — the value is written with atomicWriteString and read back with `jsonDecode(file.readAsStringSync())`. On Windows HOME/USERPROFILE is the user profile (per-user, OK); but if both are unset the path is the world-readable system temp. The stored fields ('version','changelog','assetUrl','platformKey') are only ever launched via explorer/ACTION_VIEW after another network hop, and the changelog is rendered on the Updates screen, so a local writer can pin the update card to an arbitra
findings.fix: Prefer a platform-appropriate per-user app-data directory (path_provider getApplicationSupportDirectory) instead of env-var fallbacks, and re-validate the stored assetUrl against the release host at render/install time.

findings.title: Import validates only the backup universe, never the emitted merged/replaced config; remote tags are trusted as-is (tag collisions and reserved names unvalidated)
