findings.evidence: routing_compiler.dart:80-81 checks duplicates only among groups: `if (!seenTags.add(group.tag)) { errors.add('$where: duplicate group tag ...'); }` and the `known` resolution set is a plain union (`{...groupTags, ...policy.leafOutbounds, 'DIRECT', ...}`, lines 63-67) with no group-tag vs endpoint-tag collision check and no reserved-name check. backup_service.dart:125-137 compiles only the backup universe (`leafOutbounds: endpointTags` = backup endpoint tags, line 131) and never re-compiles the post-merge/post-replace document that is actually persisted. Result: an authenticated backup (line 156 `byTag` fold — merge mode is backup-wins by attacker-chosen remote tags) containing an endpoint ta
findings.fix: After computing the merged/replaced endpoint+group universe, run the compiler once against the final document (and add a group-tag vs endpoint-tag collision check to the compiler's error list), rejecting the import before any store write.

findings.title: Replace mode is non-transactional across the four stores; malformed split payload silently dropped — contradicts the 'never a partial import' contract
findings.evidence: backup_service.dart:158-168: `await _endpointStore.save(endpoints); await _policyStore.save(policy); await _ruleStore.save(rules); final split = ...; if (split != null) { await _splitStore.save(split); }` — four independent atomic writes, no rollback if save 2 or 3 throws (crash/disk-full leaves mixed old+new state). The docstring (line 28) claims 'never as a partial import'; that holds only for wrong-password (decrypt precedes all writes — verified), not write failures. Additionally a malformed-but-authenticated split payload is silently discarded: split_store.dart:38-46 `try { ... } on Object { return null; }`, so the import reports success while the user's backed-up split choice vanished.
findings.fix: Parse/validate all four payloads (including SplitChoice) before the first store write, and stage stores to tmp then rename as one group, or keep an undo snapshot of the previous state until all four saves succeed.

findings.title: Unbounded pre-authentication parsing of the untrusted backup file on the UI isolate; pre-try casts/base64Decode escape as raw TypeError/FormatException
findings.evidence: `final raw = File(path).readAsBytesSync();` (line 88) then `envelope = jsonDecode(utf8.decode(raw)) ... base64Decode(envelope['ciphertext'] as String)` all before AEAD verification. `_decryptEnvelope` line 230: `final key = await _deriveKey(password, base64Decode(kdf['salt'] as String));` sits BEFORE the `try` at line 231-243, so a missing/garbage kdf/salt throws a raw TypeError/FormatException instead of the documented BackupFormatException (UI catch-all still fails closed, but the exception contract is broken). A crafted multi-hundred-MB .qnv forces full read + JSON parse + multiple base64 allocations on the UI isolate before any MAC check — memory/CPU DoS from a file the user was socially
findings.fix: Wrap the whole decode/derive in the BackupFormatException conversion, enforce a sane max file size (a few MB) before readAsBytesSync, validate salt length 8-64 bytes, and run inspect/import in an isolate (compute()).

findings.title: No password floor for the most sensitive payload in the app; single-field password prompt, no confirmation field, no import preview
findings.evidence: Line 69: `if (password.isEmpty) { throw ArgumentError('backup password must not be empty'); }` — the only gate for a payload whose own docstring says "the payload is 100% credentials-bearing (WG private keys, preshared keys, every protocol uuid/password)". m=19456 KiB/t=2/p=1 is the OWASP *interactive* floor, tuned for server-side rate limiting; a stolen backup file is attacked offline where that cost yields ~10k guesses/s on commodity GPUs, so '123456'-class passwords are cracked in seconds and common ones in hours. The export dialog (endpoints_screen.dart:_promptPassword) has a single field: no repeat/confirmation (typo => permanently unrecoverable backup), no length floor, no strength met
findings.fix: Require a minimum length (e.g. 12 chars) or a passphrase-strength meter, add a repeat-password field on export, and before a replace-mode import call inspect() and show the user what will be overwritten.

findings.title: Real-shaped AWG/WG private key committed in sample profile, generator tool, and 10+ test fixtures (verified non-functional fabricated pair)
findings.evidence: profiles/config.wg-awg.json:81 — `"private_key": "eCbtX5g5Pof3zH0Gu6dzulIzLB0B5xj+OhIfgVtWu1A="`, also hardcoded in tool/gen_profile.dart:13 and ~10 test files (test/awg/awg_config_test.dart:8, test/routing/routing_test.dart:20, test/vpn/endpoints_test.dart:224, etc.). Verified NOT a live credential by curve25519 derivation: public derived from this private key is `hMtztsqO0Vjekoydmo9EreoBP2jurUEd2w7+Ss8pIUU=`, which matches neither the test peer key `fz8KXfDEl+8/SgXJmjotjTxLWm5/gJGis8TV5vcIGSo=` nor the fabricated 64-hex public_key `7f3f0a5d...192a` in the same profile; the peer endpoint is TEST-NET-3 (203.0.113.10:51820). No exposure today, but it is a 32-byte curve25519 key committed to a
findings.fix: Replace the hardcoded base64 key with an obviously-invalid placeholder (e.g. 32 'x' bytes base64) or generate per-run in gen_profile.dart; document in profiles/ that real credentials must never live there; consider ignoring profiles/*.json except a tracked .sample file.

findings.title: Research doc contains vendor download URLs with embedded `key=` tokens that still resolve live — looks like credentials but is a public official link
findings.evidence: research/10-WireSock.md:576-580 — `Invoke-WebRequest "https://www.wiresock.net/sdc_download/921/?key=bekfpuvidq5x8ofg2u74j2lqk8zy9y" -OutFile "wiresock-gateway.msi"` (plus 922/key=hyilnmw..., 923/key=7m03u7c...). Live-curl check of key 921: 301 -> wp.wiresock.net -> HTTP 200, Content-Type application/octet-stream, 32357 bytes downloaded — the keys are functional. However the file itself cites the source: "PowerShell direct (from quick-start-server-core.html)" — these are the vendor's own published install-doc URLs, not a QANATVPN or user credential. Flagged so future secret scans don't mis-triage them and so they are not mistaken for rotatable secrets.
findings.fix: None required for security; optionally annotate the lines as vendor-public download links so automated scanners and future contributors recognize them as non-secret.

findings.title: Fixture verification note: committed OpenSSH ed25519 PEM and SS2022 password are confirmed throwaway/public examples, not live credentials
findings.evidence: test/p1/p1_transports_emit_test.dart:48 — `const String probeEd25519Pem = '''-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- b3BlbnNzaC1rZXktdjEAAAAABG5vbmU...'''`. Code comment on the same block: "A throwaway ed25519 OpenSSH PEM generated for this fixture, comment 'test-fixture-not-a-secret' — no real credential." Verification: decoded container shows key comment `test-fixture-not-a-secret` and the derived public key (`ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NoLWVkMjU1MTkAAAAgDTkBiht7Ng94ECEzHFS/VR0der8eDuwM9sjXrTRvOEs`) is not the author's registered key (https://github.com/QMahyar.keys returns empty); peer address in tests is TEST-NET-3. Similarly test/vpn/endpoints_test.dart:100 uses SS2022 password '8JCsPssfgS8tiRwiMlhA
findings.fix: None needed; optionally move the PEM into a test fixture file with a .NOT-A-SECRET suffix to keep future gitleaks/trufflehog runs quiet.

findings.title: A forged 403 + x-ratelimit-remaining:0 or 429 response is rethrown as a trusted rate-limit signal and blocks geo refreshes until the attacker-chosen reset time
findings.evidence: http_cache.dart:40-41: "if (response.statusCode != 200) { throw HttpException('HTTP ${response.statusCode} for $url'); }" with response.headers['x-ratelimit-remaining'] only consulted on 403 (line 29-30). GeoAsset.refreshAll then propagates it as trusted: geo_asset.dart:145-147 "on RateLimitException { rethrow; }" (comment: "403 with an exhausted rate limit surfaces as [GitHubRateLimitException] (caller schedules a retry at resetAt)"). A proxy/CDN error page returning 403 or 429 — forgeable at will by any on-path attacker for http, or by a compromised mirror CDN — freezes daily geo rule-set refreshes (routing data for the VPN) until the claimed reset epoch, with no distinction between genuin
findings.fix: Only treat 403/429 as rate limiting when the response origin is the pinned api.github.com/raw.githubusercontent.com host (check response headers or the fetched URL), and cap the honored retry-after/reset at a sane maximum before scheduling.

findings.title: Server-controlled ETag is stored unvalidated and replayed verbatim as If-None-Match, letting a hostile origin freeze arbitrary content in the 6h cache
findings.evidence: http_cache.dart:13-15: "if (entry?.etag != null) { requestHeaders['If-None-Match'] = entry!.etag!; }" and line 45 "etag: response.headers['etag']" — whatever string the server returned is echoed back on every revalidation for staleAfter. Because 304 (line 19) refreshes the timestamp of whatever body is already stored (see the poisoned-body finding) and a fresh 200 can itself be attacker bytes, a hostile origin (or MITM on an http import) controls both sides of the revalidation: it can freeze any chosen payload for the full window, or rotate content at will while the client keeps re-arming the window. No etag format validation, no max age enforcement, and no Vary/origin binding on the cached
findings.fix: Sanitize the stored etag (quoted-token length cap), cap total entry age independently of 304 refreshes (absolute expiry, not just staleAfter), and treat 304 as valid only when the response origin matches the request origin.

findings.title: Disk cache meta JSON is trusted wholesale: any local process can plant fetchedAt=9999-... to freeze all cached content permanently
findings.evidence: http_cache.dart:109-114: "final meta = jsonDecode(metaFile.readAsStringSync()) as Map<String, dynamic>; final entry = _CacheEntry(body: bodyFile.readAsBytesSync(), etag: meta['etag'] as String?, fetchedAt: DateTime.parse(meta['fetchedAt'] as String));". fetchedAt is only compared via `_now().difference(entry.fetchedAt) > staleAfter` (line 40) — a far-future timestamp makes the entry permanently fresh (getBytes returns at line 43-44 `if (entry != null && !isStale) return entry.body;` with no network use), and a planted etag is then replayed (line 13-15). On Windows the cache lives under %USERPROFILE%\.qanatvpn\geo\http (or system temp — separate finding), where any co-running process or malwar
findings.fix: Clamp fetchedAt to now on load (reject timestamps > now), cap entry age with an absolute maximum regardless of freshness, and authenticate cache files with an HMAC keyed from app-protected storage, or at minimum drop entries whose etag/meta fails a sanity check.

findings.title: plainFetch buffers the whole response body unbounded in memory (no Content-Length/size cap) — remote server can OOM the UI isolate during subscription import
findings.evidence: plain_fetch.dart:14-17: "final body = await response.fold<List<int>>(<int>[], (acc, chunk) => acc..addAll(chunk));" — no cap is applied and no Content-Length is consulted before buffering; plainFetch is called from the UI isolate (EndpointsController.importText for user-pasted subscription URLs) and from the workmanager background task. A hostile or misbehaving subscription URL (attacker-influenced content in this app's threat model — users import third-party share links) can stream unbounded bytes; addAll on a growable list multiplies peak memory and can OOM the isolate mid-import. The cache layer's own 32-entry ingestion cap (decisions.tsv row 65 "cache unbounded ... 32-entry cap") shows t
findings.fix: Enforce a hard max (e.g. 10-16 MB) while folding: track accumulated length, throw a dedicated exception on overflow, and let the caller surface it as an import failure.

findings.title: Query/fragment fields accepted with embedded CR/LF: crafted sni lands verbatim in engine TLS server_name; newline tags become engine identifiers
findings.evidence: VlessUriParser etc. copy `query['sni']`, `query['path']`, `wsHost`, and `Uri.decodeComponent(uri.fragment)` (parsers.dart:826-829 tag derivation, :664-666) straight into NormalizedEndpoint fields which endpoint_outbound.dart emits into the engine JSON. Reproduced: link with `?sni=a%0d%0aHost:%20evil` -> parsed server_name bytes `[97, 13, 10, 98]` = `a\r\nHost: evil`; `sing-box check` exits 0 (TLS SNI is sent verbatim on the wire, so a crafted SNI is a smuggling primitive against middleboxes); fragment `#tag%0aHTTP/1.1` -> tag contains a real newline which then becomes StoredEndpoint.tag, a groups-editor member and the sing-box outbound `tag` - enabling tag collisions in group references (imp
findings.fix: Strip or reject CR/LF and other C0 control chars in query-derived fields (sni, host, path, uuid, password, fragment-derived tag) at parse time; validate tags against `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$` since they become engine identifiers and group references.

findings.title: _hasExited() uses exit code -1 as a 'still running' sentinel, conflating real exit code -1 (Windows abort/0xFFFFFFFF) with running state
findings.evidence: Future<bool> _hasExited() async { ... final result = await process.exitCode.timeout(Duration.zero, onTimeout: () => -1).catchError((_) => -1); return result != -1; } — exit code -1 (what a Go binary emits on abort/panic via os.Exit(-1) mapping, or 0xFFFFFFFF) is indistinguishable from the timeout sentinel. In start(), 'if (await _hasExited()) { await _exitWait; throw StateError(...); }' would then treat a dead process as running, emit BoxEventKind.started, and the caller (Tunnel.connect) can publish connected; recovery depends solely on the crash event that follows from _exitWait. The stop() backstop also treats the timeout -1 as success.
findings.fix: Use a dedicated wrapper (e.g. a Completer completed by process.exitCode.then, or check via a nullable sentinel like -0x7FFFFFFF plus a separate isAlive probe) instead of conflating real exit code -1 with the timeout marker.

findings.title: Startup success is guessed after a fixed 300ms probe; FATAL after that window is not rethrown from start(), so connect() can briefly report success on a dying engine
findings.evidence: // Give the process a beat to fail on bad config; a still-running process at this point is considered started. await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 300)); if (await _hasExited()) { ... throw StateError(_lastErrorLine ?? 'sing-box.exe exited during startup'); } _events.add(const BoxEvent(BoxEventKind.started)); — a config that fails later than 300ms (e.g. slow wintun driver open, DNS bind error, reality handshake-time config errors) yields a 'started' event first; Tunnel then enforces the (no-op) firewall and sets TunnelState.connected before the crash event arrives, so the user is told 'connected' on a tunnel that is already dead. The _lastErrorLine message is also whateve
findings.fix: Wait on an early-exit race with a startup confirmation signal (e.g. first INFO 'started'/inbound log line or a Clash-API health probe) instead of a fixed 300ms, and hold TunnelState in connecting until the engine is confirmed serving, so a late FATAL cannot be announced as connected.

findings.title: Engine crash detection keys on substring "FATAL" in arbitrary log lines that embed user/subscription-controlled tags
findings.evidence: attachLogWatcher: `if (message.contains("FATAL")) { emitEvent("crashed", message); engineRunning = false; ... }` (BoxEngine.kt:140-146) — no log-level or prefix check, raw substring over every line. The engine embeds user-controlled config tags directly into log prefixes (go/amnezia-box/box.go:360: `logFactory.NewLogger(F.ToString("outbound/", outboundOptions.Type, "[", tag, "]"))`), and tags come from imported share links/subscriptions. A crafted endpoint tag containing "FATAL" makes any INFO/WARN line about that outbound flip engineRunning=false and emit a 'crashed' event, which Dart turns into `_block(TunnelBlockReason.boxCrashed)` (tunnel.dart:586-588) — a remote-triggerable teardown/loc
findings.fix: Match on the structured FATAL level prefix (e.g. line starts with "FATAL[") or consume a proper status/level API instead of substring-scanning; sanitize tags at ingestion (strip/reject control-prefix-like tags).

findings.title: Battery-optimization request intent launched without a resolver check (crash on devices without a settings handler)
findings.evidence: requestIgnoreBatteryOptimizations does `val intent = Intent(Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS).apply { data = Uri.parse("package:...") } ... context.startActivity(intent)` (BatteryOptHelper.kt:27-35) with no try/catch and no resolveActivity check. The permission itself (REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS, manifest line 9) is legitimate here — it is used only for this app's own VPN tunnel, matching the project's 'VPN acceptable use' rule — but a hostile OEM/ROM without a settings handler turns 'requestIgnoreBatteryOptimizations' into an app crash via the vpn_service channel (the Dart caller does not guard either).
findings.fix: Guard with intent.resolveActivity(packageManager) != null (or try/catch) and fall back to Settings.ACTION_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATION_SETTINGS.

findings.title: Tunnel._block() marks the firewall enforced even when enforce() throws or times out, contradicting its own fail-closed comment
findings.evidence: tunnel.dart:553-563: `try { await firewall.enforce().timeout(timeouts.firewallEnforce); } on Object { // ...just without the flag that would relax it later. } _firewallEnforced = true;` — the flag is set on the success path of the try/catch regardless of the exception, so disconnect() will later call `firewall.relax()` for an adapter that never enforced. Harmless today only because PolicyFirewallAdapter is a validation no-op; it is a fail-open seam in exactly the state machine that will drive the real (missing) native firewall.
findings.fix: Set _firewallEnforced = true only inside the try (after enforce() succeeds), or have enforce() return a bool; then relax() on disconnect only when the flag was actually set.

findings.title: Direct dependency set relies on very young, unverified-publisher, single-maintainer packages under caret ranges (file_picker fork platform packages are 2.5 weeks old; material_3_expressive 6 weeks; cue stale 3.5 months)
findings.evidence: pub.dev API data gathered during audit: file_picker platform split `android_file_picker` and `windows_file_picker` — 5 versions each, first published 2026-08-14 (2.5 weeks old), used in lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_screen.dart:155,176 (`FilePicker.saveFile` / `FilePicker.pickFiles`); material_3_expressive — 13 versions since 2026-07-25, third-party repo github.com/paadevelopments/material_3_expressive; cue — 13 versions 2026-04-06..2026-05-19, personal repo Milad-Akarie/cue, no release in ~3.5 months; motor, material_new_shapes — single-maintainer transitive packages. Every checked package has `publisher=(none)` (no verified publisher). All lockfile sha256s verified MATCH against p
findings.fix: Pin exact versions for young/unverified-publisher packages (drop ^ for file_picker, cue, material_3_expressive at minimum), and record a review step for dependency upgrades in docs/decisions.tsv.

findings.title: Lock contains upstream-declared end-of-life no-op SQLite/SQLCipher shims via unused drift_flutter; no encrypted-at-rest database path exists anywhere in the code
findings.evidence: pubspec.lock contains `sqlcipher_flutter_libs ... version: "0.7.0+eol"` and `sqlite3_flutter_libs ... version: "0.6.0+eol"` (both transitive, pulled only by drift_flutter 0.3.1, whose pubspec comment says the deps "don't do anything"). Upstream README of sqlite3_flutter_libs-0.6.0+eol: "Not used anymore, update to version 3.x of package:sqlite3 instead" and "Starting from version 0.6.0, this package no longer does anything." Repo grep confirms no `PRAGMA key` and no sqlcipher reference in lib/ (only two unrelated @pragma('vm:entry-point') hits). Today drift is unused so this is latent, but the declared dependency shape implies a drift/SQLCipher persistence layer that does not exist — if wire
findings.fix: Either implement real SQLCipher encryption (sqlite3 3.x SQLCipher builds + PRAGMA key at DB open) before any drift wiring, or remove the drift/sqlcipher dependencies and the encrypted-DB assumption from the spec/docs.

findings.title: upstream-check.yml is the only workflow without a permissions block — scheduled job's GITHUB_TOKEN inherits repo-default scope instead of least privilege
findings.evidence: upstream-check.yml (947 bytes) declares no `permissions:` key, unlike build-android/build-windows (contents: write) and gh-pages (read/pages/id-token). The weekly scheduled job runs `uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: submodules: recursive` plus `git fetch --all --tags` in go/amnezia-box under the default token scope; on repos whose default workflow permissions are permissive this is a write-scoped token with no need for it. Git actions here are read-only fetch/report, so current impact is limited, but the default-scope grant contradicts the explicit least-privilege pattern used in the other four workflows.
findings.fix: Add a top-level `permissions: contents: read` block to upstream-check.yml.

findings.title: build-android grants contents: write workflow-wide, so build/test steps run with a release-capable token
findings.evidence: build-android.yml:8-9 `permissions: contents: write` (workflow level, applies to both `apk` and `metadata` jobs). Steps that need no write access — 'Install sagernet gomobile' (go install of two binaries), 'Build libbox.aar (with_awg)', 'Flutter test + analyze' (network fetches), 'Build APKs', and the strings sanity check — all execute with a token that can create releases and rewrite repo contents. An action or build-script compromise in any of these steps gains release powers it never needs. Windows is a single job so write is only over-broad per-step, but Android could scope the write to the release/metadata steps via a separate release job.
findings.fix: Move the release upload + metadata generation into a dedicated job with contents: write and give the build/test job contents: read (job-level permissions block).

findings.title: Vendored default profile ships a hardcoded AWG-format private key in the public repo and inside every shipped APK asset / engine config
findings.evidence: ""type": "awg", "tag": "awg-hkg-02", "private_key": "eCbtX5g5Pof3zH0Gu6dzulIzLB0B5xj+OhIfgVtWu1A=", ... "address": "203.0.113.10"" — the same string is used as goodPrivateKey in test/awg/awg_config_test.dart:15, and the peer public_key is invalid hex (not base64 WG key), peer address is TEST-NET-3, so it is a fixture, not a live credential. But the file is committed since the initial MVP commit (5592cf3) in the public repo, declared as a shipped asset in pubspec.yaml ('assets: - profiles/config.wg-awg.json'), and ProfileConfigSource loads it as the base for every merge — profile_config_source.dart keeps it in the engine config: patched['endpoints'] = wgEndpoints + the profile's endpoints. So
findings.fix: Remove the private_key/peer from the vendored profile (keep the schema shape with an empty or clearly dummy value outside the repo history convention), regenerate the key at first run, and note in docs that the committed key is a test fixture (the tests already do: 'test-fixture-not-a-secret').

findings.title: Android manifest omits allowBackup/dataExtractionRules — default cloud backup of app-private dirs (libbox working/temp under filesDir) is enabled
findings.evidence: The <application> element declares only android:label, android:name, android:icon — no android:allowBackup, no android:dataExtractionRules, no android:fullBackupContent. With the attribute absent, the platform default is allowBackup=true, so the app-private dirs auto-participate in cloud/device-to-device backup: this includes libbox's SetupOptions paths (BoxEngine.ensureSetup: "basePath = filesDir.absolutePath; workingPath = filesDir.resolve(\"working\"); tempPath = filesDir.resolve(\"temp\")") and any future drift DB. There are no credentials there today (engine config travels in-memory over the vpn_service MethodChannel), but once the store layout is fixed (finding 4) the backup surface be
findings.fix: Set android:allowBackup="false" (or add dataExtractionRules with cloud-backup/device-transfer exclusion for the secrets/working dirs) before the secure-storage migration lands.

findings.title: System tools spawned by bare name via app-dir/CWD/PATH search order; engine inherits the app CWD; the workingDir constructor parameter is dead code
findings.evidence: `final result = await Process.run('taskkill', <String>['/PID', process.pid.toString()]);` (lines 166-169 and 171-174) and `await Process.start('explorer', <String>[info.assetUrl]);` (updates_screen.dart:129) resolve the program through the CreateProcess search order (app dir → parent CWD → System32 → PATH) because no directory is given. WindowsBoxProcessAdapter never passes a working directory to Process.start, so the engine inherits the app CWD (e.g., a Downloads folder when run from an extracted zip) and all relative resolution inside the child starts there. The constructor field `final String? workingDir;` (line 29) is dead code — declared, never referenced — so the intended pin-down is s
findings.fix: Spawn `%SystemRoot%\System32\taskkill.exe` (expand environment explicitly) and drop the explorer spawn for `url_launcher`/`PlatformRoute`-style https handling; either wire workingDir into Process.start with a pinned safe directory (the bundle dir) and set it for the engine child, or delete the dead parameter.

findings.title: Engine binary has no provenance: gitignored, unsigned, unattested, and never hash-validated at spawn or bundled — silent local replacement is undetectable
findings.evidence: .gitignore lines 18 and 36 exclude `windows/libbox.dll` and `windows/sing-box.exe`, so the 71 MB engine that WindowsBoxProcessAdapter blindly executes is built only by CI (`go build ... -o ../../windows/sing-box.exe ./cmd/sing-box`, build-windows.yml:36) with no Authenticode signing, no cosign/SBOM attestation step (grep for 'sign|attest|cosign' in build-windows.yml: 0 matches), and no bundled digest. start() verifies nothing about the file: it goes straight to `process = await processFactory(_resolvedExe, ...)` — no size/hash check against a pinned constant, and the release zip contains no per-exe manifest the app could verify (sha256-windows.json is a release artifact the app never reads).
findings.fix: Sign the release artifacts (Azure Trusted Signing or self-signed cert distributed in the installer), embed the sing-box.exe SHA-256 from the CI build into the app bundle (asset or compile-time define) and verify it in WindowsBoxProcessAdapter before Process.start, failing closed with a diagnostics message on mismatch.

findings.title: plainFetch buffers the entire response body in memory with no size cap and no per-call isolation of oversized redirect chains
findings.evidence: final response = await request.close(); final body = await response.fold<List<int>>(<int>[], (acc, chunk) => acc..addAll(chunk)); ... return CachedResponse(statusCode: response.statusCode, headers: flatHeaders, body: Uint8List.fromList(body));  // callers parse with jsonDecode/utf8.decode without length checks
findings.fix: Impose a sane response-size ceiling (e.g. 16-64MB, matching the ingestion cache cap philosophy) inside plainFetch by counting chunks and throwing past it.

findings.title: Update mirror fetch (qmahyar.github.io/latest.json) has no integrity pinning and no scheme/host check on the entry url it returns
findings.evidence: static const String defaultMirrorUrl = 'https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/latest.json'; ... final response = await fetchImpl(Uri.parse(url), const <String, String>{}); if (response.statusCode != 200) { return null; } ... assetUrl: entry['url'] as String? ?? '',
findings.fix: Validate that the mirror entry's url is https and within the same GitHub Pages / release origin, and verify it against the sha256 the release pipeline already publishes for latest.json.

findings.title: Wrong-password error class degrades to 'corrupt backup' for tampered envelopes (ArgumentError for wrong nonce size), weakening the documented fail-closed diagnostics
findings.evidence: `on Object catch (error) { throw BackupFormatException('corrupt backup envelope: $error'); }` (lines 242-244) wraps every non-SecretBoxAuthenticationError failure, including ArgumentError for a nonce whose length != 12 (the cryptography 2.9.0 AesGcm enforces 96-bit nonces in checkParameters and throws ArgumentError). So an attacker can tamper with the envelope (e.g. swap nonce length) and the user sees 'Import failed: corrupt backup envelope: ...' instead of an authentication failure, obscuring tampering; conversely a genuine wrong password sometimes surfaces as BackupFormatException (e.g. corrupted MAC bytes) rather than SecretBoxAuthenticationError. The fail-closed property itself holds —
findings.fix: Validate envelope field shapes (nonce exactly 12 bytes after base64Decode, mac exactly 16 bytes) before calling decrypt and map all of them to BackupFormatException; reserve SecretBoxAuthenticationError strictly for MAC verification failure. Add tests for truncated/edited nonce and mac fields.

findings.title: Merge-by-tag 'backup wins' silently overwrites local endpoint credentials on tag collision, with no per-tag confirmation
findings.evidence: Merge folds by tag with backup winning: `final byTag = <String, StoredEndpoint>{ for (final item in existing) item.tag: item, for (final item in endpoints) item.tag: item, }; await _endpointStore.save(byTag.values.toList());` (lines 224-228) — a colliding tag silently replaces the local endpoint's address and credentials (test backup_service_test.dart lines 131-135 confirms 'backup wins on tag collision — the address comes from the backup'). Rules are appended with no dedup: `RuleDocument(rules: <RouteRule>[...existingRules, ...rules.rules])` (lines 240-242), so repeated imports of the same backup accumulate duplicates. The only feedback is 'Restored ${summary.endpoints} endpoints, ${summary
findings.fix: Return and display the list of overwritten/merged tags in BackupSummary before persisting (or require explicit confirmation listing tag collisions), and dedupe appended rules by a stable key (domain+port+outbound) in merge mode.

findings.title: Vendored profile ships a 32-byte credential-shaped private key under an `awg` endpoint and is published on the public GitHub repo (v0.1.0 tag and master)
findings.evidence: profiles/config.wg-awg.json:80-81: `"type": "awg"` with `"private_key": "eCbtX5g5Pof3zH0Gu6dzulIzLB0B5xj+OhIfgVtWu1A="` (44-char base64, WireGuard/awg engine-internal key), plus peer public_key, and zero AmneziaWG I1-I5/Id/Ip fields; H1-H4/S1-S2/Jc/Jmin/Jmax are present and are public junk parameters. Committed since the initial MVP commit `5592cf3` and shipped in tag v0.1.0; the repo is public (api.github.com/repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn → 200) and raw.githubusercontent.com serves the file (→ 200). This is the config the Logs screen surface and sing-box check wrap around, so tooling that prints configs on failure (IDE logs, CI runners, future bug-report exporters) would emit this key verbatim. Inv
findings.fix: Generate a fresh random private_key at build time (or use an obviously fake pattern like all-'A' 44-char base64), add a CI check that fails on any committed key matching base64(hmac)-shaped 32-byte material, and document that the vendored profile is example-only.

findings.title: Logs 'export' is a stub that prints the raw log to platform stdout (logcat on Android, debug console on Windows) instead of copying to clipboard
findings.evidence: `print(buffer.toString())` (logs_screen.dart:242) sends every visible line — including FATAL/ERROR lines with key-decode text, server addresses, and per-connection domains (probed: `outbound connection to github.com:443`) — to the process stdout, which on Android is `flutter` logcat output retained by the system logger, and on Windows `flutter run` console output. The function's own doc comment claims 'copy the visible lines to a buffer the user pastes into a bug report', but no Clipboard.setData call exists, so the only actual side effect is the stdout dump plus a misleading 'Exported (N)' snackbar.
findings.fix: Replace the two print() calls with Clipboard.setData(ClipboardData(text: buffer.toString())) after running the redaction pass from finding 1; add a 'share diagnostics' path later if needed.

findings.title: Engine log listener is the only crash sensor and is scoped by construction — no includeCredentials/config-log command is ever registered, keeping FATAL content down to decode errors (defense-in-depth is one flag away from regressing)
findings.evidence: `SetupOptions().apply { ... logMaxLines = 300; debug = false; commandServerSecret = ""; commandServerListenPort = 0 }` (BoxEngine.kt:203-208). The command client adds only Libbox.CommandLog (line 172); there is no call equivalent to sing-box's config-export with credentials, and no log-level is set beyond `debug = false` (defaults to info) — so no config JSON or key body is dumped today. But the only guard is the default: nothing at the Dart/Kotlin boundary prevents a future command option, a config import carrying `"log":{"level":"debug"}` into a pass-through shape, or a debug build flip from placing full configs on the same `box_events` log channel that the LogsScreen renders verbatim (cha
findings.fix: Keep the allowlist as-is but add a Dart-side assertion/test that TypedConfig JSON never contains 'log' overrides above info, and document in BoxEngine that CommandLog is the sole approved command; add a redaction shim at the LogBus boundary (finding 1) so future level changes are contained.

findings.title: upstream-check.yml and build-linux.yml run without an explicit least-privilege permissions block
findings.evidence: Neither file declares any `permissions:` block (unlike build-android.yml:8, build-windows.yml:8, gh-pages.yml:8 which scope them). The only scheduled workflow in the repo (upstream-check.yml:4-5 `cron: '0 6 * * 1'`) therefore runs with whatever repo-default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions exist; if the repo default is ever permissive (or GitHub policy changes), a scheduled job gains write it never needs. Today the job uses the token for nothing but checkout, so impact is nil — but least privilege is not enforced.
findings.fix: Add `permissions: contents: read` to upstream-check.yml and build-linux.yml (and ideally a repo-level default of `contents: read` with per-job elevation only where releases are written).

findings.title: All third-party actions pinned by mutable tag, not commit SHA, inside contents:write release jobs
findings.evidence: Every `uses:` is a mutable tag reference (`actions/checkout@v4`, `subosito/flutter-action@v2`, `android-actions/setup-android@v3`, `actions/setup-java@v4`, `actions/setup-go@v5`, `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` at build-android.yml:116 and build-windows.yml:62, `actions/deploy-pages@v4` in gh-pages.yml). The release jobs hold `permissions: contents: write` (build-android.yml:8), so if any of these action repos/reused tags is compromised or a tag is moved, attacker code runs with write access to the release channel the app auto-updates from. This is the standard supply-chain gap the rubric calls defense-in-depth.
findings.fix: Pin all third-party `uses:` to full commit SHAs (Dependabot can keep SHAs updated with comments). Highest priority: `softprops/action-gh-release` and `actions/checkout` in the two release workflows.

findings.title: .gitmodules branch field can float past the 57276220 pin via `git submodule update --remote`; no CI pin-equality assertion
findings.evidence: .gitmodules declares `branch = 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15` next to the pinned gitlink `160000 commit 57276220a20679cad762c9644f6abdaf39ab7688`. CI is safe today — grep shows the only submodule usage is `submodules: recursive` (checkout@v4 uses the recorded SHA, no `git submodule update --remote` anywhere), so hoaxisr/amnezia-box cannot push into builds without a human commit moving the gitlink plus a human `v*` tag. But `git submodule update --remote` (or a future checkout config change) would float builds to the upstream branch tip, bypassing the documented pin (Makefile header: 'Fork: hoaxisr/amnezia-box @ ... (SHA 57276220...)'). Nothing in CI asserts the built submodule SHA equals the pin.
findings.fix: Drop the `branch` line from .gitmodules (keep pins explicit), or add a cheap CI assertion before builds: `test "$(git -C go/amnezia-box rev-parse HEAD)" = 57276220a20679cad762c9644f6abdaf39ab7688` so any accidental float fails loudly.

findings.title: VERIFIED CONTROL: no auto-PR/auto-merge path from upstream fork to release artifacts — malicious upstream commit cannot enter builds without a human gitlink bump plus a human tag push (informational record)
findings.evidence: Workflow answers, verified by reading the file end to end: (1) On new upstream commits it does nothing automated — steps are `git fetch --all --tags` (upstream-check.yml:23), `git describe --tags || true`, `git log --oneline -5`, then only `echo "If upstream has a new awg tag, open a bump PR:"` (:31). No `gh pr create`, no gitlink bump, no merge. (2) It runs on schedule (:5) with NO secrets — the file contains no `secrets:` reference and no token usage; the default token is used only for checkout. (3) A malicious hoaxisr/amnezia-box commit cannot reach release artifacts without review: both build workflows check out `submodules: recursive` (build-android.yml:17, build-windows.yml:17) which h
findings.fix: No change required for the auto-merge question. Retain the human gate; consider enabling branch protection on master and adding the automated drift alerting from the related finding so the manual gate actually gets exercised.

findings.title: DesktopPlatformAdapter hard-codes every guard to 'safe' true/false, making the entire guarded connect sequence vacuous on Windows
findings.evidence: desktop_platform_adapter.dart: "Future<bool> isVpnPermissionGranted() async => true; Future<bool> isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations() async => true; Future<bool> isAirplaneMode() async => false;". Tunnel.connect's guarded sequence therefore checks nothing before foreground/config/box.start on Windows — acceptable in principle (no VpnService on desktop), but it means the firewall/permission guarantees claimed in tunnel.dart's doc ("falls back to firewall-enforced `blocked` on every failure path, so no caller can skip a step and leak") are, on Windows, entirely dependent on PolicyFirewallAdapter's no-op validation.
findings.fix: Replace hard-coded true stubs with the real guards as they land (e.g. config-exists check before start), and document which guards are intentionally vacuous on desktop.

findings.title: Endpoints list shows no per-endpoint latency despite the TCP ping sweeper already existing
findings.evidence: goal.md §15 Extra Deeps (frozen): 'Simple Ping TCP 5000ms + sort by ping'; research/09-WG-Tunnel.md §6: ping monitor with 'Display Detailed Ping Stats toggle shows latency/jitter/packets sent/lost/last success'. App: LatencyController/SocketLatencyPinger (lib/modules/routing/latency.dart) sweeps endpoints, but its only consumer is groups_screen.dart:37 (refresh() for the _bestMsSuffix); endpoints_screen list rows (ListView.builder at line 89) show label/protocol/source and delete only — no latency column or sort control.
findings.fix: Watch latencyProvider in the endpoints list rows (tag→ms lookup already exists in LatencyState) and add a sort toggle; the sweep and pinger are already implemented and just need UI wiring.

findings.title: Blocked/connecting states drop the endpoint tag from the UI: StateTile shows 'no endpoint' exactly when the user needs to see which server failed
findings.evidence: Competitors keep the failing server identity visible: v2rayNG notification 'Connected: <remark>' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:448); WG Tunnel per-tunnel health LED on the main screen (research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:297-302). App: tasks/review-swarm-full.md:129-131 already flagged it internally; VpnState.blocked() constructs with tag null (vpn_notifier.dart:30-31) and _lastTag is not carried into the blocked state, so after a crash StateTile falls back to l10n.homeNoEndpoint (home.dart) and the user cannot tell which of their endpoints died without opening the endpoints screen.
findings.fix: Thread the tag through VpnState.blocked/connecting (keep _lastTag in the notifier mapping) so StateTile and the future notification both show which endpoint is connecting, reconnecting, or failed.

findings.title: Diagnostics ping is one fixed target (1.1.1.1:443); the frozen PingRoute per-hop traceroute and sort-by-ping diagnostics UI are absent
findings.evidence: goal.md:111 (frozen) locks "PingRoute per-hop"; goal.md:131 gives `diag` responsibility "DNS scanner + ping + traceroute + Drift"; docs/prototype-final.html:299-302 ships 'Ping all (TCP 5000ms)', 'Sort by ping', 'Traceroute' buttons and "PingRoute per-hop • Min/Max/Avg/Last • fl_chart". SPEC.md:246 defines the interface as "`snapshot() -> HealthReport {score 0-6, hijacked, pingMs, stability, hops}`". App: HealthReport has no hops field (lib/modules/health/health.dart:11-19); the diagnostics tab shows exactly one probe, 'Ping (TCP 1.1.1.1:443)' with a single ms value (lib/modules/health/diagnostics_screen.dart:58-64) on a 10s timer to a hardcoded target (lib/modules/health/health.dart:55-56);
findings.fix: Add a per-hop PingRoute (traceroute) behind HealthReport.hops per the SPEC.md:246 interface, plus a ping-target picker and per-endpoint ping list in diagnostics, matching the prototype's Ping & traceroute tile.

findings.title: Engine log level hardcoded to 'info' — no debug-level setting for diagnosing DPI failures
findings.evidence: lib/modules/routing/config_assembler.dart:67 emits 'log': {'level': 'info'} with no input parameter and no setting (grep 'log_level|LogLevel' in lib/ matches only the Logs screen's client-side all/errors filter in lib/modules/logs/logs_screen.dart:14-16, which cannot raise engine verbosity). research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:249: 'log-level: info (debug/info/warning/error/silent) — Settings → Log Level'; research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:309: 'Settings → Local Logs Monitor (Go LOG_LEVEL=debug)'; research/04-Nekoray.md:332: 'Init status->result->coreConfig["log"]={"level":log_level}'. Debugging a censored-network failure requires DEBUG-level engine logs (route decisions, sniffs) that 'info' never produce
findings.fix: Add a log-level setting (info/debug/warn/error) persisted and fed into the assembler's log block; the Logs screen filter then becomes genuinely useful.

findings.title: Update cadence not configurable and no data-reset action anywhere in the app
findings.evidence: lib/main.dart:129 hardcodes Workmanager frequency 'Duration(hours: 24)' with no user control, and grep 'reset|wipe|clear data' across lib/ matches only HTTP rate-limit headers — no factory-reset or clear-all-stores action exists on any screen (backup export/import live buried in the endpoints screen toolbar, lib/modules/vpn/repositories/endpoints_screen.dart:50-56). research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:52: update check 'can be disabled in Settings → Update' for users who must not phone GitHub; docs/prototype-final.html:335-336 plans an Updates tile with 'Rule sets: 24h ETag/6h/Manual' and 'App updater: Daily platform-aware/Manual' selects. Users on metered or monitored networks cannot turn the dai
findings.fix: Add an Updates section on the settings screen (enable daily check, interval) consulted before Workmanager registration, plus a Danger-zone 'reset all data' action that clears ~/.qanatvpn stores.

findings.title: Health probes are only meaningful while the tab is open — no Drift persistence or history view of score/stability across sessions
findings.evidence: Tunnel.connect keeps only `lastConnectMetrics` phase timings (StatsTile, home.dart:225-272) and Health keeps an in-memory `_pingResults` ring of 20 booleans (health.dart:71-72,96-102); nothing is persisted, so after a crash/restart the diagnostics tab starts at 0% with no knowledge of whether the tunnel was failing an hour ago. SPEC.md:246 ('Drift retention `db.db` + `dbCacheLimit`') and todo.md:63 acceptance ('Drift + network_reachability Rust') define the sink; tasks/review-swarm-full.md:139-141 already records this as 'no hops, no stream' spec drift. Competitor model: WG-Tunnel's health LED is 'hierarchical determination every ~2-5s' with a 2-minute log-signal window and configurable ping
findings.fix: Persist each snapshot (timestamp, score, hijacked, pingMs) into the drift DB behind the existing Health interface and add an interval control; the stability window then survives process restarts.

findings.title: No rule-verification / routing-observation flow for the 30-field editor — users cannot test which rule matches a given destination
findings.evidence: The only diagnostic view of rule behavior is nothing — grep for observatory/traceroute/per-hop/hops in lib/ returns zero matches; the compiler validates ordering statically (firewall.validateOrdering) and urltest sweeps exist only for auto-select (routing/latency.dart). SPEC.md:246 explicitly promises 'PingRoute per-hop (fl_chart)' and goal.md §15 'PingRoute per-hop', with the prototype carrying a PingRoute tile on the diagnostics screen (docs/prototype-final.html:288). When a user adds a rule for `package_name: com.foo -> PROXY` and com.foo still goes direct, there is no in-app way to see which rule matched; competitors can: v2rayNG's 'Test routing' simulates the rule chain for a given URL
findings.fix: Phase 1 (cheap): add a rule-dry-run field on the diagnostics tab that evaluates the compiled RoutingPolicy against a user-entered domain/IP and prints the matched rule. Phase 2: hops list in HealthReport for per-hop display.

findings.title: Diagnostics has no connection to the 7-scenario leak-test suite the project markets — leak verification is an external manual ritual, not a product flow
findings.evidence: grep for dnsleak/ipleak/browserleaks in lib/ is empty and there is no way to run the promised leak tests from the product; they exist only as a CI shell script + manual checklist (scripts/leak_test.sh, SPEC.md:343 '7 scenarios: reboot+startup... split audit'). SPEC.md:334 even requires coverage for `lib/modules/diagnostics` — the leak-test path is a spec-locked product capability, not just dev tooling, and the sec deep module lists '7 tests' as its responsibility (AGENTS.md capability map: `sec` = AGPL + secrets + max firewall + 7 tests). Competitors embed the check: Hiddify's troubleshooting docs walk users through dnsleaktest.com/ipleak.net (research/07-Hiddify.md:325) and FlClash's DNS do
findings.fix: Ship the in-tunnel echo checks (DNS resolver identity, egress IP via mixed/SOCKS inbound) as a 'Run leak check' action on the diagnostics tab; keep the full 7-scenario matrix as the on-device manual pass.

findings.title: Unlocalized numerals and a raw ISO-8601 timestamp shown to FA users
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/07-Hiddify.md:435 'Persian-friendly UI' as the FA-audience benchmark; goal.md:15 deep lock 'i18n/RTL ... like GRoute EN/FA' implies full locale formatting. Code side: lib/modules/updates/updates_screen.dart:32 renders `lastCheckedAt?.toIso8601String()` directly as the idle-card text — FA users see '2026-09-04T12:34:56.000Z' instead of an intl-formatted date. lib/l10n/app_localizations_fa.dart:63 generates plain interpolation `'مرحله $step از 3'` (Western digits, literal ASCII '3') with no NumberFormat; lib/modules/vpn/screens/home.dart:215 'connect ${metrics.total.inMilliseconds} ms' and diagnostics '${report.pingMs} ms' keep Western digits; endpoints_screen.dart:10
findings.fix: Format the last-checked timestamp with intl DateFormat + fa locale and use NumberFormat for counts/milliseconds so Persian digits (۱۲۳) render in the FA locale; translate the 'manual' source suffix.

findings.title: Semantics labels themselves are hardcoded English and diverge from the visible label (screen readers announce different text than sighted users see)
findings.evidence: goal.md:110 lock 'Semantics ... (like GRoute EN/FA)' and AGENTS.md l10n rule. Code: StatsTile Semantics label 'Connect metrics: $headline' (home.dart:278) is English and not even button:true although the tile is inside a tappable grid; UpdateTile announces hardcoded 'Updates' (home.dart:352) even when the visible text says 'Update ${info.version}' (345) - screen reader and sighted users get different information; groups 'Measure latency' and diagnostics 'Refresh' tooltips announce in English to Persian users while ARB already has diagnosticsRefresh and updatesInstall keys that zero screens consume (grep confirms unused).
findings.fix: Localize every Semantics label through ARB (reuse diagnosticsRefresh/updatesInstall), make StatsTile's label reflect the localized headline, and add a test asserting Semantics label == visible label for status tiles.

findings.title: Status-color contrast is unverified: M3 dynamic fromSeed defaults are trusted with no WCAG AA test for primary-on-primaryContainer / error-on-errorContainer pairs
findings.evidence: SPEC.md:36 a11y column promises 'WCAG AA' but lists no contrast verification mechanism; AGENTS.md asks for M3 token discipline. Code: theme uses ColorScheme.fromSeed(0xFF245C4F) for both brightnesses (app.dart:64-77) with no contrast assertions in test/ (grep finds none), and screens compose non-guaranteed pairs - primary icon on primaryContainer in PowerTile connected state (home.dart:87-99), error text on errorContainer in rules validation card (rules_screen.dart:99-107) - Material only guarantees contrast for designed on-color pairs (onPrimary/onErrorContainer), not arbitrary cross-pair combos chosen here.
findings.fix: Add a unit test computing WCAG ratios from the generated scheme for each used pair (primary-on-primaryContainer, error-on-errorContainer, error-on-surface) and switch to the guaranteed pairs (onPrimaryContainer etc.) where the ratio falls below 4.5:1.

findings.title: Group editor members picker has a silent empty state: with zero endpoints the Members section is blank and Save is disabled with no hint
findings.evidence: GroupsScreen._GroupFormSheet renders 'Members' title then 'for (final tag in widget.knownTags)' — with no endpoints imported and no groups, knownTags is empty and the section is a bare heading followed by nothing; Save's onPressed is '_members.isEmpty || _tagController.text.isEmpty ? null' with no message, so the button looks broken. Karing validates inputs up front and gives feedback ('ServerManager.validAddSubscription(url, remark) checks non-empty, URL form...' research/01-Karing.md:405). There is also no loading state on the add-rule/add-group path: saving writes through the debounced saver with no confirmation, and validation only appears after the sheet closes via the error card on the
findings.fix: Show an inline empty-state in the Members section ('Import endpoints first' + a link to /endpoints) and a helper text under the disabled Save explaining why it is disabled.

findings.title: Diagnostics first load is an unlabeled spinner (up to ~8s of DNS+ping probes) with no probing/error state and no in-progress feedback on Refresh
findings.evidence: Build() runs '_tick()' fire-and-forget and returns null; the screen renders 'if (report == null) const Expanded(child: Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator()))' with no timeout, no 'probing…' label, and no error state — _tick swallows probe exceptions ('on Object { // Probe failure leaves the last report on screen }'), so if the first snapshot ever throws the spinner persists with the Refresh IconButton as the only escape. Once loaded there is no stale/probing distinction between the 10s ticks. Compare v2rayNG's bounded probes with visible results (research/06-V2RayNG.md:426) and Hiddify's per-probe delay/error display (research/07-Hiddify.md:381) — both show bounded, labelled probe state
findings.fix: Give DiagnosticsController a tri-state (loading/ready/error) with a timeout on the first snapshot, render a labelled 'running probes…' placeholder instead of the bare spinner, and keep the last report visible with a 'stale' badge between ticks.

findings.title: No post-finish confirmation or review of what the wizard configured (grants can silently fail with success shown)
findings.evidence: Competitor: WireSock validates profile fields live in its wizard — research/10-WireSock.md:421 ('text mode validates keys live: unknown params highlighted red, illegal Jc>200 etc. block save') — and the vendor-fork reference (go/amnezia-box/clients/android/.../MainActivity.kt:280-284) shows permission state echoed back to the UI. App: requestBatteryExemption() sets batteryExempt: true unconditionally even when requestIgnoreBatteryOptimizations was denied (lib/modules/onboarding/wizard.dart:76-83), so the granted state is a lie; requestVpnPermission() reports only the l10n 'Granted' button label (lines 210-214). After finish(), the wizard vanishes (step=done, wizard.dart:112) — no summary of
findings.fix: Mirror the real grant result into batteryExempt/vpnGranted, and add a completion summary (mode + app count, like the prototype's status dump) on the home grid after finish(); surface the stored SplitChoice in a read-only card.

findings.title: Home tiles and updates screen leak hardcoded English status strings ('No connect yet', 'connect N ms', 'Updates', 'Download & install')
findings.evidence: Competitor: research/01-Karing.md:42 — 30+ languages including فارسی across all surfaces. App: home.dart:269-278 shows 'No connect yet'/'Disconnected'/'connect ${metrics.total.inMilliseconds} ms' with Semantics label 'Connect metrics: $headline'; home.dart:347,352 'Updates'/'Update ${info.version}'; updates_screen.dart:29 title 'Updates', :47 'Update v${info.version} for ${info.platformKey}', :101 'Download & install' — none appear in app_en.arb/app_fa.arb (which stop at updatesCheckNowButton). goal.md §15 and the progress log ('UI polish (l10n everywhere...)') mark l10n as done; these status/error-adjacent strings slipped through. Persian users see a mixed-language home screen exactly in th
findings.fix: Add ARB keys for stats states (noConnect, disconnected, connectMs) and update strings (title, versionForPlatform, downloadInstall), then use l10n in StatsTile, UpdateTile, and UpdatesScreen.

findings.title: Every TOR-CHAIN endpoint connect fails with a misleading 'Tor chain is down' error although no Tor sidecar exists in the build
findings.evidence: Competitor: research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:577 — spawn failures explain the fix: 'spawn failure toast Insufficient privileges → Install Service Mode or run as administrator'. App: channel_adapters.dart:123-125 LocalSocksTorAdapter.isSocksUp probes 127.0.0.1:9050 and 'The Tor sidecar is a later milestone; until it exists the port is down', so tunnel.dart:354-369 deterministically blocks with TunnelBlockReason.torDown → tunnel_l10n.dart blockTorDown 'Tor chain is down' / 'زنجیره تور قطع است'. The wording implies a transient outage of a working chain (retry later), when in fact no Tor sidecar ships in this build; there is no hint to switch to a non-TOR endpoint or that the feature is not yet av
findings.fix: Add a distinct block reason/message ('Tor sidecar is not installed in this build — pick a non-Tor endpoint') and/or a badge on TOR-CHAIN endpoints before connect, instead of reusing the transient-sounding 'chain is down' wording.

findings.title: No share-out of endpoints (QR image, copy link, system share sheet): import without export breaks device-to-device migration
findings.evidence: v2rayN: 'Right-click node -> Share -> QR Code generates qrcode.png... Share -> Copy Link copies to clipboard... multi-select nodes -> Share -> Export selected as Base64 subscription' (research/05-V2RayN.md:458); V2RayNG: 'Share -> Export to Clipboard -> FmtBase.toUri() + QR code bitmap via ZXing' (research/06-V2RayNG.md:265); WG Tunnel exports '.conf or ZIP... via FileProvider + Intent.ACTION_SEND' (research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:361). App: the endpoints ListTile trailing action is delete-only (endpoints_screen.dart), no share_plus/qr_flutter/zxing2 in pubspec.yaml, and the l10n surface has no share strings; moving one node from phone to PC requires the encrypted .qnv backup or re-copying from the
findings.fix: Add per-endpoint share: copy the share-link URI (the URI parsers already know each format) and render a QR (qr_flutter) in a bottom sheet; expose .conf export for WG/AWG entries via ACTION_SEND/FileProvider on Android.

findings.title: No helper to build an auto-pick urltest group from all measured endpoints (Karing/Throne have one-tap auto groups)
findings.evidence: Competitor: research/03-NekoBox-Android.md:446-447 documents UI Groups where urltest groups are created and 'ConfigBuilder.buildGroups() writes selector/urltest outbounds'; research/02-Throne.md:192 'Add Auto-selector: GUI create profile group of type Auto Selector that probes a selector list and picks best via urltest'. App: the groups form sheet (groups_screen.dart:183-283) lets the user create urltest groups but offers no 'add best/fastest members' action — _members is a plain checkbox list over knownTags with no latency column in the member picker rows (CheckboxListTile(title: Text(tag)) at line ~226), and LatencyState is not consulted during editing; grep for bestTag in lib/ confirms no
findings.fix: In the urltest group form, show each candidate member's last measured ms and offer an 'auto-fill from fastest N' action driven by LatencyState.bestTag()/samples.

findings.title: No share-link / QR export of endpoints — only encrypted full-store backup
findings.evidence: v2rayNG's outbound flow is symmetric: 'Share → Export to Clipboard → FmtBase.toUri() + QR code bitmap via ZXing' (research/06-V2RayNG.md §5), and v2rayN adds 'v2rayn://' internal share preserving non-standard fields (research/05-V2RayN.md §5). The app's endpoints screen offers only the encrypted backup '.qnv' export (endpoints_screen.dart:153-171 via BackupService.exportBytes) and the parsers define import-only URI decoding (parsers.dart has *_UriParser with no toUri counterpart); grep for qr|share-link emit across lib/ finds nothing. Moving one endpoint to another device or sharing with a colleague requires shipping the whole encrypted store.
findings.fix: Add per-endpoint share-link emit (serialize NormalizedEndpoint back to vless/vmess/ss/trojan/... URIs) with copy-to-clipboard and QR generation on mobile.

findings.title: No per-endpoint detail view: imported nodes cannot be inspected before connecting
findings.evidence: Competitors provide per-profile detail: research/13-Matsuri-SagerNet.md:372 per-profile detail activity with live traffic; v2rayNG detail + share per profile (06-V2RayNG.md:452 swipe/list actions). Here the endpoints card shows only 'label · protocol · sourceUrl' (endpoints_screen.dart:96-100) — after importing an unknown subscription the user cannot verify a node's address/port/uuid/reality params before connecting to it, and combined with the missing detail view cannot even confirm which node maps to which tag used in groups/rules.
findings.fix: Open the same per-protocol read-only detail sheet built for editing (finding 2) on tap — one widget serves inspection now and editing later.

findings.title: Health/diagnostics state is in-memory only — no history persistence despite the Drift lock in the diag deep module
findings.evidence: goal.md:15 lists 'Drift sqlite' inside the diagnostics deep and the capability map assigns diag 'DNS scanner + ping + traceroute + Drift' (goal.md:16). Health keeps everything in process memory: _pingResults ring of 20 booleans (health.dart:65-66), stability recomputed per probe, HealthReport state held by an autoDispose DiagnosticsController that dies with the tab (diagnostics_controller.dart:10-20). pubspec.yaml includes drift ^2.34.3 but grep finds zero Drift usage in lib/. After an app restart the user has no stability trend, no score history, nothing to correlate 'it worked yesterday, fails today' — a power-user feature Slipnet-style competitors and the project's own design treat as tab
findings.fix: Persist each HealthReport row (timestamp, score, hijacked, pingMs, stability) into a Drift table written from DiagnosticsController._tick, and render a 24h sparkline/history list on the Diagnostics tab; prune rows older than 7 days.

findings.title: StatsTile hardcodes English status text including its screen-reader Semantics label
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/09-WG-Tunnel.md:369 shows the bar — AWG invariant errors surfaced with a toast and inline checks ('S1+56 != S2 toast'). App side: AWG validation is good, but StatsTile (modules/vpn/screens/home.dart:219-227) hardcodes 'No connect yet' / 'Disconnected' / 'connect N ms' and even the accessibility label 'Semantics(label: "Connect metrics: $headline")' — English strings announced to screen readers on a Persian UI. The connect-metrics phase names ('grant', 'box', 'firewall') are also raw English identifiers shown directly to the user (home.dart:229-237).
findings.fix: Add ARB keys for the metrics tile states and localize the Semantics label; map phase names to localized words.

findings.title: Dead l10n keys (diagnosticsTitle, updatesTitle, updatesCheckNowButton) while screens hardcode the same titles in English
findings.evidence: Competitor side: research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md:283 shows consistent localized failure presentation on the update path. App side: app_en.arb:95-96 ships "diagnosticsTitle": "Diagnostics" / "updatesTitle": "Updates" (both locales) plus "updatesCheckNowButton" (app_en.arb:97), but updates_screen.dart:29 renders Text('Updates') hardcoded and diagnostics_screen.dart:32 uses tooltip: 'Refresh' hardcoded — the l10n keys were generated and abandoned. Same dead-key risk applies to updatesCheckNowButton (screen builds its own 'Check now' via l10n.updatesCheckNow instead).
findings.fix: Wire the existing ARB keys into the two screens (or delete them from both ARBs) so the l10n surface stays truthful.

findings.title: Artifact naming doc drift: AGENTS.md/SPEC.md promise qanatvpn_v1.2.3_arm64/_arm/_amd64 APKs from '3 jobs'; the workflow emits ABI-dir names (_arm64-v8a/_armeabi-v7a/_x86_64) from 4 workflows
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:113: 'Tag v1.2.3 -> 3 jobs produce qanatvpn_v1.2.3_arm64.apk etc.'; SPEC.md:405: 'produce qanatvpn_v1.2.3_arm64.apk, _arm.apk, _amd64.apk, _windows_amd64.zip'. Reality: build-android.yml 'Rename artifacts + sha256' loops abi in {arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64} producing qanatvpn_v0.1.0_arm64-v8a.apk / _armeabi-v7a.apk / _x86_64.apk (metadata job filters likewise match 'arm64-v8a'). Repo also contains 4 release workflows (build-android, build-windows, build-linux, gh-pages) + upstream-check, not '3 jobs'.
findings.fix: Update AGENTS.md:113 and SPEC.md:405 to the real ABI-based names (arm64-v8a / armeabi-v7a / x86_64) and count, or rename the workflow outputs to the documented short names (would require updating the metadata job filters and SPEC.md:404 updater asset patterns together).

findings.title: No caching in the android job; setup-go's implicit module cache fails every run because go.sum lives in the submodule, not the repo root
findings.evidence: Run 33900799214 annotations: '! Restore cache failed: Dependencies file is not found in /home/runner/work/qanatvpn/qanatvpn. Supported file pattern: go.sum' — setup-go@v5 (no cache: input set) tries to cache but the Go module lives in submodule go/amnezia-box (go/amnezia-box/go.sum exists; repo root has none), so every run re-downloads Go modules. The job also has no actions/cache for pub (~200MB re-fetch each run), gradle (~2GB), or the ~2GB NDK install.
findings.fix: Either set 'cache: false' on setup-go or 'cache-dependency-path: go/amnezia-box/go.sum'; add actions/cache for ~/.gradle, ~/.pub-cache, and consider caching $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/28.2.13676358 keyed on the NDK version.

findings.title: workflow_dispatch on master can never complete: release/upload steps resolve a non-tag ref (TAG="master")
findings.evidence: build-android.yml metadata step: 'TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}' then 'gh release upload "$TAG" latest.json --clobber' — on a master dispatch this is 'gh release upload master latest.json' against a repo with no 'master' release (gh errors: release not found), and the apk job's softprops/action-gh-release step similarly resolves its target from a tag ref. Evidence path: dispatch run 33900399270 currently fails earlier (sdkmanager 127) so this has never been exercised, but by construction a master dispatch can only fail at the release steps.
findings.fix: Gate the release and metadata jobs to tag refs only: add 'if: startsWith(github.ref, "refs/tags/v")' to the softprops step and the metadata job (or restrict workflow_dispatch to a bare dry-run without release steps).

findings.title: npm belief check: no QANATVPN/Qanat package exists on npm under any related name
findings.evidence: Reality: curl https://registry.npmjs.org/qanatvpn → {"error":"Not found"}; /qanat-vpn → Not found; /qanatvpn → Not found; /@qmahyar%2fqanatvpn → Not found; registry search text=qanatvpn → 0 results; text=qanat → only an unrelated junk package "@dsr-rollback-org-geans-tunny-qanat-their/...". No QANATVPN or Qanat package exists under any plausible name (no doc claims one, so this is verification rather than drift, but the belief should be corrected: the only real distribution artifacts are the GitHub release assets).
findings.fix: No action needed beyond telling the user there is nothing on npm; if a package is ever desired it would have to be published first.

findings.title: setup-go cache restore fails on every CI job because the repo has no go.sum — the root go.mod is an empty vestige
findings.evidence: Reality: run 33900799141 annotation "Restore cache failed: Dependencies file is not found in D:\a\qanatvpn\qanatvpn. Supported file pattern: go.sum" (same on the android runner). Root go.mod is an empty module ("module qanatvpn / go 1.25") with no Go code and no go.sum at the tag (`git cat-file -e v0.1.0:go.sum` → fatal: path 'go.sum' does not exist). The real build in go/amnezia-box has its own committed go.mod + go.sum, so builds are reproducible; only the useless root-level cache attempt and the vestigial root go.mod are noise. Not a doc claim, cosmetic.
findings.fix: Delete the empty root go.mod, or add `cache-dependency-path: go/amnezia-box/go.sum` to actions/setup-go@v5 so the cache actually works.

findings.title: Stub job lacks the least-privilege permissions block both sibling workflows declare
findings.evidence: Doc/peer claim — build-android.yml:11-12: "permissions:\n  contents: write" and build-windows.yml:11-12: "permissions:\n  contents: write" (both need write to upload release assets). Reality — build-linux.yml has no `permissions:` key at all (verified: grep "permissions" over the file returns nothing), so job `stub` runs with the repo-default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions (write-capable on repos with default settings) for a job whose only actions are checkout and echo.
findings.fix: Add `permissions: contents: read` to build-linux.yml for least privilege — or simply delete the workflow per the kill recommendation, which moots this.

findings.title: AGENTS.md still lists push/CI as open ('no git remote — user creates repo') after the repo went live with tags pushed
findings.evidence: Doc claim (AGENTS.md:138): "- **Open (all need external resources):** on-device proof (no adb device), push/CI (no git remote — user creates repo), website polish, logical AND/OR rule-groups UI (compiler+store support it), on-device 7 leak tests." Reality: `gh run list --repo QMahyar/qanatvpn` returns tag v0.1.0 runs for build-android/build-windows/build-linux/gh-pages (remote exists, tag pushed); handoff.md:31 itself says "repo live at `github.com/QMahyar/qanatvpn` (public, AGPL). Tag `v0.1.0` pushed". Stale in the opposite direction from handoff: the remote exists, though CI is not green.
findings.fix: Update the Open list: replace 'push/CI (no git remote — user creates repo)' with the current open CI items (Android NDK install fix, github-pages tag policy, latest.json on the release).

findings.title: Node 20 deprecation: actions/checkout@v4 and actions/configure-pages@v5 force-run on Node 24
findings.evidence: Run 33897419099 annotation: "! Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v4, actions/configure-pages@v5. For more information see: https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/". gh-pages.yml:21 uses actions/checkout@v4; :36 uses actions/configure-pages@v5.
findings.fix: When next editing the workflow, bump actions/checkout and actions/configure-pages to versions targeting Node 24; purely future-proofing, no functional impact today.

findings.title: go-version '1.25' in workflow vs toolchain actually used to build libbox (1.26.5 per todo.md)
findings.evidence: Doc: AGENTS.md pins the stack at "Go 1.25" and SPEC.md:Commands uses Go 1.25 in CI, which the yml follows (`go-version: '1.25'`). Reality: tasks/todo.md:18 records the actual build toolchain as "Go 1.26.5 + gomobile + NDK 28 + JDK 17", and root go.mod/go.amnezia-box go.mod may declare a higher toolchain. The setup-go step is also unused by any subsequent step (no go build/test in this workflow), so it is dead weight either way — but as written, a future expansion of this workflow (e.g. `make lib_android` per plan.md:54) would build the aar with Go 1.25 while local verification uses 1.26.5.
findings.fix: Drop the setup-go step until the workflow actually builds Go artifacts, or align it with the go.mod toolchain directive in one place (AGENTS.md says Ask-first for toolchain pin changes).

findings.title: Semver comparison collapses prerelease and build metadata, diverging from the documented 'semver compare'
findings.evidence: Doc: SPEC.md:404 — "semver compare, filter asset by `platform`". Reality: updater.dart:29-35 — `core = version.replaceFirst(RegExp(r'^v'), '').split('-').first` then a 3-component loop with `int.tryParse(parts[i]) ?? 0` → '1.2.3-rc.1' == '1.2.3' (a user on a prerelease build is never prompted for the stable of the same numbers), and '1.0.0+9' == '1.0.0+1' ('0+9'.tryParse → null → 0) so pubspec build numbers are invisible to the comparison. Mitigating: releases/latest excludes prereleases, and PackageInfo.version drops the +build suffix locally — but mirror/API 'version' strings with suffixes compare equal, not newer.
findings.fix: Either strip '+build' and compare prerelease tags explicitly (semver: prerelease < release) in _semverKey, or document the 3-numeric-component limitation; add a test for v1.2.4-rc.1 vs 1.2.3.

findings.title: gh-pages downloads release assets from the frozen tag ref — future re-runs of old tags publish stale mirrors
findings.evidence: Code claim (gh-pages.yml:29-32): "Mirror latest.json straight from the release the metadata job attached" via `gh release download "$TAG"` inside a checkout that is `on: push: tags` — `gh` resolves the TAG's assets at run time, but the workflow file itself is the tag's frozen version. Reality: this run downloaded (or tried to) from release v0.1.0 which has no latest.json; had the metadata job uploaded it an hour later, the deployed site would carry a version of latest.json from whenever deploy happened, and a future v0.2.0 re-deploy of the old tag would re-serve stale assets. Handoff doc claim (tasks/handoff.md:31) treats the mirror as a live artifact: "then site mirror at https://qmahyar.gi
findings.fix: After re-cutting the tag with the sequenced gh-pages fix, the mirror is refreshed on every tag push — document that gh-pages deploys are per-release (tag) events and that manual hotfixes to the site require re-running gh-pages against the newest tag.

findings.title: UPDATE_CHANNEL dart-define is emitted by workflows and SPEC but no code reads it
findings.evidence: Reality: build-android.yml:91 `flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi --no-tree-shake-icons --dart-define=UPDATE_CHANNEL=androidApk` and SPEC.md:78/89 repeat the pattern (`--dart-define=UPDATE_CHANNEL=androidApk`, windowsPortable). `grep -r UPDATE_CHANNEL lib/` and `grep -r fromEnvironment lib/` -> no matches; the define is dead in the built app. SPEC.md:Commands presents it as part of the documented release command.
findings.fix: Either implement the channel read (String.fromEnvironment('UPDATE_CHANNEL')) where channel matters (e.g. updater source selection) or drop the define from workflows and SPEC.md:Commands to keep the documented release command truthful.

findings.fix: Update AGENTS.md:46/:113 and SPEC.md:120 to match the real workflow: 4 tag-triggered workflows, asset pattern qanatvpn_v{V}_{arm64-v8a|armeabi-v7a|x86_64}.apk + windows zip, latest.json from the metadata job, NDK 28.2.13676358 / android-37 / build-tools 37.0.0, and build-linux documented as a stub until v1.1.

findings.title: Success Criteria 7 asset naming and CI shape do not match the workflows: spec promises qanatvpn_v1.2.3_windows_amd64.zip + sha256; workflow emits qanatvpn_v0.1.0_windows-x64.zip + sha256-windows.json, and a gh-pages job exists outside the '3 jobs parallel' model

findings.fix: Align SC7 asset names and sha256 format with build-windows.yml output (qanatvpn_vX_windows-x64.zip + sha256-windows.json) and add the gh-pages/latest.json producer contract to the CI section.

findings.title: Git workflow says branch is "main" — reality is master (local and GitHub default)
findings.evidence: Doc claim (AGENTS.md:113): "Branch: `main` + feature branches `feat/<module-id>` (e.g., `feat/tunnel-lifecycle-03`)." Reality: `git branch -a` → "* master" only; `gh api repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn --jq .default_branch` → "master"; all 7 recent commits landed directly on master (git log). An agent following AGENTS.md would push/branch against main, which does not exist.
findings.fix: Change "Branch: `main`" to "Branch: `master`" (or actually rename the default branch to main on GitHub + locally, and update handoff.md which already says "Git `master`").

findings.title: AGENTS.md says "22 locks" (twice); goal.md header says "All 21 locks"
findings.evidence: Doc claims (AGENTS.md:14): "13 VPNs matrix vs your 22 locks"; (AGENTS.md:15): "22 locks, 10 glossary terms, grilling Q1-10". Reality: goal.md:3 states "FROZEN 2026-08-30 07:00 UTC. All 21 locks + 3 refines + 4 extra deeps …"; no "22" appears in goal.md. CONTEXT.md (the glossary) mentions neither count. One of the two numbers is wrong, so agents auditing against the spec cannot trust the lock inventory referenced as frozen.

findings.title: CONTEXT.md Tunnel interface is wrong: connect(tag) -> TunnelState; actual connect returns Future<void>, state via getter/stream — plus stale "decision pending round 2" on NormalizedEndpoint
findings.evidence: CONTEXT.md: "Interface `Tunnel.connect(tag) -> TunnelState`"; and under NormalizedEndpoint: "Not a flat struct with type tag (decision pending round 2)". Reality: lib/core/services/tunnel.dart `Future<void> connect(String tag)` returns void — state is observed via `TunnelState get state` and `Stream<TunnelState> get status` (blocking outcome via blocked/boxStartFailed reason enum). The union decision is closed: `sealed class NormalizedEndpoint` with 8 variants shipped (also noted in CONTEXT's own Decisions section), so "pending round 2" is stale.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Tunnel term as connect(tag) → Future<void> with state/status stream + blockReason, and drop "decision pending round 2" from the NormalizedEndpoint term.

findings.title: decisions.tsv contains verbatim duplicate rows, corrupting the one-row-per-decision audit log
findings.evidence: decisions.tsv lines 29-31 ('geosite/geoip compile to rule_set tags', 'BLOCK outbound → action reject', 'decodeBase64Flex standard-first') are repeated verbatim (modulo one comma) at lines 33-35, so the show-me-your-work log double-counts the same decisions with slightly different wording.

findings.title: Prototype 'promised UX' names features with zero implementation: Prism HMAC, 10-tile bento home, DNS scanner
findings.evidence: prototype-final.html:288 promises 'Slipnet-like DNS scanner 0–6 score + Prism HMAC + Simple Ping TCP 5000ms + network_reachability Rust stability 0–100 + PingRoute per-hop' and AGENTS.md:21 'bento home 10 tiles, … DNS scanner 0-6'. Reality: grep -ri 'prism|hmac' lib/ → no matches (no Prism HMAC anywhere); lib/modules/vpn/screens/home.dart:43-49 ships 7 tiles (Power, State, Endpoint, Split, Stats, Update, Wizard); the diagnostics screen renders the Health module's 0-6 hierarchical score plus hijack/ping/stability probes (decisions.tsv 'Health 0-6 hierarchical score', 'diagnostics tab wired to real Health module'), not a DNS scanner.
