findings.title: libbox.ps1 encodes the fork version and with_awg tag correctly but omits the pinned SHA entirely — no script verifies the submodule sits at 57276220 before building
findings.evidence: Assignment check: does libbox.ps1 encode pin SHA 57276220 and with_awg? with_awg: yes — `$tagsMain` ends `...,ts_omit_synology,ts_omit_bird,with_awg` and is byte-identical to Makefile TAGS_MAIN (verified by string compare: 'TAGS IDENTICAL'). Pin SHA: absent — the script's only pin artifact is `$version = '1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15'` (line 11); '57276220' appears nowhere in scripts/. The pin is enforced solely by the submodule gitlink (`git submodule status` → `57276220a20679cad762c9644f6abdaf39ab7688 go/amnezia-box`, matching the Makefile:4 comment), and neither Makefile nor libbox.ps1 validates `git -C go/amnezia-box rev-parse HEAD` before building — a moved/stale checkout would silently produce
findings.fix: Add a cheap guard at the top of both scripts: `$sha = git -C go/amnezia-box rev-parse HEAD; if ($sha -ne '57276220a20679cad762c9644f6abdaf39ab7688') { throw "fork not at pinned SHA 57276220 (got $sha)" }`.

findings.title: Vendored SRS: format version 1, engine-accepted, but geosite-cn.srs already diverged from upstream and nothing refreshes the fallback
findings.evidence: Doc claim: docs/decisions.tsv:14: 'geosite-cn.srs 55.5KB + geoip-cn.srs 34KB from SagerNet rule-set branch; sing-box rule-set decompile passes'. Reality: both files are SRS binary format version 1 (decompile output '"version": 1', magic bytes 53 52 53 01) and are accepted by the engine — a temp config with type:local entries referencing them passes `sing-box check` (exit 0), and both decompile cleanly. Freshness vs upstream (fetched today): geoip-cn.srs is byte-identical (sha256 0acf5dad... matches), but geosite-cn.srs drifted (vendored db171cd3... / 55,506 bytes vs upstream f657669b... / 55,507 bytes); both vendored 2026-09-02 (git 5592cf3). No CI workflow or script refreshes them (grep of
findings.fix: Record the vendored date + upstream URL in decisions.tsv and add a release-time (or CI) refresh step that re-vendors both SRS from the SagerNet sing-geosite/sing-geoip rule-set branches.

findings.title: 130KB libbox-sources.jar (generated gomobile byproduct) is committed although nothing references it
findings.evidence: Doc: .gitignore declares the Go build outputs under '# Go': 'android/app/libs/libbox.aar' and 'android/app/libs/libbox-legacy.aar'; android/app/build.gradle.kts:45 'implementation(files("libs/libbox.aar"))' — the .aar is regenerated every CI run by 'make -C . lib_android'. Reality: git ls-files includes android/app/libs/libbox-sources.jar (130,753 bytes); unzip -l shows generated gomobile bindings (com/qanatvpn/libbox/*.java); grep 'libbox-sources' across the repo returns zero references. It is a byproduct of a local gomobile bind, unreferenced by the build, and can silently drift from the pinned fork SHA 57276220.
findings.fix: git rm android/app/libs/libbox-sources.jar and add 'android/app/libs/libbox-sources.jar' (or android/app/libs/*.jar minus .gitkeep) to .gitignore alongside libbox.aar.

findings.title: .gitignore misses agent-runtime scratch: .pi/tasks session artifacts and tmp test files are untracked but not ignored
findings.evidence: Reality: git status --porcelain -> '?? .pi/tasks/session-25556-25556/b284351b1.json' + 5 more .pi/tasks files, whose content records 'cwd: E:\\code\\Qanat-VPN' and agent command history; git check-ignore -v .pi/tasks -> no match (rc=1), and .gitignore has no .pi/ or test/tmp_* entries. A scratch test test/tmp_ep_audit_store_test.dart (assert-free, print-only EndpointStore debugging artifact) also sat untracked at test/ root, where any committed copy would execute under flutter test. Root .gitignore covers build/, coverage/, secrets (android/key.properties, *.jks, *.p12), windows/sing-box.exe, latest.json — but not agent-runtime junk.
findings.fix: Append '.pi/' and 'test/tmp_*' (or a tmp/ scratch dir) to .gitignore and delete the local .pi/tasks session artifacts before any git add -A.

findings.title: ~1.2MB of agent-verification artifacts dominate repo weight: archify.html 713KB + 4 visual-check PNGs ~497KB
findings.evidence: Doc: AGENTS.md:67 'archify.visual-check.*.png + .json/.html  # containment evidence' (tracked by design, no size budget stated). Reality: stat sizes — docs/archify.html 712,921 bytes; docs/archify.visual-check.2048x1320.dark.png 141,931; .light 140,750; 1440x900 pair 106,933+106,933 (496,547 bytes total PNGs) plus visual-check.html/json; gh api repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn size = 1622 KB, so these agent-verification artifacts are roughly three quarters of total repo weight, in a code repo whose real payload is ~500KB of research + source.
findings.fix: Either drop the PNG/JSON/HTML visual-check evidence from git (keep only docs/archify-candidate.json as the source spec) or move heavy artifacts to GitHub Releases / Pages; keep git history lean for a client binary repo.

findings.title: No npm package exists under qanatvpn/qanat-vpn or related names; nothing in the repo documents npm publishing
findings.evidence: Claim (audit brief: user believes something is on npm; investigate related names). Reality: curl -s -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} https://registry.npmjs.org/<name> for qanatvpn, qanat-vpn, qanatvpn, qanat, your-vpn, qanatvpn-vpn -> 404 for all six. git grep -in 'npm' -- '*.md' returns only competitor-research mentions (research/07-Hiddify.md, research/11-FlClash.md, research/12-Clash-Verge-Rev.md) — no tracked doc promises an npm package. The GitHub release and Pages site are the only distribution surfaces (and both are currently broken per earlier findings).
findings.fix: No repo action needed for npm; if a registry package was ever expected, treat it as never set up. Ensure release notes and the site (once it deploys) point only to GitHub release assets + latest.json.

findings.title: Site is English-only while the app ships a Persian (FA/RTL) locale — landing page l10n gap for the target audience
findings.evidence: Reality: docs/site/index.html is `<html lang="en">` with all strings hardcoded in English, no dir attribute handling, no alternate-language versions. In-app: `lib/l10n/` contains app_en.arb AND app_fa.arb (verified by ls), and AGENTS.md code style mandates Persian RTL safety ('EdgeInsetsDirectional not EdgeInsets.only(left:) (FA RTL)'), with 'new locale beyond EN/FA' as an explicit Ask-first boundary — FA is a first-class locale. For a self-described 'VPN client built for censored networks' whose Persian-locale users are among the most censored, the EN-only landing page underserves the core audience. No false claim is made (the page never promises FA), hence low rather than medium.
findings.fix: Add a Persian (dir="rtl") variant or a language toggle served by the same static page; at minimum ship the lead paragraph and download labels in both EN and FA.

findings.title: Page quality: invalid disabled attribute on anchors, keyboard-accessible dead links, and dead code
findings.evidence: Reality: lines 36 and 41 read `Download APK` and `... id="dl-windows" ... disabled>Download ZIP` — the HTML spec has no disabled attribute for anchors, so `.btn[disabled]{opacity:.45;pointer-events:none}` blocks mouse clicks but the anchors remain keyboard-focusable and Enter navigates to href="#" (scroll-to-top dead click); screen readers also announce them as active links. Line 54 defines `const pick = id => { const a = document.getElementById(id); if (a) a.disabled = false; };` which is never called — dead code in an already-2.9KB page. Responsive/design otherwise verified clean: viewport meta present, clamp() type scale, auto-fit m
findings.fix: Replace the disabled-attribute pattern with aria-disabled + conditional href removal (or render the buttons only when a URL exists), and delete the unused pick() function.

findings.title: Default branch is master while AGENTS.md specifies main; no branch protection on master
findings.evidence: Doc claim: AGENTS.md 'Branch: `main` + feature branches `feat/<module-id>`'; handoff.md 'Git `master`'. Reality: `gh api repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn` → `"default_branch":"master"`; master's protection endpoint returns 'Branch not protected (HTTP 404)'. Minor drift plus zero guardrails on the default branch of a public VPN app.
findings.fix: Align AGENTS.md to `master` (or rename the branch), and consider requiring PRs/status checks on master before open development starts.

findings.title: Discoverability fields empty and docs/archify.html advertised by AGENTS.md does not exist on the remote (homepage/topics also null/[])

findings.title: docs/decisions.tsv audit trail contains duplicated rows, weakening the show-me-your-work record
findings.evidence: Doc (AGENTS.md 'Tracking progress across sessions'): "append `docs/decisions.tsv` (what/why/evidence/result)" — the TSV is the show-me-your-work audit record. findings.title: AGENTS.md pointer table references a Temp-path architecture review artifact that no longer exists
findings.evidence: Doc (AGENTS.md:20): "| **Architecture review** | `C:\Users\qmahyar\AppData\Local\Temp\architecture-review-20260830-074725.html` | 6 deepening candidates, top pick 03 Tunnel, before/after Mermaid |". findings.title: In-app update fallback URL is hardcoded to the gh-pages mirror that has never existed
findings.evidence: DOC: lib/modules/updates/updater.dart:149-150 — 'Production default for [mirrorUrl]: the gh-pages mirror written by the release pipeline (single producer)' with `static const String defaultMirrorUrl = 'https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/latest.json';` and line 141 doc: 'the `latest.json` mirror (gh-pages) as fallback'. REALITY: `curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} https://qmahyar.github.io/qanatvpn/latest.json` → 404; the mirror was never written because gh-pages never deployed and the metadata job never ran. The primary GitHub-API path still works, so no user-facing breakage yet, but the documented fallback chain is entirely dead until findings 1-3 land.
findings.fix: No code change needed beyond landing the pipeline fixes; after gh-pages deploy, verify the URL returns 200 with the {version, platforms} shape before relying on the fallback (or add a mirror-health smoke test once the URL is live).

findings.title: User's belief that a package is on npm is unfounded: no qanatvpn/qanat-vpn/@qmahyar scoped package exists on npm or pub.dev, and no npm-publish machinery is in the repo
findings.evidence: CLAIM INVESTIGATED (user believes something is on npm): curl https://registry.npmjs.org/qanatvpn -> 404 (retried twice); https://registry.npmjs.org/qanat-vpn -> 404; npm search "qanatvpn vpn" returns only unrelated packages (@scaleway/sdk-s2s-vpn, react-native-vpn-detector, ip2proxy-nodejs, is-vpn, react-native-vpn-status); pub.dev/packages/qanatvpn -> 404 with pub.dev/api/search?q=qanatvpn -> {"packages":[]}; the repo has no root package.json (only hits are inside the go/amnezia-box submodule's upstream dashboard) and .github/workflows/ contains build-android/build-linux/build-windows/gh-pages/upstream-check — no npm-publish job; pubspec.yaml:3 "publish_to: \"none\"". Nothing about npm exists t
findings.fix: None in repo — do not add an npm install section or npm publishing; record in AGENTS.md memory that npm is not a distribution channel for this Flutter+Go project.

findings.title: Version mismatch between pubspec (1.0.0+1) and the only published tag/release (v0.1.0) — any README release/version section would state contradictory numbers
findings.evidence: DOC CLAIM: pubspec.yaml:4 "version: 1.0.0+1" (name: qanatvpn, publish_to: "none"). REALITY: gh release view v0.1.0 --repo QMahyar/qanatvpn -> "title: v0.1.0 ... published 2026-09-04" and gh release list shows no other release; handoff.md:31 "Tag v0.1.0 pushed". A README that documents the current release as 1.0.0 (from pubspec) or v0.1.0 (from Releases) would disagree with the other source; the app's PackageInfo would report 1.0.0+1 while the asset is named qanatvpn_v0.1.0.
findings.fix: Decide one version line: either bump pubspec to 0.1.0+1 to match the tag for v0.1.x, or treat v0.1.0 as pre-release and state the convention in the README Release section before writing it.

findings.title: Release notes body is a bare auto-generated stub, and the tag annotation markets 'first CI-verified release' while 2 of 4 tag workflows failed
findings.evidence: Doc: tag v0.1.0 message: "v0.1.0: first CI-verified release — AWG + 8 protocols, transports parity, encrypted backup, urltest auto-select, updates fail-closed. 302 tests, engine-probed shapes." Reality: release body = "**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/QMahyar/qanatvpn/commits/v0.1.0" only; of the 4 tag-triggered runs, build-android (33900799214) and gh-pages (33900799115) have conclusion "failure". The windows job's 302 tests did not run on tag (its own suite), and the release page displays no feature description.
findings.fix: After fixing the android/gh-pages jobs, edit the release to add real notes (or a RELEASE_NOTES.md consumed by the workflow) and drop or re-qualify the 'CI-verified' tag annotation until all tag-triggered jobs pass.

findings.title: Dependabot security updates disabled while secret scanning is enabled on a public VPN repo
findings.evidence: Reality — gh api repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn → "security_and_analysis":{"secret_scanning":{"status":"enabled"},"secret_scanning_push_protection":{"status":"enabled"},"dependabot_security_updates":{"status":"disabled"},"secret_scanning_validity_checks":{"status":"disabled"}}. For an app whose value proposition is network security, silently disabled dependency security updates is a supply-chain gap; no doc explicitly claims dependabot is on, so this is a config gap rather than doc drift.
findings.fix: Enable dependabot_security_updates in repo Security settings (and optionally add a .github/dependabot.yml for pub/go.mod ecosystems to complement it).

findings.title: ~497 KB of one-off visual-check screenshots tracked in docs/
findings.evidence: Doc claim: AGENTS.md "docs/archify.visual-check.*.png + .json/.html  # containment evidence". These four PNGs record that the archify.html render stayed inside bounds at two viewport sizes — a one-time QA artifact, not documentation someone reads.
findings.fix: Move the PNGs plus archify.visual-check.json/html out of git (keep the QA evidence in releases or LFS) or reduce to one image per theme; alternatively regenerate at lower resolution. Low priority — 0.5 MB is annoying, not harmful.

findings.title: AGENTS.md documents branch 'main' but default branch is 'master'
findings.evidence: Doc claim: AGENTS.md Git workflow "Branch: `main` + feature branches feat/<module-id> ... Commit `feat:`, `fix:` ...". findings.title: Tracked docs/prototype-final.html names competitors (Throne, Karing), conflicting with the spec's no-external-names policy
findings.evidence: Doc claim: SPEC.md:370 "Keep README/docs self-contained original (no external VPN names)" and SPEC.md:129 "README/docs contain no external project names". findings.title: Site is English-only while the app's target audience includes FA (RTL) users with first-class app localization
findings.evidence: Site: index.html:2 `<html lang="en">` and all copy English-only. Reality: app ships lib/l10n/app_fa.arb (`"@@locale": "fa", "appTitle": "QANATVPN"`) and AGENTS.md code style enforces FA RTL rules ('EdgeInsetsDirectional not EdgeInsets.only(left:) (breaks FA)'). The stated audience — 'highly censored networks' (AGENTS.md:7) — is largely Persian-speaking.

findings.title: Site CSS hardcodes hex colors outside :root, violating the project's own token-lock rule
findings.evidence: index.html:12 `border:1px solid #233029` and :23 `color:#08120f` are raw hex outside the :root block (which only defines --bg/--fg/--accent/--card/--muted), while :root elsewhere follows the token pattern. Project rule: 'Tokens locked: var(--color-*) + var(--font-*) — no inline oklch() outside :root (Hallmark)'.
findings.fix: Promote #233029 and #08120f into :root as --border/--btn-fg custom properties.

findings.title: Download buttons use invalid <a disabled> — CSS-only disabling leaves links keyboard-activatable
findings.evidence: index.html:36 `Download APK`; index.html:22 `.btn[disabled]{opacity:.45;pointer-events:none}`. HTML has no disabled attribute for anchors, so the CSS only blocks mouse; keyboard users can Tab to it and Enter navigates to '#'. No evidence quote needed beyond the markup itself — it is a correctness issue vs intent 'disabled'.
findings.fix: Render real <button disabled> elements, or omit href until a URL exists and set aria-disabled="true"; re-enable by assigning href in JS.

findings.title: No in-app license or third-party notice surface — zero 'license' matches in lib/
findings.evidence: Doc claim: SPEC.md:129 promises third-party notices exist 'as required by law' somewhere user-visible. Reality: `grep -rniE 'license|notices' lib/ --include='*.dart'` → 0 matches; no showLicensePage/AboutDialog wired, so the Windows binary (where NOTICE files are not auto-surfaced by any platform mechanism) exposes the embedded GPLv3 engine with no notice surface at all. Android's settings APK convention would at least surface NOTICES via the system; Windows has nothing.
findings.fix: Wire showLicensePage() (or a dedicated Settings entry reading THIRD_PARTY.md bundled as an asset) so the GPL engine notice and third-party licenses are visible from inside the shipped app.

findings.title: The engine fork carries a non-standard trademark/association clause that the THIRD_PARTY plan does not account for and GitHub cannot detect (license: NOASSERTION)
findings.evidence: Doc claim: SPEC.md:406 treats fork compliance as just 'THIRD_PARTY.md (fork SHAs: hoaxisr/amnezia-box@awg-1.14-rc1, ...)'. Reality: go/amnezia-box/LICENSE (GPLv3, checked out at pinned SHA 5727622) ends with: 'In addition, no derivative work may use the name or imply association with this application without prior consent.' GitHub's API reports hoaxisr/amnezia-box license as NOASSERTION (custom file), so automated license scanning cannot catch this clause. The sing-box version string is stamped at build ('-X github.com/sagernet/sing-box/constant.Version=...') — branding/naming decisions for the app and its engine display must respect the upstream association restriction, which no project doc
findings.fix: Record the trademark/association clause in THIRD_PARTY.md when it is created, and keep 'qanatvpn' branding decoupled from any amnezia-box/sing-box name in UI and marketing; note that GitHub shows the fork as NOASSERTION so compliance checks must be manual.

findings.title: .gitmodules branch field names a tag, not a branch — workflow never uses it, latent trap for --remote rebases
findings.evidence: Doc/repo side: .gitmodules:4 declares "branch = 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15" while AGENTS.md:137 and Makefile:11 consistently call 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 the pin. Reality: gh api repos/hoaxisr/amnezia-box/branches returns exactly one branch, "awg-1.14-rc1", whose head is 57276220a20679cad762c9644f6abdaf39ab7688 — identical to the recorded submodule SHA (git submodule status); 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 exists only as an annotated tag (tag object 336ce64d817abc057456ff6549e669045218a757 peeling to 57276220...). The yml never references the branch field either — actions/checkout with submodules:recursive checks out the recorded SHA. So today it is inert (and no upstream drift exists: branch head == pin as of 20
findings.fix: Either remove the branch field from .gitmodules (pin is SHA-based) or set branch = awg-1.14-rc1 so submodule tooling resolves a real upstream branch; document that awgm.* identifiers are tags.

findings.title: Dead dart-define: --dart-define=UPDATE_CHANNEL=androidApk is passed in CI but no code consumes it; the windows job passes no channel define
findings.evidence: Reality: build-android.yml:91 — "flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi --no-tree-shake-icons --dart-define=UPDATE_CHANNEL=androidApk"; repo-wide grep for UPDATE_CHANNEL across *.dart, *.kt, *.gradle* returns zero hits (only the workflow file). build-windows.yml has no UPDATE_CHANNEL define, so the two release jobs already take different define sets for a value nothing reads. If a consumer is ever added (the name suggests the updates module should record install channel), the Windows zip would silently get the default channel while Android gets androidApk — an undocumented cross-job asymmetry today.
findings.fix: Remove the dead --dart-define from build-android.yml:91, or wire UPDATE_CHANNEL into lib/modules/updates (e.g. String.fromEnvironment) and pass a matching value on the windows job if channel tracking is actually wanted.

findings.title: No concurrency group in any of the 5 workflows — overlapping tag/dispatch runs can race the shared release (two softprops writers + latest.json --clobber)
findings.evidence: Reality: full reads of all five files show no 'concurrency:' key anywhere. Two softprops/action-gh-release@v2 writers (build-android apk job and build-windows exe job) plus the metadata job's "gh release upload \"$TAG\" latest.json --clobber" (build-android.yml:167) all mutate the same per-tag release. The assignment's single-producer note (build-android.yml:123 "no two writers can race the file") only holds when exactly one run exists per tag; a re-dispatched build-android while a previous metadata job is inside its 2400s wait loop (build-android.yml:138) can clobber latest.json mid-write, and rapid successive tags run fully in parallel with no cancel-in-progress protection for shared runne
findings.fix: Add concurrency to the three tag-triggered build workflows, e.g. concurrency: { group: release-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: false } (and group: upstream-check for upstream-check.yml) so same-ref runs serialize instead of racing the shared release.

findings.title: Zero caching in all 5 workflows — no actions/cache, pub cache, gradle cache, or gomobile reuse; every tag run cold-installs NDK (~2 GB), gomobile, and pub deps
findings.evidence: Reality: full reads of all five files show no 'actions/cache', no cache:' inputs, no .pub-cache/go-mod-cache saves. build-android.yml:35-37 re-installs gomobile every run ("go install -v github.com/sagernet/gomobile/cmd/gomobile@v0.1.13 ..."), build-android.yml:48 re-downloads NDK 28.2.13676358 (~2 GB) via sdkmanager every tag, and both build jobs re-run "flutter pub get" from zero. setup-go@v5's implicit module cache is the only cache-like behavior, and it is incidental, not a shared strategy. No doc claims caching either, so this is a consistency gap rather than doc drift: android and windows pay the same cold-start costs on every tag.
findings.fix: Add actions/setup-go's built-in caching explicitly plus actions/cache for pub (~/.pub-cache) and gradle (~/.gradle) on the android job; NDK 28.2.13676358 is preinstalled on ubuntu-latest images, so replacing the sdkmanager install with a pinned-path env would also skip the ~2 GB download.

findings.title: Permissions drift: build-linux.yml and upstream-check.yml declare no permissions block while the other three workflows pin least-privilege scopes
findings.evidence: Doc side (repo convention, AGENTS.md Boundaries 'Never: Commit secrets...'): build-android.yml:7-8 and build-windows.yml:7-8 each pin "permissions: contents: write"; gh-pages.yml:9-12 pins contents:read + pages:write + id-token:write. Reality: build-linux.yml (lines 1-15, runs a stub job on every v* tag) and upstream-check.yml (lines 1-28, weekly cron) contain no permissions block, so both inherit the repo-default GITHUB_TOKEN scopes; on repos without restricted default permissions that grants the stub/cron jobs write access to all scopes for no reason — inconsistent with the least-privilege pattern the other three workflows establish.
findings.fix: Add permissions: contents: read to build-linux.yml and upstream-check.yml so all five workflows declare explicit, minimal token scopes.

findings.title: setup-go cache never hits on Windows build: go.sum lives in the submodule, workflow has no cache-dependency-path
findings.evidence: Doc/implied: actions/setup-go@v5 default caching (no cache-dependency-path set in build-windows.yml:24-26). Reality: run 33900799141 annotation - "Restore cache failed: Dependencies file is not found in D:\a\qanatvpn\qanatvpn. Supported file pattern: go.sum"; `ls go.sum` in repo root -> not found, go.sum lives at go/amnezia-box/go.sum. Every windows (and android) build re-downloads the full Go module graph (run log shows `go: downloading github.com/hoaxisr/amneziawg-go/v3 v3.1.0-awgm.2` etc.). Correctness unaffected; only cache hit rate / build time.
findings.fix: Set `cache-dependency-path: go/amnezia-box/go.sum` in the setup-go step of build-windows.yml (and build-android.yml).

findings.title: workflow_dispatch on a branch misnames the artifact and misfires the release step (GITHUB_REF_NAME is not a tag)
findings.evidence: Workflow trigger includes workflow_dispatch with no tag guard. Reality path: `$v = $env:GITHUB_REF_NAME.TrimStart('v')` (build-windows.yml:54) on a branch dispatch yields "master" -> Compress-Archive names the asset qanatvpn_vmaster_windows-x64.zip and softprops/action-gh-release@v2 (line 62, no tag_name input) infers the ref name as the release tag, creating a junk "master" release with a misnamed asset. v0.1.0 was tag-triggered so unaffected, but the documented '3 jobs produce ... without manual steps' contract breaks for manual runs.
findings.fix: Guard the bundle step: `if (-not $env:GITHUB_REF_NAME.StartsWith('v')) { throw "workflow_dispatch requires a vX.Y.Z tag ref, got $env:GITHUB_REF_NAME" }`, or pass an explicit tag_name input to the release action for dispatch runs.

findings.title: Actions referenced by mutable tag refs while the workflow holds contents:write on tag pushes (supply-chain hardening gap)
findings.evidence: Doc: AGENTS.md:107 pins toolchains ("Pin flutter 3.47.2, Go 1.25, NDK 28, JDK 17") and the repo pins the sing-box fork by SHA, but nothing pins action versions by digest. Reality: build-windows.yml:15 `uses: actions/checkout@v4`, :24 `uses: actions/setup-go@v5`, :62 `uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2` (same pattern in all 5 workflows) - each holds contents:write on tag-triggered runs, so a compromised upstream action tag executes inside this release pipeline with write access to releases and Pages. The run log also shows Node 20 deprecation warnings for these actions.
findings.fix: Pin all third-party actions to full commit SHAs (actions/checkout@<sha> etc.) via dependabot/renovate updates, or at minimum pin the release-upload action (softprops) which holds contents:write.

findings.title: Verified OK (no defect): Windows engine provenance, zip bundling, and checksum integrity all check out
findings.evidence: Reality checks (all passed): (1) provenance - `git ls-tree v0.1.0 go/` -> `160000 commit 57276220a20679cad762c9644f6abdaf39ab7688 go/amnezia-box` (matches the AGENTS.md pin '1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 SHA 57276220'), `git show v0.1.0:.gitmodules` present at tag, and the workflow's 'Build sing-box.exe' step (build-windows.yml:28-39) runs `go build -o ../../windows/sing-box.exe ./cmd/sing-box` inside the submodule - no downloaded engine binary in the pipeline; (2) run log for 33900799141 prints `sing-box version 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15` with the full with_awg tag set; (3) downloaded release zip's bundled sing-box.exe re-run locally reports the identical version 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15, go1.25.14, CGO disable

findings.title: sha256-android.json will be raw sha256sum text (invalid JSON), inconsistent with the windows job's JSON object
findings.evidence: Doc: AGENTS.md:113 'Tag `v1.2.3` → 3 jobs produce `qanatvpn_v1.2.3_arm64.apk` etc. + `latest.json` + `sha256` via `softprops` without manual steps.' Reality: build-android.yml:112 `sha256sum "$name" >> sha256-android.json` appends plain 'hash  filename' lines (invalid JSON under a .json name), while build-windows.yml:59 `@{ "qanatvpn_v${v}_windows-x64.zip" = $hash } | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content sha256-windows.json` emits a JSON object — confirmed by fetching the live release asset: {"qanatvpn_v0.1.0_windows-x64.zip":"d159f806..."}. Two different checksum formats ship under matching names; lib/ contains no checksum-verification code (grep 'sha256' lib/ --include=*.dart → no hits), so today it
findings.fix: Mirror the windows job: build a JSON map with python3 or jq and write sha256-android.json (or drop the .json extension and name it sha256-android.txt consistently).

findings.title: submodules: recursive pulls SagerNet client repos (sing-box-for-android, apple, desktop, Runestone) that the libbox build never uses
findings.evidence: Doc: build-android.yml:17 `submodules: recursive`; tasks/handoff.md:31 '.gitmodules was missing while CI runs `submodules: recursive`' (fixed, checkout now succeeds). Reality: run 33900799214 log shows checkout cloning 'Submodule clients/android (https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box-for-android.git) ... checked out aed2b6ea' plus clients/apple, clients/desktop, Runestone, iterm2-color-schemes — the fork's client-app submodules, none of which the aar build uses (root Makefile:21 only binds ./experimental/libbox). Every release build gates on the availability of SagerNet repos and wastes clone minutes/GB. Fix: submodules: false plus `git submodule update --init go/amnezia-box` (non-recursive —
findings.fix: Use submodules: false + `git submodule update --init go/amnezia-box` (non-recursive) before `make -C . lib_android`.

findings.title: No caching anywhere in the android pipeline: pub, gradle, Go modules, and the ~2GB NDK re-download on every tag build
findings.evidence: Doc: AGENTS.md:46 'CI: 3 jobs parallel ... → `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` + `latest.json` + `sha256`' — no caching is promised anywhere, but every tagged release rebuilds from zero: build-android.yml has no `cache: true` on subosito/flutter-action (pub cache off by default), no actions/cache for ~/.gradle, no NDK cache, and setup-go@v5 cannot cache go modules because go.mod lives only in the go/amnezia-box submodule (no cache-dependency-path). Comparable windows cold build took 10m32s; android adds a ~2GB NDK download plus full gomobile/sing-box compilation on every tag. Not a failure cause (v0.1.0 failed earlier at sdkmanager), purely cost/latency.
findings.fix: Add cache: true to flutter-action, actions/cache for ~/.gradle keyed on **/*.gradle*/**/gradle-wrapper.properties, and actions/setup-go cache-dependency-path: go/amnezia-box/go.mod (or actions/cache for GOMODCACHE).

findings.title: npm belief check: no qanatvpn/qanat-vpn or related package exists on npm, and nothing in the repo could publish one
findings.evidence: Recon claim: "npm registry has no qanatvpn/qanat-vpn package (user believes something is on npm)". Reality: `npm view qanatvpn` -> E404 Not found; same for qanat-vpn, qanatvpn, your-vpn, qanatvpn-cli — all E404. In-repo: pubspec.yaml:3 `publish_to: "none"` (Dart/Flutter package, not npm), no package.json at repo root, no npm publish step in any workflow. Nothing was ever on npm; the belief has no artifact behind it.
findings.fix: No action beyond recording it in decisions.tsv / handoff: the project's only distribution channel is GitHub Releases + gh-pages latest.json (both currently broken per the findings above); any npm presence the user remembers belongs to a different project.

findings.title: Documented rollback procedure (tag delete + softprops overwrite) cannot produce the documented result
findings.evidence: Doc: tasks/plan.md:152 "**Rollback:** Tag `v1.2.3` → `v1.2.2` via `git tag -d` + `softprops` overwrite, plus `latest.json` revert." Reality: `git tag -d` removes only the local ref — the remote tag needs `git push origin :refs/tags/v1.2.3` (or --force); softprops/action-gh-release only uploads assets, it never deletes the superseding v1.2.3 release or its APKs, and GitHub's releases/latest pointer + 6h client cache keep serving v1.2.3 metadata until both are cleaned. Running the documented steps would leave v1.2.2 assets attached to a release nobody's updater selects.
findings.fix: Rewrite plan.md:152 as a real rollback runbook: delete remote tag + release (`gh release delete v1.2.3 --cleanup-tag`), re-point latest.json to v1.2.2 (single producer re-run), and note clients honor the 6h cache / x-ratelimit-reset window before the downgrade propagates.

findings.title: Two hand-synced implementations of the latest.json builder: test-only Dart function duplicates CI's inline Python
findings.evidence: REALITY: updater.dart:103-121 `latestJsonFromRelease` builds {'platforms': {...}, 'version': tag} with filters identical to build-android.yml:139-163's inline Python (same four filter lists, same first-match-asset logic); grep for latestJsonFromRelease across lib/ shows no caller — only test/updater/updater_test.dart:146-162 exercises it. The workflow comment at build-android.yml:126-129 describes the Python script as the single producer, so the Dart copy is dead code that must be hand-synced with CI; a future filter change (e.g. adding linux) applied in one place silently diverges the mirror schema from what the app's _fromMirror parser (updater.dart:184-200) reads back.
findings.fix: Either delete latestJsonFromRelease or have CI emit exactly this shape via a checked-in script the workflow calls, keeping one implementation as the contract source.

findings.title: progress-09-03 and decisions.tsv still say pubspec.lock is untracked — it is tracked and committed
findings.evidence: DOC tasks/progress-2026-09-03.md:19: "`pubspec.lock` is untracked — `git add` it on next commit."; docs/decisions.tsv:67 evidence column: ".gitignore un-ignores pubspec.lock (untracked, add on commit)". REALITY: `git ls-files pubspec.lock` -> tracked at HEAD; .gitignore:12 has "!pubspec.lock".
findings.fix: No action needed beyond awareness — the add happened; optionally backfill a decisions.tsv row noting the lockfile is now committed so the stale "untracked" wording does not mislead the next agent.

findings.title: npm belief is ungrounded: registry has no qanatvpn/qanat-vpn package and no tracker mentions npm at all
findings.evidence: REALITY: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} https://registry.npmjs.org/qanatvpn` -> 404; https://registry.npmjs.org/qanat-vpn -> 404. `grep -ri npm tasks/ AGENTS.md docs/decisions.tsv` -> no matches — no tracker row, handoff item, or progress log claims or plans an npm publication. Distribution targets in docs/releases are GitHub Releases + GitHub Pages only.

findings.title: SPEC promises a go/tor sidecar directory and 'tor --version # must exist' prerequisite; repo has neither
findings.evidence: Doc: SPEC.md:168 "`go/tor/` tor binary sidecar (detached, socks 127.0.0.1:9050, not type: tor)" and SPEC.md:72 "tor --version  # must exist". Reality: `ls go/` -> amnezia-box only; lib/core/services/channel_adapters.dart:123 comment states "The Tor SOCKS probe on 127.0.0.1:9050. The Tor sidecar is a later milestone;" (LocalSocksTorAdapter exists in code but no tor binary, submodule, or packaging exists in the repo).

findings.title: Overview names 'cue/motion_kit' in the stack — motion_kit is in neither pubspec.yaml nor pubspec.lock
findings.evidence: Doc: "Stack: Flutter 3.47.2 + material_3_expressive 45 M3E + cue/motion_kit + Go 1.25 ..." Reality: pubspec.yaml dependencies include material_3_expressive ^1.1.1, material_ui, cue ^0.3.1 — `grep motion_kit pubspec.yaml pubspec.lock` → no match; the scaffold recipe "flutter pub add material_3_expressive cue drift go_router + melos" also names melos, which is absent from pubspec (dev deps: build_runner, drift_dev, flutter_lints, path). Flutter 3.47.2, Go 1.25, drift, go_router, cue claims check out.
findings.fix: Drop 'motion_kit' (and 'melos') from the stack/scaffold lines or add the dependency if it was intended.

findings.title: Git workflow says branch 'main' — actual branch is master (local and remote default)
findings.evidence: Doc: "Branch: `main` + feature branches `feat/<module-id>` (e.g., `feat/tunnel-lifecycle-03`)." Reality: `git branch --show-current` → master; `gh api repos/QMahyar/qanatvpn --jq .default_branch` → master; tasks/handoff.md also says 'Git `master`'. An agent following AGENTS.md would branch/push to main which does not exist upstream.
findings.fix: Change AGENTS.md to 'Branch: master' (or actually rename to main and update remote + workflows).

findings.title: Stale doc comment in ConfigAssembler.build: says endpoint payload 'goes into route.endpoints' but the code (and the 1.14 schema) uses top-level `endpoints` — route.endpoints FATALs
findings.evidence: PROBE: `{"route":{"endpoints":[...]}}` -> EXIT=1 `FATAL decode config at route_endpoints.json: route.endpoints: json: unknown field "endpoints"`; the same payload at top level passes (awg_full.json EXIT=0; vendored profiles/config.wg-awg.json EXIT=0). Upstream docs place Endpoint at the document root (sing-box.sagernet.org/configuration/endpoint/wireguard/). The comment misleads future edits into 'fixing' the assembler to the FATAL location.
findings.fix: Update the doc comment to 'top-level endpoints' (matches the 1.14 schema and the code).

findings.title: quicMimic preset emits no I1-I5 CPS packets although the fork accepts them — the preset named 'QUIC mimic' sends no protocol-imitation traffic
findings.evidence: Fork AwgEndpointOptions accepts I1-I5 strings and they are emitted by the parser round-trip and accepted by the engine (probe awg_full.json with i1-i5 set -> EXIT=0; option/awg.go:26-30). docs.amnezia.org AmneziaWG spec describes I1-I5 as the 'Obfuscation Packets (Signature Chain)' — the actual protocol-imitation packets; without them the preset sends only junk (Jc/Jmin/Jmax), header values (H1-H4), and padding (S1/S2). UI copy promises 'QUIC mimic'; the value set delivers generic obfuscation. Wire-side invariants H1∩H2=∅ and S1+56≠S2 verified held by AwgConfig.validate; full preset-derived shape passes real check (test/awg 19/19 green incl. real sing-box.exe runs).
findings.fix: Either add an editable I1-I5 hex-blob field to the preset/advanced editor or rename/annotate the preset so the UI does not promise protocol imitation it does not emit.

findings.title: _echConfigString keeps only the first entry of a multi-block ECH config list, silently discarding the rest
findings.evidence: Fork `config` is Listable[string] (upstream outbound tls.ech `config: []`); engine accepted a 1-entry list. _echConfigString does `raw.firstOrNull?.toString()` for List input, so entries 2..n of a multi-block PEM are discarded with no log. Mitigating: my 2-fake-block control FATALed engine-side, so real-world multi-block reliability is unproven; but if a subscription ships several config blocks, the dropped ones can only reduce fallback, not corrupt data.
findings.fix: Either store List<String> on the model and emit the full list, or log when list.length > 1 so the drop is observable.

findings.title: No regression test pins the emitter's never-emit guard for legacy ECH keys (pq_signature_schemes_enabled / dynamic_record_sizing_disabled)
findings.evidence: test/p1/p1_transports_emit_test.dart ECH group (lines 268-301) covers only no-config and PEM-config emission. The never-emit guarantee currently rests on the comment at endpoint_outbound.dart:204-206. Real-binary FATAL text recorded for both forbidden keys: `FATAL[0000] initialize outbound[0]: legacy ECH options are deprecated in sing-box 1.12.0 and removed in sing-box 1.13.0`. Structural verification done this audit: driving the real emitter (ech-dns/ech-pem/ech-disabled-with-pem cases) emits ech exactly {enabled, config?}; grep over lib/ and test/ finds pq_signature_schemes_enabled/dynamic_record_sizing_disabled only inside that comment.
findings.fix: Add one test: build a VlessEndpoint with echEnabled true, assert `expect(ech.keys, unorderedEquals({'enabled','config'}))` (or notContains pq_signature_schemes_enabled/dynamic_record_sizing_disabled) so a future field addition cannot regress the FATAL guard silently.

findings.title: grpc permit_without_stream parsed-and-dropped (cannot be emitted)
findings.evidence: Fork V2RayGRPCOptions has PermitWithoutStream bool `json:"permit_without_stream,omitempty"` (option/v2ray_transport.go). _transport (parsers.dart:313-341) does not read it and the grpc emit branch (endpoint_outbound.dart:273-280) emits only service_name/idle_timeout/ping_timeout, so a sing-box JSON vmess/vless/trojan grpc node with permit_without_stream loses it on round-trip.
findings.fix: Add permitWithoutStream to TransportOptions, parse and emit it in the grpc branch.

findings.title: _vmess 'reality' branch would emit TLS without utls/reality keys — latent FATAL trap, currently unreachable
findings.evidence: `if (e.tls == 'tls' || e.tls == 'reality') 'tls': _tls(enabled: true, serverName: e.sni ?? e.address)` — no utls or reality keys are passed (reality REQUIRES utls per verified engine truth). All vmess producers can only yield 'tls' or null (parsers.dart:694 `doc['tls'] == 'tls' ? 'tls' : null`; sing-box import line 420 `tls?['enabled'] == true ? 'tls' : null`), so unreachable today; but any future parser/edited store JSON yielding 'reality' would emit a TLS block the fork rejects at reality init (utls missing) — probed class of FATAL for vless reality without utls in earlier probe sessions.
findings.fix: Drop 'reality' from the condition (vmess has no reality in practice) or emit a complete reality+utls block if it is ever legitimately produced.

findings.title: VmessUriParser: non-string/missing 'add' or 'id' throws TypeError (not FormatException) — one malformed vmess line aborts the whole bundle import
findings.evidence: `address: doc['add'] as String` and `uuid: doc['id'] as String` (parsers.dart:689-690) throw _TypeError on a missing or numeric field (e.g. {"add":123}), but parseShareLines (ingestion_adapter.dart) wraps _parseOne only `on FormatException catch`. A subscription containing one such vmess line aborts the entire import with the raw TypeError (importText's `on Object catch` surfaces it), while malformed lines of every other format are skipped individually — inconsistent blast radius for a real-world malformed v2rayN payload. aid/port already coerce via intField (FormatException), so this is only the string-cast fields.
findings.fix: Use stringField(doc['add'], 'vmess add') / stringField(doc['id'], 'vmess id') so a bad payload throws FormatException and the line is skipped like all other formats, or catch Object per line in parseShareLines.

findings.title: TUIC udp_relay_mode invalid value is silently treated as native by the engine (no validation at parse or emit)
findings.evidence: Probes: udp_relay_mode 'turbo' -> EXIT=0 (accepted, silently native); 'native'/'quic' EXIT=0. Fork protocol/tuic/outbound.go switch has no default error branch (only native/quic are handled). Upstream doc defines only native|quic. A typo'd link value imports cleanly but behaves differently than the node author intended, with no diagnostic.
findings.fix: Validate {native,quic} at parse (parsers.dart:876 / Clash udp-relay-mode) and throw FormatException, mirroring the congestion_control whitelist.

findings.title: Clash hy2 up/down bandwidth mangled by digit-stripping: '20-50' becomes 2050 Mbps, '1 Gbps' becomes 1 Mbps (Brutal CC misconfigured)
findings.evidence: ClashYamlParser upMbps: _asInt(node['up']) where _asInt strips all non-digits then int.tryParse. Hy2 up/down are client bandwidth hints for Hysteria (Brutal) CC — upstream hy2 doc: 'Max bandwidth, in Mbps; if empty, BBR is used instead of Hysteria CC'. '20-50' -> 2050 and '1 Gbps' -> 1 both change CC behavior materially with no warning. Well-formed '200 mbps'/'500' inputs verified fine (full hy2 shape EXIT=0).
findings.fix: Parse only pure integers or '<n> mbps' forms (case-insensitive); reject/ignore anything else (also consider Gbps multiplier) instead of digit-stripping.

findings.title: The two urltest emit sites format the same interval field differently ('90s' vs '1m30s'); compiler also emits the interval key even when it just flagged it invalid
findings.evidence: routing_compiler.dart:112-118 `_formatDuration`: `seconds % 60 == 0 → '${seconds ~/ 60}m' else '${seconds}s'` (90s → '90s'); profile_config_source.dart:320-327: minutes+remainder (`90s` → '1m30s'). Probe: urltest interval "2m30s" passes `sing-box.exe check` EXIT=0 (badoption.Duration accepts both), so no runtime risk — but the duplicated helpers will drift (the connect-path copy already guards `> Duration.zero` while the compiler errors-and-still-emits `if (interval != null)`, routing_compiler.dart:106 vs profile_config_source.dart:308). Compiler outboundsJson also carries an invalid interval alongside its own validation error, a contract wart only reachable via ConfigAssembler.build (gen_pr
findings.fix: Extract one shared duration formatter (and one interval guard) used by both emitter sites; in the compiler, omit the interval key when the positivity error was raised so outboundsJson never contains fields the compiler itself flagged invalid.

findings.title: sing-box SSH import silently drops private_key_path and the 1.14.0 cipher/mac/kex_algorithm/host_key_algorithms/client_version fields without surfacing the loss
findings.evidence: SingboxJsonParser ssh case (parsers.dart:450-467) reads only server/server_port/user/password/private_key/private_key_passphrase/host_key; `private_key_path` and the sing-box 1.14.0-added `host_key_algorithms`/`client_version`/`cipher`/`mac`/`kex_algorithm` (upstream SSH docs: 'Since sing-box 1.14.0'; fork option/ssh.go has all fields) are dropped with no warning, so an imported node re-emits without them. For private_key_path this is near-unavoidable (path is machine-specific, and _ssh deliberately never emits the path form — endpoint_outbound.dart comment), and cipher/mac/kex pass check with defaults (handoff.md:12 notes they are not check-validated), so impact is silent configuration loss
findings.fix: Surface skipped SSH fields in the import result (e.g. a per-node warning list on SshEndpoint or the IngestionAdapter result) so a user importing a config that relied on private_key_path or restricted ciphers knows the settings did not carry over; optionally add client_version/cipher/mac/kex to SshEndpoint as pass-through fields.

findings.title: clash_mode DNS rules are dead in every shipped config: no experimental.clash_api block is emitted, and ClashModeItem.Match returns false when clashServer is nil
findings.evidence: assembler and vendored profile emit no experimental block (grep 'experimental' lib/ → none). Fork route/rule/rule_item_clash_mode.go:30-31: Match() returns false when clashServer is nil, and the clash server only exists when experimental.clash_api is configured. So {'clash_mode':'Direct'→dns-local} and {'clash_mode':'Global'→dns-proxy} never fire in any shipped config; they are inert weight that suggests a Direct/Global override that does not exist. (Matching itself is case-insensitive EqualFold, so 'Direct'/'Global' casing is fine once an API block exists; probe p11 with lowercase values passes check.)
findings.fix: Either emit experimental.clash_api (external_controller on localhost) so the rules can fire, or drop the two clash_mode rules until the clash dashboard lands.

findings.title: dhcp DNS server shape FATALs on the shipped binary (build-tag limitation to remember if a DNS server picker ever exists)
findings.evidence: windows/sing-box.exe check with {type:'dhcp'} server → FATAL 'initialize DNS server[2]: DHCP is not included in this build, rebuild with -tags with_dhcp' (probe p6d; binary version output tag list confirms no with_dhcp). udp/tls/https/local/fakeip/mdns/hosts all pass check (probe p6e exit 0). DnsConfig hardcodes only https/local/fakeip today, so no shipped path hits this; recorded so a future DNS-server picker or import mapping to dhcp does not ship a FATAL.
findings.fix: If DNS-server selection is ever added, exclude 'dhcp' for this build (or gate it per binary tags); no change needed in the current emitter.

findings.title: DnsConfig.toDnsJson takes a geoAsset parameter it never uses (dead parameter)
findings.evidence: The method body never references geoAsset; only rule tags geosite-cn (hardcoded) are used. All callers pass a constructed GeoAsset just to satisfy the signature (test/dns/dns_config_test.dart:36, test/p0/p0_fail_closed_test.dart:97). Pure API hygiene; no behavioral effect.
findings.fix: Drop the parameter, or use it to derive the DNS rule_set tags instead of hardcoding 'geosite-cn'.

findings.title: DnsConfig.hijackRules() is dead code: assembler comment itself says FirewallPolicy.baseRules()[0] subsumes it
findings.evidence: config_assembler.dart:67-70 comment: 'FirewallPolicy.baseRules()[0] is already hijack-dns, so the separate dns.hijackRules() call is subsumed here (no duplicate)' — yet the public method remains and is only referenced by test/dns/dns_config_test.dart:64. Two sources of truth for the hijack rule shape can drift.
findings.fix: Delete hijackRules() and its test, or have FirewallPolicy.baseRules() call it so the shape has one owner.

findings.title: Clash alpn lists dropped for tuic/vless/trojan (tuic silently defaults to h3)
findings.evidence: TuicEndpoint.alpn defaults to ['h3'] (normalized_endpoint.dart:145) and _tuic always emits tls.alpn — the clash tuic branch never reads the node's alpn list, so alpn [h2, h3] servers get a mismatched client alpn. vless/trojan have no alpn field in the model at all, though mihomo vless TLS 'alpn: [h2, http/1.1]' is a documented common field (wiki.metacubex.one/config/proxies/vless/) and the fork's tls struct accepts alpn (emitted for tuic/hy2 already). Lower priority than the reality/transport drops because the h3 default usually matches reality-server deployments.
findings.fix: Add alpn to the clash tuic branch (node['alpn'] via stringList), and consider an alpn field on VlessEndpoint/TrojanEndpoint with emit through _tls(alpn:) — or document the limitation next to the emit.

findings.title: Id/Ip/Ib masquerade validation accepts sign-prefixed and negative decimals via int.tryParse, and the comment understates it
findings.evidence: int.tryParse('-5') != null so '-5' passes as 'decimal'; the doc comment says 'Id additionally accepts decimal' but the code applies isHex || isDecimal to all three. These keys are correctly excluded from engine JSON (toEngineJson, ground truth: endpoints[].id FATALs unknown field), so impact is editor-cosmetic, but the validator accepts values no server could ever match (negative masks).
findings.fix: Require a sign-free decimal (RegExp(r'^\d+$')) or hex in the mask check for Id/Ip/Ib.

findings.title: Only CommandLog of the 6 commands subscribed; StatusMessage traffic stream (CommandStatus) exported and unused
findings.evidence: attachLogWatcher: options.addCommand(Libbox.CommandLog) only; override fun writeStatus(message: StatusMessage?) {} is a no-op. The other five dispatch streams (Status/Group/ClashMode/Connections/Outbounds) are supported by dispatchCommands (command_client.go) and javap confirms the aar methods (selectOutbound, urlTest, setGroupExpand). StatusMessage carries Memory/Goroutines/ConnectionsIn/Out/Uplink/Downlink/UplinkTotal/DownlinkTotal (javap) — free live metrics currently unused; StatsTile shows only connect-phase durations (home.dart:259+). Correct usage of the one command actually subscribed; no misuse found.
findings.fix: When live stats are wanted, add CommandStatus to CommandClientOptions and forward writeStatus to Dart via the box_events channel (throttled); keep CommandLog for logs.

findings.title: CommandServerHandlerImpl.serviceStop/serviceReload are no-ops — engine-initiated stop/reload requests would leave VpnService up
findings.evidence: Handler only logs on serviceStop. Verified callers: daemon/managed_service.go:39 (StopService) and :47 (ReloadService) are the only trigger points, reached via ManagedService gRPC (CommandClient.serviceClose/serviceReload) — BoxEngine never calls those, so unreachable today (comment in file already says 'not wired yet'). But it means a future wiring of the managed API would silently no-op instead of stopping/reloading the tunnel.
findings.fix: Wire serviceStop to perform the boxStop flow (closeService + emit stopped) and serviceReload to re-run startOrReloadService with the last config, or leave documented as inert.

findings.title: EngineLogLine.parse misses level prefix on ANSI-colored log lines (platform log formatter runs with colors enabled)
findings.evidence: Stream messages come from platformFormatter = Formatter{BaseTime, DisableLineBreak: true} (log/observable.go:55-58) — DisableColors unset, so ERROR/WARN/INFO lines are emitted like "\x1b[31mERROR\x1b[0m[0001] ..." (aurora colorize in log/format.go Format). BoxEngine forwards message raw; the parse regex ^\[?(INFO|WARN|ERROR|FATAL|DEBUG|TRACE)\]? never matches a leading escape char → level empty and ANSI bytes rendered on the Logs screen. Also makes the BoxEngine FATAL/ERROR text-scan brittle.
findings.fix: Strip ANSI escapes in Kotlin before emitEvent (message.replace(Regex("\\u001B\\[[0-9;]*m"), "")) or allow optional leading escapes in the _levelPrefix regex.

findings.title: No test or CI step asserts the exe's version/build-tags; engine-parity tests silently skip when the exe is absent and run unverified when present
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'awgm|constant.Version|version' across test/ and lib/ returns zero version assertions; every real-engine test does existence-check-then-skip (e.g. test/routing/routing_test.dart:390, test/awg/awg_config_test.dart:185/295, test/dns/dns_config_test.dart:77, test/p1/p1_emit_parity_test.dart:33 'sing-box.exe absent'). So a fresh clone silently drops all engine probes, and a dev with a leftover old binary (e.g. rc.1 without the fork's mandatory x_padding_bytes struct, or a build without with_awg) probes the wrong engine with no error. Current exe verified correct today: version line contains 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 and Tags contain with_awg,with_purego.
findings.fix: In the shared exe-locator/helper (the pattern duplicated in 6 test files), add one assertion: run `windows/sing-box.exe version`, require output contains '1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15' and 'with_awg' (constants shared with lib/ or a test fixture), otherwise skip with a message naming the mismatch — turns silent staleness into a visible one-line failure.

findings.title: Version string 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 is defined in three independent places (Makefile VERSION, libbox.ps1 $version, CI git describe) with no single source of truth — a submodule bump that misses two of them ships a mis-stamped engine
findings.evidence: Makefile:11 `VERSION := 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15`; scripts/libbox.ps1:10 `$version = '1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15'`; build-windows.yml:33 derives it via `git describe --tags` (which fails empty per the medium finding above); .gitmodules pins `branch = 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15` while the actual pin is commit SHA 5727622 (git submodule status). upstream-check.yml's own bump recipe (lines 27-32: 'chore(upstream): bump amnezia-box to <tag> -> make lib_android + strings sanity + flutter test + sing-box check') does not mention updating Makefile/libbox.ps1 — following it verbatim yields a rebuilt exe/aar reporting the OLD version while containing new code.
findings.fix: Single source of truth: derive the stamp at build time (`git -C go/amnezia-box describe --tags --exact-match || fail`) in libbox.ps1/Makefile, or keep the hardcoded string but have the weekly upstream-check workflow diff it against the submodule tag and fail on mismatch.

findings.title: What check validated vs what it cannot: id/ip/ib FATAL reconfirmed; DNS rule_set tag resolution IS checked; full list of runtime probes still required
findings.evidence: Positive probes (check EXIT=0): (1) endpoints[].id/ip/ib still decode-FATAL as expected — config with endpoints[0].id='x' -> FATAL 'decode config ... endpoints[0].id: json: unknown field "id"'; (2) AWG fields jc/jmin/jmax/s1/s2/h1-h4 all valid per go/amnezia-box/option/awg.go — H1-H4 are strings so quoted values are correct; s3/s4/i1-i5 exist in the fork but are unexercised (optional); (3) local rule_set entries referencing rule_sets/initial_assets/geoip-cn.srs + geosite-cn.srs -> check EXIT=0, both files are valid v1 rule-set binaries (decompile: geoip-cn 1 rule ip_cidr list, geosite-cn 1 rule domain/domain_regex/domain_suffix list); (4) tun address includes the FakeIP range 198.18.0.0/15 c
findings.fix: Turn the probe list into named runtime test fixtures (Android device + Windows VMs) and wire the dangling-tag variants into the Windows crash-detection tests.

findings.title: clash_mode DNS rules reference a clash_api the config never enables — permanently dead rules
findings.evidence: dns.rules lines 33/37 use clash_mode matching; no experimental.clash_api section exists in the profile (ConfigAssembler.build emits no experimental block either — grep of lib/ finds no cache_file/clash_api emission). sing-box evaluates clash_mode only when the clash API sets the mode; rules never fire.
findings.fix: Either add an experimental.clash_api block when the Clash surface ships, or drop the two rules until then so the profile documents only live behavior.

findings.title: Placeholder credentials committed to a public repo: a valid-format 32-byte private key and a TEST-NET-3 peer address ship in the profile
findings.evidence: private_key 'eCbtX5g5Pof3zH0Gu6dzulIzLB0B5xj+OhIfgVtWu1A=' is a well-formed 44-char base64 32-byte key committed in tool/gen_profile.dart (line 14) and the generated profile (public repo); peer address 203.0.113.10 is RFC 5737 TEST-NET-3 and never handshakes. tasks/progress-2026-09-02.md: 'Profiles: only the vendored config.wg-awg.json (placeholder keys) ship' — placeholder is intended, but nothing marks the values as non-credentials and the malformed peer key additionally triggers the runtime FATAL finding.
findings.fix: Add a '# placeholder, not a secret' comment in gen_profile.dart, generate distinct throwaway placeholders per release (wg-keypair), and keep TEST-NET-3 for the address so scans do not flag real infrastructure.

findings.evidence: Env: Flutter 3.47.2 (framework d3b14c8769), Dart 3.13.2, windows/sing-box.exe 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15 (Tags: with_awg,with_gvisor,with_quic,with_utls,...), worktree clean. RUN 1: `C:/tools/flutter/bin/flutter.bat test --no-pub --reporter expanded` exit 0, final line `00:11 +302: All tests passed!` (log .pi/tasks/session-25556-25556/bbd37c20f.output). findings.title: No tolerance/threshold configuration for golden comparison and goldens never verified on the CI they ship to: pixel-exact LocalFileComparator with no flutter_test_config.dart, Windows-generated PNGs consumed by ubuntu+windows CI jobs that have never run (no git remote)
findings.evidence: No test/flutter_test_config.dart exists and no goldenFileComparator/threshold configuration anywhere in test/ (grep). Flutter's default _goldens_io.dart LocalFileComparator.compare is exact-pixel (any AA/hinting delta fails). CI runs plain `flutter test` on both ubuntu-latest and windows-latest (.github/workflows/build-android.yml:68, build-windows.yml:46), but the committed PNGs were generated only on Windows (git log -1: 8277f07, Sep 3) and the repo has no git remote, so CI has never executed — cross-platform rasterization equality (embedded test font + bundled MaterialIcons) is an assumption, not a verified fact. There is no documented regeneration path (no scripts/, no comment saying 'ru
findings.fix: Add flutter_test_config.dart pinning goldenFileComparator with a small tolerance (or keep exact and document), and a scripts/update-goldens note; run the suite under Linux once before relying on CI, or gate goldens to a single OS job (e.g. run goldens only on windows-latest) to avoid first-CI red.

findings.title: Layout matrix tested at a single width bucket and dpr: the 200% overflow pass runs only at 375x720 (2-column); the 1-column (<320) and 4-column (>=640) breakpoints and non-1.0 device pixel ratios are never exercised
findings.evidence: home.dart computes columns: width >= 640 ? 4 : (width >= 320 ? 2 : 1) (line 28) — three layout regimes. Tests set physicalSize only to 375x720 (line 76), 360x800 (105), 360x240 (126), all dpr 1.0 with addTearDown reset. The 2-col grid is the only regime where 'no overflow at 200%' is claimed; 1-col wide tiles (long lines at 2.0x scale) and 4-col tablet tiles are never laid out. Low severity because tiles are scrollable and the grid is fluid, but the 'survives the accessibility ceiling' claim is proven for one width bucket only.
findings.fix: Parameterize the 200% overflow pass over physicalSize {320x720, 375x720, 640x900} so all three column regimes are exercised; keep one golden per regime if cost allows.

findings.title: polish_test.dart contains no golden infrastructure at all — clamp-bypass behavior is validated only as pure math, never through the real QanatVpnApp.builder clamp wiring
findings.evidence: The file contains only a clampTextScaler unit group (double clamped(scale) => clampTextScaler(TextScaler.linear(scale)).scale(10)) and a TunnelStateL10n string group with lookupAppLocalizations — no pumpWidget, no golden, no widget render. The clamp's integration (QanatVpnApp.builder wrapping the whole app, app.dart:100-106) is never exercised: nothing verifies that the real builder actually applies the clamp to the tree the user sees (e.g. a pumpWidget of QanatVpnApp with a MediaQuery textScaleFactor of 2.0 asserting a Text renders at 13.5px). If someone removed or reordered the clamp call in the builder, every test would stay green.
findings.fix: Add one widget test that pumps QanatVpnApp with platformDispatcher.textScaleFactorTestValue = 2.0 and asserts find.text(...).textScaleFactor <= 1.35 end-to-end, so the clamp wiring (not just the math) is regression-protected.

findings.evidence: Command 1: C:/tools/flutter/bin/flutter.bat test --no-pub (cwd E:/code/Qanat-VPN) -> exit code 0; final line '00:16 +302: All tests passed!' = 302 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. findings.title: Engine exe is an untracked gitignored artifact with no recorded hash or version guard — provenance verified only by my rebuild, nothing in the repo pins it
findings.evidence: Real binary: `windows/sing-box.exe version` → `sing-box version 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15`, tags with_awg,with_purego, CGO disabled — exactly matches scripts/libbox.ps1 -Variant windows recipe ($tagsMain,with_purego, CGO_ENABLED=0) and submodule pin (git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD = 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15; submodule SHA 57276220 per git submodule status). The exe is NOT tracked by git: `git ls-files windows/` contains no sing-box.exe; root .gitignore line `windows/sing-box.exe`. No sha256 of the exe is recorded anywhere in the repo (grep for e79cf6f… over *.md/*.tsv/*.yml/*.json: zero hits; decisions.tsv records only the version string, not a hash). Reproduced build from the pinned source wit
findings.fix: Record the reference sha256 (e79cf6f19c41f294899144832979cff49bab4e4e1580e63494711ea777723bd4) plus Go toolchain in docs/decisions.tsv, and add a one-line smoke assertion (spawn exe, expect exact version string `1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15`) so a stale/foreign exe fails loudly instead of silently validating parity tests.

findings.title: Engine version string is hardcoded in two build scripts and derived a third way — three sources that can drift after a submodule bump
findings.evidence: Makefile: `VERSION := 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15` and libbox.ps1: `$version = '1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15'` are hardcoded, while build-windows.yml derives `$version = git describe --tags` inside go/amnezia-box. Today all three agree (submodule HEAD is exactly the tag: `git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD` = 1.14.0-rc.1-awgm.15). If the submodule pin moves to a new tag or an untagged commit without updating the two literals, local `make lib_windows`/libbox.ps1 exes keep stamping the OLD version (constant.Version is what `sing-box version` prints and can surface in remote user-agents) while CI stamps the fresh one — and -buildvcs=false means no VCS stamping catches the mismatch.
findings.fix: Derive instead of hardcode: change Makefile/libbox.ps1 to `VERSION := $(shell git -C go/amnezia-box describe --tags)` / `$version = git describe --tags` so a submodule bump updates the stamp in all three places at once.

findings.title: upstream-check.yml 'Report drift' step is echo-only — it never programmatically compares the pin to fetched tags and never notifies
findings.evidence: The job runs `git fetch --all --tags` in go/amnezia-box and then only echoes: `PINNED=$(git -C go/amnezia-box rev-parse HEAD); echo "pinned: $PINNED"` plus a static instruction line. It never computes the latest upstream tag, never compares it to the pin, never fails or opens an issue on drift — a newer awgm tag is only caught if a human reads the weekly logs. It also monitors only the fork (hoaxisr/amnezia-box); upstream sing-box stable progression (rc.1 base vs v1.14.0 shipped) is invisible to it entirely.
findings.fix: Add a compare step: fetch upstream tags, compute `git tag --sort=-v:refname | head -1` vs `git describe --tags`, and fail the job (or open an issue via a pinned action) when a newer awgm tag or a newer upstream sing-box base exists; add a second fetch of SagerNet/sing-box to report base-level drift.

findings.title: Clamp-bypass 200% test exercises a state users can never see while the reachable ceiling (1.35) is barely guarded
findings.evidence: The real app clamps through QanatVpnApp.builder (app.dart:29-33, max 1.35), so raw 2.0 never renders for users; the test duplicates the clamp in its own _wrap builder instead of pumping QanatVpnApp, so if the production builder's clamp changed (removed, widened, applied after MediaQuery), the golden suite would not notice. At the user-visible ceiling 1.35 the only checks are the 3 PNGs (2 tiles) and an implicit pump-throw; a 1.35-only clipping regression inside the 4 scroll-wrapped tiles passes everything (same blindness as the 200% check).
findings.fix: Keep the 2.0 stress margin if desired, but add a 1.35 clip assertion (scroll-extent == 0 per tile) and render through the real clamp path (QanatVpnApp or the production builder body) rather than a parallel implementation.

findings.title: clampTextScaler flattens non-linear TextScalers to a linear scale, and polish_test only ever feeds it linear inputs; file is misplaced under test/ui/
findings.evidence: clampTextScaler (app.dart:26-28) does scale(10)/10 — for a non-linear TextScaler (TextScaler.nonlinear exists as a first-class API in flutter text_scaler.dart; MediaQuery docs describe nonlinear system text scaling) this samples one point and replaces the curve with TextScaler.linear, so different sp sizes lose their differentiated system scaling. polish_test.dart:14-27 feeds only TextScaler.linear inputs, so the production behavior for the OS-level non-linear scaler Android 14+ provides is untested. Separately, test/ui/polish_test.dart contains no testWidgets/pump/golden at all — its UI-polish name is misleading for a pure-logic file.
findings.fix: Add a test asserting clampTextScaler's behavior on TextScaler.nonlinear (document the chosen semantics: flat-clamp is acceptable but should be deliberate), and either rename/relocate polish_test.dart to test/core/ or add actual widget-level polish coverage under test/ui/.

findings.title: FATAL-truth regression tests scattered outside the p1 gate file; the gate does not enumerate the documented engine truths
findings.evidence: p1_transports_emit_test.dart self-describes as the 'Engine-probe gate', but the truths recorded in docs/decisions.tsv lines 38 (AWG id/ip/ib parse-but-never-emit), 72 (tuic alpn under tls.alpn, reality REQUIRES utls), 79 (xhttp x_padding_bytes MANDATORY, ECH legacy removed) are asserted — where at all — in test/vpn/endpoints_test.dart (alpn at :64, id at :253), test/awg/awg_config_test.dart (id/ip/ib at :209), and p1_transports_emit_test.dart (x_padding at :110). Reality-needs-utls is covered positively (p1_emit_parity_test.dart:141 default-chrome + real check) but no test asserts the emitter cannot produce reality-without-utls. A new engine truth added to decisions.tsv has no designated hom
findings.fix: Consolidate: either move/duplicate the truth-case tests into test/p1 as the single engine-truth gate, or add a truth-index comment in p1 listing each decisions.tsv truth with its test location, so the next engine truth lands in the gate by convention.
